I also like that it has dual stage feet which most 65% keyboards do without with them, and I like the way they made the USB port going in the case so the cable can sit flush in it, which does help prevent wearing out the USB Type C port or getting broken. And it feels really good while gaming or typing on it with the new HE magnetic switches, they are really smooth and has a nice clacky sound profile and it is very responsive, the PBT keycaps feels really good and I really do love the grippy texture they have on them that my fingers do not slide off them when gaming for long sessions, and they are shine through legends and they are very easy to see in the dark. The rgb lighting looks really good which I have to say Razer always had the best RGB lighting in my opinion, which there is tons of effects to choose from and to make with the Synapse software, only thing I do notice is the backlighting is not really bright because they did choose to use a diffuser on the switches were the LED are at and the switches have a frosted housing to them, but I really not picky about backlighting on keyboards so it's not an issue for me, but it still looks really good. And you do have to use the software to change the lighting because it can't be done on the keyboard itself, only the brightness can be done on the keyboard itself, but a workaround with that is using the onboard memory which has up to 6 profiles which that can be used for different lighting effects and it works good that way. Another thing I really love, is this keyboard does have gamepad control mode, meaning it can emulate a gamepad which works really well when I don't want to use my controller, not many HE keyboards have this feature but this keyboard does which was great to see! Overall, I really like this keyboard, I love the 65% layout and the clean design it has, and the build quality is solid, and the features it has is great like the gamepad mode, sure it needs Synapse to customize the settings but I really never had issues with the software even on my other keyboards and mouses and I do like it, call me lucky I don't know, I also like that it came with a really nice 6 foot braided cord which is long enough to reach from my PC way behind my monitor with more to spare. So if you love the design and the 65% layout and hall effect switches, the value you get from this keyboard is great in my opinion, so it does get a solid 5 stars from me, I haven't had an issue yet and I had it for a couple weeks now👍

product_title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini 65% 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
headline: Razer’s Hall Effect Switches Are a Major Improvement
review_text_raw: Razer has made adjustable-actuation keyboards before, but its previous analog Huntsman models relied on optical switches. This is its first real move into the Hall effect keyboard space, and the switch change is not just a spec-sheet distinction. These new magnetic switches feel noticeably smoother and less scratchy than the optical analog switches I have used in the past, especially when pressing a key slowly or typing for longer periods. They also retain a full 4.0mm range of travel, which is less common than I expected among Hall effect gaming keyboards. I can set a very shallow actuation point for movement keys in competitive games without making the entire board feel like a hair trigger. For typing, I prefer a deeper actuation and the full key travel because it feels more natural and gives me fewer accidental inputs. That flexibility makes the Huntsman V3 HE easier to live with as an everyday keyboard rather than something designed exclusively for ranked matches. Rapid trigger works as expected, resetting each key based on movement rather than waiting for it to return to a fixed reset point. In shooters, directional inputs feel crisp and immediate, particularly when rapidly stopping, strafing, or changing direction. Snap Tap can prioritize the newest input between two movement keys, while Snap Flex adds another way to activate commands based on releasing a key. These features will matter most to serious FPS players, but the adjustable actuation is useful even outside competitive gaming. The 8000Hz polling rate gives the keyboard plenty of performance headroom. I cannot pretend the jump from an already fast gaming keyboard is transformative in every game, but inputs feel consistently immediate, and there is no sense that the keyboard is holding anything back. It is also possible to store multiple profiles, which is useful when I want aggressive gaming settings without using those same settings while typing or programming. headline: Hall Effect Makes The Difference
review_text_raw: Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic TKL 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard | Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, 8000 Hz Polling, Razer Snap Flex,Razer Snap Tap, Rapid Trigger, Adjustable Actuation So this listing is for the v3 ten key less Hunstman v3 8K HE keyboard specifically designed for gaming with hall effect switches and snap tap actions. The keyboard has an 8000 Hz polling rate and has onboard memory to store profiles. I have both the v1 and v2 version of this exact keyboard so comparing all three of these keyboards, they all have the exact same solid build quality and sound quality which is a quite thocky experience. The keyboards are solidly built and made of premium material which leads to a very comfortable typing experience. The keyboard is constructed of a solid plastic and metal material which makes them feel premium. The keyboard is about 14" x 5" x 2" high and weighs in with a heft and weight that allows it to sit solidly on your desk. I have been using this keyboard exclusively for nearly two weeks now and it is now my daily driver. I am thoroughly impressed by the HE switches and how very comfortable it is to type on. The software is the one short area as the Synapse software really does not effectively work on Mac but it does sort of work on Windows but don't expect much. The keyboard itself is highly customizable and allows for full customization in color along with key press. Also there is no Linux support either but you can use SignalRGB to control lighting. Also Synapse itself really bogs down your PC and slowly causes a memory leak which means you need to regularly reboot your PC. That being said, the level of customization is something to behold. You can customize everything from tap throw distances to macro's and feature sets. The keyboard can literally be customized by key for color if you want to go through and do that - all though I just keep them one solid color purple for my keyboard. The elevators on the back of the keyboard also help make the keyboard much more comfortable to type on at an angle. The keyboard's compact size really makes it ideal for someone who is limited in space. The price for this keyboard is a premium and is not always the best value for the money but that is not why you are buying this keyboard. This keyboard is designed for someone already in the ecosystem for this keyboard and for the enthusiast who wants the latest and greatest product from the company. Overall I'm very happy with my purchase

product_title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini 65% 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
headline: Elite Magnetic TKL Keyboard With Precision Control
review_text_raw: The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless is engineered as a competitive‐grade keyboard built around Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, offering adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm and a 100‐million keystroke lifespan (). This switch architecture eliminates debounce delay entirely, enabling instantaneous actuation and reset behavior that mechanical switches simply cannot match. The magnetic sensing provides exceptionally consistent input recognition, and the keyboard’s internal calibration system compensates for magnetic interference to maintain stable performance over time. Combined with the TKL layout, which frees up desk space for low‐sensitivity mouse movement, the Huntsman V3 HE is clearly designed for players who rely on precision micro‐adjustments and rapid directional changes. One of the most defining features is Rapid Trigger, which allows keys to reset the moment they begin to rise rather than waiting for a fixed reset point. This dramatically increases responsiveness in FPS titles, enabling faster counter‐strafes, smoother movement corrections, and more reliable repeated inputs. Esports.gg’s testing highlights how Rapid Trigger transforms WASD control, making movement feel “snappy, predictable, and extremely responsive” — a sentiment that aligns with real‐world gameplay impressions. The keyboard also supports Dynamic Keystroke, allowing up to four actions on a single key at different actuation depths, and Snap Flex, which assigns one action on press and another on release. These features give competitive players granular control over movement, utility activation, and complex keybind setups, especially in games like Valorant, CS2, and Apex Legends (). The Huntsman V3 HE’s 8000 Hz HyperPolling is another major technical advantage. With true 8000 Hz performance, the keyboard sends input data to the PC eight times more frequently than standard 1000 Hz keyboards, reducing average latency to 0.60 ms — roughly 8% faster than competing high‐end boards (). In fast‐paced shooters, this reduction in input delay contributes to more immediate movement and firing responses. Esports.gg’s analysis notes that the keyboard feels “instantaneous,” with no perceptible delay between keypress and on‐screen action. For competitive players who rely on tight timing windows, this level of responsiveness provides a measurable advantage. Build quality is another strong point. The keyboard uses a 5052 aluminum alloy top case, which gives it a rigid, premium feel while keeping weight manageable for LAN events. The switches are factory‐lubricated, and a dense internal foam layer improves acoustics, reducing hollow resonance and delivering a smoother, more muted sound profile. The doubleshot PBT keycaps resist shine and wear, maintaining texture even under heavy daily use. The detachable USB‐C cable and hybrid onboard storage for up to six profiles add practical flexibility, especially for players who switch between systems or travel frequently (). Razer’s software approach is also noteworthy. The Huntsman V3 HE supports Synapse for Web, allowing users to adjust actuation, Rapid Trigger sensitivity, polling rate, lighting, and keybinds directly through a browser without installing software — ideal for tournament environments or shared PCs. The keyboard’s Chroma RGB is bright and evenly diffused, and while lighting is not the focus of this model, it integrates cleanly with competitive setups. Real‐world impressions consistently highlight the keyboard’s stability, predictable actuation behavior, and the immediate improvement in movement control during gameplay. Overall, the Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless delivers exceptional responsiveness, deep customization, durable construction, and esports‐grade precision. Its combination of Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, Rapid Trigger, Dynamic Keystroke, Snap Tap, and true 8000 Hz HyperPolling makes it one of the most technically advanced competitive keyboards available. For players who prioritize movement accuracy, instant input recognition, and customizable actuation, this keyboard offers a genuine performance advantage that is immediately noticeable in high‐speed FPS environments.

product_title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini 65% 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
headline: Maybe im ready to give Razer another chance
review_text_raw: The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini keyboard is the latest addition to their Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard lineup. If you haven't been keeping up with keyboard technologies, compared to traditional keyboard switches made by companies like Cherry, they are now utilizing magnets and lasers to create a much more responsive key press reducing latency and allowing for customizable key actuation based on the users preference. I am a hobbyist with keyboard tech, where I have built a good variety of keyboards with DIY kits, customized some of my own, and tend to go out of my way to try new technologies. This is my third time trying a Hall Effect keyboard, with my first being the Steelseries Apex Pro ( with HyperMagnetic switches) and the original Razer Huntsman. I didn't hold onto either of those keyboards very long as at the time they were very expensive compared to their traditional counterparts. They also didn't wow me out of the box with their switch technology. Keypresses felt weak, as if there was no feedback to register that I had hit a key. It also took a lot of tweaking to get them to what I would consider a usable state with accurate typing. Which leaves me with the new Razer Huntsman, where I am happy to report it doesn't share any of these problems. The recent revisions have made many changes, improving the texture on the keycaps, the sound of the keypresses, the out of box actuation is exactly what I want, and the 8khz polling is probably helping with how responsive the keys feel. I generally use full size keyboards as I like to have a numpad, but the feel of this keyboard is winning me over to make it my daily driver away from my Mountain Everest Max with Cherry Blues. Lubed Holy Panda switches are the only ones I own that might feel a little bit better than these, but the overall responsiveness of these HE Magentics is something I haven't had the pleasure of experiencing before. My closing statement will be that I started my PC peripheral journey with Razer back when they released the first Blackwidow keyboard & OG Razer Naga. I have watched their products go through sharp declines, and had a time of regret after recommending them to several friends and watching their mice break down on them within a year each. I am hesitant to recommend them again due to the many issues I have had across a few years before ultimately moving away from their products entirely. I will update this review if I encounter any issues with the keyboard as I daily drive it. Post note: I forgot to mention Synapse in this review, as I don't really want to use it. I will add it in if I change my mind but luckily the keyboard works fine without it. Windows Dynamic Lighting isn't working with the keyboard out of the box but I know of other 3rd party software that used to work with Razer that I preferred. After one pop up the Razer software installer hasn't appeared again which is nice.

headline: It's my favorite style of keyboard
review_text_raw: Great keyboard with 99% in common with my all time favorite keyboard... the ASUS keyboard MODEL: AW211. The only reason I'm switching out my keyboard after 8-9 years is because of the amount of dirt that builds up over that time period. I am hoping the Amazon Basics brand MD-005 keyboard has the same longevity. Immediately you'll notice the keyboard layout is the same until you reach the only 3 lights on the top right, but I believe the cord is a foot longer on the Amazon model. With my ASUS motherboard and AMD chipset, this keyboard fails to be recognized (unlike my ASUS one) on startup. I simply have to unplug my MD-005 USB and plug it back in and no further issues until I turn my PC off again. I use this keyboard for internet browsing and some work, but mostly for gaming actually. The responsiveness and feel of these keyboards is unmatched, but the amazon one (for better or worse) has slightly stiffer keys in terms of how much effort they require to push down. On rare occasion, one time so far, a keystroke will be missed. This could very well be user error. All in all, even with the issue of needing to plug it back in every restart, this keyboard well worth it. It's nothing fancy, but it's exactly what I wanted. I removed a star as my hands get more tired of typing on this keyboard than my ASUS one and the inconvenience of needing to unplug and plug it back in on startup. I would however still recommend this keyboard despite these flaws. While I am gaming the stiff keys are not noticed.

headline: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
review_text_raw: It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

headline: Satisfying typing experience
review_text_raw: I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so. This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to. It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever. As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience. The only complaint from my daughter is that it doesn't have colored backlight. It's just plain white.

headline: Beautiful keyboard
review_text_raw: So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below. -The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch. -Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment. -Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.) One minor negative is the backlight. The first problem was even getting the keyboard to light up at all. The keys for the keyboard backlight simply did not seem to function at all, no matter if I had the FN key held or not. Puzzled, I installed logitech's software and looked for options there. No luck. A bit annoyed at this point. Luckily, their software offered me access to an upcoming beta version of their software, "Logitech Options", so I downloaded that to poke around and see if there were more settings there. As it turns out there were. Oddly, they didn't work though. The keyboard refused to light up, the keys meant to dim or brighten it doing nothing at all. As I began a search to see if this was a common issue, the backlight finally came on. No idea what changed. Pretty standard white LED backlights. Lots of pissed off customers on forums about it though. Apparently, Logitech has been pretty silent about the issue. headline: Very disappointing for a $150+ keyboard.
review_text_raw: I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard. First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off. I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is... And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck. At first I thought I just had to adjust the timeout settings on the Logi Options+ app. Nope! No options! Just a couple of annoying, distracting backlight animations (like, random keys illuminating, why would anyone want that?!). I'm not sure who signed-off on the design for this thing or what they were thinking. Furthermore, the caps lock key has a distracting blinking whenever it is on, especially annoying if you are gaming and caps lock is set to something like toggle run/walk. The keyboard is Bluetooth only, which seems to work fine. But I would have liked to have the option to plug it in like a normal USB keyboard. As far as I know the USB plug is only for charging, but also leaves an always illuminated and fairly bright "charging" LED, very obnoxious if your computer is in your bedroom. In short: Don't waste your money on this. I will be returning mine.

headline: Beware the USB dongles
review_text_raw: Original review: It's a keyboard an it works After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing). I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had. Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that. For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software. Honestly, at this price, I am not sure I would recommend this keyboard. Ok, so why 4 stars? It does have some positive points. First, it looks pretty sharp. Second, aside from not sitting flat, it feels solid / well-built / quality. It is small, yet it is heavier than most keyboards. I am used to keyboards lasting "forever", so I will update here if/when I run into issues. Third, switching between different machines works flawlessly. Fourth, it allows me to bring my settings to all computers (e.g. remapping the screen capture key). Fifth, it has a rechargeable battery and it lasts long enough that I never have to worry. I do have a charging cable right on my desk, so every once in a while I just leave it plugged in, so I have never seen it go below 85%. What else can I say, it is a keyboard and it works. ----- Updated review: beware the USB dongles. Logitech mouses and keyboards (e.g. "MX Mechanical", "MX Master 3s", "MX Anywhere 3") connect either via Bluetooth, or via a USB dongle. However, the USB dongles are not all the same. For example, the "MX mechanical" keyboard only connects to a "bolt" dongle; and the "MX Anywhere 3" mouse only connects to a "unifying" dongle. Unfortunately, there is no clear guide / summary for which devices go together. You just have to check each device before buying to see what dongle it uses. Devices in the same generation are *not* guaranteed to use the same type of dongle. Here is my experience: I setup for myself a MX mechanical keyboard + MX Master 3s mouse and everything works fine. Both devices connect to a "bolt" dongle, so I have a "bolt" dongle on my laptop, and another "bolt" dongle on a desktop computer. I can switch between laptop and desktop with a press of a button. The keyboard/mouse itself is fine, the review can be seen above. My wife saw my setup and wanted the same, but she didn't want the MX Master 3s mouse ("it is too big"), so I got her a this same "MX Mechanical" keyboard and a pink "MX Anywhere 3". As it turns out, the mouse does not come with a "bolt" dongle, it comes with a "unifying" dongle. So now I have one "bolt" dongle which connects only to the keyboard, and one "unifying" dongle which connects only to the mouse. Thus, to "fix" this situation, I either need to use Bluetooth for everything (which I was trying to avoid to begin with), or I need to purchase 1 extra bolt dongle and 1 extra unifying dongle, so that each computer has both a "unifying" and a "bolt" dongle. Let's hope I have enough USB ports, or I will also need a USB hub. Even if you are aware that different dongles exist, you still need to be careful. If you buy a "MX Anywhere 3", you get a "unifying" dongle, but if you buy a "MX Anywhere 3 for business", then it has a "bolt" dongle. This is, by the way, how I ended up with a "unifying" dongle - while browsing the products, I opened up two tabs, one with a black MX Anywhere 3, and one with a pink MX Anywhere 3, except one of them was "for business" and the other was not. You might think this mess would warrant giant disclaimers ("DOES NOT HAVE A BOLT CONNECTOR"), or some kind of guide for which devices go together, but nope. For extra hilarity, Amazon bundles a "MX mechanical mini" (bolt) with a "MX Anywhere 3" (unifying). The whole thing is confusing, misleading, and just terrible user/customer experience. If I could start over, I would just get something else.

headline: It's my favorite style of keyboard
review_text_raw: Great keyboard with 99% in common with my all time favorite keyboard... the ASUS keyboard MODEL: AW211. The only reason I'm switching out my keyboard after 8-9 years is because of the amount of dirt that builds up over that time period. I am hoping the Amazon Basics brand MD-005 keyboard has the same longevity. Immediately you'll notice the keyboard layout is the same until you reach the only 3 lights on the top right, but I believe the cord is a foot longer on the Amazon model. With my ASUS motherboard and AMD chipset, this keyboard fails to be recognized (unlike my ASUS one) on startup. I simply have to unplug my MD-005 USB and plug it back in and no further issues until I turn my PC off again. I use this keyboard for internet browsing and some work, but mostly for gaming actually. The responsiveness and feel of these keyboards is unmatched, but the amazon one (for better or worse) has slightly stiffer keys in terms of how much effort they require to push down. On rare occasion, one time so far, a keystroke will be missed. This could very well be user error. All in all, even with the issue of needing to plug it back in every restart, this keyboard well worth it. It's nothing fancy, but it's exactly what I wanted. I removed a star as my hands get more tired of typing on this keyboard than my ASUS one and the inconvenience of needing to unplug and plug it back in on startup. I would however still recommend this keyboard despite these flaws. While I am gaming the stiff keys are not noticed.

review_text_raw: Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you- A couple of things I wasn't really aware of- 1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys 2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

Eventually I decided that since I paid $100+ I was going to get a working product. product_title: SteelSeries USB Apex 5 Hybrid Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Per-Key RGB Illumination – Aircraft Grade Aluminum Alloy Frame – OLED Smart Display (Hybrid Blue Switch)
headline: Outstanding, with a possible caveat
review_text_raw: Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns. This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. product_title: SteelSeries USB Apex 5 Hybrid Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Per-Key RGB Illumination – Aircraft Grade Aluminum Alloy Frame – OLED Smart Display (Hybrid Blue Switch)
headline: SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)
review_text_raw: The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. It’s a well-built keyboard with some excellent features and clever design choices. The cable is thick, long, and even has a nice touch — the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug. The RGB effects are top-notch, with smooth transitions both on keypress and when idle. I was genuinely excited about all of this... until I noticed what was missing. And for me, that’s a big deal. Let’s break it down.😁 ### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃 - Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient. - Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting. - Smart OLED Display: It shows the status of Num Lock, Caps Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Windows key is disabled. Very handy (though there’s a small catch — more on that below). - Customization & Visual Feedback: Besides full per-key RGB customization and reactive effects, pressing the “Fn” key (the SteelSeries logo key) lights up related function keys in red for quick reference. It’s super helpful... but again, not perfect (you can’t change the color — more on that too). - Profile Memory Built-In: You can save up to 5 profiles directly on the keyboard and toggle them on/off without cycling through all of them. I personally use just two: one for gaming and one for productivity. ### The Not-So-Good – My Gripes😒: - No Dedicated Context Menu Key: This is my biggest issue. A full-size keyboard should include the dedicated menu key (the "right-click menu" key). SteelSeries replaced it with their custom “Fn” key, which really disrupted my usual workflow. I ended up switching to Shift + F10 to keep things consistent across devices. - Fn Key Can’t Be Reassigned: The SteelSeries logo key, which replaces the context menu key, is fixed — it can’t be remapped. Personally, I’d have preferred having the Windows key only on the left, and using the right one for Fn, keeping the menu key in its usual place. - OLED Button Always Lit: The brightness of the button next to the OLED screen cannot be dimmed or turned off. If you’re working in a dark room or watching movies, this little light will keep shining at you — kind of annoying. - OLED Icons Overlap Custom Logos: If you upload a custom image to the OLED screen, the status icons for Num Lock, Caps, etc. may overlap your logo. Not a dealbreaker, but it limits how creative you can get with personalization. - No Visual Feedback When Windows Key Is Locked: Unlike other lock states (like Caps Lock), there’s no lighting change or visual indicator on the keyboard itself when the Windows key is disabled — just a small icon on the OLED. Feels inconsistent. - Function Key Highlight Color Can’t Be Changed: When pressing “Fn,” the related keys light up red — but that red is not customizable. If your RGB theme is red, this effect becomes basically invisible. - Slight Input Delay: There’s a small delay in key activation. I don’t notice it while typing or working, but for competitive gaming, it might matter. Rtings.com confirmed this in their testing too. - Non-Replaceable Hybrid Switches This is the most serious issue. The switches aren’t standard and can’t be replaced by the user. If a key fails, you’re stuck with relying on warranty, support... or scavenging another board. Not great. ### Neutral Points – Might Be Good or Bad Depending on You🤷🏻♂️: - Actuation Distance: I switched from a keyboard with ultra-light 0.8 mm actuation, and I kept typing extra characters. The Apex 5 feels much more precise and helped reduce typos — a big plus for me. - Key Feel & Keycaps: The keycaps aren’t made from premium material, but they feel decent. Coming from linear switches, the tactile feel took a bit of getting used to — but I adjusted quickly. - Magnetic Wrist Rest: I don’t use it much, but the magnets are strong and hold it firmly in place. - Macro Labeling (M1, M2, etc.): Some keys are labeled as macro keys (M1, M2...), which can be confusing at first — but you’ll get used to it. - Customization Without Software: You can change basic RGB effects and profiles directly from the keyboard. The software adds more depth, but it’s nice that you’re not forced to use it. - USB Plug with Logo: A small but smart touch: the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug helps you spot which device you’re plugging in. - No Physical Lock LEDs: The lock indicators (Num Lock, Caps, Scroll) have been moved to the OLED screen, and you can set those keys to change color when active. Some might miss the old-school LED lights, but I’m fine with it. ### Final Verdict 💸😇 The SteelSeries Apex 5 is a well-built, visually polished keyboard with great RGB, useful media controls, and a solid set of features for gamers and professionals alike. Still, a few oversights — especially the missing context menu key and the non-replaceable switches — keep it from being a perfect 5-star device in my eyes. If those flaws don’t bother you, then this keyboard is an easy recommendation. Just know what you're getting — and what you're not

Just didn't expect that I would have to be the one doing the refurbishing on day one. But that's why I gave it 4 stars, pretty easy to perform user maintenance on it to ensure that it continues to function. Which boggles me why Amazon didn't do that.

product_title: Kisnt KN85 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, 75% Layout, Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C, Custom RGB Backlit, Hot-Swappable Linear Switch, Creamy Sound for Gaming/Typing (Retro Beige)
headline: Super impressive for the price.
review_text_raw: I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time. I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect. It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate. My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable. For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.

product_title: Kisnt KN85 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, 75% Layout, Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C, Custom RGB Backlit, Hot-Swappable Linear Switch, Creamy Sound for Gaming/Typing (Retro Beige)
headline: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
review_text_raw: This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable. My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

headline: Great mechanical keyboard for productivity
review_text_raw: Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age. The value of this keyboard is excellent. Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism. The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters. Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much. I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me). I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke. So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate. headline: Feels like the legendary Model M, sporting it strong points and its quirks.
review_text_raw: If you missed the old,clicky Model M from IBM, this keyboard emulates it pretty well. One must consider though, that it may emulate it too well. If you have fat fingers, you will find yourself making the same typos that you mad in high school when you learned to type on one. However, this is no deal breaker in my opinion. The speed at which I can type has vastly improved with the solid tactile feedback that tells you without a doubt that you press was registered. Setup couldn't be easier, just plug it into any USB port and away you go. Recognizes immediately as a 104 key with perks. Having the media controls and other immediate functions right there is nice too. As far as the design goes, it is very rugged and ready for the millions of keystrokes you will put on it as a writer. You will find a kind of typing joy you haven't experienced in quite a long time. No soft-touch or sickle keyboard will match the feel from what you get here. The only thing I find really off is the shallow height of the back stands. I think that they should be redesigned to be a bit taller. I cut a little piece of flat trim to set them on and that made the angle perfect. All-in-all, this keyboard is a joy to type on. I don't use it for gaming, because I see this as a waste of a premium feeling keyboard, wearing out the ASWD area and ruining it. I haven't had such a good keyboard in years and I'm not destroying that way. The one caveat I would warn you about is that if you use it on a KVM switch that is USB powered, this keyboard draws quite a bit of power to run the back light. be aware that you may get video background issues. Mine works just fine if I turn the backlight down low.

product_title: Cherry KC 200 MX Wired Mechanical Office Keyboard MX2A Silent RED Switches
headline: Very good for the price
review_text_raw: This is certainly a bargain priced mechanical keyboard but that doesn't mean it's bad; in fact, it's excellent. I got the model with silent red switches. I already own a Cherry silent red without the number pad but I wanted a full size. This one is ever so slightly less silent, likely due to an aluminum frame (a plus) rather than plastic. But it is still quiet enough to use in the bedroom at any hour. It is wired only. I actually prefer a wired connection rather than fooling with Bluetooth or dongles. To save space there is no plastic "frame" around the keys but this is just a matter of looks and you may prefer it, as the aluminum base is very attractive. It did take a little positioning to reach a stable state but that may have been my desk as much as the keyboard. There are tabs to raise the back but I don't use them. The keys are clearly marked and have a good feel to them. Let's see if with use they take on a shine; it's too soon to tell. This is a keyboard I will use a lot as I do most of my work on my home desktop setup. So far the typing experience has been exactly what I expect from this type of switch; there is enough of a tactile feel to be reliable but of course it's limited by the damped switches. (I do love the positive solid feedback of the very loud, clicky blue switches but my home office is in the bedroom and that doesn't work out.) The only thing I can't speak to is the software for remapping the keys. This can be downloaded from the Cherry site. But it doesn't run on my Linux system so I can't make use of it. However I really see no need to remap any of the keys, and if I really need to do that, there are other ways. I definitely rate this keyboard at 5 stars. It is great value for the money and gets you into the wonderful world of mechanical keyboards without breaking the bank. I have had great luck with Cherry products and this one is another winner.

product_title: Cherry KC 200 MX Wired Mechanical Office Keyboard MX2A Silent RED Switches
headline: I can't believe the improvement over other switches. It's crazy!
review_text_raw: If you thought other companies made good key switches, then you are in for a surprise with this keyboard. Cherry absolutely nailed it with these new MX2A switches. I purchased the version with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. Now, I basically hate linear switches. Really, I usually can't stand them, but these new silents reds are the smoothest, and most buttery feeling switches I have ever felt. I have been using mechanical keyboards my entire life. Since before the patent ran out on the Cherry MX switches and the only mechanical keyboards you could buy had Cherry switches. Now, everyone makes their own switches, with all kinds of "features" like hall effect, rapid trigger, analog, adjustable actuation, magnets, etc.. Here's the issue with all of those though, they feel like crap to type on and are super loud. I have spent thousands on keyboards over the years. I still have over 15 mechanical keyboards sitting in storage that I stopped using. I am not exaggerating either. To give you an idea of where I'm coming from, my favorite switches used to be Cherry MX Brown. Now they are Cherry MX2A Silent Reds. I haven't even mentioned how quiet they are too. Unbelievably quiet for a mechanical keyboard. It's definitely the quietest mech keyboard I have ever used, which is saying a lot. Some people may think the keyboard is fairly basic, and in all reality, it is. It doesn't require software, doesn't have RGB or any lights (besides the led for caps lock and such), it doesn't have a removeable cable, or a super high polling rate over 1000Hz. Visually and functionally speaking, the keyboard is simple. But that a huge positive in my book. It does have full N-key rollover, so if you do use it for gaming, there won't be any issues there. I don't need to install any bloat to use the keyboard. I don't need to configure anything. It's just plug and play. It's fairly compact for a full-sized keyboard too, so be aware of the slightly more compact layout. My only real complaint is that it does not have 4 rubber feet on the bottom to keep it from sliding around. There are 2 rubber feet on the bottom front, but on the bottom rear, the feet are hard plastic, so it doesn't stay in place super well. There are rubber pads on the bottom rear feet that fold out, but I don't use a keyboard angled, so they are useless for me. Other than that, one thing, this keyboard is perfect for me. Am I going to use it for my hardcore gaming sessions? No. I actually purchased it for office work, and it's going to be perfect for that. However, will I be purchasing another keyboard with these same exact switches for my gaming pc? 100% YES! Look, you may not like the design of this keyboard, or its simplicity, but do not sleep on these new Cherry switches. Cherry is back with a vengeance, and if you're looking for a new keyboard, get one with these new Cherry switches. Whether it be this keyboard or not. The switch is king, and Cherry is back on top. Update: I now own 3 of these keyboards, lol, all with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. One for the gaming pc, one for the work office, and one for the home office. They can't be beaten when it comes to typing quality. No regrets.

This is my first mechanical keyboard, and I finally understand what all the hype is about. The sound is incredibly satisfying. It has that nice mechanical sound without being overly loud or obnoxious, but it also isn't so quiet that you lose the satisfying typing experience. The typing feel is probably my favorite part—the keys feel incredibly smooth and satisfying, and so far everything has felt flawless. The build quality is also really impressive for the price. You can use it for things like Bluetooth connection and volume settings, and you can also customize it with your own photo or GIF. The one area that could definitely be improved is the software. It's not particularly user-friendly, and finding the correct software to customize the keyboard took me longer than it should have. Once I actually found it, though, it wasn't too difficult to figure out with a little patience. The software itself also feels a little chunky and dated. That said, this has zero effect on the actual performance of the keyboard, so it's a very minor complaint. I've had absolutely no issues with wireless connectivity. I've used both Bluetooth and the included cable and haven't experienced any disconnections, lag, or other problems. One thing to note is that you'll need to use the included cable when connecting the keyboard to the software for customization. The battery life has also been surprisingly good so far. I haven't actually had to charge it yet, so I can't speak to the full battery life, but I work from home about 9 hours a day and also casually game in the evenings. After two days of that, the battery has only dropped about 5%. Overall, I have very little negative to say about this keyboard. The software could definitely use some improvement, and there could be better information provided about where to find and how to use it. But that's a very small complaint compared to everything else this keyboard does well. For my first mechanical keyboard, I'm extremely happy with it. Everything about it has exceeded my expectations. 5/5 and definitely recommend!

Build? Beautiful. Sound? Amazing. Functionality? PERFECT. Price? FANTASTIC. If this keyboard fits your specifications for your desk and you happen to work with two different computers at the same time, get it ASAP. More details: Previously I had a significantly smaller RK 68 which was great for me. It was perfect for what I wanted, a small profile and clacky keyboard. Unfortunately, I spilled soda all over it and it died so I had to get a new one. Fortunately, it was this keyboard. In my search for a new keyboard I had a couple things I was looking for: - A green color way to match my set up - A nice clack to it. - A numpad attached. Clearly it's not something very specific. But during my search I came across other features that I had no idea I wanted. But this one hit pretty much what I was looking for so I decided to give it a try and boy did it blow my expectations out of the water. == Design == Pros: This keyboard looks sleek. Before, to build something like this I had considered paying my friend to build it from scratch but the colorway and the key placements are just so clean. With multifunctional keycaps, they've added the second function on the side of the keycap so you can easily see the primary and the secondary without it feeling too cluttered. The back lighting options really make it fun to customize. They give you default options you can run with and each of those options you can tweak to your liking in terms of color. The digital display seems more like a part of the design the way it links to the volume knob, rather than an after thought like some other keyboards. This provides another option for you to make the keyboard your own by letting you upload a gif to just loop by default. Cons: No complaints really, except the digital display occasionally pops off slightly, requiring you to press it back in but it hasn't become too much of an issue for me yet. Also, uploading the gif to the keyboard takes a good amount of time (something like 5 minutes) , so if they could fix that speed that would be amazing. Oh one more complaint is that it's too tall. I had to get a wrist mount just to feel comfortable typing on it. == Functionality == Pros: MAN, this keyboard is PACKED with features I never thought I would need. Aside from the aforementioned backlight customization, something that has made my life so much better is hidden behind the digital display. It's base functionality of controlling the volume of your computer works like a charm but it's when you get into the submenus that you can really see where it shines. You see, I am someone who bounces between a macbook pro for work and a windows PC for play and so I'm constantly bouncing between the two. Before, I had a mac specific keyboard and a windows specific keyboard, both occupying space on my desk. This keyboard has eliminated that need in a sleek and elegant way by allowing me to hardwire into my desktop and bluetooth to my macbook. From there, I can easily use the digital display + volume knob to switch my connection between the two. Heck, if I needed to add another couple I could. It seems like I can have up to 5 different devices connected (3 bluetooth, 1 wired, 1 wireless dongle). So if for some reason I had another device, I could easily switch between the two. You might ask yourself, but what about the difference in layout between macs and windows machines? Oh my friend, you see... THEY THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING. Through the same digital display, you can swap the layouts between the two types. I was totally fine with that until I read the manual a bit more and found you could even use a hotkey JUST for that. Remember the secondary functions of the various keys? If you look on the side of the 'A' and 'S' keys, you can see that they read 'WIN' and 'MAC' respectively. So to switch formats, all you have to do is hit 'Fn' + 'A' or 'S' to switch between the two. This really pushed my like for this keyboard to love. Cons: The only thing I can really think of is a nitpick and is possibly even already a function, I'd just have to read through the manual a bit more. It would be nice to be able to use a shortcut to bounce between the different keyboard connections like you can switch formats. == Sound and Feel == Pros: I am having a BLAST typing this review. Every keypress feels so satisfying as the switches engage and disengage making you really feel connected to the keyboard. The sound is more thocky than clacky which is extremely pleasing to my ears, especially after coming from a clackier keyboard. Cons: While this keyboard is probably 50 percent quieter than my last keyboard, it's still definitely louder than a membrane keyboard, so if you're looking for silent, this isn't what you want. But if you're looking at mechanical keyboards, then this most likely isn't you. == Price == I feel like this keyboard is well worth the 89 dollar price tag for what you get. I feel like even a couple years ago, you'd have to pay 300 bucks to someone to custom make something like this with the design options. Sure, it's not as bespoke as the true customs, but I feel like it holds up just as well. Overall, I'd give this keyboard a 'have no fear, buy away' if your needs are similar to what I've mentioned above!

It's base functionality of controlling the volume of your computer works like a charm but it's when you get into the submenus that you can really see where it shines. You see, I am someone who bounces between a macbook pro for work and a windows PC for play and so I'm constantly bouncing between the two. Before, I had a mac specific keyboard and a windows specific keyboard, both occupying space on my desk. This keyboard has eliminated that need in a sleek and elegant way by allowing me to hardwire into my desktop and bluetooth to my macbook. From there, I can easily use the digital display + volume knob to switch my connection between the two. Heck, if I needed to add another couple I could. It seems like I can have up to 5 different devices connected (3 bluetooth, 1 wired, 1 wireless dongle). So if for some reason I had another device, I could easily switch between the two. You might ask yourself, but what about the difference in layout between macs and windows machines? Oh my friend, you see... THEY THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING. Through the same digital display, you can swap the layouts between the two types. I was totally fine with that until I read the manual a bit more and found you could even use a hotkey JUST for that. Remember the secondary functions of the various keys? If you look on the side of the 'A' and 'S' keys, you can see that they read 'WIN' and 'MAC' respectively. So to switch formats, all you have to do is hit 'Fn' + 'A' or 'S' to switch between the two. This really pushed my like for this keyboard to love. Cons: The only thing I can really think of is a nitpick and is possibly even already a function, I'd just have to read through the manual a bit more. It would be nice to be able to use a shortcut to bounce between the different keyboard connections like you can switch formats. == Sound and Feel == Pros: I am having a BLAST typing this review. Every keypress feels so satisfying as the switches engage and disengage making you really feel connected to the keyboard. The sound is more thocky than clacky which is extremely pleasing to my ears, especially after coming from a clackier keyboard. Cons: While this keyboard is probably 50 percent quieter than my last keyboard, it's still definitely louder than a membrane keyboard, so if you're looking for silent, this isn't what you want. But if you're looking at mechanical keyboards, then this most likely isn't you. == Price == I feel like this keyboard is well worth the 89 dollar price tag for what you get. I feel like even a couple years ago, you'd have to pay 300 bucks to someone to custom make something like this with the design options. Sure, it's not as bespoke as the true customs, but I feel like it holds up just as well. Overall, I'd give this keyboard a 'have no fear, buy away' if your needs are similar to what I've mentioned above!

headline: All the mechanical keyboard I need
review_text_raw: First mechanical keyboard I’ve owned, can’t imagine I’d need anything different. Bought two of these, one for my workspace and one for my wife. We both needed accurate and responsive keys for frequent data and password entry, the lights and display are just bonus points. I change out my display for random gifs and RGB weekly using the web portal, easy enough once you get the hang of it, takes 5-10 minutes to upload a gif. Can confirm battery lasts about a week with moderate workday use. Keys are on the quieter end of clacky, not as obnoxious as some mechanical keyboards I’ve used in the past. Key travel registers about 75% from fully depressed which took me a tiny bit of time to adapt to. More often now, I’ll think I missed a letter because I didn’t press quite hard enough, but look back to find it registered after all. Comes with a few replacement switches, key puller, and usb-c cable which is nice. I’m sure there is better quality for more money out there but I’m not the demographic for it, this is all the keyboard I think I’ll ever need.

product_title: RK ROYAL KLUDGE S98 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard w/Smart Display & Knob
headline: A must have for anyone looking for an amazing sounding keyboard!
review_text_raw: When I first got a gaming PC, I figured I didn't really need a super expensive keyboard and that a cheap one that sounded "clicky" and had lights was fine enough. I also didn't want to bother with charging a wireless keyboard. However, I started to hear from YouTube videos and TikToks about "creamy" and "thocky" keyboards. I immediately started to do research, because I was obsessed with the sound. This is one of those rare purchases that I cannot stop thinking about how happy it makes me. I have absolutely no qualms with it. Here's what I love: The sound is excellent. Videos that I watched were a good indicator, but as other reviews have said, they really do not do the keyboard justice for how it actually sounds. The letters themselves are very creamy, while the function buttons (spacebar, shift, enter, backspace, etc.) have a much deeper "thocky" sound to them. If you're on the fence, at least try it and return if it's not for you. The functionality is incredible. There are a ton of lighting options that you can play with. You can mess around with them in the software on your PC. But because this keyboard has a small LCD screen, you can also change them directly on the keyboard itself. I have mine set to light up the entire keyboard cyan from whichever key I press, expanding out. Speaking of the LCD screen, you're able to upload GIFS or images to the screen, which is a really cool feature. As far as connectivity, you have every imaginable option available to you. I have my gaming rig connected via the 2.4USB wireless adapter. You can also connect up to three devices via bluetooth. And of course you can opt to hardware in. I love the the keyboard has both a USB-A and USB-C port. I am a huge advocate for technology having USB-C as an option, as it is much more convenient, provide faster transfer times, and faster charging times. Speaking of charging, the battery life on this keyboard is excellent. I seem to get about a week's worth of charge with extreme use daily. I know that the keyboard is hot swappable, meaning you can swap out the switches, which ultimately determine the sound of the keyboard, but personally, I haven't messed with that, as I love the way it sounds now. Overall, this is an excellent keyboard. If you're in the market for a wireless keyboard that sounds great, this is the best option out there! I typically don't like spending a ton of money on stuff unless I am absolutely sure of its value, and let me put your mind at ease that this keyboard is worth so much more than what the price tag shows.

headline: To many firmware glitches - basically unusable for any serious work
review_text_raw: Today, I initially wrote a negative review of this keyboard due to issues with missed or repeated keystrokes, or keys continuing to fire until another key was pressed. However, after extensive investigation (because I really wanted to keep this keyboard for its mechanical build), I finally discovered that the issues were caused by an obscure, lingering USB driver from a device no longer connected to my PC. That driver was behind all the trouble. I hope this revised review is published before the original one, which is no longer valid. After 15+ years of using Cherry MX Blue switches on a single keyboard that eventually got damaged, I was in search of a replacement. This keyboard seemed like a good option - more compact than my full-size board and featuring “tactile” pale green switches. I hoped they would resemble MX Blues in feel, just without the audible click. Unfortunately, these switches aren’t really that much (or at all) tactile. I don’t understand the claim. There is a point somewhere along the key travel where pressure slightly decreases, but you’d need to press very slowly and have an extremely sensitive touch to notice it. In actual typing, it feels - at least to me - indistinguishable from a regular linear switch. That said, I’ve gotten used to them and didn’t have much trouble adapting after so many years with MX Blues. And the 'thocky' sound still sounds nice. The build quality is solid. The board is sturdy, heavy, and a definite improvement over my old keyboard. I’m not particularly interested in the display or LED lighting. I don’t see the point - especially since the keycaps aren’t translucent, so the lights don’t help in the dark. Omitting those toddler-toy-like features and lowering the price - or populating that space with more keys - would be more useful, in my opinion. I used the included keycap puller to swap the positions of the 'Home' and 'Del' keys, then made the change in the RK software. It took just a few seconds. These settings are retained even if you unplug the keyboard or uninstall the RK software entirely from your PC. All things considered, in terms of mechanical construction, this is a very good keyboard. I do wish the switches were more tactile, but that’s just a matter of personal preference. These switches are still decent, and I’ll probably swap them out in the future for some Kailh clicky switches.

review_text_raw: After a ton of research into wearables that go beyond basic step counting and heart rate, I chose the WHOOP 5.0 (with the 12-month membership) specifically because I wanted way more detailed, actionable data than what my Apple Watch provides. And it's delivered big time. The band itself is incredibly lightweight and comfortable—I barely notice it's on my wrist all day and night. I only take it off for showers, which is a huge win for continuous tracking. The real game-changer is the charger: it snaps right on top while you're still wearing it, so there's zero downtime or lost data. That's a thoughtful design that makes staying consistent effortless. The metrics are fantastic—sleep stages, recovery scores, strain, HRV, respiratory rate, and all the deep physiological insights feel accurate and meaningful. What surprised me most was uploading my recent physical lab results directly into the app; WHOOP factored those biomarkers right into my overall data and trends, giving even more context to how my habits affect my health long-term. The GenAI-powered WHOOP Coach is another standout—you can chat with it to ask specific questions about your results, get personalized explanations, or dive deeper into why your recovery dipped or how to optimize training. It's like having a smart coach in your pocket. The app is clean, intuitive, and clearly well-thought-out—everything from daily summaries to long-term trends is easy to navigate and feels intentional, not overwhelming. My one complaint is the clasp. It might just be my unit, but it feels a bit finicky and harder to close securely than it should—sometimes takes a couple tries to get it to click properly. Not a dealbreaker, especially since the rest of the experience is so seamless, but it's worth noting for anyone picky about quick on/off. If you're serious about health optimization, recovery, and getting beyond surface-level tracking, the WHOOP 5.0 is worth it. The subscription unlocks all this depth, and after a few weeks, I can't imagine going back to less insightful devices. Highly recommend for data-driven folks!

However, I would like to add a few caveats: 1) The AI or algorithm that they use SOUNDS like it's personalized to you, but the conclusions and statements the device makes are based on collected, aggregated, and thoroughly-predigested data. That's not to say its inaccurate, but it's not "personal" in a real sense--the sense that a series of physiological and blood tests would deliver. that would be specific to you. You are more likely to get recos based on standardized data. 2) The app is really busy. There are so many charts and data points and subcategories that it becomes difficult (for me, anyway) to find precisely what I'm looking for. I have to ASK (query) to get to see my running stats, for instance; I can't seem to find them otherwise. 3) The loads of data and so-called personal recos are designed to keep you interested and committed, andf that's basically a good thing, but it's also to hook you into paying an annual fee FOREVER. Compared to a high-end sports watch (Garmin, Suunto, or even Apple) you will be paying ad infinitum for something others offer for free. That said, I've only had my WHOOP for about a month, so I'm expecting a fresh batch of data when I hit the 30-day point, and perhaps I'll find more of it useful when I get there. Right now it's a pleased enough with the info provided, though I do wish it "agreed". more with my watch. Not quite sure whose stats to believe! ***UPDATE*** A few days short of two full months. I DO like their AI; when I correct it ("No that wasn't a run I was digging in the garden / walking the dog") it accepts and adjust response accordingly. Nice. Though I still find the data provided kind of scattered around the site, with no simple menu to help locate something. Accuracy still a big ? mark, as it only occasionally matches what my Garmin watch reports. Who to believe??

headline: Spendy but well worth every $.
review_text_raw: I purchased this for myself as I am working toward a more healthful life and it was recommended by family members. At first, I struggled with the annual subscription $; however, after using it for over a month now, I am amazed at the amount of data and recommendations for improvements in my health. It even has what is called "Healthspan" which predicts your actual age versus chronologic age based on your health data. Each day, the user is able to recieve a summary of past 24 hours as well as what improvements can be made in the future to positively affect the user's Healthspan. I had Fitbits for at least at least 13 years and this is an absolute game changer! Well worth the $$ based on the changes I have already been able to make in just over a month's time. It is recommended to keep the tracker on at all times, including showering. It is a bit awkward recharging because the charger actually is applied to the tracker and it charges while you are on the move (I didn't know this at first). I did change the original mesh wristband for a silicone replacement because I didn't like wearing a wet band after showering. This is only a personal preference and I don't think it should be considered a negative to the overall product, but feel others should be aware. Finally, similar to Fitbit, there are communities which the user can join to encourage improvement. You can also create a new community as my family did, so we can compete against each other while obtaining positive health benefits. New communities can be shared with others by simply sending a code and, again, very easy. In my opinion this is a very well made product that can definitely lead to improved health and wellness!

headline: Everything This Thing Can Do, Something Else Can Do Better
review_text_raw: I wrote a full review for this item before the Amazon app glitched and I lost a full page of notes. I'm not going to go through that trouble again, but you NEED to know one thing before purchasing: Whatever this thing can do, something else can do better. The only "up" this has on other wearables is the battery life--which is great. Everything else is outperformed by competitors. I had a Samsung Watch 5 Pro that could tell me what exercise I was doing (lifting weights, walking, napping, etc.) at all times. This Whoop asks you what exercise you were doing, and if it's not on the list then you can't enter it on your own. Taking a shower? This device will think you were swimming. Blood pressure monitoring? It's a fake. If you go to the trouble of using an actual cuff and enter manual readings, the Whoop can give you a good estimate. That estimate is based on analyzing your activity and other metrics, though, not on actually measuring your bp. Blood sugar was teased as a possible function in the future. There's no way this thing could do this accurately in this version. Accessories like new bands have to be purchased in the Whoop store. I had to spend $50.00 for a brown fabric band because nothing was available from retailers. Want a custom band or something nicer? You're gonna have to pay big. Battery life is great. You'll get 14 to 16 days every time. That was an important consideration when making this purchase and it's the only thing that has impressed me. The app and the user interface is clunky and uncompromising. There's no way to customize the display or rearrange widgets that I have been able to find. I bought this item to replace a Samsung Watch 5 Pro because I needed something with better battery life. I got it. Absolutely nothing else is better after three months (plus) with the Whoop. Save your money and spend it on something better.

product_title: WHOOP 5.0/MG Activity Tracker - 12 Month Membership - Health and Fitness Wearable – 24/7 Activity and Sleep Tracker, Personalized Coaching, Menstrual Cycle Insights – 14+ Days Battery Life
headline: First time user
review_text_raw: Decided to give this a shot after being influenced online. Originally got the Whoop 5.0 (peak membership), but after seeing the relentless paywall on the Whoop app to upgrade to the Whoop 5.0 medical grade (life membership) to unlock the ECG feature and blood pressure insights, decided to return my standard Whoop 5.0 band and cancel my peak plan and go for the Whoop 5.0 mg device and pay the higher annual fee for the life membership, even after the pro-rated fee was reduced in months, which is what tempted me to upgrade in the first place, so my billing cycle would start in 2027, but come to find out, the company as of late has had a very bad customer experience and shady business practices since introducing the 5.0 devices with their changed upgrade policy requiring users to pay to get the newest Whoop device when that wasn’t necessary before and a premium that was included and outlined in the original membership plans before the 5.0 devices were introduced. Whoop ended up changing their terms and conditions in light of these circumstances, which felt a bit deceitful, especially being a first-time user hearing about all this right out the gate ... Moving onto the device itself, the device feels solid and it’s no larger than a binder clip or maybe even a standard pink pencil eraser in thickness, which is nice, and the battery life is very impressive, lasting 14 days exactly. However, the water resistance isn’t so great, and Whoop doesn’t recommend submerging the device in any kind of water for long periods of time but states it can be worn in the shower or in very shallow waters (10ft), which is a bit of a contradiction considering the brand message and device use case calls for this to be worn all the time 24/7, and the included battery pack further makes that statement clearer as you don’t remove the band to charge it; you slide on the battery pack, which is also water resistant by the way, to charge it while the band is strapped to your wrist, and the battery pack itself is what needs to be charged. Also, sleeping with this thing will take some time to get used to it as it can be difficult for side sleepers such as myself to feel comfortable with something on your wrist. The bands for this device feel subpar in quality, but that’s not here nor there as the real star of the show is the Whoop app and how it breaks down all the data the band collects, which is what you’re paying to use. All in all, very robust app experience with metrics and data galore. However, for me, it became too much to interact with, and certain data required manual input to gain access to further health insights, which for me became a bit much to stick to on a daily basis, which takes out of the money I’m putting into taking advantage of the full app experience. All in all, this can be a very solid product for athletes, coaches, runners, and fitness professionals/enthusiasts and for people who just hate smart watches, but definitely not for average people who just work out 5 days a week at a gym, and I already wear an Apple Watch. For those that don’t know, Apple’s health app is nowhere close to interpreting data like the Whoop, which is what drew me into getting one in the first place. Whoop also sells garments and clothing to wear the Whoop in different places of your body, not just your wrist, which is a plus and something I haven’t seen done before. Ultimately, the product lived up to the expectation, but the quality, use case, and the business side of things are what drew me to return the band.
