product_title: WHOOP 5.0/MG Activity Tracker - 12 Month Membership - Health and Fitness Wearable – 24/7 Activity and Sleep Tracker, Personalized Coaching, Menstrual Cycle Insights – 14+ Days Battery Life
headline: ***EDITED**** Not Quite JUNK - In My Humble opinion
review_text_raw: ***Updating to 4 stars*** After wearing this every day since I received it (approaching 3 weeks) - and initially being really negative due to the lack of available 'real time' data, I have grown to appreciate the insights it provides. It does utilize a LOT of data to come up with its analysis of your health. If you don't want that - but would rather have a conglomeration of real-time data that you can look at - and work to make sense of on your own, there are plenty of devices out there for that. The approach here is more about gathering lots of data to create more accurate readings over time. Which - ultimately, is what matters. It matters more than 'one moment in time' type readings of bp, RHR, etc. The access to data on this thing is so restricted, I've resorted to using a cuff to read my BP (always lower than their "estimate"). It DOES have the data - WHOOP choses not to show you the actual data for fear of being sued I suppose. Further, I just did an elliptical workout. The elliptical I used has its own heart monitor. This device showed my live heart rate (using the activity feature) at a consistently MUCH lower rate than the elliptical. I realize the elliptical is likely not terribly accurate either. However, right after my workout, I took an ECG reading with this WHOOP device, and yet, IT showed my heart rate as 20 BPM HIGHER than what it showed during my live workout session. This device may be for you if you want a bunch of suggestions on how to improve your health, but, if you have a simple plan, and just want access to real-time data, there are myriad devices available for a LOT less money that will do exactly that, for 1/3rd the price of this junk. I don't need any fancy analysis. If I really want some analysis, I'll use the multitude of free tools available on the internet to help guide me. I'm sending this thing back as soon as my replacement arrives. Worthless to me. I gave it 2 stars ONLY because it does have some decent data insights (providing the data is any good - which is suspect at least in my case). I'd just like to add, if I wanted to constantly check my BP using a cuff, I NEVER would have bought this stupid thing... If you want to look at your blood pressure readings throughout the day to come up with an average, this device is most certainly not for you. If you'd like to trust the data, I'd also suggest some other device.

headline: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
review_text_raw: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

product_title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Black
headline: The best fitness tracker I've used
review_text_raw: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. Overall I think this watch is a great fit for a more casual user who isn't running marathons but wants to track fitness and sleep and get some extras like smartphone notifications and see the weather at a glance. If you want something with more smart features and better build quality (i.e. more metal and less plastic), then the Venu might be a better fit. Or they have the Forerunner if you do run marathons. Or a bunch of other models for more specific use cases. But I would highly recommend giving this watch a try if you're looking for the same things that I am.

product_title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Black
headline: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
review_text_raw: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

Just add a titanium casing to the surrounding of the watch and provide more thorough instructions on overall use + updates for accuracy on certain apps and it would be perfect!

product_title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Ivory
headline: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
review_text_raw: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

product_title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Ivory
headline: The best fitness tracker I've used
review_text_raw: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. Overall I think this watch is a great fit for a more casual user who isn't running marathons but wants to track fitness and sleep and get some extras like smartphone notifications and see the weather at a glance. If you want something with more smart features and better build quality (i.e. more metal and less plastic), then the Venu might be a better fit. Or they have the Forerunner if you do run marathons. Or a bunch of other models for more specific use cases. But I would highly recommend giving this watch a try if you're looking for the same things that I am.

headline: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
review_text_raw: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

headline: Not Built for the Water
review_text_raw: It’s honestly a decent smart watch/exercise/step tracker, and connectivity on land is pretty good (I can go a fair distance in open space away from my phone before the watch disconnects). Battery life is pretty good, and it does receive texts and allows you to control your music. I am writing this review as someone who works in aquatics-specifically spending a lot of time in the water. While the watch does have good water resistance, the connectivity under water is non existent and it also tends to react as though I’m manipulating the screen (I am aware that all these complaints are normal with water). All in all, it’s not what I was looking for. One other MINOR complaint. The app that comes with the watch gives you the ability to personalize your home screen (which is genuinely fun/a great feature). A lot of them come with a “current outside temp” reading, but I can never get this part of the home screen to connect properly regardless of the home screen in question. A petty complaint but a complaint nonetheless XD All in all, it’s probably great for on land day to day/exercise, but definitely not for water related activities.

I just ordered and got this. So far so good. Set up was pretty simple. Customization was a breeze. I ordered it Saturday and got it Sunday. So far the step count is not very accurate, but knowing how step counters on the wrist work, it's understandable. I woke up with 26 steps, and I assure you I don't sleep walk, I have cameras to confirm that. But I am a restless sleeper so I'm sure that's how that happened. Notifications seem to work well! Alexa doesn't have much function(music, audiobook) but she is there and works.The sleep study aspect may not be entirely accurate because I know of 3 times I woke up and it said I didn't. But it shows my deep,light, and rem sleep. It's a little bulkier than I anticipated, but I have tiny wrists so it was kinda expected. So far so good! The battery seems to be holding well. Got it amd charged it at about 4p yesterday, its 7a now and only at 93%, idk if it will last a week, but we will see! I'll update as time goes since I only got it yesterday! 2 WEEK UPDATE: So i have had this for 2 weeks and wanted to provide an update. The battery seems to last pretty well. I received this on a Sunday and fully charged it then. Monday a week later it still had juice, not much but enough - 24% . I charged it fully again, which BTW only takes about 2 hours to fully charge. By the next Monday, i noticed it lost a little more battery than previously now at 10%. All in all it definitely lasts the week. However if you utilize the constant heart rate readings, etc., that may not be the case. I only checked my health rates as needed. The phone function works pretty good, and i like that it has an adjustable volume. Only once, I did notice it kicked of my watch and sent my call back to my phone after a few minutes, but again that only happened once. The band did irritate my wrist after about a week and a half. I wear it just loose enough that it stays in place, but has breathing room. I switched it to my other wrist and almost immediately had irritation, same day. i scrubbed the band down really good and will see what happens. I wear it in the shower and wash it then, but maybe it just wasn't good enough and had a little dirt/grime. That takes me to my next point - it seems to do well in my shower, giving my son a bath, dishes, washing hands, etc. It hasn't caused any audio/voice/visual issues at all. i do use the drain water function each time i shower and have not used it in the pool as of yet. I am confident the step counter is not accurate. It told me i did 10,000 steps the other day and i know that is impossible. I did however do a lot of cleaning, therefore maybe it was counting each movement as a step? Either way, i wouldn't rely on it. The sleep function i am not sure about, sometimes it seems accurate then other nights not at all. I have not use the exercise functions yet, but there are soooo many you can use if needed. Notifications come through no problem. The Alexa function is not very helpful, there is so much it does not do. I have not found it useful yet. Also i cannot get it to connect to my music, maybe this is user error? All in all, for an off-brand, low cost smart watch, it does what i wanted. I bought this as a test run to ensure i would like it and didn't mind wearing it, before i spend a few hundred on a Samsung watch. I will continue to wear this until i buy the Samsung watch, and will likely give this one to my son.

I am beyond happy with my new watch! You get the luxury without the cost. It has so many amazing features using the "Glory Fit App," which is very user-friendly. I'm able to take calls, make calls, and text from the watch. Listen to music by connecting via bluetooth. It allows you to customize countless features like temperature units, weight, and metrics. You can choose between multiple digital face diplays in your watch settings. You can also set the length of time display stays lit before it disappears. It features: training plans, goal setting and allows you to connect with friends. The watch straps are interchangeable so that you can attach different colors or styles. You can monitor your heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep, step count, weight, and more! It has a voice assistant and alarm clock as well. You can also sync most of your Apps on your paired device (I did my my phone), so that you can receive notifications and even use the same functions on your watch simultaneously. For example, I paired my youtube account so that whenever I receive a notification in the Youtube App of a new video, it shows that notification on my phone as well. I can even listen to YouTube using the play, pause, and stop buttons from my phone. I also synced our security camera device so that I can receive those notifications as well while away from home. I am able to select any number of applications I want to individually sync or not. This is great so that I can be selective and not have my watch going off every second of the day. It helps me to stay motivated as far as my fitness goes because I'm able to set goals - it sends you an achievement reward notification, which sounds once a goal has been reached. It has so many features that I haven't even begun to tap into. There is a slight learning curve, as with sny smart device, but it's very user-friendly after you patiently program and customize each feature to fit your needs and get the hang of it. I love the color selection options. I chose the black and light pink/rose gold color (for him & her), I also ordered (from another seller) face covers for protection. The covers were very easy to slip on (see in photos & video). It comes with a convenient USB, and the watch is packed in its own individual box. I just want to mention it because my pictures & video show (2) watches, but it's only because I bought them separately in those exact colors pictured on their box. I took multiple pictures to help display some of the features and to demonstrate the ease at attaching a face cover (sold separately via another seller). This is an amazing buy, and it makes the perfect gift. Be sure to check out the video ~ hope this helps!

product_title: Smart Watch for Men Women (Answer/Make Call), 1.83" HD Touchscreen Fitness Tracker, 110+ Sport Modes, Fitness Watch with Heart Rate/Sleep Monitor/Step, IP68 Waterproof Smartwatch for iPhone Android
headline: Surprisingly decent watch
review_text_raw: Good watch for the money. You do have to download an app. It is not overly complicated to navigate. I struggled some getting it to connect with the app but I’m not tech savvy. Battery life was good. It would last for two days. It charged quickly. It didn’t track my sleep well, which was one of the reasons I bought it, but it does have to be in constant contact with your wrist and I don’t like my watches that tight. It did do a decent job on vitals and had charts to show weekly levels. The negatives were you had to change your settings to a certain exercise to get a more accurate result. Especially on steps. Since I’m up doing a lot of walking, lifting, bending and sometimes crawling when cleaning the house I found you get a better representation of steps if you changed the setting to indoor walking. 😁 The drawback on any of the exercise settings I would forget to switch back to normal. Which is a negative on me. The next one is a very personal preference. I really wanted to be able to change the bands. I like sparkles and my daughter likes blues. I couldn’t find any that would fit the watch. We ended up making a few cuts here and adjustments there to get them to fit but I don’t think most people would want to do that. My husband bought me an apple watch for my birthday and my daughter didn’t like having anything on her wrist so I gave them to the grandsons 10 & 9. They are obviously not gentle with them but they are still going. I would place that into the sturdy column.

product_title: Garmin Forerunner 55, GPS Running Watch with Daily Suggested Workouts, Up to 2 Weeks of Battery Life, Black - 010-02562-00
headline: 3 years and counting!
review_text_raw: *** I've been using this watch for 3-years (& 1-month) now. It still works great and I still have zero regrets! I even got one of my sons to buy the same model. *** ------------------------------- Original 11-month review: Thanks to this watch, I was able to drop the 20+ pounds I put on during my post-covid depression. It got me moving again and whereas the original daunting number of 10k steps in a day made me nervous, I now walk around 23k steps daily without even thinking about it. The challenges on the app have helped me move from my former weight loss goals to my present toning ones and suffice it to say, all of this has helped tremendously with my mental health as well. As for the watch features, I was looking at all sorts of brands and all kinds of models and settled on this one and never looked back. I needed a time teller, a pedometer and a heart rate monitor, in no specific order. I received all of those and more with this wrist decor. Not only does the watch look nice and feel weightless on my skin when adjusted correctly, but it works so well at everything it was made to. The heart rate monitor is very accurate when compared with other heart rate monitoring devices. The watch is simple to clean although I was afraid of damaging something whilst attempting to clear out the 'gunk' around the plug-in site. I didn't purchase the watch for the sleep related feature but it is an interesting bonus. After roughly 9-10 months of continuous 24-hour use, I finally started noticing it act up during my treadmill workouts. My heart rate would drop to 0 and at one point I saw it jump to 248. Since I wasn't dead or dying during any of these times, I thought I'd start turning it off at night and I haven't noticed the issue since. It could have just been an error that required an update but like I said, I didn't buy for the sleep feature anyhow. The battery life is pretty good I'd say. When I told my husband one day that I should 'charge my watch tonight because it's been a couple weeks' he was really surprised. I keep track on my exercise calendar whenever I feel the need to plug in, which I do during the night so it doesn't interrupt my steps during the day. I normally charge once it hits somewhere in the 10-19 percentile. This takes (me specifically) about two weeks to accomplish, with roughly an hour and a half, minimum, of recorded activities at least five days a week and the watch otherwise just being turned on consistently. Of course, there are extra outings that warrant using the start button once in a while and yet I still find my charge schedule to remain the same. You can choose from a variety of watch faces that come standard but I definitely have enjoyed looking through the Garmin store at other options. The background I've used for quite some time now shows the moon in its current phase and as a lifetime star gazer, this is a face I was more than happy to throw money at. I spent just a few dollars and received something around 10 different looks, several animated such as plants or flowers that grow or open as you complete your steps for the day- amazing, if you like that sort of thing, turns out I do. Overall, I love my watch and I hope it lasts me a good, long time but if and when it finally dies from time cancer, I'll be sure to replace it with another Garmin!

product_title: Smart Watch for Women, Answer/Make Call, 1.32'' AMOLED Ultra-Clear Screen
headline: Here’s an honest review for ya!
review_text_raw: I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide. For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL. After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise. I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature! The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus! I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing. Cons: The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol. It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps. I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning. Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks. Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you. I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money. Hope this helps!! EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.

headline: Good watch if it lasts — You won’t regret this purchase
review_text_raw: The media could not be loaded. Update 6/3/26, company responded to my email and sent a new watch asap. I will report back in a couple months if it keeps working. Update 4/20/26, just short of 2 months. My watch has been acting up, the screen has not lighting up for me and the charge going from 100% to zero in just a couple minutes, and now the screen won’t turn on and Bluetooth will not connect to my phone. I have added a video of the issue that is causing me to update my review. Not the update I wanted to give as I loved this watch, but I felt compelled to come back and give an update to others so they were aware of what i experienced. I typically don’t write reviews, but I had to for this product. I used to be a Fitbit owner and very much enjoyed the fitness tracking. I was ready to move to a different style, I wanted one that looked more like a watch. I searched and reviewed garmin and nowatch. I didn’t love garmin due to the size of the watch face on my smaller wrist and the one I liked the best was around $500. The nowatch brand is beautiful but along with the expensive price, I didn’t love that you couldn’t look at the watch and see steps. So I landed on, why not give this product a try?? The watch face size was smaller which was better for my wrist size, the price was better than right and it had all the features I wanted, plus more. Once I got this watch I wore this watch and my Fitbit together to compare stats, believe it or not, this watch was closer to the miles walked measured on my treadmill compared to the Fitbit, the sleep stats were similar. Love the ability to answer calls and make calls in this watch. The weather tracking and all notifications come through well. And the screen is amazing. I did swap out my band (20mm), just for personal preference, the one that came with it was durable. Battery lasted 7 days, I used a decent amount and tracked fitness each day. 100% would recommend!!

product_title: Amazfit Bip 6 Smart Watch, 1.97" AMOLED Display, GPS, iOS/Android
headline: Solid Watch! Worth it if you're debating!
review_text_raw: This is a solid watch! I didn't want to spend money on a fitness watch that I was mostly paying for a brand name.. This does everything a fitbit does and most everything the lower end Garmins do. I really like how lightweight it is! I haven't had it long enough to test out the two week battery life but so far it was a quick charge and has been at 100% all day even after wearing it all night and having the sleep and heart rate on, steps seem accurate maybe off one or two steps but nothing is going to measure perfectly even fitbits and Garmins aren't 100% accurate. I like all of the features! However, the Zepp app has too much going on but it's not as difficult to navigate as I was expecting from the other reviews. It's a fitness watch first so those features are great... Call and text is just okay. I gave it 5 stars but I almost just did 4 because it's geared towards men; the design, watch faces, the app etc.. Are all very Male "coded" Which is fine if you don't care I just happen to like a more feminine aesthetic and I think they could do better to have more feminine options or even more neutral options would be great but that is just a nitpicky personal preference. Overall this is a good watch! I did a lot of research and I would say if you're debating it just get it! It is far less expensive to try this and not like it and get something else then it is to try a $300-$800 watch that you hate but you already spent $$ so you feel stuck. UPDATE EXACTLY 1 WEEK LATER: Still a really solid fitness watch but not everything it promises I turned off most of the notifications and app features that don't make sense for my goals and the battery lasts a week. To be fair though I have only taken it off to shower and wash dishes I have worn it day and night for the entire week and currently it's at 10% A week is pretty solid still though. I also bought a screen protector that was pink and a new purple band and it did change the aesthetic for me.

product_title: Amazfit Bip 6 Smart Watch, 1.97" AMOLED Display, GPS, iOS/Android
headline: All the features; a fraction of the cost
review_text_raw: I am so pleasantly surprised by the quality and feature availability of this affordable off-brand watch. After switching to Android, i needed a watch to replace my Apple watch. I didnt want to get reinvested in an over-priced flagship like Samsung or Garmin, so I looked for something budget but feature rich. This was a SOLID choice and i am so happy with it. Pros: Price. Its hard to beat the low price of this watch. Battery. My apple had to be charged every day or so and it drained rapidly. The Amazfit lasts me at least 5 days with normal use. But here is the best part - its still doing pretty much everything my apple watch was! Im honestly shocked how long the Amazfit battery lasts while still giving me all the features i need. Notifications. The Amazfit integrates with the phone via the Zepp app. You will still recieve all your necessary phone, messages, email, socials, etc notifications to your watch. Integration with Android. This watch works great with Android via the Zepp app. Screen size. Another big surprise was how large the screen size is. I cant believe i paid a third the price of Apple but i got 3-4x battery life and huge screen. Cons: Cosmetic weakness. The metal edge around the screen is already getting some very small dings. I dont really care and it is purely superficial. Theres really not a lot bad i can say about this watch. Im so pleased with the value and capability at the very low price point relative to apple. Other features: Tracks sleep, heart rate, sends movement alerts, has routines, offers a daily biocharge tracker (think battery but its your body's remaining daily charge), tracks steps, movement, calories.

headline: Decently solid value fitness band
review_text_raw: Okay, I bought this for Christmas, so I've been using it for about 6 months now. I do believe that this is a good value for your money. It does most of the things I want it to do. It looks good, and I found compatible bands (the original band cooked my skin, and I had to remove it and put on a fabric band). I like its functionality, and the battery lasts a long while (not 14 days but still a good while). The only really negative thing I've found about it is that it will NOT keep notifications turned on from the Zepp app that goes with it. Because I forget to turn it on when it goes off, it's almost never sending me notifications, which is one of the things I bought it for. This is a big issue that I think Amazon needs to correct, or maybe more specifically, they need to correct on the connected Zepp app. No matter how many times I tell it to allow notifications, it'll work for a few days and revert back to none. Then, I go days without noticing it and have to turn it back on again. I've checked Reddit to see what others are saying, and it's definitely a known issue that needs to be addressed.

headline: Amazing Amazfit - Excellent so far.
review_text_raw: Edit (06/10/25): Now about 8 days into the Bip 6. After a week of use, the watch was sitting at 50% charge. I charged it up to 96%+ in about an hour. I'm using a USBC charger which I think provides about 2A. Can't say for sure as it's a charger built into a lamp in my bedroom that has both USBC and USBA; the "C" charger shows my Pixel phone charges "rapidly" whereas the "A" plug charges normally (slower but fast enough for the phone to hit 100% sometime during the night). I did try the "A" port (with an A-to-C cable) but it is slower. Still totally happy with the Bip 6. More feedback in a few months. Early days but I thought it might be helpful for those trying to decide between a Fitbit and this Amazfit Bip 6 (a truly unfortunate name). I had been using a Fitbit Charge 5 for a couple of years. The first week I wore it, the Charge 5 detected Afib and that probably saved my life. So I wanted to really like the Charge 5 and continue using it. However, I discovered it was terribly inconsistent in providing a sleep score and HRV; perhaps 40% of the time it just failed. A month or so ago (after 2+ years of use), it would just go "black screen" if I did anything with the Charge 5 other than simply looking at the screen. The battery also didn't last very long and the charger "connection" (magnetic) was hit-or-miss so it was time for a new watch. After deciding against another Fitbit (reviews have gotten worse over the years and Google has already said Fitbit will soon no longer be supported properly), the choice was either an expensive Garmin (and they're all expensive), a Samsung Galaxy watch (also $$$), or one of these "cheap" Chinese brands. (Can't use an Apple watch as my phone is of the Android variety). This Amazfit seemed to have the best reviews of the cheap smartwatches so I bought it with the 3-yr warranty for under $100 total. Amazon delivered it the next morning. Followed the prompts and set it up in a few minutes so it syncs with my Pixel 6a with the Amazfit Zepp app. I charged it using the provided charger "puck" (you must provide your own USB-C cable, remember this!) and, once it reached 100% (a couple of hours maybe), I strapped it on and configured the watch both with the watch's preferences and the Zepp app. I have most of the integration with the phone switched off; why did I need to answer my phone with the watch when I have my phone on my hip all day? I just wanted the watch to keep track of my steps, heart health, and sleep (the latter the most important point). So here we are after three nights and the watch seems to be 100% accurate in sleep tracking and heart health reporting (and it keeps perfect time, of course). As I indicated above, these are still early days but I'm thrilled with this Bip 6. I even am dabbling in the watchface creation app on the web and even that works! Why would I want to use that? I hate tiny type on a large screen so why not make a watchface that really shows off how large all the information can be presented? Great stuff. I am not going to test how waterproof the watch might be; I remove it before showering or swimming and am careful otherwise. BTW: There's a function on the watch where you can "eject" any water that might have found its way into the speaker. (Yes; the watch can play music and you can speak through it to your phone but I'm not going down that patch.) The only downside I can see (and it's not for me) is the length of the band; I have a small wrist but the fourth hole in the strap makes the watch fit properly; I would have expected a longer strap for larger wrists. However, using that fourth hole leaves about 1.75" beyond the buckle (.75" of which tucks back inside the band and that's fine). I would recommend to Amazfit that they provide a longer strap for larger wrists (much like how Fitbit does it). Oh, yeah; one more thing. One of the included apps on the phone is a compass! I set it up so one of the buttons on the side of the watch launches it. You know when your GPS starts off by saying "head east"? Who knows where that is without a compass? Now I know. I'll report back in a few months with more info.

product_title: Amazfit Bip 6 Smart Watch, 1.97" AMOLED Display, GPS, iOS/Android
headline: Feature-packed smartwatch for an incredible price—if you’re willing to tackle the learning curve!
review_text_raw: This watch is fantastic! I love being able to make and receive calls, plus get text and email notifications right on my wrist. The offline navigation is a standout feature—I downloaded maps for my hometown and neighboring cities, and navigating without cell service is seamless. It’s especially convenient during workouts. Whether I’m playing pickleball or lifting weights, I can leave my phone in my bag and still catch important notifications without interrupting a match or set. I’ve used sleep tracking since 2022 (upgrading from a Bip 3 that finally gave up the ghost), and the accuracy on this model is solid. Given everything it offers, the price-to-performance ratio is hard to beat. The Drawbacks: Poor Documentation: Setup and configuration were frustrating. The official guides provided little help, so I had to rely on influencer tutorials and trial-and-error to get everything dialed in. Stock Band: The included strap is mediocre. I swapped it for a 22mm magnetic braided nylon band, which completely resolved my comfort issues. If official video tutorials or better documentation were provided, this would easily be a 5-star review.

headline: Perfect size if you feel the Active 2 is too small
review_text_raw: I previously had the Amazfit Active 2, but felt it was a bit small for my wrist. This however is perfect. Easier to see the heart rate info and whatnot with the larger screen. Plus the battery life is way longer than the 10 days claimed on the Active 2 and while it's not a huge deal to charge, it's still much more convenient to have extra battery life. One thing I was a little unsure of was the thickness. The photos kind of make it look like a beast. While it is thicker than the Active 2 it's not obnoxious and it's given me no pause whatsoever in terms of look and feel. Brightness is excellent, though I haven't had it long enough to test it on a sunny day outdoors. **Edit** Have been out in full sun with it and no problems seeing the screen The strap is very comfortable and is the same type of quick release strap with the pins that other smart watches have. Doing some googling it's a 22mm strap which shouldn't be a problem to find. One thing worth mentioning is some peoples skin is sensitive to silicone straps. My skin is not, but I've also had nylon with velcro and can recommend that if you want to use a different strap. Also there's no more tucking the tail of the strap down between your skin and under the strap, it's now routed the way most other straps are, on the outside. I'll update this review if I have any issues, but if you're up in the air between this and the Active 2 and you don't have tiny wrists I'd definitely go with this. Edit 1/22/26: Zero issues to report. One thing worth mentioning is that the face is not completely flat. The edges at the bezel curve down slightly. It doesn't cover everything but it does cover the flat part and vast majority of the screen completely and without any raised edges or bubbles. You can view my profile to see which I used. There seem to be some tempered glass screen protectors here on Amazon that curve down at the edges (with the bezel markings to match), but since this is so new I haven't bought one yet.

headline: Perfect in many ways
review_text_raw: It’s been a week now since the purchase and I can honestly say this is an excellent smart watch! Build Quality: Excellent, well thought out and very good quality controls. Zepp app: The Zepp app is used to set up / pair / customize the watch and it is an excellent app actually! Customization: Also excellent. The watch can be customized in dozens of ways. The band would be much better if the connections are like Apple’s (slide in and lock in place) instead of using pins. The instructions manual really requires a magnifying glass. But it is so intuitive that one may not need the manual and the magnifying glass! In summary: This is a terrific smart watch. I am wearing it more frequently than my Spple watch that cost 3x more! I highly recommend it , especially when on sale!

I would definitely recommend the Smart Watch for Women, especially for those who want a lot of the functions of an Apple Watch, but don't want to pay that exorbitant price! This watch is SO much more reasonable, AND it looks very nice on.

review_text_raw: So realistically, I have gone through 4 (yes this is my 4th) smart watch this year (I think?! Might be 3 but anyways) and thos one by far has FINALLY given me everything I've been looking for. Well, almost everything. Still cant text out on it but, it is what it is. So, some interesting things about this watch compared to the others ive had are the accuracy of the biometrics taken, the screen quality, and overall battery life. I am even liking that when I misplace my phone is actually rings MY ringtone and not some weird built-in one from the watch company. I even love that you can change the notification tone ON the watch itself too. Pretty snazzy there. Now here's some downfall in my opinion (this is my personal opinion, use its information as you see fit). Firstly, the paid membership app im not thrilled about and its not for the price, thats fair across the board. Its the lack of knowing the time frame parameters used as well as this being noted in the listing itself. Another is, the lack of it being fully customizable (i.e. you make it your very own) backgrounds as well as the limited number you can have (4 is the max). But again, this is my opinion and im one who likes fully customizable things as I like to be different. Only other "flaw" is that it only has 1 button which sticks out a fair ways for my liking and digs into my wrist... Do wish it was a little more, sleek if you will in that department. But ive added photos to show the level of things offered as well as how it does look very asteticly pleaseing. Which is nice little bonus! So maybe im nitpicking on some things, oh well! All in all though, its beyond worth getting. Not had a connection issue like past ones, and the band it even came with wasnt just silicone (oddly wearing that causes my skin to "eat" itself so I cant wear them). So I hope this helps someone out there!

product_title: Smart Watch for Women, 1.85" HD Smartwatch (Answer/Make Calls), 2 Bands
headline: Recommended, lots of pluses, a few caveats
review_text_raw: I've come to really like this rose gold smartwatch that I bought as a replacement for a Fitbit Charge 4. I have narrow wrists so it's big in comparison but as said, I'm getting used to it. I love being able to read it at a glance without squinting. The screen is sharp, crisp, gorgeous color and easy to read. Set up was initially easy but when I started using the watch, customizing screens, layout of icons and grant it the permissions it needs, I had to turn to googling "IDW28" and found most of the answers i needed. I am fairly tech savvy and after a lot of frustration, I could only solve my issues this way. (The companion app was no help.) The biggest problem was the watch would compete with my ear buds, phone or bedside speaker to take over Bluetooth control, and attempt to direct the audio to the watch. Audio would cut in and out as it repeatedly tried to take control. I finally figured out what was wrong when I realized a phone call I received was switched to my watch. I had a Dick Tracy watch! 😂 Lol and the audio is not nearly loud enough to make calls on our listen to music. Overall the watch with its phone app is exceptional to monitor steps, heart rate, sleep patterns, exercise sessions, stress level, water intake, weather and control your phone's music app, camera and much more. It also alerts you to notifications of messages and emails. Essentially it's the same notification that your phone displays (not the whole email or text) and you cannot respond. It does not measure blood pressure as some reviews suggest. It will connect to your AI asst but I don't need that. I do wish for a way to enter water intake in the watch but for now that has to be done on the phone app. It charges fast and is easy to hook up. The battery lasts about a week but you're mileage may vary depending on your settings. I would definitely recommend buying if you are looking for an easy to read screen that is a giant step up from something like a Fitbit. If you want to send messages or emails, respond to them, see images attached in same then look to spend 5-10 times the price. Me? I'm happy with the purchase. I don't need to make calls on a watch or compose replies to texts and emails on my wrist. I really hope they solve the problem competing for Bluetooth as I'd like to turn on some of the features I had to give up to solve the problem.

product_title: Smart Watch for Women, 1.85" HD Smartwatch (Answer/Make Calls), 2 Bands
headline: Can't complain...much
review_text_raw: Hello there, future watch owners. If you're like me, you've spent wayyy too much time agonizing over which knockoff smart watch to buy, and have probably read every review ever written. So, here is a list of every observed helpful and unfortunate aspect of this quality timepiece. I've been using it about a month. Pros: It looks nice. The screen is large enough to read and navigate easily, without feeling like you have a tablet on your wrist. The responsiveness is decent and the picture is clear. The swipe-right shortcut saves your most recent selections. There are lots of options for what it can do. Workouts, music, phone, calculator, stress, sleep, O2, heart rate, water intake, and something I found especially helpful as someone who leaves their phone lying around, Find My Phone. I've used most of these but have barely scratched the surface on the sports/workouts. Notifications show up with a red dot rather than a large icon, which I like and are easy to read and clear. I really like being able to adjust the brightness on the screen, and having a shortcut for the wake gesture; it's easy to turn off at night - because it's bright enough to burn your retnas - and back on during the day. The flashlight function is very helpful and almost absurdly bright. The alarm works well. The battery has been fantastic. I probably have less notifications set up for social media and email than some, but it easily lasts me a week+, which is way more than my poor, retired 4 year old Versa Lite ever did. Cons: The app sucks. It's like they tracked daily notifications with "app unpaired from device" and forgot to fix it. I am re-pairing every couple of days. It links up quickly but I wish it would stay linked. There are no screen protectors available that I've found and as a result, there is already a scratch on the face. There is also a chip off the wrist sensor already, which makes me wonder about the longevity, and my skins safety. I wish that when you pressed the side button from a selection, it would take you back to the menu, rather than back to the home screen, but that's minor. I also haven't found replacement bands. I don't care for the cloth band but I like the silicone. Eventually it will wear out and I would like to be able to replace it. I haven't braved the water with it yet because I'm afraid of drowning it, so I can't speak to that. I think that for the price-point, it is worth it. I threw the extended warranty on it, so I'm basically covered for three years if something messes up and then I just get a new one. Rant over, enjoy your day 🙂 hope it helps!

headline: Great for Water Sports!
review_text_raw: I have had a Samsung Galaxy watch since they first came out. My first one is still going strong, but I needed one that would track my activity in the water, since the majority of my activity is water related. This watch is great for that! It has been in the water with me now almost daily for weeks and works like a charm! I have an app that will automatically set the watch to the water mode, or I can set it myself. It counts each step, stroke and workout moment - and seems to do so accurately. The size is a nice upgrade from the earlier versions, being slightly easier to read. All my apps and information were easily transferred to this new watch, making the transition seamless. It doesn't vibrate quite as strongly as my last one did, so I miss a notification here and there, but since my phone is never more than a few feet away from me, that really isn't an issue. Time will tell if it lasts as long as my first watch did, but I am really so impressed with this watch. To me, it is worth spending the cash to have the added assurance of counting my water activities.

headline: DO NOT Buy! Failed within 15 days; Support SUCKS! Overpriced, Go Watch 7
review_text_raw: BOTTOM LINE: if you don't need the 3 Labs - Advanced Glycation End (AGE) product index, the Antioxidant index (does not work anyway), or the Vascular Load, ***Go With the WATCH 7!*** If you do get a watch 8, return it to Amazon as soon as it screws up! Watch 8 #2 is now "inching up" on its O2 measurements. At first, it was 2% points over my Innovo FDA-Approved O2 device. That's okay, because as long as it was consistent, I could deal with it. Now, it is 3% over my Innovo -- My Watch 8 #1 and Watch 7 did the same. I hope this is not a harbinger of failure. It also must be tightened down painfully snug at night. Oct 14, 2025. Bought new watch 8, now Watch 8 #2 I am riddled with inflammation, so pursue antioxidants. I take 3 supplements twice a day. Yet the Antioxidant index stays low. Farce. ****************************** Below is the Watch 8 #1 Oct 10, 2025 - Samsung refunded cost Sent it in a second time. Kept checking (two weeks) and nothing. Finally, Samsung offered a refund. Not for the tax, of course. Awaiting refund. Sep 26, 2025 Already Failing with Same Errors Was on the phone forever with Samsung, being fobbed off on every department imaginable. I bought a Brand-New Watch for $350, and they "repaired it" only to have the same problems! I am so mad I could chew a horseshoe and spit nails. I wish I'd never bought this thing! If you are stupid enough to buy it, return it to Amazon at the first fail! It is not YOU! The sensor array is P-poor and it fails. I miss my Watch 4. Sep 25, 2025 Samsung repaired the watch under warranty. It wiped out all trending in the app. "New" watch still has "blanks" in its monitoring (picture). Samsung says, "wear snugly". It is already so snug it hurts (picture). Furthermore, the "O2" monitoring is 5% MORE than my commercial O2 monitor. I guess I have to go back to wearing five different monitors that are correct. Sep 15, 2025. The watch has become worse. I will contact Samsung under the warranty. Anytime I get sweaty, the watch stops tracking on the wrist! I'm skinny - BMI 20.2. It's a fitness watch, for God's Sake! One expects it to work when you are sweaty! But no - it stops tracking the heart rate and the oxygen level. This is not at all what one wants in a Fitness tracker! Aug 31, 2025. The watch has developed issues with tracking heart rate. I was walking - spanking pace - and the watch stopped tracking my heart rate. I stopped for a directed measure. It said "put your watch on". I took the watch off and cleaned it, and had same result. I finally rebooted the watch and it worked again. I DID NOT have this problem with the Watch 4. Aug 5th, 2025. Anti-oxidant scan doesn't work right. The scan kept saying low - eat a carrot. Three days of carrots and it is still low. Also, I tried to take another scan and the software kept saying "Put your watch back on." - but the watch WAS on. Too many bugs. Aug 2nd, 2025 My initial review wasn't accepted; I am unsure why. I hemmed and hawed about Watch7 and Watch8. I went for this Watch 8 due to features. I am very disappointed. First, I have many Samsung-branded chargers. I was very disappointed that the Watch8 band would not allow the Watch 8 to work on the flat chargers. I guess you could put a weight on the watch, like 2 lbs (!) to press it down, but I believe Samsung should have designed their Watch8 to be compatible with its supporting chargers. See first pic. Second, this is a 40mm watch. I compare it to the Watch4 and the Watch 7, the only others with which I have familiarity. The Watch8 face measures 40mm, but the display is smaller by 2mm, making it a 38mm display. I cannot at this time comment on durability as I have had it three days. Color is personal choice. EDIT - Watch began failing before 30 days! I thought it was me. Functions. The Watch8 is extraordinarily bloated by location-tracking bloatware. I do not do use email, bixby, wallet, etc. from the watch, but it will not allow me to uninstall these apps. Furthermore, every app tracks your location with precision! I have no idea why outlook would need location, for example. The Watch8 has the same processor as the Watch7. Comparing it with the Watch4, I do not see any difference in performance. I would have expected better. The new Health features are AGE - Advanced Glycation End products. Not sure what the low - adequate - high means, and there isn't a lot of information on the web. It also does the antioxidant index - very low - low - adequate. I tried the recommendation --- eat carrots. My value did not change. Lastly, is vascular load. It is supposed to an indication of lifestyle factors affect on your health. Basically, get sleep, exercise, and good diet. Shrug. The Watch8 is supposed to have a better battery. However, I do not see the Watch8 lasting any longer than my Watch4. I still charge the Watch8 at my noon-ish nap time, and see the Watch 8 is down to 66% at noon, and again down to 66% at night, after having been charged at noon. If I could uninstall some of the not-used apps, it may be better, and maybe not. All in all, after seeing all the additional tracking and inability to turn it off, the questionable value of the new "features", the failure to be compatible with industry and brand standard equipment, I wish I'd gone with the Watch7.

headline: Love at first sight
review_text_raw: This watch is honestly almost perfect. Literally like a 9/10. The design is sleek, the watch face is not too big for my tiny wrist, has a vibrant and attractive display, and the watch band is really nice and soft! I had a fit bit charge 4 before this one and it finally quit on me. I wanted a low budget option because I haven't been consistent and don't have 300 dollars to waste for it to sit around if I end up not staying consistent. For 50 dollars this beauty fits nearly all my needs. Paired to my samsung phone immediately when I pulled it out of the box. Super easy to set up, and tons of different ways to customize the watch face. Have I mentioned its so pretty?? Only mildly sucks because I use the live feed heart rate monitor to help clue me in to if I might have a panic attack or if I'm overreacting. Another thing. I have been using google health to track my calories and set specific goals for some of my macros I'm trying to hit. Unfortunately, the samsung health app doesn't get this specific and just gives you the suggested daily intake as a metric rather than letting you set your own. What sucks more is that these two apps don't sync with each other. So now I have 2 seperate apps to track my health. All in all. Its really a fantastic little gadget. For $50 I would 10000% buy it again if they came out with a newer version. Will update again after I've had it a few weeks.

headline: The fitbit killer
review_text_raw: My wife and I have been fitbit fans since the Charge 2 (2016). Before the google purchase, fitbit was a strong leader in lower cost fitness trackers. It did concern us that our fitbits would die frequently (nearly each one we had died within a year from the Charge 2, 3, 4). However after talking with customer service they would send us replacement. So, ok, we can deal with that. (Even though in the past few years you had to provide a ton of documentation including, IIRC, your drivers license.) I had a fitbit 6 that I got for Christmas 2024. Wow, a color screen. LOL. I needed a replacement as the screen on my Charge 5 kept getting dimmer, and dimmer, to the point when I could not read it outdoors and barely indoors. So I was gifted the Charge 6 and it was big step up. But it took me a few months until I realized that the floors option was gone, not just not working, but removed, to make space for other features I could care less about. So I looked around in late June and discovered the Fit 3. So I bought one. I am SO GLAD I did. What do I need? Step counter, heart rate, floors, distance, calories. Oh, and the kicker for me was AIRPLANE MODE. I study various energetic sciences including BioGeometry and the EMF coming from our devices is not benign. I don't wear a tracker to sleep, don't want anything live, and keep my blue tooth turned off unless I am actively syncing. This is what I see comparing Fit 3 to Fitbit Charge 6. What the Fit 3 has as an advantage: Larger screen, airplane mode, beautiful faces, much cleaner UI on the watch and in the android app(s) (I am using this with a Pixel 7 phone). The ability to sync only turning on bluetooth. A few years ago fitbit/google basically said we aren't syncing your fitbit unless you have both location/GPS and bluetooth turned on. Sometimes you could get the fitbit to sync with location off but this was tricky/spotty. What advantages did the Charge 6 have for me, personally. None really. It cost about 3x the amount for the Charge 6 compared to the Fit 3. That's ridiculous. In a head to head comparsion of measurements this is what I see. Fitbit Charge is often slower to start your step counts and the Fit 3 is quicker on that. So you steps counts are going to go up and perhaps the Fit 3 does count some arm motions as steps when it should not. But the Fit 3 is still very close (within 1-3%) with the Charge 6. The Fit 3 tends to undercount calories compared to the Charge 6, I can't tell which is more accurate. On the Charge 6 bluetooth syncing was always a laborious pain taking sometimes minutes to get the past few days of data and often having to turn bluetooth off/on and/or restarts to get it to sync. The Fit 3 is very fast *most* of the time. I did have one instance where the Fit 3 was not syncing in the Health App and I had to open the Wearable app and trigger a sync from there, which worked. The big thing is battery life. I have automatic activity tracking turned on and except when syncing in the evening I keep it on airplane mode. I charged it overnight last Thursday/Friday before I first put it on. It's now Wednesday evening, nearing 6 complete days of use and my battery level is at 55%. That frugal energy use is really good and is on par with the earlier monochrome fitbits. I am very pleased with my Fit 3 purchase. Back in the early to mid 2000's I was very excited about Timex was doing just in digital watches (Iron Man, etc). The Fit 3 harkens back to those kind of days for me when you could get a very full functionality wrist device that looked good, worked great, and was a good deal. This is definitely worth a close look if you don't need an higher priced fitness/communication device that is emitting EMFs into your pericardium meridian 24x7. Well done.

headline: Nice fitness tracker
review_text_raw: I've had a long line of Fit Bits and when I found out Samsung has a non-smart watch tracker, I decided to give it a chance. (I don't want to pay smart watch prices.) Out of the box, the Fit 3 was in Spanish, but when I put it on the charger, it reverted to English. It stayed English until I got a new phone and had to reset the tracker in order to pair it with the new phone. The tracker reverted to Spanish and putting it on the charger did not change that this time. I pressed the top option on the device's screen and got to choose from a whole list of languages. I chose English, but this is where someone who wants another language will find it. The charge on this item is supposed to last up to 13 days. I've had this device for 3 months, and I got 6 days out of each charge (7 if I let the device die) for the first 2 months or so. Now, it last 4-5 days. I don't have the display always on and I don't consider my use of this device heavy by any means. 6 days is what I got out of my most recent Fitbit. My Fit 3 charges from 20% to 70% in about 20 minutes and to 100% in about an hour. The trick is to get the charger properly seated, because the first couple of times, I don't think it was on correctly, as I got the main display, not the charging percentage display, and it took about 2 hours to reach 100%. I wore the new Fit 3 side by side with my old Fitbit Charge 6 for 24+ hours to compare - 2 nights and one active day. The first night, the Fit 3 recorded 20 more minutes of sleep and the second night, the Fitbit recorded 20 more minutes. I don't know how either determines when I am asleep and not quietly reading, so I figure the results are comparable. The Fit 3, while behind on step count early in the day, ended the day with almost 1,500 more steps than the Fitbit. Both counted activity (cleaning, for instance), not just pure steps. I'm OK with this - I figure any movement is better than no movement. There are many more features that I don't use. I may in the future, but I'm happy with what I do use. I tried taking photos on my phone (also a Samsung) with my Fit 3 as a remote shutter button. I like that feature! Text notifications come to my Fit 3, but not all of them. When I am using my phone, notifications do not go to the tracker (I have found that this is the default and I can change it if desired). Group texts never do (they will go to my car, so I don’t know why they won't go to my Fit 3), and random regular texts don't. I found in the Health app where I can pick and choose which apps will send notifications. All told, I like this device. It’s not perfect, though. I miss the feature that Fitbit has that reminds me to move each hour. I'm now forced to choose between step count, floor count (I assume that means how many stairs I climb), or active hours. I like counting steps, so that's my main goal. I like seeing the hearts light up throughout the day as I get closer to my goals. I also have active minutes and active calories burned as goals, but I don’t care as much about those.
