product_title: XIAOMI Mi Smart Band 10 (2025) Global Version - 1.72" AMOLED Display | 21 Days Battery Life | Touchscreen, Multi-Sport Tracker, Activity Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor | BT5.4 - (Mystic Rose)
headline: A Simple and Affordable Fitness Tracker
review_text_raw: I purchased the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 after comparing it with several other fitness trackers, and the value for the price was hard to beat. After watching multiple YouTube reviews, I felt confident it was the right choice. The Smart Band 10 is simple, clean, and not overly flashy. The setup process was straightforward, though you do need to pair it with the Mi Fitness app, which requires creating an account. Once set up, the device tracks heart rate, sleep, steps, and provides handy notifications like incoming text messages. It covers all the essential features most people need. The Smart Band is pretty light weight and sometimes I don't feel it on the wrist which can be worrisome as you may bump it into things around, which I've done a few times but no scratches just yet but that's something to take note of. The battery life is truly impressive. I fully charged the device on November 22nd, 2025, and as of writing this review, it has been running for 14 days straight on that single charge and is sitting at 45% battery. With power-saving mode, you can extend it even further. However, there are a couple of downsides to consider. The most noticeable is the lack of physical buttons, which you can see in the product photos. You can power the Smart Band 10 off from the settings menu, but the only way to turn it back on is by connecting it to the included charging cable. This hasn’t caused any issues for me yet since I haven’t needed to turn it off, but it's something potential buyers should know. I also question the accuracy of the calorie and step counters at times, as the numbers don’t always feel consistent. Overall, if you’re looking for a simple, affordable, and reliable fitness tracker, whether for personal use or as a gift, the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 is a solid choice. **Update on December 13, 2025, the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 is currently on 19% of charge after a 21 day period going off one charge cycle. The Smart Band estimates that it could last for 4 more days. This device has been really impressive so far.

headline: Good value
review_text_raw: This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.

headline: Looks Great!!!
review_text_raw: Snug fit with my iPhone 17 Pro so it protects my phone quite well and I’m quite happy with it. Seems to be durable as I have dropped my phone a couple of times I’m very surfaces and so far, I haven’t seen a crack anywhere. Quality seems to be solid so far but only time will tell. Feels very slick and smooth, but maybe too smooth as it has been known to slide quite easily. There is a protector for the front screen (which I did not purchase), but I decided against it as I have discovered front screens reduce the phone‘s ability to detect commands with my finger after time has progressed and dirt/detritus builds up behind the screen after a certain length of time. I was concerned at first that the edge of the case on the back where the lenses are located would raise the phone too high and not allow charging when the phone was laying down on a charge mat, but that was not the case. Although, I did discover that exact positioning is important as just laying it down doesn’t always mean the phone is charging. So, I had to make sure to watch the screen when I wanna charge to make sure the mat and the phone aren’t position to charge when needed. All in all, this is a pretty solid product and I haven’t seen any yellowing in the plastic case as of yet, but it’s only been a couple months since I’ve been using it so maybe after a year I’ll reassess again. If there was one thing that would bug me about this case, is the raised lip of the back of the case surrounding the lenses. There was already a raised area on the phone for those lenses and this case just makes it that much more pronounced. I can only guess that the raised lip area on the back of the case is to further protect the lenses, but that also makes it harder for easy positioning for charging, and makes the phone bulkier when being placed into a pocket or bag. Still, this protects my phone and does what I want it to do so the raised area on the back is a minor issue that I can live with for now. Would I get another one? Hmmmm, maybe. Too early to tell at this point. But I won’t say no if something better comes out on the market.

product_title: OtterBox iPhone 12 & iPhone 12 Pro Commuter Series Case - Black, Slim & Tough, Pocket-Friendly, with Port Protection
headline: Great reliable case for the price. (2024 update)
review_text_raw: Bought this back in August of 2021 and just recently bought a new one after 1 1/2 years. I have a iPhone 12 and suppose to fit the 12 and 12 pro. Went with this case cause i wanted something reliable but not bulky. The case is a nice size, easy to slide in and out my pocket. I’d say it’s a Good size for most people that the phone still feels comfortable in your hand. I was very hesitant about how bulky it would be and wasn’t disappointed. The rubber layer, on the buttons it’s pretty thick and i personally struggled a bit sometimes to get it to work that i was patient enough to wait for it break in that i started to using my nail and ended up digging into the rubber of all buttons and even the socket to switch to vibrate had to dig in there to switch it. Overtime the rubber does start wearing out so dust/dirt will tend to get in between the case and the phone and will potentially scratch the phone as it did to mine. It’s only two small a scratched at the edge of the top of the phone. Also the port protection probably ripped off after about 4-6 months? But that’s due to me using my phone so much and having to charge it and still using it which made it wear out faster so i think for someone who’s not always on there phone it’ll definitely last longer than it did for me. The plastic is good but could be better. If you drop it in the bottom the plastic is the first to take the impact which will probably crack as it did for me on two spot. Can’t recall when the crack by the camera happen as i only recently noticed it when buy this for the second time. The first crack in the bottom corner happened around the 1 year mark but if you look at my photos i can easily pop it back in place and keep using it without issue. There’s also a small thin plastic that goes in front of the port protection that broke off around 6 months of having it. The plastic is pretty durable, you’d really have to put some force on it to dig into the plastic so small scratches are not really a thing to worry about. If your responsible with not dropping your phone, almost any line of work that’s not construction, i definitely suggest this case if you don’t want a bulky case. For those who work in a more active line of work like huge construction job sites, i recommend upgrading to “DEFENDER” series case. Those are the cases my job has on our work phones and they’re pretty bulky. If you’re someone who’s slightly clumsy, i suggest this case. Overall a great case if you want something reliable, looks great and isn’t bulky. This was based off my experience and other will have their own that probably won’t align with mine. I looked at the reviews before buying it the first time and some people broke it within 3 months from what i recall. it still depends how active your are and what environment your in. If your a office worker, this case will most likely last you a few years compares to someone who’s in a environment that can get pretty filthy and is fast pace. It also depends on how you take care of you things. It’s going to happen to everyone at some point so if you really want more protection with sacrifice of it’s look and size, i suggest upgrade to the defender series or get two cases and swap them for work and off work. Silly but it’s an investment on saving your self the hassle of having to fix a phone or a get a new phone. Update May 2024: Recently had to replace my case again this time it was pretty beat up. Same broken spots as before. Lasted me a good year and honestly could’ve gone longer but looked too messy to be carrying around. I still give this case 5/5 stars. I drive for work and visited construction sites and move heavy equipment and often have my phone on me and risk dropping it a lot. Luckily I’m not clumsy but have dropped it from inside the truck on to the floor outside a couple of times. Maybe like a 4ft drop? Takes the impact no problem, i don’t drop my phone to often and even so i don’t walk around carelessly thinking this case is going to protect it. Even with a bulkier case, it’s important to remember phones still can have internal damage so don’t expect it to completely protect your phone. At the end of the day you are your phones best protection. As i mentioned i recently upgraded cases and did not purchase this case again. Reason being that I’m pretty good with not dropping my phone and this is a bit too bulky to support wireless battery back charging. As i bought a wireless battery pack and could only use it if i remove the case which then I’d have to carry separately in my pocket. It works with a wireless desk charger, just have to position it right. Not sure about other types of wireless desk chargers but the one i have at home definitely needs to be positioned correctly to pick it up. I still recommend this case for anyone looking for extra protection but something not to bulky. I have changed to the “jetech” magnetic case. its a very thin case and will eventually make a review on that.

review_text_raw: I work in trades so I wanted something that would protect my phone but not make it feel like I have a scrap 2x8 in my pocket. Also being in trades it has gone through its fair share of abuse and after having this for a little over a year now the only damage I can report is some cosmetic scratches, dings, a small non important piece of plastic as well as the rubber flap that goes over the charging port ripped off (though I'm to blame on most of that...). Long story short I told myself I would get a new phone when my current iPhone 8 dies. In desperate attempts to speed that up without being too blatant (as I've now had this phone for easily 6-7 years now and I'm ready for a new one) I've thrown this thing across rooms, out of second story windows, off roofs and ladders, etc. I think you get the point... Fortunately (or unfortunately) it has protected my phone through it all. The only things I have against it though is that the opening for the charger does give some trouble to the thicker aftermarket chargers (e.g. I have a Ryobi lightning charger that's thicker to supposedly protect it but it still charges with some "convincing"). In an attempt to handle that I ripped off that rubber flap that I mentioned before (no, that solved nothing but I felt better in the end). NOTE: It actually was starting to rip off slowly through use about 6 months in but I just expedited that process. The other point is that after a year of use (and abuse) its texture has gone pretty smooth so the grip isn't anything to marvel at but it does its job. I somewhat handled this by cutting a bunch of grooves with a utility knife but I can understand others not wanting to follow suit. TL;DR - Doesn't impede in screen or button usage. Great protection in a smaller and sleek design. May have some problems with charger clearance if you have really bulky aftermarket chargers. Notes for the picture: Mostly here to show the missing rubber flap that would usually cover the charging port. There was a think plastic piece that would go right below it and create a hole that the flap would fit into but that broke off as well. Most damage is through my abuse (for example the bottom left corner) but for the most part it's still in working condition. You can also see my "custom texturing job" I did on the back lol. Does it look pretty? No. Is that my fault? Absolutely.

product_title: OtterBox iPhone 8/7 & SE (3rd/2nd Gen) Commuter Series Case - Black
headline: Great, not too bulky, yet very protective case - Just avoid Amazon shipping!!
review_text_raw: For the money especially, this is a great case. Unlike the defender series or others like it this doesn’t have the P.I.T.A. two-sided case that locks together and is difficult to remove. Some reviews say it’s hard to put on, they’re clearly doing it wrong as it’s VERY easy. It’s a 2 part design, so while it comes together, it’s key to put the rubber part on the phone before snapping the hard plastic cover in place. No doubt people saying it’s a tight fit tried both at once. That’s more difficult and puts strain on the plastic. I’m the worst about dropping my phone. ai must have dropped it (iphone 8) at least 75-100 times minimum, and I don’t even worry about breaking anything anymore. The lip of it sticks out just enough to protect the screen, and the dual layering is ultra shock absorbent. It’s also pretty thin considering the amount of protection. I gave a 4 for durability and sturdiness as over time the outer plastic snapped on me and the inner rubber cover has a few worn areas, but at $20, replacing wasn’t particularly bothersome and it certainly lasted a good 6-9 months of hard use - better the case than my screen! Still a 5 in total as sometimes something has to break, and so perhaps it’s better being a little less sturdy. To anyone asking, of course it fits a 7, there is no big difference in the shape of 8 and 7. Idk if the lip would protect the plus as well since the screen is bigger, but that’s an overall risk the Plus phones have. Finally, I wish I could rate Amazon delivery separately. If you live in a city apartment building or even a house and won’t be home, they don’t bother reading delivery instructions (which always has info to access my mail room / lobby). It’s probably Amazon’s fault for having impossible schedules, but the drivers will *sometimes* try to buzz once (not always), then ignore the delivery instructions and leave the box outside if you’re not home or can’t answer. When I wondered where my replacement case was, a quick review showed some lady walking by, noticing the pile of boxes left, and took a couple small packages on top before walking quickly off, one of course was mine. Almost more infuriatingly, customer service put it down to “delivery error” and said they’d blame the shipper.. yet Amazon is the shipper. So they blame themselves and do nothing to fix it, and outsourced customer service means people that can only answer a few basic questions before they get confused and off script. This time they promised me they were working with delivery drivers to fix the problem, yet it’s been happening for at least 2 years. If my neighbors didn’t look out for each other and bring in anything left outside, much more would have been stolen by now. And still they have my sensitive door access info, which I don’t give out lightly.. and never use it. How it’s cheaper to replace these items than just fix the problem is beyond me. My advice, if 1-day delivery is an option, is to buy it alone so as not to make the $35 minimum and let UPS handle it, since their drivers would never leave packages out on a city street (they also take note of info like door codes, how crazy). It’s to the point where if I see Amazon shipping I dread it and have to try to stay home. At the very least a notification saying the package is outside for anyone to take would be a start. That’s enough about Amazon shipping, just on my mind since the first order got stolen. UPS safely brought the replacement though

product_title: OtterBox iPhone 8/7 & SE (3rd/2nd Gen) Commuter Series Case - Black
headline: Great case, but watch your charging cable.
review_text_raw: I see the case has undergone a slight re-design since my original one. It come with in soft inner rubber shell with an outer hard rubber shell. I guess that's to better absorb impact. The original one they were molded together. Now the inner shell appears to be removeable. That said, it seems to be well made. It's a tight fit to get the phone in. The buttons line-up where they should, so they are functional. Someone mentioned in another review that they liked the dust cover for the charging port. For me, it's a a love/hate relationship. I love the idea of keeping it closed when not charging, but since the "hinge" part of the flap has a strong reflex to close, I have to keep my phone motionless while charging or the pressure the lid has will cause the cord to pop-out just enough to stop charging without visual queue to know it happened. I actually get better results on a cheaper and thinner cord, but then it wears out the cord faster. So, for sturdiness, I give this 5 stars. But overall, due the the aforementioned charging issue, I give it 4 stars. Also, the outer case is a bit slippery, I wish it had better hand grip material, but workable if you know that.

product_title: ESR for iPhone 14/13 Case for MagSafe, Anti-Yellowing, Clear
headline: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
review_text_raw: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

review_text_raw: As someone who has a history of accidental phone drops (and let's be honest, who doesn't?), investing in solid phone protection is not just a preference, it's a necessity. The OtterBox phone case I recently purchased has once again proven why this brand is synonymous with top-tier durability and peace of mind. This case is an absolute tank, and if you value your phone's survival, look no further. Design & Build Quality (5/5): My OtterBox case feels incredibly robust and well-engineered right out of the box. The multi-layer design, typically combining a hard outer shell with a softer inner slipcover, provides excellent shock absorption. Despite its protective qualities, it doesn't add excessive bulk, maintaining a surprisingly comfortable grip. All ports, buttons, and cameras are precisely cut, ensuring full functionality without compromise. The materials feel premium and durable, built to withstand daily wear and tear. Protection (5/5): This is where OtterBox truly shines. I've had several unintended "gravity tests" since putting this case on my phone – drops on concrete, tile, and even a minor tumble down some stairs. Each time, my phone emerged completely unscathed. The raised edges around the screen and camera offer crucial protection against direct impacts when laid flat. The sealed port covers (on some models) are also fantastic for keeping out dust and lint, which can be a common issue. If you're prone to dropping your phone, or if your lifestyle demands extreme durability, this case is an absolute must-have. It shrugs off impacts that would shatter an unprotected phone. Ease of Use & Accessibility (4/5): While the protection is phenomenal, the case is snug (as it should be for protection!), so taking it on and off isn't a five-second job. However, once it's on, it's on to stay, which is precisely what you want. Buttons remain tactile and easy to press, and access to the charging port and speakers is unobstructed. The glass screen protector has maintained superb clarity despite’s bumps, drops, spills, and even flinging my phone down a hill (on accident). I think the hilly road surface would have caused more harm, but just 2 1/4” scratches resulted. Because of the double layered edges, this gives really good shock and impact protection. Drops only concrete, asphalt, and tile have cause zero damage to the case or phone. The thicker edges help my grip and make this easier to hold onto, but I have large hands. Despite that this still fits neatly into a belt holster without issue. The case seals well enough, but at the same time it’s not hard to open to clear a speck of dust or drop of moisture off the screen before resealing it. I have dropped my phone into a running shower for almost zero moisture getting into the case. I highly recommend this case as someone who isn’t gentle and often a klutz while handling my electronics.

product_title: ESR for iPhone 15 Case for MagSafe, Anti-Yellowing, Clear
headline: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
review_text_raw: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

product_title: Belkin Qi2.2 25W Wireless 3 in 1 Foldable Fast Charging Station for iPhone
headline: Great charger, but weak MagSafe magnets hold it back
review_text_raw: This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked. First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it. Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of. I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice. Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product. If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it. You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. A surprisingly light bump can cause the phone to fall off the charger, and for something you may use every day for years, that matters. If you’re comparing this with the Anker Prime, which costs roughly $30–$40 more, the additional cost may be worth considering if it provides a more secure magnetic connection. Over several years of daily use, $30–$40 isn’t much of a premium to avoid an annoyance you’ll potentially deal with every day.

product_title: Belkin Qi2.2 25W Wireless 3 in 1 Foldable Fast Charging Station for iPhone
headline: Nice looking charger with very annoying quirks/bugs
review_text_raw: It's cool that this is the "official" charging dock that Apple endorses. When it works, it works well and it feels quality, with all hinges feeling sturdy. Time will tell after folding it hundreds of times whether the hinges will hold up, but I feel optimistic. This is one of the few options you have unfortunately for 25W charging if you have a newer iPhone, as they tend to be really expensive. Watch charging works fine and reasonably well, but it seems like the pad doesn't shut off and the watch continues to get warmer as it sits fully charged. Phone charging doesn't seem to have this issue, but it might be whatever cooling tech they have keeping it room temp-ish. The part I hate the most about it is the airpod charging area. It has an annoyingly bright white LED that lights up when you put it on the charger, and it takes forever to start charging, if it even does that. I've woken up contless times to my airpods not having charged at all, even though I put it down as correctly as possible. Even when I move it back and forth on the charger it takes forever to finally register the airpods are on there and frankly it's a really poorly functioning charger that tarnishes an otherwise decent dock. Even when it does successfully charge, it does the same thing where the charger doesn't shut off after fully charging and the airpods are really warm when I pick the case up. All in all, a decent charger but don't expect the airpods charger pad to work well. Frankly, I expected better for almost $100 and I'm pretty disappointing overall.

Even when I move it back and forth on the charger it takes forever to finally register the airpods are on there and frankly it's a really poorly functioning charger that tarnishes an otherwise decent dock. Even when it does successfully charge, it does the same thing where the charger doesn't shut off after fully charging and the airpods are really warm when I pick the case up. All in all, a decent charger but don't expect the airpods charger pad to work well. Frankly, I expected better for almost $100 and I'm pretty disappointing overall.

headline: Heavy, but powerful charger
review_text_raw: This is a somewhat heavy (weighs about a pound), but powerful battery. I don't mind the weight, I expect that from a 20k battery. It feels solid and well built. I like the display and how it shows the negotiated voltage and amps so you can see what it is doing. I also like that it has a trickle charge mode for lower power devices like my watch and earbuds. Most batteries will shut off because there isn't enough of a power draw, in trickle charge mode the battery will not shut off for 3 1/2 hours. Please note that they recommend that you use a minimum 65 watt charger to charge the battery. You can use less power, but the battery will take longer to charge. With the more powerful charger it takes a little over an hour to fully charge. One day my M4 MacBook Air was down to around 25% and my phone was around 40%. I plugged both into the battery at the same time. I charged my phone to 80% and computer to 100% and the battery was down to about 10% remaining charge. The computer was drawing around 60 watts the majority of the time. One thing that has left me curious is that I have yet to see it either receive or draw more than 3 volts @ 20 amps since it says it is capable of 5 volts. Both my charger and computer should be capable of 100 watts, but I also know that devices negotiate with the charger so it doesn't bother me that it is less.

headline: Buy Elsewhere - Bought Two, Neither Work Right! - Low Watts/Single Item Charging Only
review_text_raw: NOT AS DESCRIBED - DO NOT BUY First of all, I think it's interesting that this listing is back up on Amazon when it was a dead link a few days ago. I was convinced it had been taken down due to too many people finding out about the false advertising behind this product. All other reviews on here telling you these chargers are BAD are correct. I bought two, and BOTH of them can only charge one item at a time, IF THAT. I left my iWatch on one of them for 5 days,... 5... days. And when I go to use it, guess what, iWatch dead! Fun, right? Haven forbid if you try to charge a phone at the same time as anything else; Whatever else you try to charge will NOT charge at the same time. Tried to use one to keep my PC controller charged,... ALWAYS "15% Battery" even in the top highest powered slot with a compatible USB C charger! LIES! The only somewhat good thing about one of the two of them is that with the correct capacity of charging cable, ONE of them does charge my iPhone quite fast, but even with that, both products are still junk and I regret both of these purchases, and I feel foolish buying a second just to make sure it wasn't the first one that was the problem. - Fooled me twice, shame on me. Yet another case of junk products that look good and function poorly on this platform. May this be my final lesson in the need to focus on well known and reputable brands as opposed to brands you never heard of like "Floorgu", "Cremplow", "Barbintron", and "Zalim-bee-yoh"; See Ryan George of Screen Rant's video "What Shopping On Amazon Feels Like" on YouTube to see exactly what I'm talking about. You'll get a good laugh. I’d provide the link but Amazon already rejected this review for that. We all get suckered from time to time looking for a good deal. Buy nice or buy twice. Any who, search elsewhere for your charging needs. You've been warned.

headline: Finally cleared off my desk with this one charger
review_text_raw: I was tired of having four different bricks fighting for outlets so I grabbed this to consolidate everything, and it's honestly done the job better than I hoped. I've got my laptop, my phone, an iPad, and my earbuds all plugged in at once and none of them slow to a crawl the way I expected. The laptop charging is the part that surprised me most, it went from almost dead to more than halfway in about half an hour while other stuff was still hooked up. It stays cooler than my old chargers too, just barely warm even with a full load running. I like that the cord detaches and it's long enough to reach across my desk without me rearranging everything. One thing to know is the little guide it comes with is pretty bare bones, so I had to figure out on my own which ports push the most power, and the top two are the fast ones. Took me a day to sort out my layout but once I did it's been smooth. It's a solid chunk of plastic but way smaller than I figured it'd be for handling this many devices. No regrets so far.

product_title: NOCO GENIUS1 1A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
headline: Works as intended
review_text_raw: So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.

headline: Little Miracle
review_text_raw: Okay, I did NOT expect this little thing to work, but it did and might for you IF you have patience. My Grandfather who was MoAT (Mechanic of All Things) owned back in the day what I thought were REAL chargers, they were so big and heavy they had to be put on wheels and rolled around, they had giant switches that'd illuminate and while I'm probably purely imagining this they were plugged into 220-volt outlets. This thing fits in the palm of my hand, just as pictured, smaller than most mobile phones. "Huh," I said, "this should be comical." I hooked it up and, as others have said, figuring this thing out is NOT straight forward, the instruction manual is weak to say the least, the good news is, as I found, there are many intrepid experimenters who, like me, bought it on a whim and did some trial and error which it'd seem 99% of them got the thing to work to their needs, just like me hence, I'm taking the time to write this review. headline: Seems pretty good so far
review_text_raw: I have two of these. They are not exactly the same model (I think one of them is an older version of this model). The older one, I have had in the garage for several years to keep the batteries in the cars up when they are not driven very often. Some people say these are not for car batteries and I won't argue with them but the one I have out there definitely keeps the battery in my 2001 Corolla charged. And in fact, we had an incident where someone left a dome light on in that car and drained the battery to the point to where there was absolutely no response from anything electrical in the car. We started the car with a jumper pack, pulled it in the garage and connected it to the Noco and let it do it's thing. That's been at least a year and that battery is still going strong in that car. I purchased this one off Amazon to use on various SLA batteries I have around. I have two jumper packs with 18 AH SLA batteries in them. One of them had been sitting in the garage for several years due to the fact last time I tried to charge it, it wouldn't charge. I was going to order a new battery for it from Amazon but I figured I kind of needed an extra charger for SLA batteries anyway and this Noco unit was less than the price of a new battery for the old jumper pack. I figured it would be a long shot to try and charge that old battery and get any more life out of it but I thought it would be interesting to see what would happen. Can't be a tougher challenge for a SLA battery that's been sitting in a garage dead for years. Well, that jumper pack doesn't exactly have easy access to the battery but after some fighting with it, I got it open and popped the clamps on the terminals. The charging light began to pulse and after about a day, went green (was still pulsing but was pulsing green). It finally went solid green. I left it plugged in a few days. I have one of those miniature inverters that plugs into a cigarette lighter (that particular jumper pack doesn't have a built-in inverter but does have a cigarette lighter plug). So I plugged it in and tested it with a clamp light. So far, seems to be working about as well as you'd expect for a jumper pack battery that is probably approaching ten years old now. Or maybe better than you'd expect. It's only a 12 watt LED in the clamp light but my main goal was to get every last bit of value from any SLA batteries that I can. I'd definitely have a use for a small inverter like that in a power outage and if you have an extra battery that you can plug it into, so much the better. I believe the built-in charger on that jumper pack just may have died or was not up to charging it's battery for whatever reason. Remains to be seen how much more life I can get out of such batteries but it's definitely worth the price paid.

headline: Works with a REALLY low battery
review_text_raw: My wife has a 1995 Mercedes SL320 that she did not drive all winter and well into the new year... when she opened the garage door and tried to start it the battery was dead, drained by MANY months of the old style mechanical clock running without the car being started so the battery could charge My (brand name withheld) several year old 10 amp 'smart' charger would not work because the battery was too low to be detected So, I looked for a different charger with a FORCE mode to get a dead battery to start charging... I connected this one at about 7PM at night (it never would go into force mode, since the battery had 'just enough' charge to be detected) and when I get in the car at 7AM the next morning the battery had enough of a charge for the dash lights to come on, but not enough to run the starter The PDF I downloaded shows that this 1 amp charger will take 'about' 23 hours to charge a 30 AH battery... the battery in her SL320 is a 100 AH model, so I will let the charger run for another full day before I try to start the car again (or maybe 2 days to get the charger enough time to work) So far, this charger is doing exactly what I need (I thought about a larger model to charge quicker, but decided that slow charging was good enough... she hasn't driven her car since last Fall, so she can now wait a day or two)

review_text_raw: I have a truck that mostly sits in the garage. Every time I need to back it out of the garage, the battery is dead. product_title: NOCO GENIUS10 10A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
headline: Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often
review_text_raw: I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time. As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The other button I believe is for what kind of charge you want(trickle, decharge, repair) but since I have a brand new battery I simply keep it on trickle charge. The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. I keep a smoke detector next to the NOCO and battery just to be safe. I got the NOCO on sale during Prime Day so it is definitely a good value for the money. So far so good.

product_title: NOCO GENIUS10 10A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
headline: Pretty neat device, very capable as well
review_text_raw: I have a battery charger made in the 1970s, inherited from dad that passed away in 2011. It was time for another one, and I was going to buy another Schumacher that weights about 15 Lbs. Was ready to pull the trigger and decided to see if something better was out there, thus buying a Genius 10 instead based on YouTube reviews. The Genius 10 was much larger and heavier than how it looks in the picture. The build quality is really good in my eyes, looks like tough ABS polymer, very nice cords with that good feeling wire jacket insulation. The new clamps are nice looking and very practical to me. It's heavy and awkward to store, so I bought the Noco case as well; I thought the other case was too small in size. I ran some test with it, on a 12V Honda Lead Acid and Group H8 AGM battery and was happy the results. It was more intuitive than the 1970s version I have with 30 amp boost that is scary to use. What I like with Noco or Genius, it's several tools in one unit, so every 3 or 4 months, I can use the Genius to check the status of all my batteries, well that is the plan at least. One neat thing, using the 12V output to keep a battery online while changing a battery, so the cars computer keeps running and doesn't reboot from removing the battery causing weird things to happen. I have no regrets in my purchase and bought the case to enhance it more. I think the price is reasonable as well considering what a $100 buys today.

product_title: NOCO GENIUS10 10A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
headline: Saved me from buying a new battery!
review_text_raw: EDIT 2/26/24: I am now the blocks "AAA". Been helping people start their cars when jump starts with cables have not worked. Definitely handy to get other people out of an otherwise expensive pinch. I have a car battery that I purchased around 2016 (date of review 1/3/24). The car itself does not get driven much, at most 2-3 times a week no longer than 15 minutes one way. Throughout the years I've drained it by leaving the car lights on. Its always required a jump start after that to get going again. Recently I've been an idiot and been leaving my lights on more frequently. Eventually it required me to jump start everytime I wanted to turn on the car. It was becoming a hassle and I was about to call it quits and purchase a new battery until I came across Project Farm's review on battery chargers. This was at the top of the list so I figured to give it a shot. I was not disappointed! I charged it for 4 days straight, put it in my car, and it started right up. Not surprised considering it was just charged but the real test laid ahead. I was going to be out of town for two weeks and leave the car sitting. I came back two weeks later and the car started up, no hesitation whatsoever, as if it was a different battery! The NOCO Genius 10 saved me about $150-200 at least in a brand new battery. On top of that, I can now use it for other batteries in the event of any similar issues. The instructions on the other hand are a bit confusing and had to rely on YouTube comments to piece it together. For those who are confused at what to do, I did not do a 12V repair (function which this unit has) as it requires the battery to be completely charged first. All I did was charge it straight for 4 days uninterrupted. When first put on battery to the charger it will be in standby mode. You push (or hold depending on what you need) the MODE button to select your desired option. I was charging a lead acid battery so I selected 12V. The meter at the top slowly advanceD from each of the four bars until the final bar was pulsing green which indicates its charging to full (over 80% I believe). The green charging light continued to slowly pulse even on the 4th day but I took a gamble and disconnected it from the battery. For the battery to be 100% charged, the green light should stay solid. That means my battery worked 2 weeks later after sitting and it wasn't even at 100%. The unit can also force a charge on batteries that are extremely under voltage. Thats a separate setting that I haven't had to use yet. It can also charge AGM and Lithium but I believe the 12V repair function is only for lead acid. Unfortunately I had to go through 3 separate orders because the first two were from Amazon Warehouse and I encountered issues with both, consecutively. I ended up getting frustrated and just purchased a brand new charger. Pros: Solid build quality Excellent cable connections with weather covers Compatible with a wide variety of batteries Repair and Force charge batteries Cons: Poor instructions Charge is slow BUT I think thats how these chargers work TL;DR Try this first before rushing to get a new battery it is a good investment that can save you a lot of money

review_text_raw: I purchased the NOCO GENIUS5 to maintain the batteries in vehicles that don't get driven regularly, and it has been one of those tools that quickly proves its value. Setup was straightforward. The included connectors are easy to use, and the charger automatically detects the battery and selects the appropriate charging mode. I especially appreciate that it can be left connected for maintenance without worrying about overcharging, which gives me peace of mind when storing a vehicle for extended periods. Overall, this is a dependable smart charger that is easy to use, versatile, and well-built. Whether you're maintaining a seasonal vehicle, motorcycle, lawn equipment, or simply want a charger that can safely stay connected long-term, the GENIUS5 is a worthwhile investment. Helpful tip: If you're using it for battery maintenance, consider installing the included quick-connect lead permanently on the battery. It makes future charging sessions much faster and more convenient.

headline: NOCO Genius5
review_text_raw: I bought the Genius5 after neglecting a relatively new battery in my motorcycle. Due to weather and travel, I often have long gaps between rides. Unfortunately, one of these gaps was long enough to damage the battery. I didn’t realize that batteries need a minimal charge to avoid sulfation, and mine had become severely discharged. Although my NOCO GB40 starter worked fine, the battery wasn’t holding a charge even after a day of riding. Instead of immediately replacing the battery, I decided to try saving it with the Genius5. After charging the battery with the Genius5, I tested it with a battery analyzer, which reported it as damaged. I then ran the desulfation process, and afterward, the analyzer showed the battery was in good condition. I repeated the tests several days later to be sure, and the battery still appeared to be in good health. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. I still carry the GB40 in my panniers, just in case, but I haven’t needed to use it lately. Some notes on the desulfation process: The desulfation process seems to send voltage peaks, and you may hear some bubbling inside the battery. This happened to me, and from what I’ve read, it’s normal as long as there’s not too much bubbling and no vapors, heating, or swelling of the battery. The entire process takes a while, so it’s unrealistic to monitor it the whole time. However, I recommend watching it for the first 20 minutes to ensure the battery noises aren’t increasing. After that, you can leave it running while staying nearby, just in case something goes wrong. A final note on this process: because of the voltage peaks, I didn’t run it with the battery connected to the motorcycle to avoid any potential damage to the circuits. For regular maintenance charging, I do keep the battery connected. The Genius5 is designed to work with standard batteries, gel, and even lithium ones. The one I used was a Gel Yuasa, and I’m pleased with the results. I also purchased the NOCO cables (GC002 X-Connect M6) to make it easier to connect the charger without removing the seat. The cables were a bit expensive but seem well-constructed and are quite convenient. Final thoughts: If you have a vehicle that sits unused for extended periods, and this happens frequently, then this charger is ideal for you. However, if you only need it once a year or less, it might be easier and cheaper to disconnect the battery from the vehicle while you’re away to prevent discharging. For my use case, the Genius5 has been worth it, and I’d definitely buy it again.

headline: Resurrected a dead battery overnight
review_text_raw: My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed. Noco is one of the few chargers that can charge a completely dead battery. Watched a project farm youtube video on car battery chargers ( see chart at 18m29s of the video) before buying. I purchased the 5A one due to time constraint ( charged 75% in 8 hours ). You can buy the 2A version or 1A version if you have all the time and just want to keep batteries fully charged. I let it charge overnight and had a fully functional battery in the morning. This happens to me whenever I go on long trips ( 4 weeks + ). With a rechargeable jump starter, you are limited by the battery life of the starter which is only 3-4 years after which most batteries fail. The wall charger hopefully will last a long longer. Saved me a lot of time - No need to drive the car around after jump starting to get some charge into the battery. Just charge overnight and done. Love it.

headline: Yeah so don't mix up your fused alligator cables if you buy different models
review_text_raw: I bought a Genius1 and Genius5. The latter failed on first use due to my mistake mixing up the alligator clips during unboxing. I didn't look closely enough to notice that the 1 and 5 aren't just feature levels but are current ratings in Amps. The proprietary connectors are identical but the 1A unit has a 2A fuse and the 5A unit has a 10A fuse, and they're on the battery side of the connectors not the device side, so obviously the 2A fuse correctly blew when I tried using the 5A unit. They work fine after fixing my careless mix-up, but I'd like these better if the device or fuse holder were marked with a recommended fuse rating, or the connectors couldn't mate with the wrong device, or the fuse holder were on the device side of the proprietary connector, or the unit came with spare fuses, or the fuse ratings were included in the online user guide, or the user guide were included in the box, or the safety guide were printed in a typeface legible to adult human eyes. Anyway, keep your cables together with the devices and don't mix em up.

headline: High quality at a reasonable cost
review_text_raw: This charger/tender worked well to "revive" a ~80Ah lead acid battery that sat in a low state of charge for nearly a year. After an initial 2.5 hour cycle in repair mode, followed by a higher amp charge from an older/larger charger, a noticeable improvement in battery performance was observed. A shorter repair cycle, about 30 minutes total, restored some capacity on another lead acid battery still in use. There are cheaper desulfator-only options, of questionable reliability/longevity, so the additional features offered on this model were cost-effective for my intended usage. While I have not yet used this as a tender/maintainer for any length of time, the cabling to and from the charger are long enough to reach from one side of a car to the other. This unit did not seem to produce much heat in repair mode with ~75F ambient temp. In auto charge mode between 25% and 75%, it was warm to the touch. I'll have to try a longer charge period to see if it heats up further. UPDATE: after using repair & charge mode on a flat battery for a few hours, this unit can get fairly hot. Using this on a flat surface so air can get underneath is a good idea. This product did not come with a manual in the box, just the warranty booklet. product_title: NOCO GENIUS5 5A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
headline: Revived my battery
review_text_raw: I bought a used 2022 Honda Ridgeline with ~7,000 miles on it some months back. It was a "dealer demo car" and was well-maintained as a result. Now, it's got around 12,000 miles on it. One day, I left the lights on too long with the ignition off, and had the radio playing. Stupid on my part, but my battery didn't have enough charge to deliver the amps needed to turn the engine over. I bought a Noco GB40, and it worked well - it'd start my truck when needed. Yesterday, it didn't. I guess the battery had degraded too much, so I was shopping for new batteries when the sticker shock hit me. Given the age of my truck, I thought it would be silly to replace the battery. Someone recommended the Noco Genius5, so I gave it a shot. Amazon's same-day delivery got it to me quickly, and I basically hooked it up to the battery, plugged it in, set it to AGM mode, and let it go to work. I waited several hours for the charger light to show "solid green", indicating it was fully charged. I started up my truck; it sounded better than the day I bought it. However, on the dash, it had a note about an "emissions problem". My scan tool showed a permanent code with the Transmission Control Module and a bunch of other temporary codes. Since I didn't have any codes before, I figured I may have freaked out the electronics by charging the battery while the battery was hooked up to the truck, or maybe by touching the terminals out of sequence when removing the cables. Either way, I removed the battery from my truck, hooked up the Genius5, and set it to "repair mode". My truck had low mileage when I bought it, at about a year old, which likely meant that it say for a while when not in use. Maybe that could have led to sulfation or stratification, which could have meant it wouldn't charge as effectively from the alternator. I also wanted to remove the battery to allow the computers to reset in the truck. If it was still throwing codes after that, I'd bring it into the dealer. This morning, when I woke up, I noticed the Genius5 was in standby mode, meaning the repair mode had finished. I started the Genius5 back up, and set it to AGM mode again -- it took about a minute, but it said the battery was good to go with a solid green light. I Installed the battery back in my truck, fired it up, and I kid you not, it sounded better than ever -- less strained, more powerful, and all of the codes were gone. My truck had a freakout -- not due to this device, I'm sure, but likely due to me doing something stupid. It's rare for me to review a product so quickly. This thing is amazing, has lots of neat accessories available for it, and saved me money. I'll continue using it to prolong my batteries and save me money in the long-run. If you're on the fence, this little device is absolutely legit. 10/10 would recommend.

headline: It actually works for Windows 10!
review_text_raw: I was super excited to purchase this 4K webcam to help myself have crisper, clearer video chats when teaching online. Since changing from an established workplace to freelance, I had to return my previous company computer, and that left me with my old 2012 HP running Windows 10. The built-in webcam on my laptop is terrbile! At my brother's recommendation, since I needed something better (and since simply using my cell phone wouldn't work for the long-term), I began looking into external webcams. I asked Google's AI to help me find something suitable for my laptop in particular, and somehow this 4K camera came up. However, when it came in the mail and I plugged it in, my computer didn't seem to recognize it at all. No blue light! Anyway, I was beginning to wonder if I'd have to return it, but I had already attached the "privacy" adhesive over the lens and was concerned that this might mean I couldn't send it back. Also, I really wanted it to work! So I did a ton of troubleshooting, updating things on my computer here and there, installing drivers, etc. Nothing worked. I then bought an external USB 3.0 hub since my laptop's hubs aren't powerful enough for a 4K webcam evidently. Plugged everything in. Still, nothing! Then finally, I asked AI for recommendations regarding that particular webcam and my specific laptop, once again. The final recommendation it gave me was to "install Native EMEET Software." I had read earlier that everything would be supplied automatically as soon as you plug it in, but it turns out that's not always the case. I went onto the website, and there's a place listing "downloads" where you can get the needed software for either Windows PC or Mac. So, I downloaded the Windows one ... and voila! At long last, after installing that software, the camera worked! Apparently it's still not perfectly displaying in 4K, but no matter! The quality is is a step down from that, since my computer cannot quite support 4K. What it can display though is still a MASSIVE upgrade from what I had before! The low-light performance is excellent, and you can adjust the camera settings (contrast, saturation, etc.). I've never used an external webcam before so to me this is pretty cool. Plus, I can always use this camera on a newer laptop whenever I'm able to purchase one, and then I can have perfect 4K. But for now, attached to the laptop that I have, this camera quality is still beyond "good enough"; it's great. I'm glad I didn't give up and send this back. So it's completely worth it -- just know that if you have an old computer running Windows 10, you might have to jump through multiple hoops first before getting it to work. ;)

review_text_raw: FYI: I purchased this camera after seeing someone else who presented using it. Everyone was curious what camera they were using because it was such good lighting and great video. However, I'm not sure this camera is working with full functionality on my hardware. I went through a bunch of troubleshooting, and here's the conclusion per ChatGPT... Good morning ☀️ — thank you for the detailed info. That explains everything. You’re on: Surface Pro 11th Edition (ARM64) Snapdragon X (ARM) processor That is the root cause. ________________________________________ 🎯 The Real Issue Logitech RightSight is currently not supported on Windows ARM (Snapdragon X / ARM64). Here’s why: RightSight depends on: • Logitech’s middleware service • x64 camera processing components • AI framing pipeline extensions On ARM Surface devices: • Logi Tune runs under emulation • The Logitech camera extension layer does not fully attach to the Windows Modern Camera Stack • AI features (RightSight) fail to initialize • Video works (because UVC driver works) • 4K works (hardware OK) • But AI framing = unavailable That’s exactly your symptom set. ________________________________________ ✅ Why Everything Else Works ✔ Camera app works ✔ 4K works ✔ Windows Hello works ✔ Device shows correctly ✔ No USB issue ✔ No driver corruption Only vendor AI features fail — classic ARM compatibility limitation. ________________________________________ 🚫 This Is Not Fixable Via Settings Disabling: • Frame Server • Basic camera • Studio effects • Multiple apps setting Will not fix it on ARM. This is architectural, not a configuration problem. ________________________________________ 🔎 Confirmation Test (Optional) In Logi Tune: Go to Crop. If: • Field of View options work (65°, 78°) • Zoom works • But Auto-Framing is disabled That confirms it’s just the AI layer. ________________________________________ 🧠 Why This Happens Surface Pro 11 (Snapdragon X) uses: • Windows on ARM • Modern Camera Driver (MCD) • NPU-based camera pipeline Logitech RightSight expects: • x64 processing environment • Vendor extension hooks not fully exposed in ARM64 camera stack Until Logitech releases a native ARM64 version of the RightSight service, it won’t enable. ________________________________________ 📌 Current Status (Early 2026) As of now: • Logitech supports Intel/AMD Windows • ARM64 support is partial • AI features are inconsistent or unavailable ________________________________________ 💡 Your Options Option 1 — Wait for Logitech ARM-native update This will likely come, since Snapdragon X PCs are new. Option 2 — Use Windows Studio Effects (if available) Surface Pro 11 has NPU-based auto framing built in. Check: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → Built-in camera If Studio Effects exists there, you can use Windows auto-framing instead. Option 3 — Use Software Framing (Zoom / Teams) Both now have built-in auto framing. ________________________________________ ✅ Final Conclusion Your hardware is fine. Your configuration is fine. Your issue is ARM platform compatibility.

review_text_raw: ## **Logitech MX Brio Ultra HD 4K: The New Gold Standard for Video** If you haven’t upgraded your webcam in a few years, the **Logitech MX Brio** is a startling reminder of just how far imaging technology has come. Gone are the days of grainy, "good enough" video calls. We are officially in the era of ultra-crisp, professional-grade production sitting right on top of your monitor. ### **Crystal Clarity & Visual Fidelity** The jump to **Ultra HD 4K** is immediately noticeable. The clarity is staggering—it picks up textures and details that older 1080p sensors simply smudge away. Whether you’re in a high-stakes board meeting or recording content, the image looks expensive. It handles difficult lighting with ease, ensuring you don't look washed out when the sun hits your desk or like a shadow when the lights are low. ### **Pro-Grade Audio** Usually, webcam microphones are an afterthought, but the audio here is surprisingly **clear and crisp**. It manages to isolate your voice while minimizing that hollow, "bathroom" echo common in cheaper units. While dedicated mics still have their place, for 95% of users, this audio quality is more than enough to sound professional and authoritative. ### **Total Software Control** Where this camera really shines is the **Logitech G HUB or Logi Options+** integration. The level of control is deep: * **Fine-tuned adjustments:** You can tweak ISO, shutter speed, white balance, and exposure. * **Field of View:** Crop in for a tight headshot or widen it out to show your workspace. * **Show Mode:** A clever bit of tech that lets you tilt the camera down to show your desk, automatically flipping the image so your viewers can see your sketches or notes correctly. ### **The Verdict** It’s incredible to see how much technology has shifted in just the last few years. We’ve moved from "webcams" to "miniature cinema cameras." The **Logitech MX Brio** isn't just a tool for Zoom calls; it’s a high-performance piece of hardware that brings professional studio quality to a plug-and-play format. If you value how you show up in the digital world, this is the upgrade you've been waiting for.

headline: The best “professional work” webcam I’ve personally used, especially for virtual backgrounds
review_text_raw: I bought the Logitech MX Brio after spending years using a mirrorless camera setup (Lumix GH3 + prime lens) as my desk webcam. I work remotely full-time and spend most of my day in video calls (99% in Microsoft Teams), so my priorities are a little different from the average streaming-focused review. What I wanted was: • excellent image quality at normal desktop distances • reliable performance in Teams • strong virtual background segmentation • stable autofocus/exposure • easy to set up For my use case, the MX Brio has honestly been excellent. The biggest surprise was how good the image looks in real-world meetings. Yes, my GH3 (and other mirrorless cameras) can still produce a more cinematic image in ideal conditions, but in Teams specifically (where video is heavily compressed and usually capped at 1080p), the practical gap is much smaller than people think. As far as the camera is concerned, what matters most is consistency and signal quality, and this camera delivers both. The MX Brio handles exposure transitions smoothly, autofocus has been reliable, and image sharpness is very good without looking overly processed. Logitech also seems to have improved color handling compared to some older Brio models that could occasionally look harsh or over-sharpened. Where this webcam REALLY shines is virtual background and portrait segmentation. I use a virtual background almost 100% of the time, and this camera consistently gives cleaner edge separation than several other webcams I’ve tested. Good lighting absolutely helps, but the MX Brio seems to provide a very clean image feed that works well with Teams’ background processing. A few other things I appreciated: • solid low-light recovery without becoming a smeary mess • flexible field of view options • sturdy physical build • built-in microphone • easy mounting and positioning There are a couple tradeoffs worth mentioning: • Logitech’s software ecosystem is still a little fragmented (Logi Tune, G Hub, etc.) • if you are primarily a streamer/content creator, there may be better options depending on your workflow • this camera, like any, benefits significantly from proper lighting and good positioning. It's worth it to invest in a couple lights and proper mounting system But for a professional desk setup focused on video meetings, presentations, collaboration, and hybrid work, I think Logitech understood the assignment here surprisingly well. This is the first dedicated webcam I’ve used where I no longer feel tempted to drag a mirrorless camera back onto my desk.

headline: An excellent webcam that gets the important things right
review_text_raw: I think this is exactly what most people need in a webcam. It doesn't try to chase unnecessary specs or gimmicks, and for video calls, 1080p is more than enough. When your video feed is usually only a couple of inches across on someone else's screen, higher resolutions don't offer much real-world benefit. The camera itself produces a good image, but what really impressed me were the thoughtful design details. My favorite is the manual privacy shutter on the front. It's simple, works well, and gives me peace of mind when I'm not using the camera. I also appreciate the standard 1/4"-20 tripod thread on the bottom, making it easy to mount on a tripod or any other standard camera accessory. Another feature I wasn't expecting to appreciate as much is the ball-joint mount. I use two monitors that are angled toward me instead of sitting perfectly flat, so being able to fine-tune the camera's angle without moving the monitor is incredibly convenient. The roughly five-foot USB-A cable also provides plenty of length to route it neatly to my PC, and the green indicator light lets you know whenever the camera is actively being used. I honestly don't have any real complaints, especially considering the price. It was easy to set up, the image quality is exactly what I wanted, and the extra touches like the privacy shutter, tripod mount, adjustable ball joint, and activity light make it feel like a much more thoughtfully designed product than many budget webcams. Overall, I'm very impressed. If you're looking for an affordable webcam for meetings, online classes, streaming, or video calls, I'd have no hesitation recommending this one.

For years I’ve worked under an overhead light in my dining room (I own a townhouse, not huge so no extra room for an actual office, therefore my desk is downstairs in between the LR and DR) with my headaches and migraines becoming more and more frequent. I set the lamp up almost immediately upon delivery. Super simple to set up, no hassle at all, clamp it to the desk, tighten the clamp, plug it up and throw 2 AAA’s into the remote and BAM! You’re done. The strain on my eyes and my head was almost instantly relieved. The numerous light settings to choose from, AWESOMENESS. After trying them all I finally found my sweet spot (and It took less than five minutes to find). I love that it has a nightlight setting (didn’t notice that in the description) and a timer. It appears to be made very well, very sturdy but easily flexed to your liking. Love that the lights are two different bars and can be adjusted individually as well. Overall, best money I’ve spent on my workspace since I discovered the almighty mouse jiggler, honestly. If you’re on the fence and looking at every lamp Amazon has listed, save your time and energy and just click to buy, I promise, you won’t be disappointed!!

headline: Great for big monitors, but overpriced for what you get
review_text_raw: Solid monitor light, but probably not worth the price unless you have a huge screen This has been a nice addition to my desk setup. I chose it because, as you can probably tell, my monitor is massive (49 inches), and I needed something that would actually cover a decent portion of the screen. Pros: Brightness: This light really helped brighten up my space. My office tends to be pretty dark, so it’s been great for overall visibility and eye comfort. Size & Flexibility: I love how large it is and that I can move it around to get the angle I want. Quality: It feels well-made and doesn’t look cheap at all. (To be fair, this is the only monitor light I’ve tried, so I don’t have a ton to compare it to.) Cons: Price: Even though the build quality is solid, I still don’t get how this costs over $50. It’s just white and warm light with brightness adjustments. No RGB, no standout features. If you don’t have a large curved monitor like mine, I’d say go with a cheaper one that offers more features. Remote only: This part is wild to me. There are zero controls on the light itself. Everything depends on the remote. So if you misplace it, you’re basically out of luck. Final thoughts: Overall, the light works well, and the size is perfect for my ultra-wide monitor. I just think it’s overpriced for what it is. If you specifically need the large size and basic lighting, it’s a good pick. But if not, there are more affordable options out there with better features.

product_title: LED Desk Lamp with Clamp, 17" Stepless Dimming Light, Black
headline: Recommended. Could be improved but good as is.
review_text_raw: TL;DR: Recommended but could be improved. I'm using this lamp in my living room to illuminate a bluetooth keyboard in the evening. The gooseneck keeps the lamp where I put it and feels like it's well made and will last. The lamp has 3 color settings - white, amber and off-white(?). I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.
