product_title: Desk Lamp for Home Office, Eye Comfortable LED Desk Light for Long Hours, Adjustable Swing Arm with Memory Function, Black
headline: All Good except 1 Big Thing
review_text_raw: TLDR: Solid build, good light quality, useful brightness and color controls, and a swing arm that does most of what you want. The big catch is that it does not behave the way modern smart home users will expect, and the mounting geometry has some real-world limits the listing photos do not show. Four stars, with caveats worth knowing before you click buy. Let me lead with the good, because there is plenty of it. The light itself is genuinely nice. Plenty of brightness for working, reading, or close-up tasks, and the color temperature options give you warm yellow, neutral white, and a cooler white-blue depending on what you are doing. Eleven brightness levels is more granularity than I expected. The arm extends and folds well, and the head pivots to put light right where you want it. It runs on USB, the wall adapter is included, and the wattage is low enough that you can power it from a laptop port if that is convenient. The clamp mount is solid and holds tight once you have it in place. A note on installation. The clamp wants a specific amount of mounting surface, and my location had less than the lamp wanted in one direction. I pulled out a Dremel and shaved a small relief into the underside so the clamp could sit properly. Not a complaint, just a heads up if your desk has a thick lip, a beveled edge, or a rounded corner where you want this to live. Now, the big thing. This lamp does not default to on when power is restored. If you turn it off and walk away, fine. If your power blips, or if you have it on a smart switch that cuts power, the lamp comes back off. To turn it back on you have to walk over to the lamp and press the little button on the inline cord controller, which sits close to the base of the arm and is not always easy to reach. This matters because the listing advertises a memory function, and modern buyers, especially anyone with a smart home setup, are going to read that and assume something it does not actually mean. Here is what is happening. The memory function does work, in a narrow sense. When you press the on button, the lamp comes back at whatever brightness and color mode you used last. It does not have to be reset every time. That is real and it is useful. What the memory function does not do is preserve the on/off state across a power cut. The reason is that this is a soft-touch push button rather than a mechanical switch. The lamp's electronics have to be powered to know they are on, and when power is removed and restored the default state is off. A traditional mechanical switch physically holds the circuit closed and is why your bedroom lamp comes back on when the power flickers. This one does not, by design. If you live in a fully manual lighting world, this is a non-issue. You will press the button and life goes on. If you have your office lights on a smart switch, or you have ever said the words "Google (or Alexa), turn on the lights," this is going to be an ongoing minor annoyance. I had assumed, like most lights, that I could plug this into the same smart switch as the rest of the room and have it come on with everything else. Instead it sits there dark while everything else lights up, waiting for me to walk over and poke it. The other thing worth flagging is the arm geometry. The first segment, the one closest to the clamp, is not designed to swing forward. It folds up and back, which is fine on an open desk where you have empty wall behind you. If you are mounting this on the back edge of a desk that sits against a wall, on the lip of a hutch, on top of a shelving unit, or inside a cubicle, you are going to discover that the elbow needs room to bow outward behind the lamp. The listing photos all show the lamp on an open desk with nothing behind it, so this is not obvious until you have it in hand. Plan your mounting location with that in mind. There is also a 45 minute auto-off timer button on the controller. Apparently aimed at bedtime reading. I have not used it but it is there if you want it. Four stars. The light is good and the build is good. The memory function exists but means something different than a smart home buyer will assume, and the mounting flexibility has limits that the listing does not show. If you can live with those, this is a nice lamp at a fair price. If you were hoping to drop it into an automated lighting routine, you are going to want to know about the default-off behavior before you order.

product_title: LED Desk Lamp with USB Charging Port for Dorm Office, 800lm, CRI 92, Black
headline: Great simple desk lamp with nice features. Worth it!
review_text_raw: I gotta say I am really loving this lamp. It's bright, and if you need to you can adjust the brightness to better suit your eyes. It's got a sundown color setting for night time so it doesn't strain your eyes. It's kind of like the blue filter setting many computers and phones are adding that add a slightly orange filter to the screen. The lamp however uses what I would call tan LED's. They're not orange and they're not brown, they're TAN! Jokes aside it's a great feature for someone like me who is constantly reading and using my computer to study. The other great feature is this lamp has two standard wall outlets so it acts like an extension cord as well. I didn't check the rating but I'd only use it for a laptop charger or something else lightweight. On top of all that it has 3 USB ports, two which put out 1 amp at 5volts and one that puts out 2 amps at 5 volts, so you can charge multiple devices at a time or if you need more light you can buy some USB lamps, or maybe even a USB fan and just plug em into your lamp. Now the chargers are not controlled by the lamp, they're always on basically. Though they don't draw their full power unless they're charging. You can tell because the base only gets warm when it's been charging something which is what happens when transformers consume power because nothing is 100% efficient and some heat gets lost in the process. My only real qualm with this thing is how light the base is. It's not a big issue, but I wish I could put a lead weight in it just to give it more heft. Also if they moved the lamp neck closer to the middle or extended the base a little farther behind the lamp neck so you could open it one handed that'd be even better. Again not a big issue, it's a great little lamp and I'd still recommend it if you want something simple and you have a lot of electronics and accessories to keep charged like I do.

headline: Just what I was looking for!
review_text_raw: I'll be honest. I was looking for something in my local brick and mortar stores. Target, Walmart, Home Depot, Lowes... every place let me down because they all had the same unimaginative junk. And certainly not in store so I can just go get it. I have a pretty deep computer desk with dual 27" monitors on moving arms. I also have a separate soldering table. I wanted good, shadow free illumination on both and nobody had anything that would work. Lo and behold, I stumble across this on Amazon. I love when someone has a good idea and turns it into a great product. Unboxing is just ridiculously easy. There is no building. All you have to do is screw clamp it to your surface and plug it in. It seems it'll fit a pretty thick surface too. 1 1/8" (almost 3cm) thick shelf stock for a desk and it has enough space for another inch or so. No flickering that I can see. It's clean smooth light. The color temperature options are plentiful and you can cycle through presets of both temp and brightness or do a smooth transition to what you want. The side panels are separately turned on and off (together) and can fold down 90° (if you really wanted to) or all the way up to upside down on top of the main lamp. It's all folded together in the box, so just unfold and use. Only real issue is there's no telescoping function. So if you have a small desk and want it mounted at the back AND close to your surface, you might have to get creative. The auto brightness is interesting... it gets brighter when the ambient light goes down. I expected the opposite. But maybe this makes sense. I prefer manual control anyway. Overall, very great product for anyone working at a desk, writing, making, what have you. I love this thing already. There's a really good video review that will show you all you need to know. I bought two right then and there (for both tables) and I do not regret my decision at all.

You are able to adjust the brightness, there are three levels The thing to keep in mind is you navigate this one button device with the timing of your button presses. A long 3 second tap will turn it on and off. The default when you turn it on is the white color. The white is not too cool, nor too warm. You can adjust the brightness and at the highest level it is plenty bright if you need to find something in the room. I don’t think it will adequately light a large dark room on its own. But you can read using this light if you are within a few feet of the lamp (for most people). . If you want to change to the color setting, then a quick one second tap after the device is turned on. At this point, you will be on the color cycling mode. if you do nothing, the device will cycle through various shades of green, blue, red, yellow, etc. For example, you will see a turquoise blue, a cornflower blue, a hot pink, a pale green, etc. If you want to select a particular color, wait until it cycles to the color you like, and use a one second tap to select. This will pause it on the color that was lit when you tapped the button. If you want to turn the device off, just press the button for three seconds. You will have to repeat the process every time you turn the device on, It isn’t very resource-intensive so I wouldn’t let that deter you unless you are picky and this is a dealbreaker. I’m sure more expensive units have more robust memories, settings, and remote controls with more than one button to navigate. Only two items come in the box, the lamp (which is roughly 7” tall, and 4” wide at the base) and the power cord (which is not infuriatingly short) so setup is easy.. There’s no charging or batteries required. So far I like it and plan to keep it. I have insomnia, and read about light therapy. headline: Excellent lamp for use with tall monitor configurations
review_text_raw: After purchasing an Omorepa lamp to place behind my Dell UltraSharp U5226KW monitor, I discovered it was not quite tall enough to position properly without shining directly into my eyes. I ended up returning it and trying the LitONES desk lamp instead because it was slightly taller and, importantly, allowed the lamp head to rotate independently. That flexibility turned out to be exactly what I needed. I initially bought one lamp just to test the setup and quickly realized I had finally found the right solution. The lamp is tall enough to work well behind the 26.5-inch-tall Dell monitor, and the adjustable head makes it easy to angle the light over the monitor and down onto the keyboard and work area without glare. The light itself provides a soft white glow and the brightness can be adjusted easily. Because the monitor is extremely wide, I eventually purchased a second lamp and positioned one on each side behind the display. The only minor inconvenience is that each lamp must be turned on separately since there is no remote control. But honestly, that is a very small complaint — I can lean over and switch them both on in about five seconds. A pretty good sign that I may be a little spoiled at this point. If you have a tall monitor and prefer placing lights behind it so the illumination projects over the display onto your workspace, these lights are definitely worth considering.

headline: Excellent monitor light at a great value!
review_text_raw: I'd been considering a monitor desk light for some time now, but I could not justify the price tag giong as high as $200 on the BenQ "original" that sorta started it off with these types of lights. This was a couple years ago now and clearly today there are many different versions of similar monitor lights on the market, the Quntis being among them, and which appears to be a fairly close copy of the BenQ light. I found this one on Amazon, priced around $40 for the non-remote (remote being rather superfluous in my opinion) version and did a little comparison research to see if this might be a good fit. There are many similar monitor lights out there, some cheaper and going as low as ~$25 and some obviously more expensive. I figured the Quntis was a good middle ground price-wise and took a shot to see if this would fit the bill. Indeed it does! Whether or not, or how close a copy to the BenQ the Quntis is I don't know for sure, as I've never seen the alternatives, but I can say this one is very well designed and well constructed, some plastic and also some metal in the construction and on close inspection the quality is definitely there. The mounting system is simple and functional and adapted perfectly to my HP Omen gaming monitor, which I would say has a somewhat non-standard profile shape and thickness, at least at the top where the light mounts. No problem, the mount is easily adjustable and rests perfectly and securely on my top monitor edge with full confidence that it's not going anywhere, or is any way unstable or wonky. The light controls on top of the light are easily accessible, operated by touch and the tactile "buttons" are shaped so they can be easily felt when operating the light. There are stepless controls for brightness and color temperature, as well as a sort of "auto" button that adjusts the brightness based on the ambient light in the room, which is nice. The lightbar throws a very nice pool of light on your keyboard and desk space in front of, and not directly ON, your monitor - right where you need it - without any glare, or being too harsh. Again, the quality, brightness and temperature of the light is easily adjustable to your liking. The monitor mounting system is sensible, simple, highly adjustable and highly functional. Lamp is powered by USB and in my case plugs right into a USB port on my monitor and totally invisible, hidden behind. Anyway, I guess I might have got a little carried away with this review, but tldr; the Quntis is an excellent monitor light and if this is something you've been looking at, I don't think you can go wrong with this one.

headline: Perfect... in most keys
review_text_raw: I got this lamp to use on a grand piano at church. The arm reaches across reasonably well from the side (though it doesn’t extend far enough to be fully centered over the music desk). The multiple color temperatures and brightness levels are very helpful for accommodating the preferences of various users, and all our pianists seem to like it. It works smoothly and perfectly... in most keys. BUT if you like to play in D-flat, beware! I just discovered that the resonance point of the casing appears to be a D-flat (138.591 Hz). The plastic started buzzing quietly when playing strong tonic chords in that key. This was, of course, horrifying. I assume the same disturbing outcome holds true when playing in C-sharp major, since the identical notes are used, but I only had sheet music in D-flat today. More testing would be needed to determine whether the issue extends to enharmonic keys, but this didn’t seem urgent to share here, since: • I didn’t want to go into too much detail that isn’t relevant to the average consumer (because we all hate that), and • Only psychos play in C-sharp major anyway. I realize this acoustic phenomenon may not affect all potential buyers of this lamp, but it seems like this particular harmonic bug could be mentioned somewhere in the description—if not in the product title itself—just so that members of the five-flats-loving community have some warning. Oh, also, the buzzing stopped as soon as I moved the arm slightly, so there’s that.

review_text_raw: Very sleek, modern looking lamp with a variety of lighting levels. It matches my black glass desktop very nicely, adding a sophisticated modern look. Contrary to what some reviewers said, I think it has a relatively small footprint on the desk, which is nice because I'd rather utilize the desktop space for working instead of a huge lamp. I've wiped it down here for the photos, but do realize that it is a dust/fingerprint/cat hair collector. Smudges show up, so if you're not willing to wipe it down every now and then you might be disappointed with it's overall aesthetic look. Pro tip: I keep a pack of Pledge multi-surface wipes ( Pledge Multi Surface Everyday Wipes Fresh Citrus, 25-Count (Pack of 4) ) in a drawer near my desk to wipe both it and the lamp down - takes a few seconds and looks as good as new. I mostly use this lamp at its lowest setting, as it provides a nice ambience to my work area. Each of the preset light levels can be brightened and dimmed. If I'm going to be doing real work, the light gets bright enough by itself to make reading from a textbook or paperwork comfortable and without strain. Usually one of the reading or middle settings is as bright as I'll go for reading actual pages from a book, and I only use the brightest settings if I'm struggling to see something small like jewelry or I'm fiddling with some component or part of my computer. It does get quite bright. I haven't used the timer function, but there is an automatic 60 minute timer included. Overall, it's a versatile little lamp. I got mine on sale at Christmas during a flash sale, for thirty something dollars, and I think it's well worth it. The listed price, however, is complete rubbish - total waste to pay full price regardless of how well it works, as it is simply made up of plastic and LED bulbs. Wait for a sale and you'll be happy with it. I've included photos of the lamp with various light levels and in different positions.

review_text_raw: This is an amazing light for the money. I would have been happy to spend two or three times as much for this light. It is super bright for a desktop lamp, which was my first need. My mate likes much dimmer lighting, and as it turns out, this light is infinitely dimmable - so it works for both of us. It has two color tones, one is daylight, the other is warm, what you might find from an old incandescent. Both have their uses. I use the daylight when drawing or reading, and the warm when I am on the PC. But I do have two issues. One is the unit is so light, it is easy to knock over. I used some of that thick, transparent, two sided tape to hold it down, and it seems to be doing a great job. The other issue is that the USB on the light side is non standard, it is Mini USB, which is smaller than USB C and not that popular any more. I have not had a mini USB for years. Plus the plug was slightly out of alignment and it was a task to get it plugged in. However for less than $7 this light is a bargain - ordered another for the headboard bookcase.

headline: Capable desk lamp that creates a lot of light for little space.
review_text_raw: I ordered this for better lighting for miniature painting as well as lighting up my desk area. It is a light lamp and has a heavy base, I incorrectly ordered this instead of the mounting one to gain desk space, which is a small foot print so not terrible. The simple minimalist look is sleek and contemporary meeting almost any desk or setup universally. The lamp feels sturdy and solid but you can tell the material is not all metal but some pressed plastic or much cheaper thin alloy material which is non-magnetic, maybe thin aluminum. The buttons are touch sensors not actual clicky buttons so that could put some folks off but non-issue for me. The lighting has color adjustments so you can light to you preference whether warm, cool, or cold and even has an automatic brightness and stepping feature built in. Honestly I though the brightness feature was a gimmick however using it as a back light in my office has improved my eye comfort from long periods at the computer for work. While the lamp is very easy to adjust and stays in place when moved the information presented makes it seem like the lamp head would rotate 180o which it does just not in the direction expected, meaning the lamp must always be parallel to the surface it is placed on no exceptions. I dinged it a star because of this as the image shown seems to be a bit misleading whether intentional or not. It uses a power adapter with barrel socket to the lamp so is not portable and does not charge, has no remote though there are auto stepping and brightness features you must manually activate the lamp.

headline: Love its flexibility
review_text_raw: This replaced a normal living room lamp used for many tasks, from reading to cleaning to eating while watching television. The reason I like this lamp so much is its flexibility. 1) the light is adjustable for warmth, 2) the lamp leds are in 3 sections controlled by a touch, so the larger middle section of leds can be turned on or off just by reaching up and touching an area near them, 3) the main body post and arms have joints so you can move parts of the body around to shine each of the 3 led grouping wherever you want in different directions = ceiling mood light: check, bright work lights: check, mixture: check. The lamp is also sturdilly made and has a heavy base so it doesn't tip over as you move the arms and body post. This is marketed as an architects light, but I think it is the best household lamp I've ever had.

headline: Great Smart Lamp
review_text_raw: I looked all over for an actual LAMP that worked with Alexa. Everything else seems to be a lamp with an included smart bulb. The issue begins if you can't really use the app nor can verbalize Alexa commands. Since my mom is able to do neither, she didn't really have a reliable way for the lamp to be turned off at night other than a lamp's physical switch. The issue there is that means there's no power to the smart bulb to have Alexa turn it back on. With this lamp, not only are we able to have her turn it off at night, but I can also have it timed to turn on in the morning with 'sunlight' level light to help her wake up, as well as have it timed to turn on a bit before sunset so her room is lit for when she wants to do things there in the evening. Overall, this is a great lamp, and I am fully happy with the purchase and after setting it up. I will note that there are other features I didn't mention, like different types of light (soft light for reading, 'daylight' for helping wake up, etc.) as well as multiple colors of light available.

product_title: AILBTON Bright LED Desk Lamp with Clamp,Eye Caring Architect Led Desk Lights with Adjustable Swing Arm for Office Home,Dimming and Tempering Led Table Light
headline: Best light I have found
review_text_raw: I have searched for and bought so many different kinds of lights for my sewing machine station. None of them have been satisfactory until this light. There are two important properties I need. Brightness and flexibility. First Brightness: I am 80 and need a lot of light where the needle is stitching. Yes there is a sewing machine light that turns on when the machine is running but even though it gets hot enough to burn skin, it is frustratingly dim. This desk light has 4 color temperature settings from warm to cold controlled by one button and 4 brightness levels controlled by another button so 16 different choices in all. These are regulated by lightly touched buttons on the lowest arm and the highest brightness out shines any other light I have tried. AND there is no flicker like many LEDs. So many lights have claimed amazing brightness only to be completely useless. Flexibility: A sewing machine is a very challenging lighting problem since the needle (where the work is happening) is hidden under the mass of the machine. The light has to be mounted on the right side of the machine so it doesn't block the movement of fabric. The right side of the machine is also solid and won't let any light pass through! Ideally it has to be located between the sewer and the machine so the sewer does not throw a shadow. This desk light offers EXTREME flexibility with 4 joints which all articulate in multiple ways but once the arms are set where I want the angles do not slip. The light might look very awkward in its placement on my table (and please excuse the mess!) but the outermost arm is throwing light exactly where I need it. The fabric can easily move underneath it. The other two arms are lighting up the overall table nicely. It is very well made and the clamp keeps the light steady even with such a long reach. I love this light.

headline: Recommended. Could be improved but good as is.
review_text_raw: TL;DR: Recommended but could be improved. I'm using this lamp in my living room to illuminate a bluetooth keyboard in the evening. The gooseneck keeps the lamp where I put it and feels like it's well made and will last. The lamp has 3 color settings - white, amber and off-white(?). I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.

I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.

headline: So far so good
review_text_raw: Bought one for my mom and one for my sister in law. Good thing I bought it for my sister in law because a couple months later the devastating wildfire in the Palisades of Los Angeles happened. So the entire LA county was full of smoke. Hopefully it helped but I'm not entirely sure how well it cleans the air because the amount of air that gets pushed out the top is not as forceful as my own air filters at home. My decades old Hunter air purifier has a ton more air flow it's almost like a high power fan. But I think it is able to move so much air because it doesn't have a pre-filter like all the new air purifiers use. It just uses replaceable HEPA filters and I know it works because I see all the dust it catches in the filter before I have to replace it. As for the Levoit it has a pre-filter which catches most of the dust and dirt but you never know how much actually gets through to the actual HEPA filter. I recommend the Levoit for smaller bedrooms, it's too small to do anything in a large room. At least it's fairly quiet on the lowest and middle setting.

review_text_raw: Edit to original review: it’s been several months at this point and I have two in our small farmhouse. They work amazing, best purchase we’ve made. So far: it’s perfect, surpassed all expectations, ALL. Backstory: we’re living in a house from the late 1800s, that has been dormant for about ten years until we moved in a couple years ago. We have five pets, four cats which are strictly indoor and use an automatic litter box (Popur S7 which does great for the smell, it can only do so much though) and one fat, lazy, stinky pitbull. The house is musky, it’s old, it had way too much mold in the detached basement when we moved in. And the pets? They stink bad too, this is coming from someone who is very particular about the house smelling good. The litter box is horrible, the dog is gross, the house is old. I went searching for an air purifier, I’ve been wanting the SHARK never change, but couldn’t break down and buy it for $300. Didn’t try it out, can’t say if it’s good or not. While I was looking at reviews, I found the shark had only 5,000 reviews on Amazon, and it was at 4.3 stars. Okay, that’s not too bad. But this Levoit one had over 100,000 reviews and 4.8 stars. That’s nuts in comparison. I done a lot of looking on Reddit and found that the shark wasn’t even mentioned in the majority of good quality reviews, so I disregarded it. This specific one happened to be in budget and also has amazing reviews. We received it last night and set it up this morning, yep this morning, in our cat’s litter box room which is also unfortunately our closet. That room is the worst room of the house in my opinion. It’s been running for about 6 hours and I already notice a huge impact. It’s easier to breath, the air doesn’t feel so heavy, and the litter box is nonexistent, even right after they use it. Hubby sprayed cologne on himself and not 20 seconds later I walked in and it was gone, already sucked away. I put a box fan on it to help circulation and have it on 3. I’m buying another. Maybe two more. If I remember I’ll come back and review again when it gets a little later in the month. We’re leaving for vacation next Monday, so I’m curious how it will hold up against the cats stagnant litter box, which usually stinks pretty bad when we get home after a week. TLDR; Amazing for pet odor, amazing for muskiness. Perfect and worth every penny.

Would definitely recommend!

headline: Levoit Air Purifier Home Allergies, Asthma
review_text_raw: I love the Levoit Air Purifier! It is very quiet all of the time, but if you use the night time sleep mode, you can just barely hear it at all. The fan has three speeds as well as the sleep mode. You can set the sleep mode for up to 8 hours, the best I remember. I do use sleep mode but not with the timer. You can turn off the display panel and I do that at night because I prefer a totally dark room. I run it all day on low and so far, a week out from getting it and setting it up, there are no signs of anything that needs to be cleaned from the outside as I've seen in other reviews. I don't have any pets, just nasty carpet. I call it nasty, because all carpet is nasty to me. I dislike carpet so much! I don't have a choice, though. I think the filter is supposed to last around six months, so we shall see. I bought a replacement filter when I bought the purifier and several filters for the humidifier, as well. It looks like I may have to change the Humidifier filter once a week as a week out, it is starting to turn brownish-yellow around the top of it. I don't smoke and do try to keep an extremely clean place, so not sure what the discoloration is. I'm the only one who has ever lived here. I use distilled water but also bought the demineralization kit and extra filters for the humidifier in case I run out of distilled water and have to use tap water. I clean the humidifier every day. It's not hard to do once you do it. I love the modern look and it is built very well. It's really not hard to use at all. I believe it is super effective combined with my also Levoit Humidifier. I have them on opposite sides of my small bedroom as I couldn't put my humidifier under the smoke alarm. My skin feels much softer and cleaner using the both of them. I could instantly tell a difference in how well I could breathe using the them. As before purchasing them, I couldn't breathe out of my nose at all. The humidity is brutal here. I have been able to get the humidity down to 58, which is something the local meteorologist said couldn't happen in these heatwave temperatures! Ha! I only use GENUINE LEVOIT filters and they're a bit more costly, but I prefer to use the real deal and have less problems/headaches. It can be a bit catchy to find them on Amazon and the generic ones keep popping up; however, I went straight to the Levoit store to get the genuine ones. Blessed to be able to somewhat better control my Asthma and all-season Allergies with the help of these two awesome products! Thank you, Amazon and Levoit! Sorry for combining reviews but I need to do a copy and paste for the humidifier as it will save me time doing it this way.

headline: Amazing!
review_text_raw: I previously owned one purifier, an AIRROMI purifier. I kept it near the litter box because phew my cats can be stinky. Unfortunately, one of my cats recently started showing symptoms of asthma. And hearing those attacks he has is honestly extremely scary, knowing I cannot offer him direct relief. So I made the decision to get a second purifier, a bigger one this time. But not just one, I got THREE! Maybe a little over kill but I want to ensure my cat is OKAY! I have had them for about a month and there has been ZERO asthma attacks from my cat. So it is fair to say that all the bad allergens in the air have been going straight to the filter. My boyfriend works in HVAC and he said the HEPA filter combined with the activated charcoal works great for catching particles and allergens. I have yet to open it up to see the damage; the purifier has an alert that will show up on the control panel, letting you know when it is time to change the filter. I will come back and update with pictures once I change the filter on at least one of the purifiers. There is about 3 modes on the purifier, Automatic, Speed 1, 2, 3 and Pet mode. Automatic is hardly detectable in terms of noise. Pet mode and the highest mode are very loud though. I don’t mind the white noise, so I could sleep with it no problem, others might have a problem. As for looks, I think she is really pretty! I absolutely love the reader on the front that determines the air quality, all of ours sit at a range of either 5-7. I very interestingly found that my purifier in my room almost hit 400 after a hot shower, and it did not go down, the numbers fluctuated between 150-350. I unplugged it and then it read 005 again...not sure what that was about, but it only happened once, so I did not think much of it.

That said, I went on the search for an air purifier and ended up pulling the trigger on this one and can finally report on well it works. Even though at first my mom wasn’t happy that I spent money and bought this for her, after I set it up, she allowed me to leave it running on high if it meant there could be a chance that it might make her air quality suitable for my siblings start visiting again. product_title: Levoit Air Purifier for Home Pets Bedroom Dorm Room, Smart & Voice Control
headline: Affordable and effective for dust and allergens
review_text_raw: We moved into an incredibly dusty townhouse, I have terrible allergies, and we discovered our neighbors are chain smokers. We now have 3 Levoit air purifiers in our home: Vital 100 (non-smart version), Core Mini and Vital 200S. I initially bought the Vital 100 and put it in our bedroom because I have terrible allergies. It collected a ton of dust and helped a lot with the allergies. I thought I didn't need the smart version but in hindsight the availability of specialty filters and the remote control would be very helpful. It's relatively quiet although on high it's too noisy for me to sleep with. I absolutely love that you can turn the all the control lights off. We tried using this for the cigarette smell but it wasn't very effective except when the smell was very light. It did completely abolish cooking smells though. If I could go back in time I would have ordered the 100S instead but this one works fine. The smoke smell from the neighbors comes into our house through the laundry room which is a very small room. I bought the Core Mini to try to combat it. The Core Mini doesn't really do much to get rid of smells and was definitely overwhelmed by the smoke so now we move it around the house now when the pollen level is high. It works ok for dust and allergens but the range isn't great; you need to be right next to it to notice a difference. On low and medium speed it's barely audible and high is relatively quiet but overall the fan isn't very powerful. The lights on this one automatically turn off after a few seconds making it bedroom friendly. If I could do it again, I would have skipped this one and bought one of the larger ones sooner. Lastly, in an attempt to mitigate the smoke coming from next door, we got the big boi Vital 200S with the add on smoke specialty filter. So far it isn't able to remove the smell while they're smoking but it does cut down the severity and will clear it eventually provided the source stops for long enough. It's amazingly quiet on the lower speeds. It's pretty loud on the higher speeds but the fan moves a ton of air around. I'm disappointed that the auto mode doesn't detect the smoke smell but I can use the app to turn it to high speed as soon as I smell it. You don't have to use the app but it's really easy to set up and connect. The app allows you to set schedules which is really handy and as I touched on earlier, it works as a remote control. As with the others, you're able to turn the lights off completely so it's good for bedrooms. We've only had this running a few days but I'm pretty impressed with what it can do.

headline: Great small sized air purifier that does some heavy lifting
review_text_raw: I got this air purifier for my bedroom as my sleep can be disturbed by air quality pretty easily. I was highly skeptical of this product at first as the price point to me indicated that it might be cheap in terms of quality of the product but so far it has been pretty impressive. On even the lowest setting, it has substantially improved the air quality not just in the bedroom but in the adjoining room so we're looking at space of about 200-300 square feet or so. I would say I can breathe easier at night with it and my comfort level while sleeping has increased a bit. The air after it's been running for a bit smells and just seems fresher and I am considering getting a second one to see if it can handle a much larger area. Noise is pretty low on it's lowest "normal" setting and the night mode feature drops the noise to almost silent, but not quite. At it's lowest setting, there is an odd whine, for lack of better words that can just barely be heard. This whine was an annoyance at first but you get used to and can ignore it. It still works well on the lowest setting to keep the room fresh so it's a good deal. Setup was easy as can physically, however I cannot as yet speak to the application setup as I haven't gotten to that. I treat air purifiers as non-smart devices but I do plan to at least try to integrate it with Home Assistant and if that doesn't work I may try integration with Amazon Alexa. I'll update the review when that happens. Durability of the purifier long term is unknown, though the filters do seem very easy to replace and their price point does make them economical enough to justify getting a filter instead of replacing the entire air purifier. Summary: Good, powerful little air purifier that can sit on a dresser or nightstand, relatively quiet with some caveats. Long term durability is unknown but still was a good buy overall.

headline: Skeptical About Used? This Changed My Mind
review_text_raw: I chose the Amazon box option mainly so I could check whether the item shipped safely and arrived without damage to the outer packaging. The Amazon box itself arrived in good condition, but the Core 200S-P’s box was damaged, likely because it had not been handled carefully during a previous shipment. Since I bought it in Used – Acceptable condition, I inspected the purifier carefully. I found no issues with the unit itself. It came with what appears to be a new filter, had no strange smell, and works perfectly, just like my other Core 300S-P, which I recently bought new. I also bought a second unit in Used – Good condition. The only thing I noticed was a black scuff mark on the bottom of the purifier, as shown in the pictures, but it does not look like actual damage. The box for that one also appeared to have been damaged during a previous shipment. From my experience buying used items on Amazon, that seems fairly common, and it is probably one reason the price is lower when the manufacturer’s box is damaged. I ran it for an hour on level 3, the highest fan speed and it seems to be working perfectly. Afterward, the room smelled cleaner and felt easier to breathe in. I also found no visual issues. After comparing it side by side with the Core 300S-P, I honestly think the Core 200S-P is a better fit for bedrooms, while the Core 300S-P is better suited for larger rooms. headline: 1000% RECOMMEND!
review_text_raw: I bought this purifier because I really wanted one that I could turn on from my phone while laying in bed, since I am completely blind in the dark due to my vision impairment, and I don't necessarily have anywhere to place this type of electronic near my bed that was the major deal breaker for me. This air purifier is about the size of a PS5, but a little more convenient due to the cylinidrical shape of it. The app set up is easy and it allows you to auto order a new filter through the app via a scheduled set up. I have mine set up for every 6 months and you can tell the difference between the 2 filters after those 6 months.... the app also will tell you the life on your filter left and will tell you the air quality/ pollen count outside of your home. All the modes do exactly as they say and the sleep mode is ultra quiet which is nice. I've been using this air purifier for almost 2 years now and it is still working great. You can immidetly tell when you take it out of the box that it is a good high quality purifier and not a purifier where they say its high quality and after a week it stops working... My last purifier was lmof a lower quality and stopped working with-in a year, but also I paid $50 for that one and I didn't have a dog at that time. It is so nice to have a higher quality purifier that works exactly as it says on the ads. The app also includes other Levoit electronics you can add to your account so you have all your Lwvoit products in one spot on your phone which I think is so mice and easy. The app is also really easy to use and to set up everything on, it looks and feels very professional and easy which I really enjoy. I love opening up my app and seeing all my Levoit electronics in one spot, ready to turn on or off, or to change any mode it's on to something different. You can aslo set up a schedule of when you would like your devices to turn on and off and what mode to use whenbit does. The purifier has been so helpful with my allergies as it takes about 10 minutes for my severe allergy symptoms to begin subsiding a good amount after coming inside from walking the dog. To some 10 minutes may sound like a long time, but to someone with really really REALLY awful allergies 10 minutes is well worth the wait... Also, the air suction is powerful enough where I have to wipe I'm purifier down with a clean and dry paper towel to get some dog hair off of the sides where the air flows into the machine. It's also kept the infamous "dog smell" from settling in my room. I highly recommend this purifier it's great and if/when this one goes, I will definitly be purchasing another Levoit brand...

review_text_raw: This was my first time ever using an air purifier, so I was pretty skeptical even after reading all the good reviews. The first few days were honestly a little discouraging because my bedroom still smelled kind of funky. I live in an older house, and getting certain smells out of the rooms has been a big priority while I finish setting everything up. But after about a week, the difference became really noticeable. Now it’s actually refreshing to walk into my room. I’m really glad I didn’t give up on it early. I also share my bedroom with a Husky, and there’s no dog smell anymore — which is huge. The fan is pretty quiet, and even when I turn it up, the sound is kind of soothing. It actually reminds me of the ocean waves from my trip to Ormond, FL, which is a nice little bonus. The filters are easy to insert and remove (I haven’t had to replace mine yet, but I tested it out just to see), and the whole unit feels simple and user‐friendly. Overall, very happy with this purifier. It took a little time, but it absolutely did its job.

headline: Makes a noticeable difference!
review_text_raw: When my elderly cat (18 this summer! Cat tax included in review) was diagnosed with asthma, it meant that all three of us who live in my apartment (my husband and I plus cat) all have some sort of allergy or respiratory issues from different things. I've always had allergies to things like dust and pollen, and my husband had recently developed a cough and post nasal drip that the doctor could find no particular cause of. I happened to be browsing on Prime Day after looking into air purifiers and got this one for a very affordable 60 bucks. The reviews said it worked great just out of the package and setup was easy, and they were right. No assembly, nothing to fuss with. Just remove the plastic from the filter, pop it back in and plug it in. The difference was noticeable very quickly. Husband has basically stopped coughing and his post nasal drip has reduced significantly. I also noticed he isn't snoring anywhere near as loudly as he was before. My own allergy symptoms have alleviated; my sinuses used to feel stuffy which made it harder to fall asleep, but that's basically solved. My own post nasal drip has also noticeably improved. Even my cat's asthma noises have improved. I'm sort of shocked to encounter a product that actually noticeably solves a problem. Shortly after buying it, I had a small fire in my oven. Everything was okay, but the smoke was obviously a problem. I decided to put the air purifier on the counter to see what the number went up to- 130! But about an hour later, the number on the panel read about 10 or 12, and the normal range for my apartment is between 5-17. It has a sleep setting, but we keep it on 1 during the night because it's so quiet. I like to keep it on 2 during the day because it's still just light background humming. One thing I thought was nice is that there's a QR code on the side of it to link you to the correct filters to buy when you need to replace them. However, out of all the things that could actually use an app, it doesn't have one. It could be nice to have a really simple one that records the PM number so you could have an idea of the air quality patterns in your home. At the same time, it's refreshing that it doesn't have one lol My apartment is 1,300 square feet so technically this little guy should be making some difference on the whole thing, but it might be better to have it in a more central location for that; I like it in the bedroom though, since it's made such a difference in our symptoms that were impacting our sleep, and my cat mostly stays in the bedroom so it just makes sense for us. 10/10, really happy with it!

review_text_raw: We got this air purifier after our daughter was diagnosed with dog allergies. Overall we have been very impressed with its cleaning ability, different mode settings and features, quietness, and would say its fairly inexpensive for all that. We just ordered the 200S to put in the main living area.

headline: Best Bang For Your Buck
review_text_raw: I've been looking for a new air purifier for almost a year now, doing research here and there trying to find a unit that meets all the requirments I'm looking for. I need a unit that's for a larger room, has an auto feature, has good priced replacement filters, and looks good to match my home decor. A recent 80,000 acre fire hastened my research due to the thick blanket of smoke that blanket the area (and still is) every morning. With all things considered, the Winix 5500-2 met all my requiements. The unit arrived promptly and unpackaging was an ease. I literally had it set up ans running in about 5 minutes. The body is a hard, matte black plastic that feels sturdy and durable. The front panel is easy to remove, and secures to the unit via a clever magnetic clasp that is secure, yet simple to remove to access your prefilter for bi weekly cleaning and hepa/carbon filter replacement. There are 3 filters in total, and they fit snugly inside the filter chamber, amd ate secured in with the prefilter that snaps firmly into place. The control panel at the top is intuituve and user friendly. The buttons are clearly marked and visual ques explain what each button does taking out any guesswork as to what they do. A stylish indicator light bar runs along the bottom of the control panel indicating the level of air cleanliness with a 3 color scheme...green for clean, orange for okay, and red for bad. You can manually run the machine on 4 fan settings, or choose auto mode and let the machine choose the settings based on the data colected from the sensor. This means hands off operation. There's a night mode that will set the fan to its lowest setting to cut down on noise, and also dim all lights on the panel. This night mode will set automatically if you have the auto mode set on the unit, a light sensor will detect (or not detect) any light in the room and go into night mode. A filter change indicator light also is on the control panel. According to what i've researched, the hepa filter should last approx 1 year. It also comes with a remote control with a battery preinstalled. I dont plan on using it, but if that's your thing, it's there. This is the quietest air purifier I've ever owned. product_title: WINIX 5510 Air Purifier (New Generation of 5500-2 with App Support) for Home Large Room Up to 1881 Ft2 in 1 Hr, True HEPA, High Deodorization Carbon Filter and Auto Mode, Captures Pet Allergies, Smoke
headline: Super clean air purifier with unique features
review_text_raw: A really good air purifier with some unique features. In terms of noise, it is among the quietest at about 60 DB. Obviously there’s more noise the faster the fan spins, but in automatic mode, it senses the amount of gluten in the air and adjust the speed automatically which means most of the time it will be running at low speed unless there’s a lot of dust in the air. You can download an android or iOS app to control the fan speed and to see how much dust it is seeing in the air. You can also set it up for Alexa or Google Home to be able to control it through those devices. One need feature is being able to ask Alexa for a reading of air quality from the device. You can also enable an automatic sleep mode, which basically keeps the device on auto fan mode where it senses the amount of dust in the air during daylight, but when the device notices that the room is dark at night, it will put the fan speed to its slowest mode to ensure that there’s minimal noise during nighttime hours. Once the room is lit again and it is daylight the device will automatically switch to auto mode and if necessary, increase the fan speed to pull in more air if it detects an increased amount of dust. These are the main features of the device, but the other thing that I liked about it compared to similar models from other brands is that they say the standard filters it comes with should last 12 months where many other brands recommend changing filters after three months. This is probably because the HEPA filter that this device comes with is thicker at about 1 inch compared to what I have on other air purifiers filters that are generally 1/2 inch or less thick. I have not yet replaced my filters, but with an estimate of one year it should not be a substantial yearly cost because filter filters run around $20. And I say filters because as you can see in the images for the product, there are actually two separate filters that work together one is a white HEPA filter to filter out particles. The other one is a black carbon filter, which filter filters out smell smells. And holding both of those filters in place is a screen which is washable that is meant to capture, larger dust particles or pet hair before they hit the main filter filters. Overall, very satisfied with this device and the only thing I can’t really comment on is how long it will last as I’ve only recently started using it.

I’m so happy with it, I bought a second WINIX 5530 of the same color so that I’ll keep that one in the living room along with the small air purifier. I also bought replacement filters to have at hand when I need to change them out.

headline: Fantastic Machine, Automatic, Very Quiet, Great looking
review_text_raw: ** 3-week update ** After a few weeks a clicking noise developed in the fan when running on the sleep (lowest) speed. Looking at the fan it appears there maybe an imbalance that over the weeks developed into a motor shaft tapping. Make sure to inspect your unit for a balanced fan. I just issued a replacement on the 5500-2 so we'll see what happens. ** Original ** I spent weeks comparing units on Amazon and elsewhere. I didn't want to spent > 200 on an overbuilt fan, or be stuck buying overpriced filters. I ended up buying the Winix 5500-2 and Renpho AP002 and first impressions with the two units are that they both appear well built, quiet, and have the automatic mode I really wanted. TL;DR; Winix 5300-2 - Quieter w/Smarter hands off Automatic technology & Ionizer - Set and Forget! Winix 5500-2 - Identical in Black w/Remote & washable carbon filter Renpho AP001 - Incredible unit, Amazing filters, Low cost ownership! Renpho AP002 - Almost identical, slightly more air volume FILTERS The Renpho filter has a price and feature advantage over the Winix. Both units have H13 Hepa filters, both have the honeycomb active carbon filters (for capturing VOC), and both have a washable pre-filters for catching large particles. The Renpho however has 2 bonus layers, a microbial coating on the Hepa filter, and an additional charcoal filter sitting before the carbon filter to collect larger particles. The Winix does claim the active carbon filter is washable - Renpho does not make this claim, however both appear similar so it maybe purely marketing. The Renpho filter is shorter and fatter - if you ran the numbers they both likely have similar surface area, thought the Winix is CADR rated for 360 sqr/ft while the Renpho is 330 sqr/ft. They are close. Renpho OEM filters sell for $25 for a full replacement. Winix OEM filters sell for $50 for a full replacement. Renpo claims the filter should be changed every 6 months, Winix claims every 12. I assume this is reflected in their price strategy, however since the filters are so similar, I doubt both claims can be true - and this all depends on how dirty your air is! So cost of ownership is likely less with the Renpho. AIR IONIZATION The Winix comes with an Ionizer (called Plasmawave) and Renpho does NOT. The Ionizer charges any particles passing through the unit so they are heavier and will float to the ground and out of air. If you're concerned about Ozone gasses, then this is a feature you can disable and is not a feature on the Renpho. SOUND This is a real issue for me - I am sensitive to sound and like the home quiet at night. Deciding on a unit for my children makes this even more important, and I don't want to force them into a white machine for air filtration. In Sleep mode the Winix is significantly more quiet at (advertised) 26dB where the Renpho is at 35dB. With the Winix 10ft from the bed I can just barely hear it. The Renpho is noticable but not "loud". The Winix appears to have 5 speed modes, Sleep, Low, Med, High, and Turbo. The Renpho has just 3 modes, Low, Med, High, with Sleep mode being the Low mode with lights off. Here's the rub however - outside of Sleep mode, the Winix sounds "louder" having a higher pitched whine while the Renpho is more of a hum. If I was going to just set this on High in a corner and forget it, then Renpho is the winner. For a quiet bedroom the Winix appears the winner. AUTOMATIC MODE This was a huge feature for me and the Winix is a much "smarter" unit. Both units have a similar Automatic feature, sensing the air, bringing the fan speed up or down according to the readings. Both have light(s) indicating the current air quality reading. The Winix however had a light sensor that, when the unit is in Automatic mode, will place the unit in Sleep mode when the lights go out (for more than 1 min). In the morning the unit goes back into Automatic mode. This is huge if you appreciate how quiet the unit is. You can set the Winix to Automatic mode and not touch it until your next filter cleaning. If you wish to use the Sleep mode on the Renpho you will need to push the Speed button to cycle through the speed options back to Sleep - and then again in the morning cycle back to Auto. In reality you maybe better covering the lights with black tape and leaving it in Auto or just leave it in Sleep mode permanently. REMOTE Winix has one, Renpho not - for my needs this is a non-issue. CHILD LOCK Renpho has one, Winix does not - this is a great feature if young kids are around! APPEARANCE Personally I think the Winix looks clean, modern, and the black color blends well into a corner near furniture. The Renpho AP002 like the Renpho AP001 have their signature funky look which is fine but not as refined. It's an air purifier, so who cares, but it is also a visible piece of equipment in your home. For us the Winix seems more appropriate for a bedroom, the Renpho for a living room. Winix higher cost of ownership justified by the features and sound levels, Renpho for lower ownership cost. If the Renpho unit was QUIETER (ahem - hint hint Renpho) then I would just go that route - save on upfront and ownership cost. SIMILAR MODELS The Winix 5300-2 and Winix 5500-2 are the exact same physical unit in different colors with different filters. The 5300 is gray, the 5500 is black. Only the 5500 has a remote. The 5500 has their "advanced" AOC Washable Active Carbon filter, while the 5300 has a disposable active carbon. The 5300 Hepa filter is slightly thicker (good) and you get 4 disposable filters with each replacement. If you buy the 5500 and don't like the washable filter it comes with you can buy the 5300 replacement pack and use them instead. For $23 more we went with the Winix 5500-2 to test the AOC filter, and for the black aesthetic. Currently you can get the 5300-2 for $129 (Amazon) and when I purchased the Winix 5500-2 for $152 (now listed at $159 on Amazon). The Renpho AP001 (often found as RP-AP001 or AP-001) and Renpho AP002 are very similar products, both using the exact same filters, having different aesthetic designs, and with the AP002 having more airflow (for supposedly the same sound levels) and covering 30 sqr/ft more space. The AP001 has a dedicated Sleep button while the AP002 Sleep mode is the first option on the Speed cycle button - more daily button work for you. Currently the AP001 sells for $99 (Renpho direct) while the AP002 for $137 (Amazon). I bought the AP002 thinking the newer model maybe more quiet than advertised. If we get another Renpho it will be the AP001 for $37 bucks less.

headline: auto setting runs fan according to air quality
review_text_raw: The auto setting of this air purifier is good: it detects when the air is dirtier, indicates that with an orange or red light, and increases the fan speed accordingly. This happens when I run the filter in my kitchen and it reacts to the smoke from the stove or oven, even when it is not enough to see with your eyes. Sometimes the light changes to orange or red in the bedroom right after someone coughs or sneezes, so I think that indicates that it is probably cleaning the air of infectious particles breathed out by someone who is ill. Sometimes it indicates dirtier air and it is not obvious to me what it detected, but I trust it since it does detect things I know about like cooking smoke and sneezes. Most of the time it runs on the lowest and quietest setting (which is reasonably quiet), but runs higher when needed. It also detects the light in the room, so if it is dark at night, it runs an even quieter mode. My sister had bought one of these air purifiers for our elderly parents in California. I don't remember whether it was smoke from wildfires or Covid that first motivated my sister to buy the air purifier, but it has been good for both of those health hazards. So when I visited them, I had seen how the auto-detection worked and when I had vacuumed out the filter for them, so I could see that cleaning and changing the filters was easy. I first bought a unit for myself in 2023 when smoke from wildfires in Canada blew down and made the air in Chicago hazy and orangish and beaches were closed because the air quality index was over 100 and was bad enough that people were told to stay inside. Our HVAC system has 4" MERV 13 filters, but I felt that smoke was still getting in whenever we opened our doors and the HVAC filters were probably not filtering enough to completely clean the air. I also have pretty bad seasonable allergies, so this unit is good for cleaning the pollen out of the air in my house. Just a couple months after I bought the unit for my own house, I sent another unit to my adult child in DC when the smoke from Canada blew into DC. They liked it so much that this year they bought one for their workplace office after they had to start working part-time in-the-office rather than fully remotely as they had done when they were hired during the height of the pandemic. The unit is a bit heavy at 17 lbs. So I got tired of taking it up and down the stairs from my bedroom to the dining room or kitchen and I bought this second unit for our household. It has a different style of activated charcoal filter that has gravel-sized pieces of charcoal in a plastic cage instead of the black fiber filter that the previous units used. The new charcoal filter is supposed to last longer than the fiber filter so I think it is better. I found that generic filer replacements of the HEPA filter and the charcoal filters fit my first unit just fine. I haven't looked for replacements for the newer type of charcoal filter yet.

review_text_raw: One of those products that you set and forget until it's time to change the filter and you realize how much it was working the whole time. A couple times my apartment's power flickered from a storm, I didn't think to check if the air purifier was still on but in a day or two I could smell the difference. Even when the air intake part gets blocked by cat hair, there's a noticeable difference in smell of my small bathroom where I keep the litter box, let alone when the filter needs changed. The filter light comes on to let you know when it's time, but it doesn't seem to notify you too early to get you to buy more; the filter is bright blue and you can tell exactly when it's really fully clogged vs the one not yet due for a switch out. The noise level is okay for me; the low and medium speed settings are quiet but smell-wise I only really notice a difference if it's left on high. But even that is still quieter than, say, a window fan. Deducting a star because I don't think the low and medium settings do much but also because the light is too bright. If you turn on the "night light" in the middle of the night, the blue light is definitely too much. But even if you turn it off, the little light bulb button is still too bright and casts a blue glow in my bedroom that I actively try to reduce with blackout curtains in the city. I don't regret buying it at all, especially for my cat's litter box. Just some stuff to consider if you're sensitive.

review_text_raw: We purchased one of these on sale in the hope it would help moderate the severity of pollen season in upstate NY and the dander generated by two large labradors. Twist the top a quarter turn and place to one side. Lift out the filter, remove the bag, lower the filter back in using the two tabs provided on it for that purpose, lift the lid back on and quarter twist to close. It takes 2 mins. Then its' plug-in, turn on and choose ""Auto" or a fan speed using the touch sensitive panel on top. You can control it from your iphone if you're into that but it certainly isn't necessary. The first thing we noticed is how quiet it is. Effectively soundless in sleep mode and at fan speed 1. Barely noticeable at fan speed 2, unless you're right next to it, noticeable at fan speed 3 when you are in the same room as it but not obnoxious. Noticeably louder at fan speed 4 which should be considered a 'Turbo" mode. Then we noticed the impact of running it - vastly reduced swelling of the eyes and sinuses of those suffering from hay fever and a significant reduction in the doggy smell of our labradors. On top of that, we have 2 indoor cats and an outdoor cat that periodically comes in, so we got to deal with pet dander x3. I was debating on getting an AirDoctor but was wanting something a little more affordable and was just as good. After hours of research, I decided on the Levoit Core 600S-P. Installation was rather easy and quick. I like that it is also a smart purifier as in it has its own app that you can manage wirelessly over a wifi or cellular connection (Purifier needs to be connected to your network). Once I turned it on, I noticed that it quickly scans the area for air quality. My air quality was so bad, I was honestly disappointed that I didnt invest in a air purifier sooner. Breathing was way easier and after just 24 hours, allergy symptoms were beginning to subside. My wife was suffering from the worst sinus congestion and pressure due to the allergies and that has now completely gone away after 2 days. What I also like about this Levoit is the air flow. Just at a lower settings I can literally feel air circulation at 20 ft away from my living room. The max fan setting pulls in air fast, which is nice if needing to filter your air quickly. The highest setting is loud, but that doesnt really bother me. Let that thing work haha. The lowest setting is super quiet, so its great for sleeping as well. Its been several days of me having this product and it truly is one of the best investments I have made. If you suffer from allergies and have multiple pets, the Levoit wont let you down. Our overall quality of life in our home has greatly improved now that we are breathing cleaner air. Definite recommend.

headline: Perfect for our asthmatic household. *Updated
review_text_raw: My toddler and I both have severe allergies and asthma. To the point that over the past month we have both been having major issues with the pollen and smog in the air, even with being home most of the time! I ordered this one after doing A LOT of research, and I decided this was the best for the money. With a true HEPA filter that you replace once a year (opposed to once a month) it would save money in the long run. I chose this one for the den in our house and over the coming weeks we will be getting smaller ones for the bed rooms. This review for right now is 24 hours in to having it on in the house, and later I will come back and add to it. Set up was easy straight out of the box, and I put it out of traffic areas in the house. I was worried with where I put it there would be trouble for good air circulation, but it is doing great! In fact with it on high I noticed a tag on the other side of the room (directly across) was moving on one of the toys yesterday as I was cleaning. Then I cooked fish last night (our den has an open doorway to the kitchen), and I couldnt even smell it cooking!! I decided to test it this morning, and sat on the couch painting my nails. Even using nail polish remover I couldnt smell it!!! (which astounds me b/c I hate doing my nails simple b/c of the toxic fumes!!) As far as noise, its not that bad. On high, with the tv and with kids running around it is a little white noise and thats it. I sleep with the bed room doors open, and having a tower computer on in the den annoyed me, however on medium I couldn't even hear it in the den! It also moves a lot of air b/c even when the ac isnt blowing air, it feels like it is b/c of this tower! I am super excited at the thought of having better air quality in the house so we dont have as many issues, and I know it will take probably a good month for me to be able to judge that (and trust me I keep up with our flair ups b/c my son sees a specialist so I can tell you if it will make a difference or not). I also liked the UV light, since we have kids over to play all the time it makes perfect sense to have it to. Also anyone that has lung issues, make sure to avoid any purifier that has the ion part (where you turn it on for a fresh smell) it actually causes lung problems (if you have underlying problems). Oh and check out the reviews on walmart . com for this purifier, it has hundreds of reviews and most are five star (which is one of the reasons I went with this model even though not everyone loved it on here). Check back in August and I will add an update =) ****************************UPDATE****************************** 12/2/2012 Hi ALL! Sorry took me so long to come back and update =) Fortunately if you see below I did give a heads up three weeks in we still loved it. This unit is holding up well, and really does a good job! Since buying it (I guess going on six months ago now --WOW THAT WENT FAST!!) it helped with our asthma and allergies. Within the first month I stopped waking up with a stuffy nose, and it was taking particles out of the air so I wasn't seeing as much dust. I still would love to have them in each room, but that is on the back burner. Make sure you have enough for the sq footage of your room. We have since moved to a larger place, that has more sq footage in the den, and also two open doorways leading to other rooms. As such, this unit is doing really well for how much air it has availability to; when I should honestly probably should have one more in here. It isn't too loud, and I love the uv light. Within the first month of us having it we were exposed to someone (a visitor) that wound up having pneumonia. With the fact we have a higher risk of catching lung illnesses, I was really nervous. I think a big contributor to not catching it is because we had this unit running on high with the uv light. I highly recommend this unit, and I hope it helps! =) ***********************************Update 6/26/13 We just about hit the year mark! Still working great and going strong! Make sure you wipe down (inside and out) once a month (as the book says). Still going strong, and working well! =) Buy this one, and you wont regret it! ***********************************Update 11/13/13 Unit is still working great! We added a second one earlier this year, and pleased with both! =) ***********************************Update 06/29/14 Both units are still going strong with no issues. Still helping with our asthma and allergies.

headline: Good value, works good and an added bonus (?) a brilliant blue nightlight
review_text_raw: So far, so good. I never thought I would buy an air purifier, but my seasonal allergies now require it. This unit running in a 20x15 foot room. It is not quite as quiet as I would have liked, but it is no louder than my warm mist humidifier. This is the only air purifier in the house so it really is doing "extra" duty because if I shut the room door, the room gets too cold. Other than the first day and when I get home from work, this unit is running on the lowest of 3 settings. Here is what I like and dislike about this air purifier: Likes: Does a really good job of removing the dust and pollens that I am allergic to When using the UV, it seems to take out the molds that I am allergic to (keep in mind this is not measured by anything other than my nose) The unit is stable even on carpet with a medium carpet pad. Doesn't take up a lot of space. Easy to get at the filters (haven't tried to get to the UV light) Everything is replaceable so I should be able to keep this for a good long time. Time to "sense" a noticeable difference in the 20x15' room - about 15 min I even notice a slight difference in other rooms of the house, this is much more than I expected Dislikes: The obnoxious blue light when the UV is on. I do understand and appreciate the safety factor that the light provides, however, I would be happy with a dot indicator next to the power switch. Settings 2 and 3 are likely to be too loud for most people to sleep with. Luckily, they really are not likely to be needed during sleeping hours. Overall, I like this unit and would consider getting another one for the rest of my house if my allergies get worse. I would recommend that you run the unit on high only when you are not in the room or are not trying to sleep. Yesterday I experimented with turning the unit off when I left for work and turned it on when I came home. Using the 1 setting, the air was better in an hour (that's when I went in the room). The blue UV indicator light does make a good nightlight if you like them. I will also add that where I live, we are still getting snow on a regular basis so my windows are not open and are covered with plastic to keep down the cold drafts. Pollens are not really in the air, but dust from road sand/salt is bad. My furnace is Gerry-rigged into the air ducts so the furnace filter is nearly useless. (I am working on a fix for that). My house was built in 1892 so I cannot complain too much. I would recommend this air purifier. It provides better than expected results and is a good value for the money. I will update this review as time goes on.
