headline: Large stainless steel pot with handles is awesome!
review_text_raw: My previous insta pot was a 6qt non-stick pot. I really enjoyed that pot. But many times I wished it was a little bigger. And getting the pot out of the unit was a bit dicy, you have to use pot holders for the heat and it could slip out of your hands. However I also became concerned about the non-stick coating on the pot. I had put a couple of scratches on the bottom so I was concerned about the coating. Enter this new pot. Very nice 8 qt size. I actually thought 8 qt might be too big but on my first use I almost filled it up, so it's not too big. The stainless steal pot is awesome and the handles make it very easy to lift out(without pot holders) and I dont feel like it's going to slip out of my hands. First use was a stew and it came out great. I did wash it in the dishwasher before use. I found the silicon seal to be hard to put back onto the lid, I had to use a little water as a 'lubricant' to get it to slip back into place. There are LOTS of options on this thing.....it took me a couple minutes just to pick one for the stew and I finally picked the 'slow cook' option which took six hours....but it was worth the wait....the meat was very tender and the potatoes and carrots were just right, not too soft and not too hard......by the way, if you shop Walmart, the organic carrots taste way better than the regular carrots......I just buy a bag of organic petite and dump them in....this time I also added a bag of frozen mushrooms and that was great.....too many times I buy fresh mushrooms and forget to use them within a day or two and have to chuck them. 10/17/25 update Still loving this pot....the only issue I have is the silicone pressure ring can be difficult to put back in place. To show how large it is, just now I put in a whole 3 lb bag of potatoes, a whole chopped up celery bunch, a large onion, 8 oz of fresh mushrooms, bag of carrots, 64oz of chicken stock and about 2 lbs of chicken......I put it on an option for 6 hours of 'slow cook'......the slow cook option is pretty cool.....

headline: Worth the extra money over the less expensive Instant Pots
review_text_raw: My first IP started having some display issues after about 5 years, so I decided to replace it since I use it just about every weekend. The replacement arrived with a dent in the side, and I worked with Amazon and received a partial refund, but it never seemed to cook well. I was constantly getting a burn notice, and I was never comfortable with the dented outer casing, so I decided to replace it again after about 1 year. I decided to not buy a less expensive model this time and spent the extra money on the Instant Pot Pro. So glad I did! The differences are very noticeable and appreciated. The slots to hold the lids are positioned at 10 and 2, which makes it much easier to work with than on the lower cost models where it is at 9 and 3. The display is much more informative, and I really love having more control over the heat when sauteing. The handles on the inner pot are a great addition. The inner pot stays level and doesn’t move around when you’re stirring so it keeps the heat even while sauteing. Also, it is easier to take in and out of the outer shell. Don’t get me wrong, the lower cost models like the DUO or the Rio are good machines. The Instant Pot Pro is just a much better device. I cooked with it last night for the first time and couldn’t believe it was possible to be MORE impressed with the Instant Pot. If you’re shopping for one and not sure which one to choose, the lower cost models are good, but the Pro is significantly better imo.

product_title: Instant Pot Pro 8 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black
headline: Why Don't You Have One Already?!
review_text_raw: I upgraded from Instapot Duo to the Pro. The fact the Instapot Pro has handles makes a world of different. On the Duo it is was a pain pulling the pot out and straining it while hot. On top of that it inner-pot of this "Pro" has a heavy bottom making a great is steel pot, so it just work like a normal pot on the stove top giving me the options in using either the electrical device or on the stove top. When in doubt get the 6 qt, is fits most things for a 1-4 person household (I'd argue even 6). Might not hold a Large whole chicken, but I manage by being able to breakdown a whole chicken (it isn't hard, just watch a video) I cook professionally. But at home the Instapot is the best appliance I've gotten. I make Bean from dried at a fraction of the time, amazing quality fresh stock that doesn't require me to to wait 8 hours on a stove top, it takes the place of crockpot, rice cooker (*), and a normal pot. Stews, Gumbo, Chili, and Braises are done greatly when you are pinch for time making what would normally for 5 hour is only an hour or two and near same quality. Which has saved me during a dinner party where my sous dropped braised short ribs 2 hours before plating. It is an investment but if you eat (or plan to eat) legumes/beans, and you use stock/broth occasionally or consistently in your diet. This will save you some money and time while giving you a better product than store-bought stock/broth and canned beans. Both the beans and stock you make freeze well, and cooked frozen bean reheat/thaw fast. And if you freeze veggie scrap (like onion skin, carrot/parsnip peel, celery tops and bottoms) as well and save bones from you chicken (rotisserie, chicken thigns, or whole chicken) you can make stock with all the stuff you were going to throw way anyway. Better than store bought while also being basically free. Lastly it is great for meal prep and you can set it to have your ingredients in it before leaving to work and being done by the time you get home from work. If you cook consistently for yourself and/or for loved ones, or want to cook more at home. An Instapot makes thing easy at a press of a button, and the Pro has very convent features (like HANDLES I cant praise enough!) that make life much more easy. When you get one you will ask also ask "Why didn't I get one sooner?". I work late nights and early morning, this gives me more time and saves me from eating out. ~*I've mentioned "rice cooker" and I want to expand on this.~ The Instapot works great as a rice cooker but compared to an actual rice cooker, it is a little slower to cook (20min vs 30-35min) and the rice (especially short-grain/sushi rice) builds starch and stick to the stainless steel pot, requiring a slight bit more finesse to clean. I personally eat rice (and grains) consistently and i like saving 10-15min of what little time I have at home, so i have both a cheap rice cooker and instapot. However if you want to minimize your appliances (i.e. have less "appliance clutter") and need to conserve space in your kitchen, then having just an Instapot will work well enough and do every thing a rice cooker can, plus much MUCH more.

headline: If you wish your IP was wider and spits less on pressure release - this is for you!
review_text_raw: I’m a long time Instant Pot user and have bought many upgrades over the years. I was attracted to this new RIO Wide because, you guessed it, it’s wide. I do a lot of sautéing as well as cooking larger bone in chicken breasts, which aren’t as convenient in the standard narrow tall 6 qt IP. I also wanted to steam larger vegetables like 5-8 ears of corn on the cob. For the functional bits - it surpassed my expectations. I cook 5 ears of corn on the cob regularly now in this guy. They are very easy to get out with tongs with the lower height of the device. The settings are a perfect variety and the controls are easy to read and configure. I’ve cooked a half chicken in there after browning it first with the wide cooking surface. It turned out tender and delicious. The chimes at ends of cycles are melodious and make me smile - not the harsh beeping of older models. Steam release is exceptional - both super quiet and without wet spitting that you can get with older IPs. That alone has made it my go to IP. It is larger, so if you want to store it, you will need some space for that. I just leave mine on the kitchen island because I use it all the time. The lid is wide, so you can’t slot it into those IP slots that hold the lid on smaller models. This just means you need to be careful to drain any liquid caught in the lid into the pot when you remove it so you don’t drip it across your counter/electronics. Because of the width, the steam trivet is very easy to remove when it is hot. That’s something I struggled with a bit on my older, narrow IP. Stir fries are a dream to cook in this cooker. It feels very safe from steam burns due to the backward facing steam vent and the steam release buttons location far in front of that vent. I’ve put the lid in the dishwasher, which held up well. But mostly I clean stuck on food bits with some Lemi Shine citric acid on high pressure for 3 minutes and a soak in that overnight. That leaves the pan looking brand new as you can see in the photo. If you were debating whether you needed this IP in your collection, I can assure you that you do.

product_title: Instant Pot Pro 8 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black
headline: BUYER BEWARE..SLOW COOK DOESN'T WORK...ZERO CUSTOMER SERVICE
review_text_raw: I we'll start this by saying if I could give this product zero stars or negative stars, I would. Absolutely. I have tried to order this product FOUR times. Amazon will not let me individually review this item for each one of those purchases, although they are different experiences. The first time Amazon sent me a defective product with a broken lid and a damaged body (I knew that I was purchasing it from the Amazon sell, but I had no idea it was gonna be unusable) My second order was with a Christmas gift card for a brand new product. I purchased the 8 qt "pro" as an upgrade from my current duo nova instant pot. I have enjoyed that product, although I do get an error code fairly frequently stating that the pot is the wrong size for the base... Instant pot told me that there is no fix for this I just need to order a brand new pot which I refuse to do so I fidget with it and it will work. Anyway, the brand new 8 quart would not come up to temperature on the slow cook function. I let it sit for four hours and it was still preheating and the food inside was raw. I had to take the food out and cook it in the oven. I sent the pot back The third time I ordered a 6 quart instant pot pro which looked beautiful, but had the exact same problem. There was also a problem getting the lid to come off the pot I had to take a butter knife and push down the steam release so that the lid would release and allow me to remove it even when I was not using the pressure cook mode. The slow Cook function absolutely would not preheat I did an experiment by putting water in the pot and turning it on for eight hours in the morning with no food in it and it never came up to temperature. Seven hours later it was still blinking preheat and the water inside was like 150°F. I contacted instant pot and they wanted me to do this almost tremendous task of taking a video showing the problem taking several photographs explaining the context of the problem blah blah blah blah. I said no I am just going to send it back until I can get one that actually works. That brings me to my fourth and final order of the instant pot Pro 6 qt. I know that it will shock you, but I had the exact same problem. I could not believe it. I looked it up online (as I should have done in the first place)and found that this is a common problem with this product. It just will not come up to heat on slow cook. One YouTube video said that it takes hours for this particular model to come up to temperature and you will need to have an instant thermometer handy so that you can check your food every few hours to ensure that it's actually cooking appropriately. I don't know about you, but when I slow cook food it is my expectation that that food is going to cook, even if I am out working in my garden or running a quick errand to the store. Why would I be on standby for eight hours when I can probably cook it in the oven in one or two and have a somewhat consistent result? Well, I did contact instant pot (again) and they required me to send photographs, and an explanation, and the whole rigmarole, which I did this time only to get a reply just a couple hours later where I was told the same thing : if you were going to cook something on slow cook it can take up to four hours to preheat on a longer cook. My reply back to instant pot was that several sites on the Internet know that there is a problem with the instant pot pro in that the slow Cook function does not work correctly. The Internet knows that this is a flaw. Amazon is becoming aware that this is a flaw. And I believe that instant pot knows that this is a flaw yet they refuse to either correct the problem or honor their warranty. I am sad to say that I will never buy another instant pot product after the runaround that I was given by this company, who refused to assist me, will not honor the warranty, made excuses for a faulty product, and ultimately just basically said if you don't like it go return it (literally). So I am. GOOD NEWS-- UPS will pick it up for free.

product_title: Instant Pot Pro 8 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black
headline: Great pressure cooker for everyday family meals
review_text_raw: The media could not be loaded. I’ve been using this Instant Pot Pro for over 4 months, and it has become one of the most useful appliances in my kitchen. The 6-quart size is perfect for a family of four — enough space for stews, soups, and batch cooking, but not too bulky on the counter. Cooking results: • Pork and beef come out incredibly tender — the meat literally falls apart. • Potatoes with meat turn out soft and perfectly cooked. • Homemade beef stew cooks in about 30 minutes, which still surprises me. • I also made beef “tushonka” and it turned out excellent. • I tried making pilaf once — the rice overcooked and the bottom browned slightly, so this recipe needs some adjusting. Ease of use: • Very simple controls, intuitive interface. • I really like that the exterior has no physical buttons — it makes wiping the surface quick and easy. • The inner pot handled the dishwasher perfectly. What could be improved: • The lid is not very convenient to wash, especially around the silicone parts. • An extra sealing ring is included, but it doesn’t completely prevent the pot from absorbing strong smells from previous dishes (paprika, curry, etc.). I haven’t tested sweet or dairy recipes yet because of this — I’m sure the aroma would transfer. • The steam release is very hot and can splash, so you need to stand back when depressurizing. Overall, it’s a great appliance that saves a lot of time and consistently delivers delicious results. I rate it 4 stars, mainly because of the lid cleaning and lingering smells, but I’m still very satisfied with how well it cooks.

review_text_raw: I’ve been using my Instant Pot more lately, so I was excited to check out The Latest Instant Pot Cookbook for Beginners by Dorothy Milburn. What I liked right away is that the recipes don’t feel intimidating, even if you’re still figuring out all those buttons and settings on the Instant Pot. The instructions are straightforward and easy to follow, which is exactly what I need on busy days. There’s a nice variety of recipes here, from soups and stews to poultry, seafood, meats, veggies, and even desserts. I especially like having so many everyday meal ideas in one place because sometimes I just stare at my pantry and have no clue what to make. The recipes also make cooking feel less like a chore and more like something I can actually enjoy. Another thing I appreciated is that the cookbook focuses on flavorful meals without making the process overly complicated. As someone who doesn’t always have hours to spend in the kitchen, I love recipes that let me get dinner going and move on to other things. I think this is a great cookbook for Instant Pot beginners or anyone who wants simple, comforting meals without a lot of fuss. It gave me several recipes I’m looking forward to trying, and it definitely made me want to use my Instant Pot more often. Definitely worth keeping handy for those busy weeknight meals!

headline: I like that the app has a "Timed Venting" option
review_text_raw: Updated 12/29/24 - My Instant Pot timed venting wish has finally come true, so I just changed my rating to five stars. They added a new app option when timed venting is selected, so now you can choose the amount of time you want to vent the pot. It takes the guessing game out of using the timed venting feature. It's the addition I have been hoping for ever since they added timed venting to the app. Updated 9/27/24: They just added a new notification feature to the app and I really like it. You get a push status notification when the pressure cooker starts preheating, then moves to the cooking cycle, then goes into venting mode and when it completes the venting cycle. It's particularly helpful to get notified when it goes into the venting process in case you want to precisely time the venting based on what you are cooking. It's a helpful enhancement. Original review - I have an older model 6 QT Instant Pot Pro and I wanted this new one for its ability to connect to wifi, so I can use the app to control it. I especially like that the app has an extra venting option that is not available on the panel of the Instant Pot itself. It's a "Timed" option (see photo) that I actually discovered by accident when I was programming a cooking cycle. It's not explained anywhere in the documentation or even in the app, but it's very helpful when doing grains where I want it to natural release for a few minutes and then quickly finish the release without manual intervention. This is where the "Timed" option comes in. It seems to kick in about five to seven minutes after natural release starts. It varies, maybe based on how full the pot is, but since there's no documentation, it's just a guess on my part. It works great because I can be anywhere in the house and not have to rush to my kitchen to manually change the venting to quick release. I really love being able to monitor the progress from my iPhone and see when it has finished whatever cycle I've chosen. The cooking pot itself is different than my older model. It has two handles on it so it makes lifting the hot pot out of the unit so easy. I also like that it automatically seals itself when you lock the lid. No more manually turning a small knob from venting to sealing. That makes it foolproof. It cooks the same way as my older model, but these new options make it my preferred pot. It doesn't have as many preprogrammed settings as my older model, but I never really used those anyway. I like to use the standard pressure cook option and choose the cooking times and the pressure and venting levels myself. I took one star off because "Timed Venting" is not a feature on the unit and it's not explained in any documentation, but it's offered as a feature in the app. I think they need to point that out somewhere and not leave it up to consumers to find it by accident or have to guess to see how it works.

headline: Techies like us, love having Bluetooth accessibility! Great InstantPot!
review_text_raw: Our original InstantPot just "bit the dust." We LOVED having it and it produced many, many wonderful memories meals for us. While we mourned the passing of our "Old Faithful" InstantPot, I decided to start researching other electric pressure cookers and again, we came back to InstantPot and wanted to see what options they had. After reading all of the reviews and articles on this particular model, I told my wife 'PLEASE, PLEASE get me this one for Christmas!" She said, you can go ahead and order it but you're not allowed to open it until Christmas! Like anyone, I said YES!!!! I opened it and then downloaded the app being that it is Bluetooth compatible. I cannot tell you enough, what a pleasant surprise it was, to see just how easy it was to set up and connect via our home WiFi. I can now use the app to set the time, the release time, etc. It's amazingly friendly to use and works great. One thing I will tell you is that if you, like me, use the Saute' mode, to first brown meat, you can NOT start hte InstantPot in this mode via the app. You must physically hit the start button in order to have the Saute' mode come on. Yes, you can set it up in the app but cannot physically start the InstantPot in this particular mode. I know I"m repating myself but I want to make sure that everyone understands this. To me, it's a safety feature and I can appreciate why it's done this way. The last thing you want to do is to accidently have your InstantPot start in this mode while you're away or remote. PROS: Excellent quality, every time I turn it on, it immediately conects to the WiFi and can be accessed via the app CONS: None noted at the time of this review.

product_title: Instant Pot Pro Plus 6 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black
headline: So far it's pretty great
review_text_raw: There are a ton of youtube videos, showing you not only how to use it but how to make one pot dinners. It's easy to use, wifi is easy to set up which afterwards connects whether you are using the app or not, to show remaining cooking time. I only have basic cooking skills, so I prefer to watch the youtube videos for recipes than the app for now. Food prep always takes the longest, but once you have everything ready, put the food in, close the lid, set the time and wait for it to finish. When you set a time according to a recipe, that is the actual Pressure Cooking time. The unit has to preheat before Pressure Cooking time begins, and that's several minutes depending on the model. Then the unit has to vent the pressure (choice of Natural, Pulse, or Quick Vent.) Be careful with Quick Vent as it may make some meats tougher than if you simply waited for the Natural vent process. If you enable push notifications, it will tell you when preheating has ended and cooking has begun, and of course when cooking has ended and venting has begun (you'll likely hear the venting process from the next room. Everything but the base is dishwasher safe on the top rack, BUT, you should use a milder soap like when washing by hand, not the regular somewhat harsh dishwasher soap. The stainless steel pot didn't come quite as clean as it should have, so a little scrubbing in the sink made it bright again. You could always wash it with your regular dishwasher load (but not the other parts (lid, sealing ring, some small vent parts.) I'm pleased with my purchase and have planned a whole week of cooking meals in it. I'm currently using a simple recipe of chicken, onions, honey, soy sauce, and garlic. Smells good.

Then the unit has to vent the pressure (choice of Natural, Pulse, or Quick Vent.) Be careful with Quick Vent as it may make some meats tougher than if you simply waited for the Natural vent process. If you enable push notifications, it will tell you when preheating has ended and cooking has begun, and of course when cooking has ended and venting has begun (you'll likely hear the venting process from the next room. Everything but the base is dishwasher safe on the top rack, BUT, you should use a milder soap like when washing by hand, not the regular somewhat harsh dishwasher soap. The stainless steel pot didn't come quite as clean as it should have, so a little scrubbing in the sink made it bright again. You could always wash it with your regular dishwasher load (but not the other parts (lid, sealing ring, some small vent parts.) I'm pleased with my purchase and have planned a whole week of cooking meals in it. I'm currently using a simple recipe of chicken, onions, honey, soy sauce, and garlic. Smells good.

product_title: Instant Pot Pro Plus 6 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black
headline: Better Features than Older Models - But Several Important Differences
review_text_raw: This is my second instant pot. My IP Ultra model recently died so I had to upgrade. Here are several important differences from previous models: 1) The inner pot has two hand holders - this is great because the previous models would swirl around when stirring. This new version prevents that from happening. 2) The cord is not removable - not a huge deal, but wondering why they would make this change. The cord is located in the back left corner. So plugging into an outlet on the back right made for a strange bend in the cord. Wondering why they can't simply place the cord in the back middle. Not a deal breaker for me, but you should be aware of it. 3) Steam valve: this works a bit differently than other models. No way to manually vent or release steam. It has to be done through the control panel. It is possible to change the setting mid-stream, but there is a delay of a few seconds once you input on the control panel. 4) Older IP accessories may not work - I used to do Pot-in-Pot cooking with a 2 level PIP on top of a trivet. This worked fine in my Instant Pot Ultra. But the first time I tried it in my IP Pro Plus, the pin got stuck, and the lid locked closed. I couldn't open it because the pin needed room to clear. I managed to figure a way out to open it by turning the pot upside down. But this new IP seems to have a slightly lower clearance. So you'll have to use a shorter trivet, or a shorter PIP. Otherwise your lid may get stuck in locked mode. The bluetooth/wireless feature seems nice, but I tend to use the pot while I'm at home anyway. So I'm not sure how helpful it will be over time. But you do have the ability to turn on the IP while you're away from home. It involves downloading an app and connecting your IP to the wifi. The phone app gives notifications when the pre-heating is done, so thats a nice feature. The other main reason I bought this was because of the pressure canning. You can fit up to 4 quart size mason jars to can food. This is really nice. Because of its higher temperature/pressure abilities, this IP can theoretically cook food faster vs older models. I haven't tried it out yet. They also have a feature called "Nutriboost". This is simply a feature where the IP lets out steam periodically. Food in the inner pot then gets agitated. If this is done periodically throughout, then the food gets stirred. Its good for things like risotto and dhals where you want a smooth consistency. Its a nice feature but the name is a little misleading -- nothing about this boosts nutrition. It is simply a fancy way to stir your food while pressure cooking.

headline: USED item sold as NEW
review_text_raw: UPDATE: Received replacement and it's the WRONG (older model with fewer features) in the box! This is insanity. Our previous Instapot died 3 days ago, and we needed another before Thanksgiving. The new one clearly arrived in a VERY used condition. Looks like someone cooked a few meals in it, then used it as a bowling ball. Shame on the manufacturer store for trying to pass this off as new. Returning immediately. Update 2: The replacement pot was in the correct box, but had a different Instant Pot in it. The ouside of the box very clearly says Instant Pot, and the device inside also is an instant pot, the same model as our old one but not the upgraded version we bought. Contacted Instant Pot directly to see what can be done about getting the WRONG item in the RIGHT box. Their incredibly lame and disappointing response is "We don't sell that" I can find the exact same model we ordered on their website. The one they "don't sell" Final update: Contacted Amazon and explained the situation. They immediately refunded our money (thank you). We ordered again without much hope. To our surprise, the package that arrived today was the correct pot in the correct box finally Buyer beware, the device itself is fantastic but if your box comes with tape all over it you probably didn't get what you ordered. I am leaving this at 1 star because Instant Pot customer servicw was absolutley abyssmal and refused to even try to correct the situation. I would buy from a local appliance store vs. online because of this...getting what we ordered has been a lot of uneccesary drama. The pot itself can be reviewed now: The set in handles that keep the pot from spinning around while you sautee are fantastic. They fit firmly in place and make lifting the pot out easy. The liner pot is MUCH higher quality than the regular instant pots. The disc bottom is thicker than the original pots, and fully 3 ply clad, and it shows. There is no convex in the center of the bottom so you can keep food where you want it. The steam release is variable and no touch. The 3 setting options are great and require much less attention/timer setting. It is also MUCH quieter than previous models. The Keep Warm setting can now be used as a reheat setting, with a high, medium, low and custom temp. The Nutriboost setting is useful for gently shaking the pot while cooking to help blend better and keep food from sticking to the bottom initially. The buld seems very sturdy, very pleased over all with the additional features and functions of this pot. Would recommend, but suggest buying in person to avoid getting scammed.

product_title: Instant Pot Duo Crisp 6 Qt 11-in-1 Air Fryer + Pressure Cooker, Steel
headline: Worth the upgrade from a 6qt Duo
review_text_raw: This was purchased as an upgrade from the 6qt Duo model. TOTALLY worth it and I've only used a single mode on each lid (Pressure Cook and Air Fry) so far. I didn't use other modes on the 6qt either including the pre-programmed settings. This is pretty much apples to apples comparison. Overall a complete win and would recommend it to others. Benefits: 1. Handles on the inner pot. This keeps the pot from spinning during saute mode and makes it easier and safer to remove the pot when it's full of food. I can do this even after a wrist injury. 2. Flat bottom on the pot. Makes any added oils spread evenly instead of running to the edge and enables #3 below. 3. Pot is stove-top safe. Even more versatility! I tried this today and the handles did get a bit too warm to touch from the gas heat flowing up the sides of the pot, but it enabled me to quickly control the temperature and still pressure cook the results in the same pot. 4. Air Fryer : I've not had an air fryer before and this definitely works well. The AirFry lid is simple to put on and take off, and doesn't require it's own cord. Results have been excellent for the chicken nuggets, fries and frozen battered fish I've tried. All in less time than the standard oven method 5. Replaced a 6qt slow cooker. I'm betting on this one a bit. My slow cooker use in the past years has primarily been to keep chili warm. Most recently, I used the 6qt duo since it travels more safely to the party/pot luck location with the pressure lid locked on. Now the Air Fry lid is stored where the slow cooker resided. And yes, the Duo also could do this, but I'd not done it based on the slow cooker function testing/reviews as not getting hot enough. The Pro test/reviews were better for slow cooking function. 6. It's a 2qt larger capacity while not that much bigger of a footprint. Yes it's bigger, but it's not as much larger than the 6 qt than I thought it may be. The Saute surface is larger by 2 chicken thighs from 4 to 6 (crowded). 7. Pressure lid doesn't build up water spots. The Duo lid has areas on top where the metal is exposed. That started getting calcium deposits around the edge starting after the 2nd washing and air drying. The 8qt pro is completely covered in plastic with a removable door over a cooling area. It's not built up the water deposits after ~20 uses even in there because it's curved. 8. The base lid lip is easier to clean: The area where the lid seals onto the base is wider on the Pro version making it easier to get a cloth and finger in there to clean the splatters from sauteing. 9. The drip catcher is easier to remove. The clear plastic cup under to back ledge that catches fluids from the lip is a drawer on the Pro. This is much easier to remove and insert than the squeeze and clip version on the Duo. 10. Auto Sealing/pressure switch: The lid automatically seals when it's turned so you don't end up wondering why the pressure hasn't built up after you forgot to turn the weight from the vent position. 11. Steam Diffusion and easy venting: The switch to vent is away from the steam so no risk of burns, but also doesn't complicate cleaning. And the the steam diffuser cap (which is called whisper quiet) contains any spitting of starches while is removable for cleaning. 12. The AirFry lid storage tray attaches and also works as a trivet while using it. 13. There are lines on the front of the Pro and pressure lid indicating the starting position for attaching it. No more fumbling to get the lid lined up. 14. Improved cord management: The cord isn't removable. This makes the connection to the base more streamlined allowing it to get closer to a wall. To compensate, there is a slot to hold the wrapped cord when it's not plugged in. It's also not at risk of getting lost. Suggested improvements: 1. The inside surface of the stainless pressure pot isn't as polished as the 6qt duo pot so it's a bit tougher to get fully clean. We use it to make rice and also saute chicken without oil as a step in broth making (then deglaze). Both of these stick to the pot a bit and require scrubbing. The new pot is less polished so it needs a cleanser step nearly every time to get all the bits off even after soaking. The 6qt pot didn't need this and the only thing that we can perceive as different is the pot internal texture. 2. The air fry pot also doesn't get fully clean with hand scrubbing. Seems to always take more than one hand wash cycle. It may be the texture or color or both, but inevitably, the thing still looks greasy after it's dried. We've not put it in the dishwasher which might do better. 3. The bottom ring for the air fry multipot arrived with a tab broke off so it doesn't stay attached to the pot. Customer service has responded in a timely manner (not yet finished the resolution). I mention it because it may be a weakness in the design. 4. The air fry lid and storage tray is always a challenge to line up for joining. If there's an indication like the pressure lid to base, I've not found it. 5. No pot lid accessory available for the 8qt pot which is sad since the pot can be used on the stovetop. This would make the item even more versatile. I never wanted one for the Duo.

headline: What was I thinking?!
review_text_raw: What was I thinking, taking so long to get this!!? Our first meal we (me and my husband) prepared in our Instant Pot was a beef pot roast with carrots and potatoes. Prep time was a whole 15 minutes. That was just to get the veggies ready. Then we seared the pot roast in the Instant Pot. Super easy! The searing isn't something everyone does, so that's a good part of the prep time. Then the cook time was 40 minutes. That's it!! Dinner time! I will say, you don't smell the food cooking. That may be a plus or a minus, depending on how you're wired. I have fibromyalgia. Smells of foods cooking are NOT my friend. So not smelling the food until right before eating was a real blessing for me! Now, to the roast. It was so tender, we were able to cut it with a fork, and it was incredibly juicy! The vegetables cooked in the roasts juices, but they still tasted like themselves, and weren't overly mushy. I honestly didn't think it was possible to get a roast and veggies to cook the same amount of time and both come out perfectly, but they did! I've yet to try all the other features. When I've done more with my Instant Pot, I'll do an update here. So far we are just using it for meals, but I feel like it pays for itself so quickly. An hour is a short amount of time to wait for a meal (for us). Being on the go so much, it's gotten to be a bad habit to just pick up fast food. Now, we just throw some good, fresh ingredients in the Instant Pot, and it pretty much just fixes dinner for us, while we unwind. There is a minimal amount that needs to be done, depending on what we're fixing. No matter how you slice it, nothing compares to a home cooked meal, especially one that can cook so quickly an doesn't need to be watched over. Both my husband and myself are wondering why he didn't get this sooner!! So far we've got no negatives at all. It does what's it's supposed to, exactly like it's supposed to.

product_title: Instant Pot Duo Crisp 6 Qt 11-in-1 Air Fryer + Pressure Cooker, Steel
headline: Glad I bought it.
review_text_raw: I decided to cheap out and bought one of these from the Amazon Warehouse. There are pros and cons to this which I will discuss at the bottom of this review. This is a great piece of cookware, that is capable of many cooking techniques. I am happy with my purchase and would buy it again. It is relatively easy to program but you have to remember to press the Start button. (Something I forgot to do a few times.) Saute - seems a little slow to get up to full temperature compared to stove top cooking, but it get there. The indicator is helpful to give you some idea of the current temp. Pressure - works well. Lid is easy to place. One feature that seems small, but I REALLY love is the little "lid" on the top that you can remove to open a spot to place ice. This feature is wonderful as it allows you to quickly cool the pressure cooker and eliminate the need to do a pressure release and blow steam all over your kitchen. In practice, I have found that a handful if ice will drop the pressure in under 3 minutes. Air Fry - this is a really nice feature to "finish" roasts. Pretty much a must have feature. It falls a little short in browning french fries, as you have to open the lid and shake the air fry basket to ensure even cooking. However, this is also true of most air fryers unless they have a tumble basket. Sous Vide - tried this several times with excellent results. The temperature control is not as exact as you could expect with a circulating type of Sous Vide appliance, but it gets the job done. You may have to experiment a bit to get the ideal temperature setting. Other settings? - haven't tried them yet, so no comment. Caution when Buying from Amazon Warehouse (AzW): I had to return the first unit that I bought as the front control panel was dented. It seems that the AzW workers will repackage these units in a box lined with plastic bags filled with spray foam. In theory this should provide excellent protection from dings and dents, however this Instant Pot is sensitive to crushing forces. The outer shell is essentially a thin metal band. My first unit was packed on its side. Something must have been placed on that box in shipping which crushed the faceplate. The replacement unit I ordered was boxed upright. It arrived with the outer metal band pressed down into the base by a quarter inch or so. I was able to gently pry it back into position and the unit has worked perfectly since. In any event these warehouse purchases do not have the same warranty, so factor that into your purchase decision. I was able to save about $70. Not sure if it was worth it.

headline: So far so good!
review_text_raw: I love my old instant pot, so when I was looking for a new one and saw that the version with the air fryer lid I was sold (after reading some reviews to make sure it wasn't terrible lol). I've been wanting an air fryer but couldn't justify another appliance when I wasn't sure I would use it that often. I like the display, although I miss being able to hit the pressure cook button (or whatever setting you're using) to switch between three saved cook times and adjust from there, since pressure cooking times vary wildly. I do find adjusting the settings to be easier to figure out and more intuitive than the old "duo" version that I had, although setting the time from 5 minutes to 90 minutes by spinning the little dial is annoying. The air fryer works fine- I can't compare it to a stand-alone model since I've never used one, but I made asparagus on the bottom rack and halibut on the top rack made with an egg wash, then a seasoned flour and Parmesan coating and both came out great. Nice and crispy compared to what I would have gotten in the oven. I can also see myself using the sous vide option occasionally. I sous vide very infrequently by heating water to temp, then putting the pan in the oven on the lowest temp and monitoring the digital thermometer I use. Without a circulator, I expect the sous vide function is probably about the same level of effectiveness and accuracy, but easier. Maybe I'll do it more often now. If nothing else, I can use it to pasteurize eggs more easily for Caesar dressing and tiramisu. I can also see myself using the broil option occasionally. The instant pot is a pain to dig out since I keep it in the cupboard above my fridge, but if I already have it out it's probably quicker than the oven. I used to have a dehydrator and got rid of it because I have a smoker now, which is 100X better for jerky. But fresh herbs? Maybe! I usually freeze fresh herbs, but I've thought about making my own seasoning mixes with an old pepper mill I have laying around. ALSO, I have borosilicate dishes that I often use to make small loaves of banana bread. They will fit perfectly in the inner pot, so I'm going to see how the bake option works. It even came with a recipe for banana bread that made me think of it. I hate heating the full sized oven for 45+ minutes for one half sized loaf of banana bread! The air fryer lid is really a game changer. I'm excited to have a little mini convection oven with just a slightly larger footprint than before (having to store the lid). I considered getting the one with "the ultimate lid" that does everything, but the 8qt version is a must have for me, and it seems like it's just adding more things that can fail and making it more difficult to repair the lid and more expensive to replace if necessary.

The iO3 also helps you time your brushing so that you the recommended two minutes. It pulses when it's time to change to a different quadrant. product_title: Oral-B Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, iO5 Limited Deep Clean & Whiten, 5 Cleaning Modes, Visual Pressure Sensor to Protect Gums, Travel Case, 3 Brush Heads, Black
headline: Better than Phillips Sonicare. App is actually useful and not just a gimmick.
review_text_raw: So, I'm a long-time user of Sonicare, which means I've gone through a number of them that always tend to break right at warranty expiry. Though I usually find them on sale, they are not cheap, nor are the brushes, and for the price they are still so prone to breaking down and various issues. So, when my current one started to have an issue (turning on randomly on its own, startling all around), I started shopping for a replacement. This Oral B brush went on sale, so I decided to check it out - maybe return if it wasn't all that great in comparison. At first, I was a little confused, because I thought these brushes mainly worked by rotation, but they are both that and sonication. I don't know if the vibration speed matches to Sonicare, but it doesn't seem critical. One immediate thing I noticed was the light ring which instantly lets you know if you are pressing too hard or not enough. As somebody with gum issues, this is appreciated. Next thing, do set up and try out the app. I was skeptical, but it really does a good job of figuring out what part of your mouth you are brushing, apparently by some kind of bluetooth-based sonar and something in the brush that can tell if it's facing up or down. It's not to the level of knowing which tooth, but it maps the front and two sides of both the top and bottom of your mouth, which is still pretty detailed. Rather than just using some kind of timer, it tracks that you spend the proper amount of time in each of the 6 regions. Your coverage within each region is then up to you. Sure, there are some times when it is a bit off, but I find that that tends to happen if I turn my head. So if you keep your head still, it seems to work more accurately. Not too hard to do. Besides the main brush tracking, you can set specific goals, and it will add recommendations for other steps like tongue brushing and flossing. I started a program for plaque removal. So now, instead of brushing or not kind of mindlessly in the shower one a day, I have started brushing twice a day, with more intention, and it's even slightly fun. And so far, my teeth feel smoother and cleaner. I also get less gum bleed, perhaps due to avoiding pressing too hard. I think this is still a bit pricey at full price, but maybe in this case it could be worth it for the improvement in your teeth and gum health. On sale, I can definitely recommend. Will it last long term? We'll see.

product_title: Philips Sonicare 4100 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, 1 Brush Head, Black
headline: A Report from the Front Lines of Oral Hygiene
review_text_raw: Dateline: A Bathroom Sink, Under the Unforgiving Glare of the Vanity Lights. For years, the act of brushing your teeth has been a sleepy, half-conscious affair. A dull, buzzing ritual performed on autopilot before you either face the horrors of the day or collapse into bed. You thought you knew what an electric toothbrush felt like. You were wrong. You were living a lie. I am here to tell you about the Philips Sonicare 4100. And I am here to tell you that it is a different beast entirely. It sits in your hand with a comfortable, substantial heft—a proper tool, not some flimsy, skinny wand. The handle is sturdy, the build quality immaculate. It feels like a serious instrument for a serious job. I applied the paste, brought the brush to my teeth with the casual indifference born of long habit, and thumbed the power button. And was immediately jolted awake by a profound, high-frequency thrum. This was not the gentle back-and-forth of a lesser brush. This was a jump scare. A sudden, powerful hum that felt like I was holding a swarm of microscopic, hyper-caffeinated jackhammers against my teeth. This is the "sonic" part of the name, a technology that vibrates with a speed and intensity that is both shocking and deeply, profoundly effective. You can feel the difference. It's a sensation of being deep-cleaned, of having years of coffee stains and bad decisions power-washed into oblivion. There are smart features, of course. A pressure sensor that gently chides you if you're pressing too hard, a built-in coach to keep you from savaging your own gums. A timer that dutifully guides you through the quadrants of your mouth. The included cap for the brush head is a simple, welcome touch of practical genius. But we must address the one, single, baffling decision that holds this marvel back from pure, unadulterated perfection: the charger. In a world that has finally, blessedly, begun to standardize around the glorious, universal USB-C port, Philips has chosen to tether this futuristic cleaning wand to a proprietary, old-world charging base. It is a strange, frustrating relic, a small annoyance that requires its own dedicated spot on your counter, unable to join the happy family of your other modern chargers. Even so, that one grievance is a whisper in the face of the roaring, high-frequency hurricane of cleaning power this toothbrush provides. The Sonicare 4100 is an impressive, powerful, and brilliantly effective piece of technology. It transforms the most mundane of daily chores into a high-performance event. A five-star champion that will leave your mouth feeling cleaner than you ever thought possible.

product_title: Philips Sonicare 4100 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, 1 Brush Head, White
headline: Not as weak as they say
review_text_raw: This is my 1st electric toothbrush. I ordered it over the oral b smart 1500 because it's cheaper and I found more people who swear by it than oral b. Later on, I read comments where people who have this 4100 for 10+ years say that the newer 2021 version has only half the power of the old version. Someone on reddit showed images of the inside of the new and old versions and the new version has a small plastic toy-like motor, while the old version has a big copper-wrapped motor and an old version user said "now I understand why the new version is lighter and less powerful". I was disappointed on the new version and tried to cancel the order but I couldn't. Once it came, I decided to try it and to my surprise, it brushes my teeth way better than my manual soft-bristled and hard-bristled toothbrushes(I use both manual brushes daily compared to my daily usage of the electric toothbrush 4100 C2 head of medium bristles. If you have gum sensitive issue, buy the S sensitive or G2 optimal brush head. If you want hard-bristled, buy W diamondclean brush head). I don't know how good the old version was but this newer version definitely brushes better than any manual toothbrush unfortunately it doesn't not come with a travel case. Update 5/16/2024: I bought the Oral B smart 1500 because it was on sale and I wanted to see how better it is compared to the sonicare. The oral B package looks nicer and bigger than the Sonicare but upon opening the smart 1500 package, I saw hair all over the toothbrush. I did read many customers saying on reddit that their Oral b toothbrush were repackaged, but I can't believe I'm a victim of this nastiness. It also took 2 weeks to reach me from Hawaii and since it says "made in China", I think the seller is located in China. I'll return this and I'll advise you to buy the Sonicare instead of the oral b if you don't want to be cheated receiving a used-repackaged toothbrush. Update 05/22/2024: On 05/17/24, I bought the Oral b smart clean 360 which has exact power as the smart 1500 that I returned but the smart 360 has 5 modes and a button to change the mode while the smart 1500 has 3 modes and no button to switch between the modes. The advantage of the oral b smart clean 360 is that the brush heads cost is cheaper than the Sonicare 4100 and I find it better at whitening my teeth than the Sonicare. That's all the advantages there. The things that I don't like with it are many, so I'm just going to name the most annoying ones: 1) The brush heads are too big compared to the Sonicare(see picture): Putting Oral b brush heads in my mouth is like putting a golf ball in my mouth(my head and mouth are wider than the average US male). 2) The brush heads have holes(see pictures) that trap saliva+toothpaste and creates more noise when the brush handle needle rotates in the presence of the liquid mixture, and moisture will be also trapped easily in the holes(most customers complain about Oral b brush heads design. Oral b corrected the needle issue with the IO version but the IO introduced a shallow hole which now traps moisture in the brush handle). When I'm using the Oral b with no choice but to have my mouth wide-open, it forces my mouth to produce more saliva which gets mixed with the toothpaste and enters the brush head and creates more noise. 3) Rattling noise: The Oral b smart clean 360 isn't as noisy as people say. It's the quality of the noise the problem. It's a very unpleasant rattling noise as if you're hearing an old car engine with broken parts in it. That noise gets worse when liquid enters the brush head holes. 4) The charger is not round like a perfect circle: You must put the Oral b brush handle in a specific position to charge it and if you place it wrong, it'll fall and might break. 5) The Daily Clean mode is rough and combined with the big brush head the experience is bad, but the smart clean 360 has more mode which make it smoother and better than the smart 1500 but not as good as the Sonicare 4100. 6)It has no auto-stop mode: You keep brushing without knowing how long you have been brushing your teeth. To summarize, the oral b non-IO brush heads are cheap but very badly designed for a pleasant toothbrushing. I won't recommend it if you're shorter than 6 foot tall or have a small mouth.

I love a seller that just wants to make their customers happy, and thats what this seller is all about ♡. But this review made her chuckle so I'll keep it up lol. ☆ I don't even know where to begin when it comes to what needs to be said about this mid-sized Sedan- I mean toothbrush. Even on the lowest setting, this thing has enough horsepower to cut clean through your tongue like a scalpel sharpened by Dexter himself. I'm exaggerating but not by much. It does come with a lot of replacement brush heads which is great for the price, so after I gained enough feeling back in my mouth, I popped on a replacment head and asked my parents (with a garbled half-numbed mouth) to try to survive a full tooth cleaning to see if I was just sensitive to vibrations. Neither of them lasted longer than 15 seconds. They both couldn't stop laughing because they found themselves yelling their responses because they still heard and felt the vibrations long after they turned off the device. Listen, if you dont turn on the device, its amazing lol. Its built with good materials, has a lot of replacement heads and the included stand and travel container was so cute! I wanted to love this toothbrush but it is not usable. Im wondering if I got a defective item because there is no way everyone giving positive reviews was using this in their mouths. Maybe to power wash their driveway, remove graffiti from brick, or to lift a few shades from some old dentures, but NOT for teeth cleaning. And im just gonna say what we are all thinking- WHO THE HECK IS SIMEN M. AND WHY SHOULD WE CARE THAT HE RECOMMENDS THIS PRODUCT? (see image) The generic actors in white lab coats cracked me up. I could almost see the Getty images watermark. This product is so insane that I didnt even return it. I keep it in my cabinet as a threat to any of my nieces/nephews who use bad language in this house. We dont need to wash their mouth out with soap when all I have to say is "go brush your teeth" to instill the fear of God in anyone. 😆

headline: I wouldn't buy it.
review_text_raw: Electrical toothbrushes come in two types, Sonic and Rotating-Oscating . The Sonic type vibrates at incredibly high speeds (up to 40,000 strokes per minute). The rapid vibration creates dynamic fluid action that drives water between teeth, which is the basis of the technique for cleaning teeth. The number of vibrations per minute must be high to do the job correctly. The Coslus which is sold as a sonic vibration type does not publish the vibration rate. I found it to be low compared with major brand sonic vibration brushes. The rest of the features are just bells and whistles. I can only be sure to clean my teeth fully by treating it like a non-electrical toothbrush and brushing for a full 5 minutes. In addition, it makes a high-pitched loud noise, which is great if you have a hangover.

headline: Simple, effective, and reliable sonic cleaning without the extra frills!
review_text_raw: As an Amazon Vine Voice, I tested the PHILIPS Sonicare 1100 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush over a two-week period, using it for twice-daily brushing routines to evaluate its cleaning power, battery life, and overall usability. If you want to step up from a manual toothbrush without paying for expensive, feature-heavy models you'll never use, this stripped-down sonic brush is a compelling option. Here is my honest breakdown of how it performs: ⭐ Cleaning Performance & Power Sonic Technology: Delivering solid vibration action, it drives fluid deep between teeth and along the gumline. It leaves your mouth feeling remarkably fresh—way cleaner than any standard manual brush. Single-Mode Simplicity: It features just one cleaning speed and one button. While it lacks multiple intensity settings or fancy pulse cycles, it focuses entirely on doing the core job exceptionally well. Easy-Start Feature: If you are new to electric toothbrushes, it includes a built-in feature that gently ramps up the power gradually over your first 14 brushing sessions to prevent gum sensitivity. 🛠️ Design & Usability Slim & Lightweight: The handle has a sleek, ergonomic profile that feels comfortable and lightweight in the hand without taking up unnecessary counter space. Smart Timers: The integrated SmarTimer automatically shuts the brush off after the dentist-recommended 2 minutes, while the QuadPacer pulses every 30 seconds to signal when you should switch quadrants of your mouth. 🔋 Battery Life & Charging Dependable Endurance: The internal rechargeable battery easily lasts up to 2 weeks (around 14 days) on a single charge under normal use. Convenient Indicator: A subtle battery level LED indicator alerts you when it's time to drop it back on its USB charging base. 🛑 Minor Cons to Consider No Pressure Sensor: Because this is a budget-friendly model, it lacks a pressure sensor warning light. If you have a heavy hand, you'll need to mind how hard you press manually. Basic Accessories: The kit keeps things minimal with just the handle, one brush head, and a USB charging stand (wall adapter block not always included). The Verdict The PHILIPS Sonicare 1100 proves you don’t need to spend a fortune to get a dentist-clean mouth. It cuts out the complicated modes in favor of reliable timers, great battery life, and powerful sonic action. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a straightforward, high-value electric toothbrush!

headline: A true Sonicare replacement but pulling the heads off takes serious grip strength
review_text_raw: I finally refused to buy another $100 Philips Sonicare after my second one died exactly when the two-year warranty expired. I picked this COSLUS up at full price strictly because getting the handle a travel case and an 18-month supply of brush heads cost less than one pack of name-brand refills. I honestly expected a hollow rattling piece of cheap plastic. Instead the matte black handle has a solid weight to it and the motor delivers that intense high-pitched sonic hum that instantly foams up your toothpaste. After brushing twice a day for six weeks my teeth have that perfectly slick feeling you normally only get leaving the dentist chair. The battery performance is what really convinced me to keep it. I left the wireless charger in the box and haven't plugged this thing in once since day one. I even took it on two weekend work trips without the cord and the motor hasn't dropped a fraction of its power. It does the standard 30-second stutter to tell you to switch quadrants which is great for mindless early morning brushing. I am capping it at four stars for two very specific physical limitations. First the five cleaning modes change the rhythm of the brushing but you cannot adjust the actual intensity up or down. If the standard mode is too aggressive for your gums you just have to switch to the softer pulsating mode. Second the replacement heads lock onto the metal shaft so aggressively that taking them off requires an absurd amount of force. I actually had to wrap a hand towel around the brush head just to get enough grip to yank it off without snapping the plastic. If you have arthritis or hand mobility issues you should definitely skip this. But if you just want a reliable powerhouse of a toothbrush and don't mind wrestling with a piece of plastic every three months this is a massive steal.

product_title: COSLUS C51C30 Water Flosser Electric Toothbrush Combo, 2-1 Oral Clean Kit
headline: Great deal for great products!
review_text_raw: I was in need of a new electric toothbrush, and as someone who has had braces for nearly 3 years (2nd round of braces as well), a water flosser is a helpful luxury. The toothbrush itself has good vibration, with different strength levels and modes, so I think it definitely gets the job done. The color is very pretty (I got pink), and it comes with 4 brush heads total. The water floss machine is very portable. It is easy to hold in your hand without being too bulky, and the water tank holds a sufficient amount. If you're still figuring out the water flossing technique like me, you may have to refill the tank once during use, but once I get the hang of it I'm sure I can stretch one tank for a single session. The water flosser comes with 4 heads total, one of them being a tongue scraper. Aside from the products and their attachments, they do not come with any sort of travel accessories. The toothbrush has a little cap that covers the end of it when there is no brush head attached, and the water flosser has space in the tank to attach 2 (i think?) heads to carry. Otherwise, there is no brush head covers that came with mine, nor is there a travel case or bag. This isn't an issue for me, as I can just buy a cheap travel case. The products themselves are great, and both the toothbrush and the water flosser come with charging cords. I haven't had any issues attaching or removing the accessories, and using the toothbrush and flosser is pretty easy and straightforward. All around, these products are pretty solid for such a good price and convenient combo!

product_title: Oral-B Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, iO5 Customizable Clean, 5 Cleaning Modes, Visual Pressure Sensor to Protect Gums, Travel Case, Black
headline: Works Great but App is Okay
review_text_raw: I had the old style Oral-B before and was ready for a new toothbrush. The IO5 was on sale so I bought it. I didn't think I'd use the app at all but it turns out that the gamification of my oral hygiene is a positive for me. I brush longer and use the guided brushing to make sure I'm getting full coverage. The only thing is that the zone identification is sketchy. On almost every brushing, it indicates the wrong active area of my teeth. I've tried Oral-B's recommendations- stand straight, do each tooth one at a time, move to different segments, repeat on inside and bite surfaces- but it still misdetects zones. What that does is make me brush even longer, so not terrible, but better accuracy would be much better and, frankly, I expected much better. Occasional it totally glitches and I need to restart the app and the brush. I also thought the battery would lastonger but it's about the same as my OG Oral-B electric that was around $40. Note that I am probably brushing longer, so maybe the battery is a little better but I hoped for 3 weeks and I'm getting less than 2 between charges. I still like the brush, but just know the app guidance doesn't work as well as you'd think. I do like that it reminds you to floss, brush your tongue, and use a mouth rinse. It also gives you a score for each session and a running score, which I like even though I thought I'd never use that. In summary, it works well and my dentist noticed a difference and told me to keep it up. It is a bit expensive for an electric toothbrush, so I hope it lasts a long time.

review_text_raw: I originally purchased two of these electric toothbrushes for my kids after our orthodontist highly recommended switching from manual brushing to help keep their braces clean. First off, my kids actually love using them. The brushing modes are incredibly effective at sweeping away food and plaque, but gentle enough that they don't irritate their gums. They find the handles easy to maneuver, and the built-in timer keeps them brushing for the right amount of time without me having to stand there and nag. It has taken the daily battle completely out of our morning and bedtime routines. The absolute best part, however, has been the results. At our last checkup, our dentist specifically went out of their way to comment on how incredibly clean their teeth are now. They noted a massive improvement in plaque removal around the orthodontic hardware compared to when we were using standard manual brushes. If you are a parent on the fence about upgrading to an electric toothbrush, especially if you are dealing with braces, this is 100% worth the investment. The quality is fantastic, the kids are happy, and the dentist is thrilled. Highly recommend!

The is not enough room to also store the charger in the case but will hold the handle and the brush (separated from the handle) in the included durable travel case. Be cautious as some models seem to have a USB charging base that would require an additional purchase of a charger to charge in a standard outlet. This model has three settings with lighting for each. The bottom of the two buttons easily move through each setting with each press. There is a low battery indicator as well. Brushing with this is amazing. It's much more effective than a standard toothbrush or any standard electric toothbrush used over time. Even the kids notice how much cleaner their teeth seem after a use. Brushing harder is not good on teeth as any dentist has told me over time so this brush helps regulate how you brush. You don't have to brush with the Sonicare. The Sonicare does the brushing. You can simply slowly guide the brush over your teeth and let the Sonicare do its job. If the brush is pressed too hard against the teeth the Sonicare vibrations will halt as a sign you are trying to brush too hard. Overall this device is highly recommended and it's even better if you watch for a good deal that does or had occurred periodically.

headline: I like brushing my teeth with it
review_text_raw: I am a lifelong manual medium bristles toothbrush user. Over the years, I have seen electric toothbrushes in my friend's and family's bathrooms and never thought I would ever want to use one. After doing some research, I decided to buy this electric toothbrush. At first, I was not sure if the small brush head would do as good of a job as my standard size manual toothbrush. It took me two days and four brushings to get use to it. The small brush head did a better job at cleaning my teeth. I can not believe how clean my teeth feel after brushing 2 minutes with this toothbrush. Even my gumline has felt cleaner after brushing with this thing multiple times for a week. With my manual toothbrush, there were times I could feel that my gumline was not as clean as it should be. Never once did I irritate my gums while brushing like I did with my manual toothbrush many of times. The electric toothbrush pressure sensor prevented me from doing that to my gums. The 2-minute timer for the clean mode is good for me. After brushing teeth, I switch the intensity to the gum care mode to clean my gums. I like how the brush head replacement reminder and pressure sensor can be deactivated if you do not like those features. My traveling case struggles to stay closed. I may have to buy a different one for traveling with this electric toothbrush. I am impressed with it and wished that I would have bought one of these years ago. 1-24-26 I'm not impressed with the charger. If I use the toothbrush until the battery indicator starts to flash auburn color LED, it takes more than eight hours to fully charge the battery. There is not enough counter space for me to keep the toothbrush docked on the charger. My Philips Norelco All-in-One Series 9000 Trimmer, Wahl Pro Series Detail Trimmer, and Wahl Lithium Ion Pro Rechargeable Cordless Hair Clippers all charge faster than this thing. Heck, a Dewalt 6Ah battery chargers faster than this toothbrush.

And if you're like me, I brush my teeth in the shower in the morning, so I know it's being exposed to water and toothpaste ECT. That is the only reason for the 4 stars and not 5. -No universal charger port, no cover to the charging port and handle is fairly inexpensive feeling, however it is a good toothBRUSH and for the price you pay it is worth the investment. I feel if they fix those few things they'd be right up there with Phillips and other well known toothbrush makers. 4 out of 5 with potential to be a solid 5 with some fine tooning.

product_title: Bitvae ADA Accepted Electric Toothbrush, 60-Day Battery Travel Toothbrush
headline: Ultrasonic Toothbrush Not True Electric
review_text_raw: First, there are two types of electric toothbrushes. True electric and ultrasonic. True electric toothbrushes have heads that spin, etc. They provide spin or rotation to the bristles needed to brush your teeth so all you have to do is move the brush across your teeth. If this is what you want, then skip this set. Then there are ultrasonic toothbrushes, like this one. These toothbrushes have heads that just vibrate. There is no spin or rotation to push the bristles between and around your teeth. You still need to physically run the brush back and forth, in a circular motion, etc, for them to work. With that clarified, this brush works great. The head a nice size - not too big, not too small. The bristles are firm but not scratch off your enamel hard - as long as you don't use too much pressure. The head has longer bristles on either side that reach between your teeth and along your gum lines. The toothbrush stops vibrating for a moment every 30 seconds and then turns off at 2 minutes. This allows you to time your brushing by quadrant (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right). This makes it easy for those non-morning folks who suddenly realize they've been brushing one tooth for 5 minutes (you'll understand if this is you). The vibrations take a bit of getting used to - in some modes they can tickle your gums. Each mode is supposed to be for a specific use: White, Clean, Soft, Polish, Gum Care. The modes appear to simply change the amount of vibration - white being the strongest and gum care being the weakest. I would suggest just finding the mode you are most comfortable with and staying with that. Yes, you DO need to put the brush in your mouth BEFORE you turn it on. Just like you put the lid on the blender before turning it on. If you don't, then there WILL be a mess. This is not a failing of the toothbrush, it is simply the nature of the beast. I like that it comes with 8 heads. I've had other electric toothbrushes only to find after 3-6 months that I couldn't get replacement heads for them anymore. At this price point ($20 as of this review), if I can't get replacement heads after going through the 8 included, then I've still spent less than if I was buying standard toothbrushes. The heads do fit snugly and securely. The more you switch them out, the weaker that connection will be, and a head could come out during brushing due to the vibrations. I recommend you buy separate toothbrushes for each member of the family rather than trying to share and switch heads out daily. The toothbrush holder is simple but effective. It keeps the head protected while allowing it to air dry and it holds the toothbrush for convenient access. I attached the cover to a textured high gloss wall next to the sink and it has stayed in place without issue. The cover opens with just a light pull on the toothbrush so there is no fighting to get your toothbrush out. Overall, I highly recommend this toothbrush if you are looking for an ultrasonic (vibrating not spinning or rotating) toothbrush.

review_text_raw: Take in mind when you read most electric toothbrush reviews, they are coming from manual so OF COURSE YOUR TEETH FEEL AMAZING AND CLEAN, but what about when you’re coming from a really good electric toothbrush (Phillips Sonicare and another cheaper one that both felt like improvements after manual) and there are so many choices without a clear understanding what makes one $79 while another is over $200? I started to go a little crazy trying to figure it out. I asked one dentist to suggest and she said either oral b or sonicare (she doesn’t sell them at the office) while another said oral b (he did sell them) so that was not really helpful. When pressed my dentist who doesn’t sell them prefers oral b and she likes the smaller head. I GET THAT NOW! It’s like I’m polishing each tooth and wrapping the head around the tooth almost and I LOVE THAT! I think the Phillips isn’t getting in between near as well. The thing about either brand is that there is such a wide price range that I couldn’t tell the real $100 difference other than maybe an app and possibly more cleaning modes but that’s about it. I decided to go with oral b to try this round more precise head and went to their website to take the quiz to see what was best for me and this is where I landed. I wanted to stay under $100 (and you can on Black Friday and other big sales but I missed it and paid $119 which isn’t terrible if it’s significantly better than my last electric). I just used it for the first time and MY TEETH FEEL AMAZING , in fact my whole mouth feels so clean. I’m someone who buys a firmer bristle head (NOT HARD but I need to feel scrubbed if makes sense). I think sometimes I may be hard on my gums trying to really scrub my teeth but the happy medium is in this oral b brush head! I’m just not clear which one it is as it came with 2 and says one is ultimate clean and the other is gentle care. I’m assuming it’s ultimate but it’s soft but really dense and just scrubs but it’s gentle on the gums. Love it. Very satisfied. It’s not loud at all and it’s got a great light sensor that indicates when you’re at the perfect pressure. I actually found it quite helpful and it’s clearly visible even if you’re not looking in the mirror. I’m kind of excited about the app because after a long lifetime of heat checkups, something has gone wrong and I’m facing some pretty big restorative dental work so perhaps I’ve been slacking I don’t know But I’m trying to be very diligent and that’s part of the reason for the new purchase. I also felt like my old one wasn’t getting me as clean as it used it so it could be I needed something more aggressive. This is really perfect and considering the price tags you can easily go up to on the big name models, I think this really is the sweet spot for an electric toothbrush ESPECIALLY IF YOU’RE NOT COMING FROM MANUAL. If you’re coming from manual, any real electric toothbrush will be so impressive but I needed to be impressed after exclusively using electric. This is it. I’ve got no doubt about the battery life.. they are all that way.. the travel case is a great touch and it’s nice. Nothing like having your electric toothbrush go off in your closed suitcase when you’re all packed. lol. I was always able to get off brand replacement heads for my sonicare that were great at a fraction of the price. I’ll be interested to see if I can get a real match to this one otherwise it may be worth it to stick brand name. Here’s to your dental health and perfect check ups.

headline: It's a nice toothbrush - but be watchful of the inside of the brush head, it can become moldy
review_text_raw: Wow. This Oral B is a big improvement over the one I replaced. It’s whisper quiet in comparison, and I really like the pressure sensor light (green if good pressure, red if too much pressure, white if too little pressure). I also like that I can set the brush mode (speed) to “sensitive”, which is what I use exclusively with a sensitive brush head. My older Oral B only oscillated. This newer one both oscillates and micro-vibrates. My old Oral B was about 10-12 yrs old. It still worked perfectly. Buying sensitive brushes had become fairly inexpensive. I’m pretty sure it would have kept on working at least another 5 yrs. However, my hygienist repeatedly told me: “You’re not doing this, you’re not doing that, blah blah blah.” Tiresome. Sometimes the brush would strike under the gum line around a crown and cause lingering pain. I learned about the new Oral B with the pressure sensor and decided to buy one. Here was the surprising thing to me: I wasn’t brushing hard enough, at least according to the pressure sensor. The first time I used it, I was repeatedly in the white zone (too little pressure). Also, here’s the thing that really did it for me, I didn’t really know how to brush correctly. I found a video on YouTube (“Tips On How To Brush with an Oral B Electric Toothbrush” by Murmann Dental Health) that explained and demonstrated exactly how to brush using an Oral B with pressure sensor. That was very illuminating. I highly recommend that or a similar video. The thing that stood out from the video was that our teeth are rounded, so we need to wrap the brush around each individual tooth . I’ve been following what I learned in the video. So far, the brush hasn’t caused pain under the gum line. The IO sensitive brush along with the “sensitive” setting on the device have been a more comfortable brushing experience for me. I’m consistently in the green zone. Hopefully, it all makes a difference at my next dental appointment. I was sorry to see my old Oral B go as it was still useful, but sometimes useful doesn’t mean effective or appropriate for teeth & gum challenges. It can still be useful for other purposes. I have never used the app, so no comment there. The travel case is very nice and will come in handy. The only thing I don’t like about it is it doesn’t include storage for what seems to be a proprietary charger. The charger is two-pin, and I guess it’s supposedly safer to use in wet environments; you may need to include it in your travel bag depending on your travel time. 5 stars from me.

headline: Worth upgrading from an older model
review_text_raw: I bought my first oral b in 2016, what would be the equivalent of this model back then. I’ve thoroughly enjoyed it, and used it religiously all these years and it’s still going strong but the rubber face is starting to degrade so I figured I’d upgrade. I was NOT expecting the technology to have advanced so much, it is MUCH more powerful than the old style, with much less vibration and noise. It feels like I’m achieving the same clean in half the time with this one, and the new brush head style doesn’t have that stupid hole that dribbles toothpaste slobber all over your face like the old one. The screen is an added “cool factor” but doesn’t really offer a life changing upgrade aside from being able to see the battery percentage. The new charging dock design is nice, makes it easier to wipe clean without the little peg in the middle. All in all, this is a very nice upgrade and well worth the price. Here’s to the next 10 years of compliments from my dentist!
