headline: Lighter touch than others; higher vibration speed; does a fine job on only one battery.
review_text_raw: I have always used the Arm & Hammer Spin-Brush, and now that it is no longer available, had to find a replacement. I specifically wanted one that used batteries, so I don't have to fuss with a charger when on a trip. I was frankly concerned that there were no two-battery units like the Spin Brush, worried that a one-battery unit would not be as aggressive as I would like. And when I first used this one, it seemed less forceful, so my concern remained. Over a few days I realized that this brush vibrates a a much higher rate than the old two-battery Spin Brush, so it seemed to be doing its job just as well as my old device. In fact, it finally occurred to me that the whole idea of an electric toothbrush was to increase the brushing action rate compared to manually brushing; therefore faster is better, offsetting any lack of aggressive power. I have come to believe that this brush is every bit as good as my old one, even with only one battery. One thing I should mention though, is after several weeks I failed to notice it was moving slower. Just as an experiment I put in a new battery and voila! It began spinning at a much higher rate - I hadn't noticed it slowing down, and will now pay attention as it may need a battery every two to three weeks. That's not a problem as my old Spin Brush needed two batteries over 4 to 5 weeks, so it's basically a "break-even" on battery usage. It's been over a month since I got this brush, and in fact ordered several because they are very well priced on Amazon; I waited to review it honestly and can now say I am comfortable with the lighter touch and faster speed as a better solution to power toothbrushing. I hope this doesn't get discontinued in a couple of years now that I find it so useful!

product_title: Oral-B 3D White Action Power Toothbrush, 1 Count (Colors May Vary), Multi-colored
headline: Works well ... but wears out FAST!
review_text_raw: Mixed feelings on this one. I've been using it for quite a few years now. I like how it works, when it works. It's just that the brush heads and the brush itself wears out a lot quicker than I like. I generally have to change the heads once a month or so. What happens is while that the bristles themselves aren't really worn down at that point, the head itself loses its back and forth rotation. It might "appear" to be still be turning, but check it in the mirror when there is pressure on it, i.e. against your teeth and gums, or test it against your fingernail, and you'll see when it's no longer effective. At that point, it's just basically vibrating in your mouth without cleaning anything. Folks who use this regularly should check for this. It took me a while to realize that after a month or so, I was merely pretending to brush my teeth but not really cleaning anything. Also, once the head wears, the seam/gap between the main piece and the rotating brush part loosens and widens quite a bit and pinches the insides of your mouth. The brush itself tends to wear out after about 4 to 5 months, where once again it still "appears" to be working, but if you check carefully, you'll find that even if you put a new head in there, the rotating properties diminish greatly. I think the inner mechanism simply wears out by then, and no longer connects and moves the brush head as well. Yes, once again, let's all thank corporate America for "Planned Obsolescence". I used to use Sonic Care. The $125 model I bought was good, but no longer held a charge after 2 years. How convenient for Sonic Care. Then I tried their battery operated $40 model, which worked OK but had a really stupidly designed battery cap which allowed water to flow into the compartment. Wow, that's TITANICALLY STUPID!!! Anyway, found this and works OK ... and have been using it since. However, not without the stated reservations. If one were to change the brush and brush heads as often as necessary (which I do), it's not really all that cheap to use. It's actually pretty expensive to use. About 10 to 12 heads and 2 or 3 brushes a year. Do the math. If I find a better alternative, I'll switch without too much nostalgia, ha ha. Note: I do want to state that my brushing routine is probably a lot more thorough and longer than most (about 5 minutes per session), so others may get a longer "effective life" than I get. But still, can't imagine their recommendation of changing the heads every 3 months being adequate. Folks who use this really should monitor the "TRUE effective life" of their brushes and heads, otherwise you might "think" you're brushing your teeth, but might actually be doing nothing to effectively "clean" them. Hope this is helpful. Cheers

reviewer_name: It's a great deal in this price. It working nice and worth buying it. Battery capacity is excellent. I suggest to get this one if you are looking for a smart watch in lower budget.
headline: ★★★★★ Great upgrade from a manual toothbrush
review_text_raw: I’ve been using the Sonicare 7300 for a few weeks now and it’s made a noticeable difference in how clean my teeth feel. The pressure sensor is genuinely useful — it lights up if I’m brushing too hard, which I didn’t realize I was doing with my old brush. The SmarTimer keeps me honest about brushing the full two minutes, and it pulses every 30 seconds to remind you to switch quadrants. Having 12 different brushing settings might sound like overkill, but I actually use a few of them — the gum care mode is gentler on my gums, and the whitening setting feels more thorough for the odd coffee stain. Battery life is excellent — I’m easily getting close to the advertised 21 days on a single charge, so I’m not scrambling to find the charger during travel. The included travel case is a nice touch and keeps everything protected in my bag. Only minor gripe: it’s a bit pricier than a standard electric toothbrush, and replacement brush heads add up over time. But for the overall brushing experience and results, it’s worth it. Bottom line: A solid, feature-packed electric toothbrush that’s easy to recommend if you want something better than a basic model without going full premium.

product_title: Philips Sonicare 7300 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, 3 Brush Head, White
headline: A new level in toothbrush performance, but no wall plug and an intrusive app
review_text_raw: This toothbrush appears to live up to the extravagant claim on the box. I have no way of knowing if the amount of plaque removed is actually 2000% more than what my previous Sonicare could do, but it is a huge improvement. I used to believe the job of an electric toothbrush was to pound my gums into submission, but this model is far more gentle and does a better job of reaching the tricky trouble spots my dentist never tires of pointing out. So I do recommend this product with almost no reservations. But before you open the box you should know that the power cord is a USB-A plug, wall unit not included. Phillips says this is to cut down on electronic waste, which is such an obvious euphemism for "it saves us money" that you wonder why they even bothered. Also, the Sonicare 7300 has Bluetooth connectivity, and you can download an app and connect to, um, your toothbrush. I said what the heck I'll give it a try. The app says it values your privacy but then it doesn't let you complete setup unless you agree to send all data to Phillips so they can help you with suggestions for improving your dental hygiene. Then the home screen comes up and it's a dental chart, at which point I killed the app and uninstalled it. Perhaps you might find such detailed help useful, but I'm not interested in being an unpaid beta tester or belonging to a floating focus group for future products. I've been using a Sonicare for years and will continue to do so. But the way this product is packaged and presented seems to make it just another way that big business is trying to carve off a big slice of my conscious awareness. And I’m getting tired of that. headline: Wait until the price is $199!
review_text_raw: Okay, if you are reading this and the price is higher than $199, WAIT. I just throw a cover on the brush head and toss in my carry-on (note: since it is a rechargeable battery, please put it in your carry-on). The cover for the brush head is useless, so use something else when putting it in luggage. My teeth feel so much cleaner when using this, and I love the discipline it gives me. However, I have seen this vary in price from $199-399. Please don't buy it when it's at its high price. You can get a much better deal!

product_title: Oral-B iO Series 9 Electric Toothbrush with 4 Brush Heads, Aqua Alabaster
headline: Cheaper than a filling & totally worth the investment after 9 months of use
review_text_raw: My dental hygienist recommended this toothbrush about nine months ago. When I mentioned how expensive it was, she said, “It’s still cheaper than getting a filling.” That changed how I looked at the price, so I went for it. The guided brushing app takes the guesswork out of whether I’m actually brushing everywhere. I used it twice a day in the beginning, which really helped me build better brushing habits. Nine months later, I don’t use the app every time anymore, but I still check in here and there to make sure I’m staying on track. The pressure sensor is also super helpful! My dentist mentioned that many people damage their gums and teeth by brushing too hard, and this makes it very obvious when you’re using too much pressure. I’ve had two dental cleanings since switching, and both were probably the quickest I’ve ever had. My dentist and hygienist said everything looked great with very little cleaning needed and mentioned they commonly see this with patients using an Oral-B iO. The brush heads indicate when they need replacing, which for me has been roughly every three months. They’re about $10 per replacement head, so that’s another ~$40 a year to factor into the cost. Not cheap, but reasonable enough for me considering how well the toothbrush has performed. My only complaint is that it’s can be a bit messy. Even after rinsing the head and shaking off excess water, some water/toothpaste tends to run down the handle once it’s on the charger, so I clean the charging base a couple times a week. It’s definitely an investment, but after nine months of daily use and two great dental checkups, I’m very happy I bought it.

At first it seemed like it wasn't brushing my teeth with much of the toothpaste (it kept slinging it everywhere in my mouth) but to fix that I manually brush the toothpaste on my teeth (just enough to cover my teeth with it) then turn on the brush. I always turn it off before I take it out of my mouth because it slings so much. I love the multiple settings you can choose but I always choose the sensitive option. It's not as strong as the daily clean option (daily clean was irritating my gums). The charge lasts a good while. I still use manual brush sometimes & I don't use the Bluetooth stuff so my charge lasts longer. I bought this in December & only had to charge it once. So if you use it more than I do you might need to charge it 2 or 3 times a month. Although I don't travel, I like that it came with a travelling charging case. Also compare the Bluetooth stuff. I don't care about the extra blue tooth stuff so I got this one which is cheaper. Whichever brush you choose, I'm sure you will not be disappointed. This brand is fantastic & I would definitely buy from them again whenever my brush is done for.

product_title: Oral-B iO Series 9 Electric Toothbrush with 4 Brush Heads, Aqua Alabaster
headline: A baffling design flaw in a very expensive toothbrush
review_text_raw: I bought the Oral-B iO Series 9 expecting a premium product. The toothbrush itself has a lot to recommend it, but the charging base has one of the worst design flaws I have encountered in a consumer product. The iO9 is a relatively tall, expensive electronic device, yet while charging it essentially balances upright on a small, shallow magnetic base. There is no meaningful post, socket, collar, or other mechanical support to keep the handle from tipping sideways. Because the handle is so tall, it takes remarkably little lateral force to knock it off the charger. This isn’t a hypothetical concern. I had a previous Oral-B toothbrush fall from its charger and break. With this one, I eventually stopped keeping it conveniently in the bathroom because I didn’t trust the charger to keep it secure. I actually improvised a second magnetic support against the handle when I kept it elsewhere, which dramatically improved its stability. What makes this especially frustrating is that the problem is neither difficult to foresee nor difficult to solve. Competing electric toothbrushes use charging designs that mechanically locate and support the handle. Even a modest post, recess, collar, or other positive restraint could dramatically reduce the chance of an expensive toothbrush being knocked onto a hard bathroom floor. For a flagship toothbrush at this price, this is particularly difficult to excuse. Oral-B put enormous engineering effort into the iO’s display, sensors, pressure detection, Bluetooth connectivity, brushing modes, and app integration. The company should have put comparable thought into the much simpler requirement that the toothbrush remain standing securely while it charges. Prospective buyers should know about this before purchasing because it isn’t something obvious from the feature list. If you buy one, be very careful where you place the charger

I switched to the Oral-B Pro 1000 which was only about $50 and has lasted a very long time. I have a smaller mouth so the heads on the Oral-B work better for me. I heard a dentist say that we should change which hand we brush with to get even cleaning -and he is not wrong! I definitely get one side more than the other. Who knew! I only hope that this one lasts a long time since it was a LOT of money. So far it has been worth it!!

headline: Not as many settings as fancier models, but all the settings I really need
review_text_raw: I've long used Sonicare toothbrushes and since I get good reviews from the dentist, I trust them to keep my teeth fresh and clean. I'm replacing a "fancier" model of toothbrush, but this one has all I need as I always used the regular setting and never paid attention to the brush head replacement warning anyway, replacing my brush head when it seemed worn. It has the same quality of buzz I remember from when my old Sonicare was new (it had in the last month or so seemed clunky, that's why I replaced it.) It's actually easier to use since it has fewer buttons, so I'm not accidentally pushing a button and changing a setting as often. The only thing I don't like is the brush head that came with it, but I replaced it with the Diamond Clean head that I'm used to and it's now basically all the same, just a better price. The brush seems well made and the usual quality of Sonicare products, I'll update if it dies sooner than normal. Overall, I like it. I won't discourage you from buying one of the more expensive models if you want the additional settings, but this has all I really need. So I'll stick with it and making sure to floss to keep my dentist happy.

product_title: Waterpik Sonic-Fusion Flossing Electric Toothbrush Water Flosser, White
headline: Mostly Love
review_text_raw: I had an old waterpik which had seen better days. I had a sonic toothbrush which made my teeth feel wonderful but gave me repetitive stress issues. I finally decided to spend the money on this combo unit and it really is better than the the sum of its parts. It finds all the little hidden bits of leaves and such that distress one's teeth while efficiently cleaning that all important gumline. That is, it does exactly what it's supposed to do. And there's no spitting! Bonus! So, only *mostly* love, because it's just a little too smart for its own good. The brush pulses to make four time divisions then turns off. The only way to have enough water to make it to the end is to have it overflow while filling. Filled up to what looks like the same point is not sufficient. I'm big on saving water, but just a tad more generosity in the tank would actually save water. The old hunch is necessary while doing the combination, or else water will run down one's forearm. I'm not sure if there could be any design solution to that, but it's the brushing part that takes that long. Those who can't hunch can use the brushing part and waterpik part separately. It was hard at first to set the toothbrush in the receptacle, but I learned that holding the hose coil in place, against the unit, it's much easier to seat the brush. The only really bad thing about this is the price--and I paid up not to have black. :)

headline: Takes a bit to figure out and adjust to...
review_text_raw: One thing to know is that although its advertised that you can brush and floss at the same time, the actual application of this concept leaves something to be desired. When you activate the floss and bruch together feature, the flossing rinses all the toothpaste from you mouth before it can be used. So, I brush, then floss. The deep clean is amazing and this has enough power. The brush is set for two minutes and the it will stop automatically. FLAW: if you pause it briefly while brushing, the two minutes restarts. Unlike my phillips sonic care, which you could pause and restart without resetting the two minute time limit. This comes with two heads, one normal size and one for travel, i found they work equally well until one literally broke off in my mouth. I ordered more from Amazon and they have lasted well, so maybe a fluke. Bottom line: This thing does what it does well, but one must be patient and brush first, then floor. Also, don't forget to fill the water reservoir with warm water prior to using flosser. The flosser is super powerful and will clean the heck out of your teeth. Which, as I think about it, is the entire purpose of this thing: clean teeth. This doesn't disappoint.

I'm at this moment going to another brand and I will not buy a Philips product of any kind again. It's a matter of principle to me. I won't. I refuse to bow down to these greedy and wasteful and arrogant corporations who try to manipulate me into more sales by intentionally manufacturing failure into their products. I realize that this has become par for the course, and to many people it doesn't matter-- they're not bothered by constantly buying a new item, over and over and over again. I really don't care. Volume packs (not just 2 heads per Pack) would be good because less shipping and packaging waste would be better for the environment.

headline: Fresh from the dentist clean, tiny design flaws.
review_text_raw: The positive reviews concerning the distinctive clean feel even after the first use are all true. As a matter of fact, almost all positive reviews on this item are somewhat accurate. I would like to focus on the details that I searched for and couldn’t find on reviews both written or in video format. They may seem like “cons” but I must add that for me they were not deal breakers. Instead I’d like to think of them as constructive criticism, since they are details that I would like to see on later generations of this item. Cable management: It is difficult to tell the power source and cable situation from all the photos and videos online, which are edited for aesthetic purposes. I kind of knew what the set up would be from previous experiences with other electronic devices so I knew what to expect. However, for those who are expecting the same sleek, cable-free look from the photos online please take note that if your bathroom has power outlets above the sink area, like most homes in america, there will be a cable bunch up on your countertop. Even if the cable is wound up and tied together, it may still be an atrocious sight for that OCD gem in your home, who probably spends a lot of time at the sink. Power Adaptor: Once plugged in, the power adaptor sticks out over three and a quarter inches from the power outlet, yet another design flaw. With the amount of compact usb adaptors available this shouldn’t be difficult to correct since the company would only need to replace one part. Power adaptor plug: The placement of the power socket on the base station is a bit awkward and creates a distance of about two and a half inches from the wall or backsplash. I have similar electronics with the power socket located below the item, which makes for a neater appearance and freedom to push the item flush to the wall when necessary. Other small details that the shopper should be aware of is the size of the item and color of the brush handle. Please take a closer look and notice that the brush handle is two toned. I think it looks good but, anyone expecting it to be solid white will be thoroughly disappointed. Also, please double check the dimensions of this item and know that it is not a compact design. Definitely not for a countertop where space is at a premium. With all that being said...or typed; I would like to reiterate that all these may seem like “cons” but they really are small details that everyone should know to ensure that they are completely happy with their purchase upon receipt. So, In conclusion this item would be perfect if it was a bit more compact, and the cable/power adaptor issue was resolved. With the portable power core technology available now a days I don’t see why we shouldn’t expect a wireless base station that could hold a charge for a few days in the near future. If you made it this far, thanks for taking the time to read and I hope this helped out even just a lil bit. Bitty boppity, give me the zoppity!

headline: Slightly expensive, but a beast all around!
review_text_raw: Absolutely love this toothbrush! Our dentist recommended we use Phillips Sonicare brushes and at first I was a bit skeptical. I order this about 1 year ago and waited to see how much I liked it before writing a review. After using it for a year, I'm not sure why I never checked one of these out before. Ergonomically, the base of the unit fits well in my hand and is easy to maneuver. The buttons are placed in great positions so I can change the brushing modes or intensity levels easily on the fly. I keep it on a shelf mounted in the battery charger at home, but I have travelled with it a few times and the battery holds a good charge for more than a few days easily. I've never had a situation where I've taken it with me and had it run out of battery. It cleans very nicely and isn't too bulky to have any issue reaching the back molars and has great maneuverability while brushing. I like the fact that it's not very loud as far as noise, and it has convenient 30 second notifications to let you know how long you've been brushing. I typically do one quadrant for 30 seconds for a total of 2 minutes, so it's nice to have the 30 second 'buzz' go off and let me know it's time to move. Two of the coolest features about this electronic toothbrush: (1) - the pressure sensor that let's you know if you're brushing too hard. It's easy to see the light come on when I tend to put too much pressure on the head. (2) I use it in the shower so it's nice that it's mainly waterproof (even if it's not sold as that in the description) but I have been using it in the shower for a while and it's not had any issues. The travel case is nice to have when you need to pack it up and head out on the road. I stay away from home about 4-5 times a year for work and it packs up really nicely and the case obviously keeps it protected. If I had one complaint it would be the unit cost and the replacement head cost. When I first looked them up, I thought the price was crazy!! But it's held up and continues to be my favorite toothbrush of my life, and I've had many in my 50 years on this planet. If you're thinking about getting an electronic toothbrush, this one definitely delivers.

review_text_raw: Second follow-up: This chromebook is worthless. My previous review and follow-up are below. This Asus chromebook is absolute garbage. Don't waste your money on one. Follow-up, 2 months after original review: My original review appears below. I've dropped my rating on this Chromebook from 3 stars to 2. It clearly has issues related to the keyboard. I've had to start using an external keyboard, because no matter how carefully I type on the Chromebook keyboard the cursor randomly jumps to another place on the screen. With an external keyboard, the cursor behaves normally. So much for the convenience of having a laptop when you have to carry a separate keyboard with you wherever you go. Bottom Line: I don't recommend this Chromebook. There's no way I'd buy another Asus product. --------------------- Original Review (November 2023): I bought this after my old Chromebook died. I read a bunch of "best Chromebooks" articles on line, saw this one mentioned a couple of times, and figured it would be a good choice. I should have taken more time to shop. This will work for most of my needs, but after using it for a while I realized I could have gotten another mediocre Chromebook for about half the price without sacrificing functionality. Bottom Line: Shop around. You'll probably find a better deal than this one. I wouldn't recommend it to family or friends. Various pluses and minuses: - No touch screen. I rarely used the touch screen on my previous Chromebook, but on this one I find myself missing that feature. Really, what’s the point of a laptop that can open 180 degrees if you can’t take advantage of a touch screen? Plenty of Chromebooks costing less than this one offer that feature. - What exactly is the “Plus” of a Chromebook Plus? This has the same basic keyboard as other Chromebooks. It has no better battery life than regular Chromebooks. The audio is inferior to my old Chromebook’s. - Bright display with great detail and color saturation. - Looks nice, with the pearl white / light grey color scheme. - Backlit keyboard is a major plus. - Oversized touchpad creates problems if you’re like me and tend to rest the heel of your palms on the deck while typing. You’ll find the cursor jumping all over the place or the screen scrolling down if your palm presses on the touchpad. I’ve had to learn to type without letting any part of my hand other than my fingers touch the computer. - Despite at least a decade of Chromebooks being available, they still refuse to include a Delete key or a Caps Lock key or Page Up/Page Down/Home/End keys. And even though this is a 14-inch display laptop, there is no 10-key numeric pad, even though there's plenty of room for one. - Audio quality is really poor. The speakers are on the bottom of the laptop. If you're going to listen to music, get ready to be disappointed. - Battery life is pretty unimpressive. I use the Chromebook for internet browsing (including viewing videos) and for minor document creation and editing. I usually have between 3 and 5 tabs open. I have not gotten more than 8 hours out of a full charge. The battery indicator is erratic and can't be relied on. (My old Chromebook used to get at least 10 hours on a full charge.)

headline: Amazing Value for Money
review_text_raw: For the price point this laptop delivers an amazing amount of value. I hadn't considered Chromebooks before because I thought of them as underpowered machines that could only do the most basic tasks, but that definitely isn't true here. This laptop boots up within seconds and runs extremely smoothly even when handling a lot of different browser tabs and apps at once. I'm sure it wouldn't be able to compete with computers like a Macbook Pro if you threw computationally intensive tasks at it (video editing, etc.), but it would be unreasonable to expect that at this price point. The touchpad is very generously sized and the keyboard is very comfortable and has a good amount of travel, which I prefer to the flatter keyboards on Macbooks. USB-C charging is also a nice touch as you could use a phone charger on this laptop in a pinch. The construction is plastic, not metal, but it feels very solid and I expect it to hold up well. If you are an Android user, there are a lot of useful integrations with your phone. The availability of many Android and Linux apps (for developers and open source enthusiasts) also opens up a lot of possibilities. Overall, I'd highly recommend this computer as long as you don't absolutely need apps that are only found on Windows or Mac.

headline: Samsung Galaxy Chromebook Go — Affordable, Lightweight, and Built for Basic Computing
review_text_raw: The Galaxy Chromebook Go is exactly what it appears to be: an affordable Chromebook designed for web-based work, education, and everyday tasks. It is not a performance machine, but for the right user it delivers a reliable and straightforward experience. The biggest strengths are portability and simplicity. The laptop is lightweight, easy to carry, and boots quickly. ChromeOS remains one of the easiest operating systems to maintain, making this a good choice for students, casual users, or anyone who primarily works in a browser. Battery life is another positive. In normal use, it easily gets through a day of web browsing, email, document editing, and video streaming without constantly searching for a charger. The 14-inch display provides a comfortable amount of screen space for schoolwork and everyday tasks. While the resolution and color quality won't compete with premium laptops, it is perfectly adequate for browsing, Google Docs, YouTube, and video calls. The integration with Android phones is convenient, particularly for users already invested in the Google ecosystem. File transfers, notifications, and cloud synchronization work smoothly. Performance is where expectations need to be realistic. The Intel Celeron processor and 4GB of RAM handle basic tasks well enough, but heavy multitasking can slow things down. Running numerous browser tabs, streaming video, and using multiple applications simultaneously will push the system to its limits. Storage is limited at 64GB, although ChromeOS relies heavily on cloud services, which helps offset the smaller local storage capacity. For users who primarily work online, this is less of a concern than it would be on a traditional Windows laptop. The build quality is respectable for the price point. It feels durable enough for student use, travel, and everyday carrying. The lightweight design makes it easy to toss into a backpack without much thought. Overall, the Galaxy Chromebook Go is a practical budget laptop that performs well within its intended role. If you need a device for web browsing, email, schoolwork, streaming, and cloud-based productivity, it offers good value. Just don't expect the speed, multitasking ability, or storage capacity of a higher-end laptop.

headline: Good Laptop At A Fair Price
review_text_raw: For the price, this laptop gets a 5 star rating. Well, more like 4.5 but I couldn't give it that. It's a good sized laptop with a clear screen. It's pretty darn fast and it looks pretty sharp. Speakers are decent but not mind-blowing and for what it's worth, it has a camera, which is, again, passable, not mind-blowing. The keyboard on the one I got is more of a darker grey (it's advertised as ash grey, which I believe is a lighter color) but I actually like the darker keyboard better. Typing on the keyboard is pretty smooth too. It could use one or two more outlets on the sides though. You only get one USB Type-A port, one USB Type-C port and a headphone jack. Fine if you're more of a minimalist, but not ideal for multi-tasking work. Also, a little tip; When powering on, all you need to do is press the power button, NOT press and hold. I didn't realize that at first and thought initially that their was a problem. Just a piece of advice. Overall, it's a good laptop, at a fair price and should work well for the "Average Joe". I just got it, so the only question I have is, how long will it last? Hopefully it lasts me quite a while. But we'll see. I also got one of the recommended carrying cases for it, but that's another review for another time. Overall Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

headline: Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.
review_text_raw: This review is mostly about the refurbish service, the computer itself is absolutely fantastic. My expectations for a refurbished computer was that I would get something that would show very modest wear, but work perfectly. I was delighted when I first opened my new Lenovo computer. The screen, keyboard, and touchpad appeared like it was brand new had never been touched. I was initially delighted with my purchase and started loading software and restoring my data. On the second day however, I noticed some unusual indentations around the power button. As I explored it further, I found that the computer had probably been dropped on its side. It actually bent the case enough to make the SD card slot unusable. It also makes the USB connectors quite tight (which may not actually be a bad thing in and of itself - but it's not right). The bottom of the case shows a physical crack and I am moderately concerned about whether there's some hairline fractures or other damage that isn't immediately obvious. The bottom line is, I've decided to keep the computer since it seems to be working fine and I really appreciate the pristine screen and keyboard that I received. I don't use the SD card slot so it's not a big deal to me for that. But I guess I'm just a little disappointed to have received a laptop that was clearly dropped hard enough to bend the case. I know this happed before shipping as the box it was delivered in showed no signs of any drop. It is a bit of a testament to the high-quality build that Lenovo puts into their computers but not a great example of careful oversight on the Amazon reconditioning service. I think they should have been more descriptive about this kind of damage on this particular item (maybe offered it with a bit more discount?)

product_title: HP 14" Laptop 2026 Edition, Intel Processor, 4GB RAM, 128GB Storage
headline: Great Buy, was what i expected it to be
review_text_raw: Keep in mind that this is more of a rant, and I'm half asleep, but this is what I've gone through so far with the product. Originally came from an hp g62 2010 - 2018, was able to make the laptop last. Finally wanted to upgrade and saw this on sale, so I went for it and it was what I wanted in a laptop for what I do: Music, School, Youtube, Slaughtering Demons. The rant and rave of an individual: The screen is very nice, I can confirm it is an In-plane Switching Monitor or (IPS) as I do not have to center the screen or move my body to get a great view of it, unlike a lot of TN panels that I've used back in the day. The disassembly of the device is very very simple, remove the screws from the bottom of the case and the case pops off, might need a thin tool to pry the case off a bit (only con here) and you'll see the ram and the hard drive and the nvme along with the fans which make it easy for upgrades and cleaning. Also the battery is not soldered into the board and easily comes out for replacement after you remove some screws. All screws I noticed were Phillip's head. (I like to watch disassembly videos in case something happened, that way I can tear into it and hopefully fix the issue.) The ram is decent for 12 gigs, a 4 gig stick and an 8 gig stick, but I plan on upgrading the ram soon. Now after uninstalling a few things and setting windows to use less resources, I idle at about 18-19% which isn't bad at all, depends on what you do though. I do believe the manufacturer specifications have tested up to 16 gigs of 2666 on the board, however; there are cases with other omen laptops, where you can plop in 16 gigs in each dimm slot for a total of 32 gigs, wouldn't recommend it because it's not officially supported, but I will go ahead and try it (making sure i'm at the latest bios update from hp), and will provide an additional review/update. (I like to run a lot of things at once.) The processor is very nice, windows shows that i have 4 physical cpus and 8 logical processors, and I idle at 0% after turning the thing on (which mine booted into windows less than 3 seconds with the nvme 128 gig harddrive). I plan on upgrading the nvme from 128 gigs to 1 terabyte, might clone the drive or just grab a fresh install of windows 10 and slap it on a usb drive and fresh install, go from there. From what I read on the specification sheet for the dc0010nr, I think a cap of 512 Gigs nvme was officially tested and supported, but I'm going another 512 and see how the machine fairs. The 1 terabyte hard drive isn't slow at all, but I have nothing on it but a few games and some music, I constantly keep it defragged. The sound on the laptop is definitely an upgrade from my old hp g62 via software and hardware, but i use headphones into the 3.5mm jacks for mic and playback anyways. when it comes to gaming: Doom 2016 gives about 100 to 130fps on 1080p, ultra + open glide settings.... battlefield 1 on 1080p ultra gives about 45+ on mp and 60+ sp, drop it to high and it gives about 60+ but it depends on what map and what all is going on via gameplay. The heat on the laptop isn't bad, the machine will get warm and the fans will kick into high gear almost like a delay, but there is absolutely no throttling and when i'm finished with my gaming, the fans kick off to silent almost immediately. Also with the gpu, this is a verified gtx 1050 ti with 4096MB of vram in it. Final note: I think it's worth what I payed for: 799.99. If my desktop crashes and burns, it's a great replacement for it. It absolutely destroys solitaire and minesweeper along with other office products like excel spread-sheeting and you're in need for a couple of Pareto diagrams or 3 point beta distributions to resolve employee padding with P.M.O affairs making sure the stakeholders are happy. Alas I digress... I unboxed it, i pressed the power button and it immediately shot into windows and was ready to go. :)

headline: Good hardware for the money but don't upgrade or fix yourself
review_text_raw: Pros: good hardware, SSD running the OS is very fast. Runs games better and smoother than my Xbox one. Light and durable case. Cons: writing this about a month in. This is a laptop for setting on a desk and plugged in at all times. Too hot to game in your lap and the power supply could boil an egg. The power receptacle into the laptop feels fragile and could wiggle and start to break if you aren't careful, and probably is not an easy fix if you can't charge your battery anymore. Windows 10 is full of bloatware and self advertising for Microsoft and takes some settings surfing to disable apps and widgets that you cannot uninstall. After 2 weeks I sat the laptop down to use the bathroom and when I came back there was a huge crack in the LCD screen. No big deal I thought I watched a video to replace it myself and ordered "omen replacement LCD 15.6" for 60 dollars. When I pulled the case and battery I started to realise why this is so cheap. I DO NOT recommend replacing or doing any work on them yourself, I bet when you send yours in for repair they just throw it in the garbage and send you a new one. The Screen was unnecessarily high bond taped to the case and crumpled as I peeled it off. Once I got rid of the tape and the now ball of screen I saw that what I bought isn't the same screen at all and doesn't even fit inside the case. After some hard googling I finally found the screen I need and it's $150 dollars. If you buy this I highly recommend getting the warranty and just send it in, probably a rule for laptops in general

review_text_raw: Eh... My fault for not really researching the laptop before buying but didn't realize Chromebooks use their own operating system and not windows. I usually try to stay away from touch screen laptops because the screens use to have a noticable "fake" or hazy look to them but this one you wouldn't even be able to tell if they didn't tell you. Keyboard has a very plastic feel too it, and for whatever reason they replaced the caps lock button with a button that opens the apps tab. Setup was great if you have a Google phone/Google account definitely the fastest I've ever been able to set up a new computer. Overall.... Great for a highschool student and probably can't beat the price. Otherwise I'd spend a little more and get something that actually has windows the chrome OS looks similar to MacBook.

headline: Absolutely amazing for the size and price.
review_text_raw: I don't write a lot of product reviews, but this item deserves one. This speaker is tiny - about 4 inches square and perhaps 1.25 inches thick. It's heavy, solid, good-looking, and seemingly well made. But it's the performance that amazes me. I have been an audio technician since 1977, and I have never seen a speaker this small, bluetooth or not, at any price, that sounds this good. Within its limited volume limit of about 80dBa, it is positively amazing. Even the smallest details are well-executed. It has rubber feet on the bottom and on the back, and those feet are pneumatic - they work very effectively as dampeners to keep the speaker from vibrating the surface they sit on, or from moving around. The metal mesh grille has a black grille cloth behind it to keep dust out of the driver and to make it look that much better. Want to be amazed? Pair this with your phone, pull up a music streaming service, and the set the little thing on the floor in a corner. Be prepared to be amazed. And for 20 bucks? I'm buying about three more of them.

headline: Cuts through gym interference, music never stutters
review_text_raw: I’m a group fitness instructor at a busy gym, and I teach high-energy classes like HIIT and bootcamp. My speaker is on for about four hours straight every morning, and it needs to handle a room full of wireless interference: Apple Watches, wireless earbuds, fitness trackers, even other small Bluetooth speakers. The X2 cuts through all of that like it’s nothing. I leave my phone at the front of the studio, then walk to the back row to check squat form, grab weights by the windows, step outside to get water. The music never skips, never stutters, never drops. Not once in over 30 classes. The sound quality matters too. I need the beat to be crisp so my class can follow along, and the bass needs to punch through without getting muddy. The X2 delivers. My students can hear every count clearly even at the back of the room. And the IPX7 waterproofing has been a lifesaver: sweat, spilled water bottles, even a rogue splash from someone’s hydro flask. Just wipe and go. For any fitness instructor or personal trainer working in a busy wireless environment, the X2’s Bluetooth is a workhorse. It doesn’t get overwhelmed. And the sound and waterproofing make it perfect for the gym. Class after class, it just delivers without any drama.

It was recommended by my brother, and for the price, it performs better than a lot of bigger-name brands I’ve tried. The sound quality is crisp and clear, with no noticeable degradation so far even after regular use. It delivers enough volume and fullness to work well indoors or outdoors without sounding muddy or overly distorted. Connection has also been straightforward. Devices pair quickly, and the USB-C support is a welcome feature compared to older connection types. It holds a charge for a long time, which makes it reliable for extended use or outdoor settings. The tradeoff is that it’s not a particularly fast recharge, so you’ll want to plan ahead rather than expect a quick top-off before heading out. The waterproofing is another plus, especially for outdoor use or keeping around a work area where accidents happen. Combined with the long battery life, it feels like a speaker designed more for actual use than just shelf appeal. Now comes the real test: durability. In this era of planned obsolescence, the question is how well it will hold up after a year or more of regular use. That’s ultimately what separates decent electronics from genuinely reliable gear. Still, first impressions are strong. The overall design feels practical and time-tested, with a bit of an old-school sensibility that focuses more on utility than gimmicks. Overall, this speaker punches above its price point. It’s practical, sounds good, connects quickly, and avoids a lot of the overhyped branding that bigger companies rely on. For the money, it’s been a solid buy.

headline: Excellent audio with consistent levels
review_text_raw: This is my third and hopefully final soundbar in my hunt for something that just works. I did a bit of research that landed me on the Bose TV Speaker. This is for a living room with a 20' ceiling and a TV mounted above the fireplace. With young kids, the TV is usually on their shows during the day or mom and dad trying to watch something in the evening. We aren't looking to be fully immersed in booming action movies, dialogue is the focus. The last one I had would drown out dialogue with background music and I was always trying to adjust the levels. This is perfect, I don't have to fiddle with it and it does a great job of staying consistent and I never have an issue hearing dialogue. It connected easily to my Roku TV and even supports Roku TV integration, allowing me to adjust things through the TV interface. I like that it's relatively small while packing powerful audio. The only problem I had may have been due to my TV - when I connected to the Bose over Bluetooth it messed up the hdmi-arc connection and my TV was no longer powering the Bose on and off, I had to factory reset the TV to resolve this and I haven't tried the Bluetooth connection since. Bottom line is that I didn't want to spend more than $200 and I just wanted something that would just work - apparently that is a unicorn in today's age of soundbars - and the Bose TV Speaker is that unicorn

headline: GREAT Lil Speaker! Louder Than Most & Crisp Sound
review_text_raw: So this little speaker packs a punch! It is far more than I expected. We have a bunch of small speakers around the house, the kids love to listen to music, I like to listen when I'm in the shower or kitchen. You can never have too many. It sounds phenomenal if you stand in the corner of your room and hold it up above your head. It will fill the whole room. If you laid on the counter the sound deadens a little it's not as full but it's still great. I carry it around from room to room and toss it wherever I can when I am cleaning or doing something. The battery is really good! I charge it every couple of days and I use it for several hours every day. I like the lights, my kids especially like the lights, it paired literally instantly. I flipped my Bluetooth on and turned the speaker on and had a request to pair. Literally could not be any easier, it could not be any more portable if it had to be, comes with charging cable and instructions but I don't think anyone would need the instructions. I love it! I would recommend it across the board! If you didn't carry it around like I do I would say this would be great as an alternative for speakers in a small room. Obviously it's not going to blow your eardrums out but it's loud enough that it overpowers water running, sounds throughout the house, and when you get it in the right place it really just fills the room. Great bass, not too much not too little. Some portable speakers have so much bass that it hurts my ears when I turn it up loud. Very clean sound, crisp. But please revert back to what I said earlier about its location. Very happy with this little fella and its functionality. Easy easy!

headline: A good unit with many features, and perhaps a tad pricey because of those features
review_text_raw: In the world of Bluetooth speakers, this one struck me as a tad pricey, but not overly so. I am hoping for quality of build to let this thing last many years, and we'll see how that works. Meantime, the sound is nice. I use it mostly to listen to podcasts (including podcasts with music) and to stream stuff from Amazon music and Pandora, and the sound quality is OK for me for those purposes. I haven't used the bass emphasis button, finding I don't need that for what I listen to. The lighting feature is amusing, but I keep it off to lengthen battery life. The speakers provide a stereo sound, but I can't really discern a stereo result. Which is OK, I wasn't really expecting much in those regards, considering the speakers are so close to one another. The unit pairs with my iPhone extremely quickly. Haven't had it long enough to assess battery life (which can be a function of volume, use of lighting effects, use of the bass effect, and perhaps the phase of the moon). Overall, it meets my expectations fully and feels like it is well made.

product_title: DOSS SoundBox Pro Bluetooth Speaker, 20W Stereo Sound, Active Extra Bass
headline: Sound is flat and muddy. EQ is required to listen to this
review_text_raw: I have been using a FUGOO bluetooth speaker for about two years and have been very happy with it. I have been working from home since the beginning of the pandemic and decided I wanted another speaker. One to set to the laptop and another for my phone. I always peruse the various offerings and extensively read the reviews. The reviews were high for this speaker so I thought I would give it a shot. What sold me was the "stereo" connection between two speakers, price and ratings. I bought two. I have Prime so the speakers were delivered quickly and safely the next day. Packaging was fine. The speakers come with a male-to-male 3.5 mm aux cable, which can come in handy if you wish to connect directly to a music source. It also comes with a USB-B charging cable. |The speakers were 50% charged when I received them. I fairly quickly connected to my phone (Android) with the bluetooth pairing. The "party lights" are ok and you have your choice of three primary solid colors or four changing colors. I just keep it on the solid Blue color as I find them a bit distracting when working. I wish they gave the option for either a solid (not flashing) border color or the ability to just turn the lights off, but they do not. The build is solid and not a light , cheap "plasticky" feel. The buttons are rubber and have a good feel when pressed. After playing a round with the different settings and volume controls I decided to give the second speaker a run and see what the "stereo" connection sounded like. Connecting the stereo connection was a bit more cumbersome but, finally was able to get he speakers to talk to each other and I was good to go. I had read an earlier review that said the stereo sound was not true stereo and the same sound came out of both speakers. That was not true for my first run. I found excellent stereo separation and I recommend you try a few songs to test the capabilities of the speakers connected to each other. My first song to go was the classic Led Zepplin "Whole Lotta Love", if you are familiar with that song you know it was originally recorded for "quad" sound to give the feeling of a swarming and swirling wall of sound. The stereo effect was quite noticeable and clear. Other songs were The Cars, "Moving in Stereo" and the seminal Billy Thorpe "Children of the Sun". The stereo works! Sound. To this point, I have had nothing but good things to say about these speakers. However, here is where I am disspointed. The sound of my music comes across very flat. My recording are FLAC (lossless) and I expect to hear the full range of music with bright crisp and clean highs as well as clear solid bass and crisp mid-range. In a word these speakers are "muddy". I don't need to apply the Bass boost as I feel it would only degrade the quality further. The speakers do put out a fair amount of sound and even at low settings tend to be a bit loud (when working). I needed to play with my equalizer settings to try and resolve the muddy issues and that helped to some extent, but it only works on downloaded songs played directly through an installed player. If you are going to utilize a streaming service, such as Spotify, Pandora, Radio Paradise or even a cloud based player such as Google Player, then you are stuck with the muddiness quality. It would be nice if DOSS had a sound app that other bluetooth speakers, ear buds and head phones have. Until then you are relegated to a well-built speaker with limited capabilities. One note the sound will tend to do better at about a 2/3 to 3/4 volume, but at that level you would probably want to be outside as it tends to be a bit loud for inside use, unless you are cleaning and want to be able to listen to the music from any room in the house. I then switched to a few different genres, Jazz, Blues, Classical.....again the sound, though a bit better was flat to me. I did use the speakers for a phone call and the microphone worked well, with the other person saying they did not hear back ground noise or echo. Over all, I suppose you get what you pay for. The build is good and solid, functionality is fairly easy and intuitive. The stereo aspect with two speakers is a huge plus! Unfortunately, the sound quality pulls this speaker set down from a solid 4 stars to a standard 3 stars. They aren't bad speakers, I just can't get over how flat they are.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Max Bluetooth Speaker - Portable Wireless Party Speaker, IP67 Waterproof, Rope Handle, Up to 20 Hours of Playtime, USB-C, Built-in 3.5mm AUX Input, Black
headline: It brings the bass
review_text_raw: As a long-time owner of the first-generation Bose SoundLink Mini, I had high expectations for the Bose SoundLink Max, and it did not disappoint. This review covers various aspects of the speaker, including sound quality, durability, ease of use, compatibility, setup, and design. The SoundLink Max lives up to the Bose name. After testing it with a myriad of musical genres, I was blown away by the fullness of the sound. The bass is so powerful that you can feel it, yet it does not drown out the mid and treble frequencies. It is worth noting that the initial EQ settings are flat, which might be why some users have complained about the lack of fullness. This could be addressed by repurposing the shortcut button for quick EQ adjustment. The SoundLink Max meets the IP67 standards, making it rugged, dustproof, and waterproof. Weighing nearly five pounds, it is heavy, but this is an acceptable trade-off for the durability it offers. In a pinch, you could even use it as a brick or a weapon for defending yourself from zombies! Using the SoundLink Max is straightforward. Press the power button, then play to start enjoying your music. When it’s time to change settings, the buttons are clearly labeled. The Max charges via a supplied USB-C cord and power block and can also serve as a portable power device. This is my main point of contention and it is not specifically with the Max, but with Bose as a whole. They have partnered with Qualcomm/Snapdragon for their HD Audio, which is currently confined to the Android ecosystem. As an iPhone user, I felt a little left out in the cold. Straight out-of-the-box, the Max was nearly ready to go. It took two seconds to pair and less than that to start charging, thanks to the included USB-C cable and power brick. The Bose app was easy to find and quick to install. I was able to set up an account and start using the app right away. While the setup was easy, more emphasis should be placed on the necessity of using the app to achieve the best sound, as the default EQ settings are a bit flat. The SoundLink Max boasts a sleek and simple design. There are no unnecessary lights or reminiscent designs to distract you—just a rugged exterior that protects the speakers while delivering excellent sound quality. The rope handle is a nice feature that accentuates the rugged yet simple design. They are easily changeable for other colored handles and shoulder straps, which are available at a steep premium on the Bose website. The Bose SoundLink Max is a phenomenal portable speaker that lives up to the high standards we expect from Bose. After several days of testing in various locations and with different music genres, I have not been disappointed. While there have been some reports of less-than-fantastic sound quality, this issue is easily resolved by adjusting the EQ settings in the Bose app. The final question is, is the SoundLink Max worth the $400 price tag? The simple answer is yes, it is worth every penny.

headline: Sounds like a box of farts, and not in a good way. Maybe it is broken?
review_text_raw: When I first unpacked this product and listened to it, I was completely won over. What an amazing first impression. Excellent soundstage. Wide, detailed, clear, everything you could want. Unfortunately, once you take the volume to even close to 50%, which you'd want to do in many situations and certainly outside, and it all falls apart. Hero to zero in the blink of an eye. The bass has a fart-like quality to it which ruins everything. The only way to make this sound acceptable is to use the EQ to take the bass pretty much to nothing or even a negative setting. In which case, you could buy almost any other Bluetooth speaker for less than half the price that is going to sound just as good. Many of the reviews talk about bass and presence, but that's only true at really low levels. At least assuming the unit I was sent is working to factory spec. And don't get me wrong, I'm not listening to music at window rattling levels designed to annoy the neighbors. I'm not even listening to tracks that I think are especially bass heavy. As an example I listened to Clocks by Coldplay. Hardly a hardcore bass fest. The opening bars sounded amazing. But as soon as the gentle bass chords joined the music, the speaker lost itself. I tried the product on a hard wooden stool. A hard wooden deck. A patio table. A different patio table. A few feet away. A few meters away. It really didn't matter. I played with numerous EQ settings. But the bottom line is that it just can't put out bass in any real capacity unless you are willing to lower the sound to a background volume. In which case, it's amazing. To me, the bass being available in such a quiet and tiny sweet spot, makes it kind of worthless to include it at all. I have a pair of B&O Explore speakers, that sound amazing and can be set as a stereo pair. If you buy them well you can have two of them for $100 less than this Bose. What they lack in bass, they more than make up for in incredible sound stage, stereo separation and can go toe to toe in terms of detail. The thing is, they also KNOW they can't do much bass, so they don't even try. Bose, is trying too hard to make bass happen that apparently isn't possible in this system. Just like I don't drive my car at 100 mph ever, I want it to be capable of that. I want it to accelerate from zero to sixty in under seven seconds, even though it's not how I drive. And when it comes to speakers, I want to know that if I want to turn up the volume a little, it isn't going to sound like a box of farts. I tried to give it every opportunity to impress, but it failed at everything except very quiet listening levels. I was mainly streaming from Apple Music, and I even looked for songs offered at their highest bitrate or including spacial audio technology. For the price they are charging, there is no way I keep this item. It is already in the box ready to go to UPS. Maybe it would be different if you have a different sound source, are using a different streaming service, are using AUX or Android. My tests were iOS based, and bluetooth streaming. Tracks that I have previously tested on my Marshall Woburn II speaker as an example, with the same source equipment.

review_text_raw: Overall Impression This is my second speaker from the JBL Charge line, and once again, I’m impressed. The Charge 6 builds on what already worked well in previous models while delivering dependable performance, strong sound quality, and easy usability. Design & Build Quality The speaker feels sturdy and well-constructed without being overly bulky. It’s portable, easy to move around, and sits securely on a variety of surfaces. Whether placed on a kitchen counter, coffee table, or taken outdoors, it feels durable enough for everyday use. Setup & Connectivity Setup is quick and straightforward. I’ve had no issues pairing the Charge 6 with any of my devices. Bluetooth connection is stable and reliable, something I really value, as I’ve owned other speakers that occasionally failed to appear or dropped connection. In this area, the Charge 6 performs consistently well. Sound Quality For a speaker in this price range, the sound quality is impressive. Volume: Gets surprisingly loud for its size. Clarity: Remains stable and clear even at higher volumes, with minimal distortion. Bass: Punchy and full without overpowering the mids and highs. Vocals: Crisp and easy to distinguish. The overall sound profile feels balanced and energetic, making it versatile for different genres of music. Compared to the JBL Charge 5 I upgraded from the Charge 5, which already delivered excellent sound. The difference here isn’t dramatic, but the Charge 6 feels slightly louder and punchier, with a bit more fullness at higher volumes. It’s more of a refinement than a complete redesign, but a noticeable and appreciated one. Ideal Use Cases This speaker is well-suited for small to medium-sized rooms and performs great for small outdoor gatherings or backyard settings. I liked it enough to purchase a second unit and place one in each corner of my living space for a more balanced, room-filling setup. In my experience, listening at around 60% volume yields approximately 17–19 hours on a single charge, which has been more than sufficient for daily use. If I had one minor critique, it would be that battery life drops more noticeably at very high volumes. For example, during an all-day beach trip or extended outdoor event where the speaker is running near maximum volume, you may need to recharge sooner than expected. While the upgrade from the Charge 5 isn’t dramatic, it’s a meaningful refinement. Overall, it’s a great value for the performance it provides and an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a versatile Bluetooth speaker.

headline: The Ultimate Audio Wingman: Why the JBL Charge 6 Brings the Boom Without the Bulk!
review_text_raw: We all know that feeling of finding the perfect piece of gear that just clicks with our lifestyle, and that is exactly what happened when I got my hands on the JBL Charge 6. In a sea of portable speakers that overpromise and underdeliver, this crisp, white beauty stands out as a true heavyweight in a surprisingly compact package. I am always on the move, whether I am out working in the garage, heading to the beach, or just kicking back by the backyard fire pit, and I need a device that can keep up. What struck me immediately about this particular model is how it completely redefines what a mid-sized portable speaker should be capable of handling. It is not just about making noise; it is about delivering a premium experience that seamlessly integrates into whatever crazy adventure my weekend throws at me. Let us talk about the absolute core of this device: the sound. The Bold JBL Pro Sound alone is phenomenal, but the real magic here is the AI Sound Boost technology. I have listened to countless audio setups, and I can confidently say that this proprietary audio processing algorithm fundamentally changes the game. It actively analyzes the music in real-time, pulling maximum acoustic performance out of the drivers while keeping distortion virtually non-existent, even when you crank the volume all the way up. The low-end bass kicks with a satisfying, punchy depth that you can feel in your chest, while the mids and highs remain exceptionally crisp and clear. Whether I am blasting classic rock anthems or heavy hip-hop tracks, the soundstage feels massive, filling up the entire patio or living room with rich, immersive audio that makes you forget you are listening to a portable unit. Now, an incredible-sounding speaker is useless to me if I have to baby it, which is why the rugged build of the Charge 6 is such a massive win. This thing is built like an absolute tank. It boasts serious waterproof and drop-proof credentials, meaning I never sweat it when a sudden rainstorm rolls in or when someone inevitably knocks it off the picnic table. I have watched it take a tumble directly onto hard concrete and brush it off like it was nothing, keeping the tunes rolling without a single hiccup. Adding to its utilitarian charm is the newly integrated, sturdy removable carrying strap. It sounds like a minor detail, but having that secure strap makes hauling it around infinitely easier. I can sling it over a bag, hang it from a hook in the workshop, or just keep a solid grip on it while hiking, all without compromising its sleek, streamlined white aesthetic. Perhaps the most crucial factor for a device that travels this much is endurance, and the battery life on the Charge 6 is nothing short of legendary. JBL packed this beast with up to 28 hours of playtime, and it absolutely delivers on that promise. I have taken it on multi-day camping trips and never once had to reach for a wall charger. But the absolute lifesaver is the built-in powerbank feature. We all know how fast smartphones drain when streaming high-quality music outdoors, so having the ability to plug my phone directly into the speaker to juice it back up while the playlist keeps pumping is incredibly practical. It is the ultimate two-in-one companion that ensures neither the party nor my phone dies prematurely. This speaker does not just meet my high standards for portable audio; it utterly shatters them.

headline: Honest review of the JBL Charge 6 portable bluetooth speaker
review_text_raw: At almost 60 years old, I’ve experienced just about every kind of audio system imaginable — component stereo systems, high-end car audio setups, premium headphones, earbuds, home theater systems, and portable speakers from many of the biggest brands. Because of that, it takes quite a bit to genuinely impress me when it comes to sound quality. The JBL Charge 6 absolutely impressed me. What JBL accomplished with this speaker is remarkable. The sound is incredibly powerful considering such a small footprint. This thing is compact enough to fit easily into almost any backpack, yet it produces bold, room-filling sound that feels much larger than the speaker itself. The audio quality is excellent. The highs are crystal clear, vocals sound clean and detailed, and the bass is deep, punchy, and robust without sounding muddy or distorted. Even at higher volumes, the sound remains balanced and enjoyable. The volume range is outstanding — this speaker gets surprisingly loud while still maintaining clarity. I’ve owned expensive audio equipment over the years, and honestly, the sound coming from this little speaker is shocking for its size. Whether indoors, outdoors, traveling, relaxing at home, or using it near water, the JBL Charge 6 consistently delivers an impressive listening experience. Bluetooth connectivity is fast and simple, and the portability is one of its biggest strengths. JBL also did a great job with durability. The waterproof and drop-proof design makes it ideal for everyday life, travel, and outdoor use without constantly worrying about damaging it. Battery life and durability seem to vary somewhat based on user experiences. Many people report excellent battery life that lasts all day, while others feel it could be better depending on usage and volume levels. Most users praise the rugged build quality, though a few have experienced durability concerns after heavy use. Overall, this speaker exceeded my expectations. After decades of owning and listening to high-end audio equipment, I can honestly say the JBL Charge 6 delivers an incredible amount of performance, clarity, and power for such a compact portable speaker. Small speaker. Massive sound. Very impressive product from JBL.

product_title: Sony SRS-XB100 Wireless Bluetooth Portable Lightweight Speaker, Black
headline: XB100 vs. ULT 1
review_text_raw: Tested it side by side with rhe ULT 1. Item is good, but the ULT 1 is louder / has more bass. I would still recommend to someone on a limited budget, but they're getting what they pay for. I tested next to a busy road. Noticeably quieter than the ULT 1, but you can still hear it. Bass is definitely weaker than the ULT 1. All that being said, it is impressive for a small speaker. You can see the size difference in the photo. Definitely great for indoors, suitable for personal listening (right next to you) outside. You'll lose the sound 25-50 feet away from you outside though. Its a good deal under $40, I grabbed it for $33. Not worth it over $50. I picked the ULT 1 up for $78, just to compare. Ended up returning this one because I don't need both. Also, you can customize EQ on the ULT 1, but not this one. Sound is very clear, great for a small speaker, but max loudness is comparable to a phone on max volume rather than a portable speaker. Worth it if you want a speaker that is tiny and cheap, but if you're looking for great bass without the cord / bulkiness - consider the ULT 1. Btw, ULT 1 is a good deal under $100, don't pay over that for that one. But its legit worth it, if you're willing to pay about double the price of this one. Sound improvement isn't double exactly, but the bass and overall loudness are definitely noticeable. Final note - form factor, design, size, and build quality are great on both. You could feel comfortable using either inside or outside and both are light. 4 stars here instead of 5 because of the bass limitation and lack of EQ - keep in mind the bass is better than every other speaker at this price point (under $50), just can't compete with others under $100.

product_title: Sony SRS-XB100 Wireless Bluetooth Portable Lightweight Speaker, Black
headline: Relax, It's a Sony
review_text_raw: I love the sound. This little Bluetooth speaker cost me a little more than half a Benjamin and turns my smartphone into a respectable sound system. Plus, it’s compact, portable, battery powered (for approximately six to eight hours at high volumes w/quick recharge using the newest standardized rechargeable/data connection that has a small, rounded-rectangular “pill”-shaped reversible plug), waterproof, and incredibly drop-resistant. When I drop it, instead of worrying I tell myself, "Relax, it's a Sony, it will be fine," and it always is. This is actually my second one. I dropped the first speaker many dozens of times over the past four years (easily 50+) and it continued to play flawlessly. What finally pushed me to replace it wasn’t normal wear and tear. During a cross-town move from Brooklyn to Manhattan, I carelessly packed it in an open box. A sudden stop from the moving van bounced it out of the unsecured box, and a heavy table ended up resting on top of it. Amazingly, it wasn’t crushed or dented. The only issue was a slight decline in sound quality at higher volumes — the bass was no longer as clean. Considering what it survived, I was thrilled to find another one just like it for sale on Amazon. Because it’s affordable and so durable, I kept the original as a backup and bought a new one.

product_title: Sony SRS-XB100 Wireless Bluetooth Portable Lightweight Speaker, Black
headline: High Quality, Low Volume
review_text_raw: The SRS-XB100 is a lightweight, highly portable speaker. The sound quality is excellent, especially for such a small unit. Highs are crisp and clean, mids are solid and clear, and lows are punchy and robust. The interface is easy to use, although the stereo pairing function can be a little finicky. But where this small speaker really falls short is the volume. For several years I've used two similar, slightly larger speakers from a different brand: one in my bathroom and one in my kitchen, pairing them both together for outdoor listening. When it was time to replace them I ordered two of the SRS-XB100 and tried the same approach. But I found that a single speaker was barely loud enough to be heard over the shower, and that I needed to pair them together to hear music clearly while cooking. I wouldn't even try to use them for outdoor activities. In short, if you want a small speaker for use at moderate volumes in a sterile listening environment, this is an excellent choice. But if you enjoy music at higher volumes while participating in other activities you should look elsewhere.

product_title: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 Portable Waterproof Speaker - Black
headline: Definitely in the "You Can't Go Wrong With It" category.
review_text_raw: Great speaker. I have tried several brands of these bt speakers; Tribit, Soundcore, Harmon Kardon, Bose, B&O and a few others. None compare to this for the qualities I want in a bluetooth speaker. I see it as a personal speaker for listening to music privately and for podcasts. I have a nice stereo system for serious listening, but it's not always convenient to do that. What I found was that there is a lot of sound profile manipulation by the producers of these products favoring bass output, because that's what a large portion of the buying public thinks is "good sound", with the resulting side effects on the rest of the profile.. The Wonderboom might tweak it a little, but not even close to overdone. The sound quality is really solid, including the mids and trebles. Clear and full; undistorted. Bass is solid, but balanced. Clearly present but not obnoxious. That's number one. It is light, and it is the easiest to use of the bunch. The 360 degree sound is a real plus and does fill the room. It is well protected against dust and moisture, and it floats if you drop it in the lake. It is very nicely shaped, easy to pick up, hold, carry , pack. Use it anywhere. It also has zero over compensating frills, like apps and equalizers, which are a total waste of time on something that you just want to work and not have to fuss over. This one does just that, and it has better sound quality than all the others tested, except the Luna 2 and B&O a1, but, at lower volumes it is pretty much indistinguishible.. I've sent one to my son and one to my daughter, who took it to the lake house last weekend and said it was a real hit on the dock and the boat with over a dozen people in the group, whom she said were universally complimentary. It does have two adjustments. The basic mode is "standard'. Push the button once and it gives you an "outdoor boost"; again and you get "podcast mode", which I found not to be necessary, but it does help if there is ambient noise, like, say, a shower. I also tried it in stereo with another unit and it's great. I don't really need that function, but I just might hang onto the second one and do the stereo anyway. These these little guys are affordable enough that you can get two for less than a competitive single unit will cost and you can bet that they'll sound better. Great product. Well conceived, well designed and well executed. A truly great product.

product_title: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 Portable Waterproof Speaker - Black
headline: Sound-mode Announcer Voice is TOO LOUD
review_text_raw: This speaker could have been great. I still use it, but I wouldn't buy it again and wouldn't recommend it to others, for two reasons. The primary reason is the volume of the voice that speaks when the sound mode is changed. To others it may be a minor thing and not at all a dealbreaker, but it has not yet ceased to be very jarring to me. When in the shower, I use this speaker to listen to audiobooks, so every time I turn it on, I switch to "Podcast Mode". I suppose because it is waterproof, it only has sealed buttons that must be repeatedly pressed to cycle through options, rather than switches that one can "set and forget". I wish the speaker had memory for the last configuration used, because without that or toggle switches, this means that every time I turn it on I have to press the button on the bottom of the speaker twice so that it cycles to my preferred sound mode setting. Which in turn means that every. single. time. it shouts out "OUTDOOR BOOST!", "PODCAST MODE!" Because no matter how low the volume is turned down, the sound mode is completely independent and has one volume level: SHOUTING. Okay... maybe it's not truly shouting, but it's very loud and cannot be altered. As I said, it's quite jarring. The secondary reason I'd hesitate to recommend it to others is that I've noticed the sound cuts out every once in a while. This is with the paired source only a foot or two away, and I've never had the sound cut out like this with any other bluetooth speaker, so it seems like the issue is with this speaker itself. It's too bad, because if it wasn't for those two complaints, I could really love this speaker. It's waterproof, which obviously was a big selling point for me and my "I don't want to waste listening time with such mundane things like a shower" attitude. It's compact and has a small sturdy loop at the top which makes it easy to carry around and hang--you guessed it--in the shower (from a sturdy in-shower towel rack, using an S-hook). It's not a cheap lightweight speaker, so I wouldn't trust a suction-cupped device to hold it. And despite its small size, it is easily loud enough, with no distortion, to hear clearly over noisy things like the shower or running fans. I wish I could give it another half-star, because listing all these positive qualities almost makes me think three stars is not enough. But I wish the review that led me to buying this speaker had warned how loud that sound-mode announcer voice is, and with that and the sound cut-outs, I just can't give it four.
