product_title: Ninja Specialty Drip Coffee Maker, DualBrew Pro, Black, CFP301
headline: Great Coffee, But Not Perfect
review_text_raw: The media could not be loaded. Let it be known: I love coffee, things that make my life easier, and multi-functional products. Unfortunately for Ninja, I also love to criticize, and I certainly have some issues with this coffee maker. But before that, what's good about it? It is incredibly easy to switch from K-Cups, grounds, or hot water needs. Since I moved to grinding my own beans, I no longer have much of a use for the K-Cup adapter, but it is incredibly easy to use and clean. Strangely, Ninja didn't put notches in the K-Cup holder, so if it seals just right it will take some prying with fingernails to get the pod out, but as someone who doesn't really use it, I don't find it terribly annoying. I also really appreciate that this brewer uses a shower/fountain head for the grounds, since that way the water doesn't just drill down the middle of your coffee, and has the best chance to evenly disperse throughout the basket. So I don't want to get too long-winded on what's great, because this machine just has so many little things that I'd end up writing a dissertation, and I think other people have already covered what's great. What I do want to talk about, is the little things that stick out as "odd or annoying." My biggest complaint comes from the dial used to select brew sizes; not in its physical function, but what sizes Ninja has selected. It seems that Ninja decided to base their sizes on things like "A big cup" or "1/4 of a carafe," instead of actual "number of cups." Because of this, you get measurement options like 15 or 28oz. This is hardly the end of the world, but if you grind your own beans you have to end up doing some weird mental math for "well that's 2 cups and 3 oz, so 2.5 cups, which means I need 25 grams of beans......" Like I said, not the end of the world, just weird. What is another weird inconvenience is the Keep Warm button; it only lights up/lets you click it once you get into sizes it deems worthy of the carafe. And the smallest size? 28 ounces. So if you want to make 2-3 cups of coffee, but leave it in the carafe since you only want 1 cup now, you have to choose your batch size, wait for it to brew, and then turn the nob to 28oz so it will let you press Keep Warm. I understand the minimalism-chic choice to have as few things lit up as possible, but this is truly the definition of Form Over Function. Ninja won't let me keep 18 ounces of coffee warm because they decided I should just put it all in a big travel mug. Now, none of these issues would stop me from recommending this coffee maker. Coffee is such an expensive hobby/interest that a 150$ coffee maker is still technically mid-tier, so I don't expect it to be flawless. It has a lot of functionality that I think a lot of people will find enjoyable, and makes a great cup/carafe of coffee quickly and easily. But because of weird choices by Ninja I can't say it is a 5/5. It is a solid 4/5, and worth your time, but definitely not perfect.

headline: Great for 6 Months, Now Dead
review_text_raw: If you’re looking for a short term coffee solution to get you through a few months of great coffee, this machine is for you. Easy to use, very convenient, makes a great cup of crema. It doesn’t have all the bells and whistles, just straight espresso and coffee which is exactly what I wanted. I’ve been diligent - religious even about replacing the filter on time, using official Jura tablets for descaling and cleaning. Over the last few weeks, coffee started to come out of the spouts slower and slower. Now it won’t make coffee at all. It’s clearly clogged somewhere. As a last ditch effort. I’ve run 2 back to back cleaning and descaling operations (yes using official Jura tablets). Nadda. She’s done for. Jura support has been useless. Placed multiple calls and no real results. I’m sure if I take the whole thing apart piece by piece I could fix it, but that’s not what I do or how I want to spend hours of my time. So I spent $200 a month for 7 months of great coffee. Funny to think I could have actually saved money going to the local coffee shop every single day.

headline: Excellent Coffee Quality but Much Louder Than Expected for a Premium Machine
review_text_raw: I’ve been using the Jura E4 Piano White Automatic Coffee Machine for a while now and overall the coffee quality is excellent. The espresso it makes is rich, creamy, and very consistent. The flavor extraction is impressive and definitely delivers a café-quality cup at home. However, for a machine at this price point, I expected it to be much quieter. The grinder is quite loud, and recently I’ve noticed the noise has increased even more when the machine turns on and off or when it starts grinding the beans. One thing to keep in mind if you have a baby at home, the machine is loud enough to wake mine up when we use it early in the morning. headline: Looks Great, But Comfort and Build Quality Are Just Average
review_text_raw: I’ve been using this chair for a little while now, and I have mixed feelings about it. First, the design is definitely one of its strongest points. It looks great, especially if you’re going for a gaming or modern office setup. It has a clean, sporty look, and from a distance it honestly looks more expensive than it is. That said, once you get up close, the overall build quality isn’t quite as impressive. The finishes could definitely be better. There are a few small details that make it feel a bit cheaper than I expected, and the materials don’t really give off a premium feel. It’s not terrible by any means, but you can tell where some corners were cut. As for comfort, I’d give it about a 7/10. It’s perfectly usable for everyday work or gaming sessions, but it’s not one of those chairs you immediately sink into and never want to leave. After a few hours, I definitely notice that it’s more of a budget chair than an ergonomic one. Overall, I think it’s a fair value for the money. If you’re expecting premium quality or all-day comfort, you may be a little disappointed. But if you’re shopping in this price range and mainly want something that looks good and gets the job done, it’s a reasonable choice. Just keep your expectations realistic.

headline: Those legs are ANNOYING to assemble, but otherwise decent chair
review_text_raw: The hardest part about putting this thing together is the legs. It says "slap on floor" or something to get the screw holes to line up. THEY WON'T! What you really need to do is get it as close as possible to lining up, then put the bolt in at an angle but DO NOT SCREW IT IN! Put the tool into the bolt and then use the two to press inwards and kinda pry back the leg piece until the bolt stands upright like it should. THEN screw it in! A screwdriver won't work because it tends to slide right back out if you aren't holding it in place when you start to screw in the bolt. So when you remove the screwdriver to put the bolt in, you'll lose the alignment anyway. And you need the tool (included with it) in the bolt to be able to apply enough pressure while at an angle to "catch" the screw hole before pulling it into line. HEAD. ACHE. Aside from that, here's my assessment of the chair's use compared to about 4 or 5 others that I've used in my lifetime: The assembly is easy and straightforward after you get those leg screw holes lined up. The arms seem to be shorter in length and height than some other chairs I've had. But that's a good thing for me because when the seat is at the correct height, the arms of other chairs were rubbing against the underside of my *GLASS* top desk. Occasionally that little bit of give in the chair when I get up or descent when I sit down would snap the arms against the glass of my desk, and it always sounded like I would break it. Thankfully, I didn't. Also, I love the fabric covering! I ordered this specifically for that one reason. The one I'm about to throw out now has the typical vinyl covering and as it aged, it cracked, especially on the arm rests, and my arms were getting torn up by it! While this cloth will also wear over time (especially being microfiber), it shouldn't create sharp vinyl pieces to scratch up my arms, so that's a plus! The back of the chair has a really thick dense foam that isn't quite conforming to my spine just yet. It's going to take some wearing in to really feel comfy. My worry is that once it breaks down enough to wear in, the foam may deteriorate very quickly afterwards. That's something to watch for in the future though. The arms may have a lighter foam, or maybe the foam just conforms better to sharper points, like elbows. But they seem to have more give to them, for which ever reason. The back also doesn't lean back as far as some gaming chairs I have had. That could be bad for me as I sometimes get *very random* vertigo and need to lie flat for a few minutes until it goes away. With this chair, I'll probably have to stumble to a couch or bed to lie down if it happens. The seat itself is not too long or short either. I've had some that were short enough I felt like I would fall off the front of the chair. And others that were so long that when I saw back, my knees were ON the seat of the chair. This one is, thankfully, right in between. The foot rest isn't anything special nor bad, but it "attaches" in the slides with a bolt on the back of one side. That will make it easy to remove when it's time to buy another chair. With the exception of the gas lift, most of this will be easy to take apart to fit inside of a large trash collection container when it's time for that. (Yes, I've gone through enough chairs for that to be a concern now!) I never use the lumbar supports, so I can't give any information on that.

headline: Honest review/4 years with this chair/second purchase of this chair
review_text_raw: I'll tell you what, I bought this chair 4 years ago and yes, many of the one star reviews are true, the chair does rip apart, it does get slightly uncomfortable, it does have little ergonomic features, it's casters aren't great, and it doesn't have lumbar support. But believe me when I tell ya it can take a beating. I put this chair into the deepest pits of hell and it held up for 4 years. I literally laid on my back in this chair some days, criss cross applesauce religiously, lifted myself up on the arms (I weigh 180), did this chair so dirty and ask me how it broke. Since I sat criss cross applesauce it pushed out the arms overtime and eventually came loose on the bracket that holds the arm to the back. 4 YEARS OF CRISS CROSS APPLESAUCE AND IT JUST NOW FAILED. Ill tell ya what, I didn't rarely use this chair either, I'm a degenerate, many 14 hour days in this chair. Get a seat cushion and lumbar support and live with the rip, if you don't abuse it like I did than it'll last you forever. I bought a furmax at a similar price point before this and with the way I abused it I swear to you it broke in less than a month, if you don't believe me you can look at my review on it 4 years ago lol. I bought this one cause I like to lean back and the arms being connected to the back gave it good support. Seriously guys, if you can make it work and just want to buy a cheap chair to get ya by this is the way to go. It isn't a five star chair because of what I mentioned earlier but it isn't a one star chair forsure. Edit: It is a five star chair, they've updated the design from having internals made out of wood to being a full metal frame. This means that the way my previous chair broke will not happen again, extending its durability. If you want a chair that can take a beating at this price point then I truly think your getting a chair well worth your money. Because of this im updating my review to 5 stars.

review_text_raw: For some reason, the beige or “white” color of this chair is priced about $20 less than its brown and black counterparts. While I can understand the appeal of a darker, more traditional office chair, I personally enjoy the bit of contrast this lighter color brings to my setup. Against my all-black desk and monitor, it adds a small but noticeable touch of brightness that feels refreshing without being distracting. Build Quality & Assembly This chair is sturdy, well-constructed, and easy to assemble. From the moment I unboxed it, the materials felt solid—there’s no flimsy or cheap sensation when sitting in it for extended periods. Assembly was straightforward, and from the time I received the package at my apartment door to the moment I had it fully set up, no more than 20 minutes had passed. All excess packaging was easily stowed back into the box, making cleanup just as seamless as the setup process. Comfort & Adjustability After two weeks of use, I can confidently say the cushions strike a great balance between firmness and comfort. They are not so soft that they lose support over time, nor so rigid that they cause discomfort during long work sessions. As someone who stands at 5’9”, the height adjustment is perfect for my setup, and I believe it would accommodate a wide range of users comfortably. I made the switch from a four-year-old chair of a similar style, which had developed persistent squeaking and no longer held its height adjustment. The difference is night and day—this chair remains silent, stable, and supportive throughout my workday. Value & Longevity While I cannot yet provide a long-term durability review, I believe that at this price point, even if this chair were to last only two years, it would still feel like a worthwhile investment. Compared to significantly more expensive alternatives, it delivers a high-quality experience at a fraction of the cost. What impresses me most is that this does not feel like a budget compromise. Instead, it feels like an intelligently designed, well-priced option that blends affordability, modern aesthetics, and practical comfort into a single package. The adjustability in height and tilt ensures that you can fine-tune it to your preference, making it adaptable for different workflows and sitting styles. Final Recommendation For those seeking a comfortable, stylish, and budget-friendly desk chair, I would highly recommend this model. It provides the kind of comfort, stability, and professional appearance that you would expect from something at a higher price point, while still being easy on both your body and your wallet.

headline: It's what you expect for $80...and nothing more.
review_text_raw: The assembly is easy, but it does take 30-45 minutes. The hardest part is aligning the back to the arm, which is easier if you don't tighten any of the armrest screws until they are all in place. I too was worried about the back being hollow, so I took another reviewer's advice and put a smaller Harbor Freight blanket folded to size in there. It provided extra padding and you can't tell once it's zipped up. This isn't the only chair that ships with the parts in the back cushion (no padding), so it wasn't a deal-breaker for me, but I would probably avoid it in the future. It does feel like you are sitting forward/more upright than what is normal, but that could be because my old chair was too far back and I just got used to it. I'll have to wait and see if I get used to it, but it is probably better for my back since it forces me to sit upright, although not as comfortable. The cushion is padded enough, but you still kind of bottom out on it, but not so much that it's hard on your backside. Let's face it, I bought it because it was cheap, and you get what you pay for. If you really want a super soft chair with all the adjustments, it's going to cost you $250 and up. This chair looks nice, is sturdy enough and doesn't creak like my old chair did, but I don't expect it to last more than 5 years before the covering starts to wear and it starts falling apart. I'm 6'2"/230 lbs and it works, but isn't the most comfortable chair I've ever sat in (not the worst either). It's going to feel different for different people, so you can't judge by one review whether this is the chair for you. The quality and looks are okay, but since I'm going to be in this for 8 hours a day, I don't love the comfort. Maybe I'm just used to my old chair and will get used to it in time, but it's average overall, so I give it 3 stars. I think it's better for shorter/lighter people. As far as the reviews with broken lifts or ripped cushions, either they were too heavy for the chair or they got a bad one shipped to them...I wouldn't worry about that too much. My average review is mostly because of the comfort and lack of adjustments. In hindsight, I'd probably pay more for a chair that allows me to adjust the angle of the back to the seat instead of this 'one size fits all' approach.

headline: Another Amazon Basics Great Value For The Budget & Simple-Minded
review_text_raw: This replaced a second hand desk chair which was losing all of it's adjustability options. And though the seat back holder was metal, it was starting to crack, and had me leaning back more and more, so I had to get a new chair. Which brought me to this chair for my home computer desk... Not as many adjustment options on this one (just the raise/lower and the slight recline lock on/off), but I wasn't expecting that on this budget-minded chair. At least the maximum pitch of the recline option is on par with your average airline seat, which is far better than my older, rickety chair. The entire chair is upholstered in a easy-to-clean leather-like fabric (no mesh anywhere), which I believe will survive scratching cats than meshy fabrics. The back support is comfy-sturdy, but has an accessible inner cavity (more on this later) and the seat is also cushioned well. The legs and the base are all metal, including the five leg coverings. The plastic sections that shroud the pneumatic lift are flimsier plastic sheaths. The armrests are non-adjustable and a bit shoter than my old chair. Minimal softer plastic-like cushioning on the armrests, but I'm fine with that. My only real issue about this chair is the cheap plastic armrest caps which cover the bolt assemblies between the armrests and the seats and seat backs -- they randomly pop off -- but it shouldn't be an issue unless you are anal about the cosmetic look about the chair. Assembly was fairly easy, with all the tools, nuts, bolts and screws were all grouped and labled in a sturdy "blister pack" (think OTC cold capsule packaging at the drug store). *** ABOUT THE BACKREST CAVITY -- NOTE *** This is where Amazon Basics saves packaging space. Your delivery box may look a bit on the smaller side. Don't worry! Much of the chair assembly (legs, tools, caps,etc...) is stored INSIDE the backrest during shipping. All you need to do is to unzip the contents from that cavity and voila! Everything is there. There should be red ribbons and/or strips RED tape to remind you the essentials are zipped up in the cavity. Once everything is out of the inside of the backrest, you theoretically can add more cushioning, back massager or similar -- although I haven't needed to do it yet. 4 stars due to the flimsy plastic caps and lift sheaths. But again, that is just cosmetic stuff and not durability issues.

headline: 18 Months of Mediocrity: This Chair Is Falling Apart and So Is My Patience
review_text_raw: Let me save you the time, money, and lower-back regret: do not buy this chair. At first glance, like a gas station breakfast sandwich, the Amazon Basics "Classic Puresoft PU" office chair looks harmless enough. A decent price, clean lines, and a name long enough to sound like someone tried really hard. But don’t be fooled. After living with this chair for 18 months, I can confidently say that calling it “basic” is generous. This thing is a slow-motion ergonomic tragedy. I'm not even a heavy user...this chair sits at a home desk, not a call center and yet it’s falling apart like a toddler’s Lego tower. Comfort: For the first week or two, the chair is passably comfortable. Then the padding compresses, the seat flattens like a pancake at a truck stop diner, and every hour feels like you're being punished for a crime you didn’t commit. The back support? Non-existent. I’d get more lumbar support leaning against a wall. Sitting in this chair for more than an hour at a time feels like penance and no amount of adjusting will save you. Adjustability: Sure, it adjusts up and down. That’s about where the good news ends. The tilt mechanism is laughable — either it’s locked upright like a church pew, or it reclines with all the grace and stability of a shopping cart with a broken wheel. The tension knob? Pure decoration. Turning it does about as much as yelling at a thunderstorm. Durability: After only 18 months, mine is literally falling apart. The seat cushion is collapsing. One of the casters feels like it’s about to snap off. The armrests creak under minimal pressure. It feels wobbly, unstable, and generally unfit for long-term use. This chair was designed to die young. Style: Deceptively Bland It tries to look sleek and minimal, but really it just screams “budget bulk order.” There’s nothing classic about this thing, and the Puresoft name is a masterclass in ironic branding — it’s about as “pure” and “soft” as a gravel driveway. Are there any Pros? I Guess It Technically Exists * It was easy to assemble. * It did, technically, hold my body off the floor for over a year. * That’s it. That’s the list. Final Verdict: If you're looking for a short-term chair for a rental office you never plan to return to, or maybe need to furnish the background of a Zoom call, maybe this will do. But if you actually plan to sit in it regularly? Don’t do it. You’re better off buying a decent secondhand chair on Craigslist. Or honestly, sitting on a milk crate. This chair is a monument to the bare minimum. It’s uncomfortable, poorly built, aging faster than unrefrigerated mayonnaise and destined for the landfill before its second birthday. 1/5 stars. Would give zero if I could.

After living with this chair for 18 months, I can confidently say that calling it “basic” is generous. This thing is a slow-motion ergonomic tragedy. I'm not even a heavy user...this chair sits at a home desk, not a call center and yet it’s falling apart like a toddler’s Lego tower. Comfort: For the first week or two, the chair is passably comfortable. Then the padding compresses, the seat flattens like a pancake at a truck stop diner, and every hour feels like you're being punished for a crime you didn’t commit. The back support? Non-existent. I’d get more lumbar support leaning against a wall. Sitting in this chair for more than an hour at a time feels like penance and no amount of adjusting will save you. Adjustability: Sure, it adjusts up and down. That’s about where the good news ends. The tilt mechanism is laughable — either it’s locked upright like a church pew, or it reclines with all the grace and stability of a shopping cart with a broken wheel. The tension knob? Pure decoration. Turning it does about as much as yelling at a thunderstorm. Durability: After only 18 months, mine is literally falling apart. The seat cushion is collapsing. One of the casters feels like it’s about to snap off. The armrests creak under minimal pressure. It feels wobbly, unstable, and generally unfit for long-term use. This chair was designed to die young. Style: Deceptively Bland It tries to look sleek and minimal, but really it just screams “budget bulk order.” There’s nothing classic about this thing, and the Puresoft name is a masterclass in ironic branding — it’s about as “pure” and “soft” as a gravel driveway. Are there any Pros? I Guess It Technically Exists * It was easy to assemble. * It did, technically, hold my body off the floor for over a year. * That’s it. That’s the list. Final Verdict: If you're looking for a short-term chair for a rental office you never plan to return to, or maybe need to furnish the background of a Zoom call, maybe this will do. But if you actually plan to sit in it regularly? Don’t do it. You’re better off buying a decent secondhand chair on Craigslist. Or honestly, sitting on a milk crate. This chair is a monument to the bare minimum. It’s uncomfortable, poorly built, aging faster than unrefrigerated mayonnaise and destined for the landfill before its second birthday. 1/5 stars. Would give zero if I could.

headline: High quality gaming chair
review_text_raw: This chair is a replacement for another gaming chair I had for a number of years that had the fake leather on it and tore off over time, so I decided to get one with a cloth cover instead. I'm happy with the quality of the chair and it looks like it will hold up well over time. It also looks really good. One thing to be aware of is that the chair seat is very firm. If you want a chair that is softer, this is probably not the best option for you. It is still comfortable and I'd still recommend it for anyone who doesn't mind a more firm seat. Another thing to be aware of is that the width of the back between the raised sides is rather narrow. If you have broad shoulders or are a bigger person, you may not be able to lean back comfortably in the chair. The chair can be put together pretty easily by one person and the only issue I had was the picture for attaching the seat back to the seat... the bar that attaches is shown in the picture backwards from what it is supposed to be. If you watch the video that they provide, it's clear how to attach it, but if you're following the instruction images, it may be confusing. The reclining lever is the type that you can push or pull and let go while adjusting the back rather than the spring ones where you have to hold it while adjusting the back. Either option is fine, but I find this style to be slightly more convenient.

headline: The Beige is where it’s at!
review_text_raw: For some reason, the beige or “white” color of this chair is priced about $20 less than its brown and black counterparts. While I can understand the appeal of a darker, more traditional office chair, I personally enjoy the bit of contrast this lighter color brings to my setup. Against my all-black desk and monitor, it adds a small but noticeable touch of brightness that feels refreshing without being distracting. Build Quality & Assembly This chair is sturdy, well-constructed, and easy to assemble. From the moment I unboxed it, the materials felt solid—there’s no flimsy or cheap sensation when sitting in it for extended periods. Assembly was straightforward, and from the time I received the package at my apartment door to the moment I had it fully set up, no more than 20 minutes had passed. All excess packaging was easily stowed back into the box, making cleanup just as seamless as the setup process. Comfort & Adjustability After two weeks of use, I can confidently say the cushions strike a great balance between firmness and comfort. They are not so soft that they lose support over time, nor so rigid that they cause discomfort during long work sessions. As someone who stands at 5’9”, the height adjustment is perfect for my setup, and I believe it would accommodate a wide range of users comfortably. I made the switch from a four-year-old chair of a similar style, which had developed persistent squeaking and no longer held its height adjustment. The difference is night and day—this chair remains silent, stable, and supportive throughout my workday. Value & Longevity While I cannot yet provide a long-term durability review, I believe that at this price point, even if this chair were to last only two years, it would still feel like a worthwhile investment. Compared to significantly more expensive alternatives, it delivers a high-quality experience at a fraction of the cost. What impresses me most is that this does not feel like a budget compromise. Instead, it feels like an intelligently designed, well-priced option that blends affordability, modern aesthetics, and practical comfort into a single package. The adjustability in height and tilt ensures that you can fine-tune it to your preference, making it adaptable for different workflows and sitting styles. Final Recommendation For those seeking a comfortable, stylish, and budget-friendly desk chair, I would highly recommend this model. It provides the kind of comfort, stability, and professional appearance that you would expect from something at a higher price point, while still being easy on both your body and your wallet.

headline: It's what you expect for $80...and nothing more.
review_text_raw: The assembly is easy, but it does take 30-45 minutes. The hardest part is aligning the back to the arm, which is easier if you don't tighten any of the armrest screws until they are all in place. I too was worried about the back being hollow, so I took another reviewer's advice and put a smaller Harbor Freight blanket folded to size in there. It provided extra padding and you can't tell once it's zipped up. This isn't the only chair that ships with the parts in the back cushion (no padding), so it wasn't a deal-breaker for me, but I would probably avoid it in the future. It does feel like you are sitting forward/more upright than what is normal, but that could be because my old chair was too far back and I just got used to it. I'll have to wait and see if I get used to it, but it is probably better for my back since it forces me to sit upright, although not as comfortable. The cushion is padded enough, but you still kind of bottom out on it, but not so much that it's hard on your backside. Let's face it, I bought it because it was cheap, and you get what you pay for. If you really want a super soft chair with all the adjustments, it's going to cost you $250 and up. This chair looks nice, is sturdy enough and doesn't creak like my old chair did, but I don't expect it to last more than 5 years before the covering starts to wear and it starts falling apart. I'm 6'2"/230 lbs and it works, but isn't the most comfortable chair I've ever sat in (not the worst either). It's going to feel different for different people, so you can't judge by one review whether this is the chair for you. The quality and looks are okay, but since I'm going to be in this for 8 hours a day, I don't love the comfort. Maybe I'm just used to my old chair and will get used to it in time, but it's average overall, so I give it 3 stars. I think it's better for shorter/lighter people. As far as the reviews with broken lifts or ripped cushions, either they were too heavy for the chair or they got a bad one shipped to them...I wouldn't worry about that too much. My average review is mostly because of the comfort and lack of adjustments. In hindsight, I'd probably pay more for a chair that allows me to adjust the angle of the back to the seat instead of this 'one size fits all' approach.

headline: Another Amazon Basics Great Value For The Budget & Simple-Minded
review_text_raw: This replaced a second hand desk chair which was losing all of it's adjustability options. And though the seat back holder was metal, it was starting to crack, and had me leaning back more and more, so I had to get a new chair. Which brought me to this chair for my home computer desk... Not as many adjustment options on this one (just the raise/lower and the slight recline lock on/off), but I wasn't expecting that on this budget-minded chair. At least the maximum pitch of the recline option is on par with your average airline seat, which is far better than my older, rickety chair. The entire chair is upholstered in a easy-to-clean leather-like fabric (no mesh anywhere), which I believe will survive scratching cats than meshy fabrics. The back support is comfy-sturdy, but has an accessible inner cavity (more on this later) and the seat is also cushioned well. The legs and the base are all metal, including the five leg coverings. The plastic sections that shroud the pneumatic lift are flimsier plastic sheaths. The armrests are non-adjustable and a bit shoter than my old chair. Minimal softer plastic-like cushioning on the armrests, but I'm fine with that. My only real issue about this chair is the cheap plastic armrest caps which cover the bolt assemblies between the armrests and the seats and seat backs -- they randomly pop off -- but it shouldn't be an issue unless you are anal about the cosmetic look about the chair. Assembly was fairly easy, with all the tools, nuts, bolts and screws were all grouped and labled in a sturdy "blister pack" (think OTC cold capsule packaging at the drug store). *** ABOUT THE BACKREST CAVITY -- NOTE *** This is where Amazon Basics saves packaging space. Your delivery box may look a bit on the smaller side. Don't worry! Much of the chair assembly (legs, tools, caps,etc...) is stored INSIDE the backrest during shipping. All you need to do is to unzip the contents from that cavity and voila! Everything is there. There should be red ribbons and/or strips RED tape to remind you the essentials are zipped up in the cavity. Once everything is out of the inside of the backrest, you theoretically can add more cushioning, back massager or similar -- although I haven't needed to do it yet. 4 stars due to the flimsy plastic caps and lift sheaths. But again, that is just cosmetic stuff and not durability issues.

Your delivery box may look a bit on the smaller side. Don't worry! Much of the chair assembly (legs, tools, caps,etc...) is stored INSIDE the backrest during shipping. All you need to do is to unzip the contents from that cavity and voila! Everything is there. There should be red ribbons and/or strips RED tape to remind you the essentials are zipped up in the cavity. Once everything is out of the inside of the backrest, you theoretically can add more cushioning, back massager or similar -- although I haven't needed to do it yet. 4 stars due to the flimsy plastic caps and lift sheaths. headline: 18 Months of Mediocrity: This Chair Is Falling Apart and So Is My Patience
review_text_raw: Let me save you the time, money, and lower-back regret: do not buy this chair. At first glance, like a gas station breakfast sandwich, the Amazon Basics "Classic Puresoft PU" office chair looks harmless enough. A decent price, clean lines, and a name long enough to sound like someone tried really hard. But don’t be fooled. After living with this chair for 18 months, I can confidently say that calling it “basic” is generous. This thing is a slow-motion ergonomic tragedy. I'm not even a heavy user...this chair sits at a home desk, not a call center and yet it’s falling apart like a toddler’s Lego tower. Comfort: For the first week or two, the chair is passably comfortable. Then the padding compresses, the seat flattens like a pancake at a truck stop diner, and every hour feels like you're being punished for a crime you didn’t commit. The back support? Non-existent. I’d get more lumbar support leaning against a wall. Sitting in this chair for more than an hour at a time feels like penance and no amount of adjusting will save you. Adjustability: Sure, it adjusts up and down. That’s about where the good news ends. The tilt mechanism is laughable — either it’s locked upright like a church pew, or it reclines with all the grace and stability of a shopping cart with a broken wheel. The tension knob? Pure decoration. Turning it does about as much as yelling at a thunderstorm. Durability: After only 18 months, mine is literally falling apart. The seat cushion is collapsing. One of the casters feels like it’s about to snap off. The armrests creak under minimal pressure. It feels wobbly, unstable, and generally unfit for long-term use. This chair was designed to die young. Style: Deceptively Bland It tries to look sleek and minimal, but really it just screams “budget bulk order.” There’s nothing classic about this thing, and the Puresoft name is a masterclass in ironic branding — it’s about as “pure” and “soft” as a gravel driveway. Are there any Pros? I Guess It Technically Exists * It was easy to assemble. * It did, technically, hold my body off the floor for over a year. * That’s it. That’s the list. Final Verdict: If you're looking for a short-term chair for a rental office you never plan to return to, or maybe need to furnish the background of a Zoom call, maybe this will do. But if you actually plan to sit in it regularly? Don’t do it. You’re better off buying a decent secondhand chair on Craigslist. Or honestly, sitting on a milk crate. This chair is a monument to the bare minimum. It’s uncomfortable, poorly built, aging faster than unrefrigerated mayonnaise and destined for the landfill before its second birthday. 1/5 stars. Would give zero if I could.

review_text_raw: I'll tell you what, I bought this chair 4 years ago and yes, many of the one star reviews are true, the chair does rip apart, it does get slightly uncomfortable, it does have little ergonomic features, it's casters aren't great, and it doesn't have lumbar support. But believe me when I tell ya it can take a beating. I put this chair into the deepest pits of hell and it held up for 4 years. I literally laid on my back in this chair some days, criss cross applesauce religiously, lifted myself up on the arms (I weigh 180), did this chair so dirty and ask me how it broke. Since I sat criss cross applesauce it pushed out the arms overtime and eventually came loose on the bracket that holds the arm to the back. 4 YEARS OF CRISS CROSS APPLESAUCE AND IT JUST NOW FAILED. Ill tell ya what, I didn't rarely use this chair either, I'm a degenerate, many 14 hour days in this chair. Get a seat cushion and lumbar support and live with the rip, if you don't abuse it like I did than it'll last you forever. I bought a furmax at a similar price point before this and with the way I abused it I swear to you it broke in less than a month, if you don't believe me you can look at my review on it 4 years ago lol. I bought this one cause I like to lean back and the arms being connected to the back gave it good support. Seriously guys, if you can make it work and just want to buy a cheap chair to get ya by this is the way to go. It isn't a five star chair because of what I mentioned earlier but it isn't a one star chair forsure. Edit: It is a five star chair, they've updated the design from having internals made out of wood to being a full metal frame. This means that the way my previous chair broke will not happen again, extending its durability. If you want a chair that can take a beating at this price point then I truly think your getting a chair well worth your money. Because of this im updating my review to 5 stars.

Against my all-black desk and monitor, it adds a small but noticeable touch of brightness that feels refreshing without being distracting. Build Quality & Assembly This chair is sturdy, well-constructed, and easy to assemble. From the moment I unboxed it, the materials felt solid—there’s no flimsy or cheap sensation when sitting in it for extended periods. Assembly was straightforward, and from the time I received the package at my apartment door to the moment I had it fully set up, no more than 20 minutes had passed. All excess packaging was easily stowed back into the box, making cleanup just as seamless as the setup process. Comfort & Adjustability After two weeks of use, I can confidently say the cushions strike a great balance between firmness and comfort. They are not so soft that they lose support over time, nor so rigid that they cause discomfort during long work sessions. As someone who stands at 5’9”, the height adjustment is perfect for my setup, and I believe it would accommodate a wide range of users comfortably. I made the switch from a four-year-old chair of a similar style, which had developed persistent squeaking and no longer held its height adjustment. The difference is night and day—this chair remains silent, stable, and supportive throughout my workday. Value & Longevity While I cannot yet provide a long-term durability review, I believe that at this price point, even if this chair were to last only two years, it would still feel like a worthwhile investment. Compared to significantly more expensive alternatives, it delivers a high-quality experience at a fraction of the cost. What impresses me most is that this does not feel like a budget compromise. Instead, it feels like an intelligently designed, well-priced option that blends affordability, modern aesthetics, and practical comfort into a single package. The adjustability in height and tilt ensures that you can fine-tune it to your preference, making it adaptable for different workflows and sitting styles. Final Recommendation For those seeking a comfortable, stylish, and budget-friendly desk chair, I would highly recommend this model. It provides the kind of comfort, stability, and professional appearance that you would expect from something at a higher price point, while still being easy on both your body and your wallet.

From the moment I unboxed it, the materials felt solid—there’s no flimsy or cheap sensation when sitting in it for extended periods. Assembly was straightforward, and from the time I received the package at my apartment door to the moment I had it fully set up, no more than 20 minutes had passed. All excess packaging was easily stowed back into the box, making cleanup just as seamless as the setup process. They are not so soft that they lose support over time, nor so rigid that they cause discomfort during long work sessions. As someone who stands at 5’9”, the height adjustment is perfect for my setup, and I believe it would accommodate a wide range of users comfortably. The difference is night and day—this chair remains silent, stable, and supportive throughout my workday. Instead, it feels like an intelligently designed, well-priced option that blends affordability, modern aesthetics, and practical comfort into a single package. The adjustability in height and tilt ensures that you can fine-tune it to your preference, making it adaptable for different workflows and sitting styles. headline: It's what you expect for $80...and nothing more.
review_text_raw: The assembly is easy, but it does take 30-45 minutes. The hardest part is aligning the back to the arm, which is easier if you don't tighten any of the armrest screws until they are all in place. I too was worried about the back being hollow, so I took another reviewer's advice and put a smaller Harbor Freight blanket folded to size in there. It provided extra padding and you can't tell once it's zipped up. This isn't the only chair that ships with the parts in the back cushion (no padding), so it wasn't a deal-breaker for me, but I would probably avoid it in the future. It does feel like you are sitting forward/more upright than what is normal, but that could be because my old chair was too far back and I just got used to it. I'll have to wait and see if I get used to it, but it is probably better for my back since it forces me to sit upright, although not as comfortable. The cushion is padded enough, but you still kind of bottom out on it, but not so much that it's hard on your backside. Let's face it, I bought it because it was cheap, and you get what you pay for. If you really want a super soft chair with all the adjustments, it's going to cost you $250 and up. This chair looks nice, is sturdy enough and doesn't creak like my old chair did, but I don't expect it to last more than 5 years before the covering starts to wear and it starts falling apart. I'm 6'2"/230 lbs and it works, but isn't the most comfortable chair I've ever sat in (not the worst either). It's going to feel different for different people, so you can't judge by one review whether this is the chair for you. The quality and looks are okay, but since I'm going to be in this for 8 hours a day, I don't love the comfort. Maybe I'm just used to my old chair and will get used to it in time, but it's average overall, so I give it 3 stars. I think it's better for shorter/lighter people. As far as the reviews with broken lifts or ripped cushions, either they were too heavy for the chair or they got a bad one shipped to them...I wouldn't worry about that too much. My average review is mostly because of the comfort and lack of adjustments. In hindsight, I'd probably pay more for a chair that allows me to adjust the angle of the back to the seat instead of this 'one size fits all' approach.

headline: Another Amazon Basics Great Value For The Budget & Simple-Minded
review_text_raw: This replaced a second hand desk chair which was losing all of it's adjustability options. And though the seat back holder was metal, it was starting to crack, and had me leaning back more and more, so I had to get a new chair. Which brought me to this chair for my home computer desk... Not as many adjustment options on this one (just the raise/lower and the slight recline lock on/off), but I wasn't expecting that on this budget-minded chair. At least the maximum pitch of the recline option is on par with your average airline seat, which is far better than my older, rickety chair. The entire chair is upholstered in a easy-to-clean leather-like fabric (no mesh anywhere), which I believe will survive scratching cats than meshy fabrics. The back support is comfy-sturdy, but has an accessible inner cavity (more on this later) and the seat is also cushioned well. The legs and the base are all metal, including the five leg coverings. The plastic sections that shroud the pneumatic lift are flimsier plastic sheaths. The armrests are non-adjustable and a bit shoter than my old chair. Minimal softer plastic-like cushioning on the armrests, but I'm fine with that. My only real issue about this chair is the cheap plastic armrest caps which cover the bolt assemblies between the armrests and the seats and seat backs -- they randomly pop off -- but it shouldn't be an issue unless you are anal about the cosmetic look about the chair. Assembly was fairly easy, with all the tools, nuts, bolts and screws were all grouped and labled in a sturdy "blister pack" (think OTC cold capsule packaging at the drug store). *** ABOUT THE BACKREST CAVITY -- NOTE *** This is where Amazon Basics saves packaging space. Your delivery box may look a bit on the smaller side. Don't worry! Much of the chair assembly (legs, tools, caps,etc...) is stored INSIDE the backrest during shipping. All you need to do is to unzip the contents from that cavity and voila! Everything is there. There should be red ribbons and/or strips RED tape to remind you the essentials are zipped up in the cavity. Once everything is out of the inside of the backrest, you theoretically can add more cushioning, back massager or similar -- although I haven't needed to do it yet. 4 stars due to the flimsy plastic caps and lift sheaths. But again, that is just cosmetic stuff and not durability issues.

headline: 18 Months of Mediocrity: This Chair Is Falling Apart and So Is My Patience
review_text_raw: Let me save you the time, money, and lower-back regret: do not buy this chair. At first glance, like a gas station breakfast sandwich, the Amazon Basics "Classic Puresoft PU" office chair looks harmless enough. A decent price, clean lines, and a name long enough to sound like someone tried really hard. But don’t be fooled. After living with this chair for 18 months, I can confidently say that calling it “basic” is generous. This thing is a slow-motion ergonomic tragedy. I'm not even a heavy user...this chair sits at a home desk, not a call center and yet it’s falling apart like a toddler’s Lego tower. Comfort: For the first week or two, the chair is passably comfortable. Then the padding compresses, the seat flattens like a pancake at a truck stop diner, and every hour feels like you're being punished for a crime you didn’t commit. The back support? Non-existent. I’d get more lumbar support leaning against a wall. Sitting in this chair for more than an hour at a time feels like penance and no amount of adjusting will save you. Adjustability: Sure, it adjusts up and down. That’s about where the good news ends. The tilt mechanism is laughable — either it’s locked upright like a church pew, or it reclines with all the grace and stability of a shopping cart with a broken wheel. The tension knob? Pure decoration. Turning it does about as much as yelling at a thunderstorm. Durability: After only 18 months, mine is literally falling apart. The seat cushion is collapsing. One of the casters feels like it’s about to snap off. The armrests creak under minimal pressure. It feels wobbly, unstable, and generally unfit for long-term use. This chair was designed to die young. Style: Deceptively Bland It tries to look sleek and minimal, but really it just screams “budget bulk order.” There’s nothing classic about this thing, and the Puresoft name is a masterclass in ironic branding — it’s about as “pure” and “soft” as a gravel driveway. Are there any Pros? I Guess It Technically Exists * It was easy to assemble. * It did, technically, hold my body off the floor for over a year. * That’s it. That’s the list. Final Verdict: If you're looking for a short-term chair for a rental office you never plan to return to, or maybe need to furnish the background of a Zoom call, maybe this will do. But if you actually plan to sit in it regularly? Don’t do it. You’re better off buying a decent secondhand chair on Craigslist. Or honestly, sitting on a milk crate. This chair is a monument to the bare minimum. It’s uncomfortable, poorly built, aging faster than unrefrigerated mayonnaise and destined for the landfill before its second birthday. 1/5 stars. Would give zero if I could.

It looks great, especially if you’re going for a gaming or modern office setup. It has a clean, sporty look, and from a distance it honestly looks more expensive than it is. That said, once you get up close, the overall build quality isn’t quite as impressive. The finishes could definitely be better. There are a few small details that make it feel a bit cheaper than I expected, and the materials don’t really give off a premium feel. It’s not terrible by any means, but you can tell where some corners were cut. As for comfort, I’d give it about a 7/10. It’s perfectly usable for everyday work or gaming sessions, but it’s not one of those chairs you immediately sink into and never want to leave. After a few hours, I definitely notice that it’s more of a budget chair than an ergonomic one. Overall, I think it’s a fair value for the money. If you’re expecting premium quality or all-day comfort, you may be a little disappointed. But if you’re shopping in this price range and mainly want something that looks good and gets the job done, it’s a reasonable choice. Just keep your expectations realistic.

headline: Quality lacks and material is scratchy. Recline is good though!
review_text_raw: I’ve had this chair for a little over a year now. I think overall 3/5 stars. There are a few reasons why I wouldn’t buy this chair again, unless it was on sale but there are a few things I like about it. First off, the material of the cushions SUCK. It’s scratchy and uncomfortable, making me want to put a blanket over the arm rests constantly. The arm rests also are slightly too far apart for me to actually use them while typing so not a good chair if you’re looking for that. I do use the arm rests often when leaning back and now that it’s been over a year, the left arm is giving up and almost falling off which is a huge disappointment. Second, the cushion isn’t the best but with a memory foam cushion, it works for me. It stains easily. The recline is one of the only good parts that I like about the chair in addition to the wide cushion. The ergonomics are ok the back bit slides down so if you want it adjusted higher, it probably won’t work for you. Overall, the recline is what makes it 3 stars for me so it’s not a bad chair. Short life, quality, and discomfort are the main downsides so it’s a borderline 2 stars chair. If it’s a char you won’t use constantly, it’s probably fine! Buy at your own risk!

headline: Absolutely worth it! A great deal!
review_text_raw: This chair has been a fantastic purchase! I thought I would have to get a super expensive chair to get the comfort and support I wanted but this one was very reasonably priced and I got it on sale too. It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.) It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat. All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

headline: Bad, bad, and also not good.
review_text_raw: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable. Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

headline: Love it so far! Short & tiny people approved!
review_text_raw: Just got this today, but my first impression is that it’s exactly what I needed! Is this a gaming chair? Yes. Did I buy it to use in my work office at 41yrs old? Also yes. My nephew got this over xmas and when he showed it to me, he made me try it. It was love at first sit. I’m pretty small, 4’11 and 95lbs, so all of my work chairs are very uncomfortable for me. My feet never touch the floor, the chairs didn’t recline and my head was too short to have it hit the actual headrest. After I saw my nephews, I knew I had to get this. It’s everything I need. My feet hit the floor, it has a pillow that sits under my neck, back support and even the foot rest. I love that it reclines as well and impressed with how well it came together. I’m very excited to bring to work and finally be comfortable! Price: I got this on sale for 109$. It’s normally 129$ but 20$ shipping. I wish it would stay at 99$ all around since the shipping isn’t free. It was a super heavy package though so I get it. Style: I got all black so it blends in at work and it’s as pictured. I wish the logo wasn’t so big and bright for those who don’t use this as a gaming chair but I may use a black sharpie & color it to make this more discreet. Size: If you are on the shorter side, this is a great chair. Great for kids obviously and tinier adults. Not sure this is a heavy duty chair for the regular sized adult so keep in mind. Delivery: said it would take a week but came next day which was impressive and I was very happy with that. Arrives in great condition. Setup: the directions are so so. My husband put this together and it took wayyyyy longer than it should have because some of the directions were mislabeled. Screws numbers were added that weren’t needed for this chair and some of the images were so tiny you couldn’t see much. For some reason we had the biggest issue with the footrest. We had to do it like 3xs b/c we couldn’t tell from the image how it actually sat. Got it done none the less and worth the struggle. Bottom line: worth the buy and seems good quality for the price but I’ll see how it hold up when I bring it to the office for actual use.

review_text_raw: I didn't expect much for how much it cost. I thought it would be okay, but knew I couldn't afford a super fancy chair, so didn't my hopes up. It's actually a fantastic chair! I'll start with the TINIEST gripe. It was filthy. GROSS. I had to get a magic eraser to get the grime off of it, grease and stuff from the factory. But it's a gorgeous pink and white chair, feels so sturdy and comfortable. Great support for your back, and that's even without the lumbar pillow that comes with it. I will say, the instructions were clearly written by ChatGPT. Awful. But the pictures were just fine, so it was actually easy to put together, haha. So don't fret if you read it and it's confusing. The diagrams are accurate and easy to read. It also didn't take long at all to put together. OH! I personally didn't want rollers, as I have a pup and didn't want to squish toes. So I bought office chair gliders to replace the wheels (which are beautiful, sadly, would've loved to use them) and they fit just fine! So if you're like me and wanted to change them, they're compatible. But the wheels are super cute. :) Honestly so pleased with this chair. I am very happy with it, and look forward to using it while I work and draw and game for a long time to come.

review_text_raw: Its an alright chair. It is fairly comfy and the material feels nice. The assembly wasnt too complicated but the instructions were extremely hard to follow (the instructions showed very tiny pictures that were hard to see, and the written instructions only said to fasten the screws down, no actual worded instructions on how to assemble it). The locking mechanism for the leaning is different from any chair and kinda awkward to use because it goes so far down that you have to reallllyyy lean sideways to unlock it and re-lock it, which makes it awkward to lean back or forward to adjust it. The footrest is garbage because it goes straight out but not far enough, making it so your feet dont actually rest on it but rather your lower calves do (or if you do out your feet on it youll be in an awkward squat position) and its held with extremely thin aluminum rods run through plastic screwed into the bottom which means the footrest has give and feels like itll bend or break easily from putting any substancial weight on it. I also had a shipping delay of 5 days after it was supposed to take over a week anyways, which was an inconvenience. Its not necessarily a bad chair, especially if youre a shorter persom who can use the footrest comfortably. product_title: TRALT Office Chair Ergonomic Desk Chair - Gaming Chair with Lumbar Support
headline: Comfort Meets Functionality in One Great Office Chair
review_text_raw: I am very happy with this chair and would absolutely give it 5 stars. It is incredibly comfortable, and one of my favorite features is the wider seat. I'm 5'8 and 126lbs, so I don't necessarily NEED a wide chair, but I LOVE not feeling cramped while sitting. I tend to tuck one leg up in a sort of half-crossed position, and this chair is perfect for that siting style. The flip-up armrests are another huge plus! They lift completely out of the way, allowing me to slide the entire chair neatly under my desk when I'm not using it, which helps save space. The lumbar support is adjustable and provides great support. Because I tend to sit closer to the edge of the seat, I still prefer using an additional lumbar cushion. However, for anyone who naturally sits further back in the chair, the adjustable lumbar support would be ideal. The headrest is also adjustable up and down, making it easy to find a comfortable position. The mesh material feels high-quality, supportive and breathable which I really appreciate considering I work from home and am in this chair for long periods of time. Assembly was straightforward as well. I put it together by myself in about 30 minutes to an hour and I wasn't rushing. The instructions were easy to follow, and all of the pieces were clearly labeled. The only small issue I encountered was that one black washer was missing from the hardware pack. Fortunately, I had a spare from another piece of furniture, so it wasn't a problem for me. Overall, this chair exceeded my expectations. It's comfortable, adjustable, well-designed, and versatile enough to accommodate different sitting styles. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a supportive office desk chair.

headline: Decent chair but not for us taller people
review_text_raw: I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with. For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive. After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected. The good: 1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal. 2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems. 3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me. 4. Appearance. Very nice. 5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy. The not so good. 1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

product_title: TRALT Office Chair Ergonomic Desk Chair - Gaming Chair with Lumbar Support
headline: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
review_text_raw: I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended. Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame). The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for). While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down. Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes. Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

headline: Good chair, comfortable for work day use, a little creaky.
review_text_raw: I've had the chair for 7 months, and it is a good pick overall with no buyer's remorse. I am 6'2 and 180lbs and sit in the chair for ~7 hours a day. The support is okay, as they are just adjustable lumbar/neck pillows and nothing rigid. I have a 30" waist, and I would say a 34" or 36" is around the max to fit within the seat bolster. The arms do not adjust out, only up and down, which is not an issue for me. If you are larger, that is something to consider. The recline feature works hilariously well as you can recline nearly flat and not fall over. The leather is still in great shape with hardly any creasing and no damage or wear to the material. It's comfortable to sit in for the whole day. The chair was very simple to assemble in ~5 minutes and comes together like every standard office chair with 4 bolts for the base, and 6 for each arm. This chair has started to creak which can't be helped. I would give it a 3.5-4 rating due to this alone. The creak comes from the pressed steel pin the chair tilts on at the top of the post, so it can't be tightened or adjusted in any way. It is a little obnoxious, but my only real issue with the chair. To compare, I have a $1,500 Humanscale Freedom Task Chair with Headrest at home, and I feel no real difference in the chair's comfort or overall quality. The Humanscale does have better built-in ergonomic adjustments like the arms, seat pan depth, and lumbar position versus the Corsair, which only includes a couple pillows for lumbar and neck support. The Humanscale is really underwhelming for the price, very loud with the smallest movements, and not that comfortable. Do not feel compelled to spend more expecting better quality. Overall, I would probably purchase the Corsair TC500 Luxe for a little more next time for more adjustability, and the built in lumbar system.

headline: Looks good in pictures and description. Return before 30 day window ends.
review_text_raw: Looks good in pictures but shows it flaws quickly. I love the Corsair brand and took a chance on this chair because it looks great. Some issues I found include: lumbar cushion is too large and impractical/uncomfortable; unusable. Head cushion is fine, but taller people will have to slouch for it to fit your neck and cause lower back pain; remove it and there is no neck support at all. back cushion material is very thin and will quickly give way to the lumbar frame, which is not comfortable at all. The entire chair mechanism and controls are cheap quality. Even in the locked position the chair still rocks back and forth to a small degree. You are constantly flexing your muscles just to stay in one because of the sway. The bolt holes are flimsy and even when tightened beyond capacity, the entire chair still rocks and flexes. No stability at all. Arm rests are completely fixed in place and can only go up and down. Arm rest surface is hard and uncomfortable. Arm rests stay in place when leaning back causing your arms to completely come off the arm rest or having to stretch both arms just to stay on the armrest, another huge inconvenience and ergonomic issue. Seat cushion is just thin as the back support. Thin cheap poly stuffing across metal frames. Get ready for serious lower back issues. Unless you are a small child, this chair is not for you. Now I know why they only give you 30 days to return the item. The chair shows its issues after that window closes.

headline: Glad I bought it...Well not for long
review_text_raw: I was hesitant to buy this chair. Every review I read was an emotional rollercoaster. One minute it’s great, one minute it’s trash, I wasn’t sure what to believe. I decided to just commit to it and order since I’ve always wanted this chair, and it matches my Corsair peripherals. I ordered it Monday, it came Wednesday, which is pretty awesome. Everything was well packaged. Branded bags, a lot of protection surrounding the products, I was impressed. It does NOT come with physical instructions, but you can just find them online. Super straight forward install which took me a solid half an hour at most. Now, the final verdict. First sit down and I was really impressed. The bottom cushion is honestly nice, and the two back pillows work well and fit my body like a glove. I’ve already used this for a consecutive couple of hours and I’m happier than I was in my other chair. I was rocking a Respawn 110 Pro, which is very large and plush but is very cheap feeling in comparison. For those looking to get this chair, every single one of the complaints I’ve seen did NOT fit my experience. Whether it be the parts, the bolts, the cushion, whatever. But I do understand where some of these may come from. Let me advise that this chair is absolutely perfect for me. Im 5’11 and 145 so I’m not your average bodybuilder. It still has some room but just be mindful of that since it does seem like it’s meant for the “smaller” peeps. Besides that, everything feels great and is premium. It left me surprised, and I will continue to not trust reviews and just get the dang thing myself. Glad I made the decision. EDIT: LMAO I sold it less than a year later because it started hurting to sit for long periods of time. The chair formed to my seating position but it never felt soft/comfortable enough. Sadly my 5 star didn’t last that long. Recently got a GT Player suede chair for half the price and it’s 10 times better. It’s ight you live and you learn. Just get an ergonomic chair if you want comfort

The headrest is particularly noteworthy; unlike more expensive chairs I’ve owned where the headrest constantly slips, this one is very sturdy. The lumbar support is also highly effective, allowing you to adjust both the height and the support strength. The 3D armrests are another highlight, moving back and forth, twisting, and flipping up 90 degrees so you can either use them for support or move them out of the way to push the chair fully under the desk. The seat cushion is equally impressive, with 3.14-inch thick foam that feels deep and resilient, giving me confidence that it won't flatten out or lose its shape with regular use. There are a few areas where the product could be refined. The armrests are made from a PU-padded material, which I find to be a negative as it is prone to friction damage over time; I would have preferred a simple high-quality plastic or a full mesh/cloth finish. Additionally, the assembly gloves included were far too small for an average adult. I also have a suggestion for the company regarding the extra hardware provided: since these chairs often come with spare screws or tools, it would be a fantastic and unique innovation to build a small, dedicated compartment into the frame of the chair to store these extra materials. I haven't seen this feature on other chairs, but it would be a very pragmatic way to ensure the spare parts aren't lost over the years. Despite these small points, this remains a five-star quality chair in my opinion.

headline: A review after a year of owning this chair
review_text_raw: It’s been over a year since I bought this and have decided to write my review. My experience with this chair during this time- since I bought it and up till now is overall good experience. It’s not the greatest chair out there available on the market, but especially for the price and usability, I would say it was worth it. A few Pros worth mentioning: • adjustability • comfortable cushion • lightweight and easy to move around A few cons worth mentioning: • No reclining- just a “rocking back and fourth” which you have to twist below the seat to adjust the sensitivity- which I find very tedious, tiring, and long. • Headrest is honestly not the best and kind of protrudes your head forward a bit- although adjustable, still not as comfortable as I would like. • Cushion will eventually wear out- BUT not too much and still lowkey comfortable, but I started to felt the need to change my sitting position more overtime. As stated before the chair is decent- especially for the price. For me personally, I love that the seat encourages you to sit up straight and nicely, but naturally, it does get “tiring” after a bit of time. Even then, not sitting the way it intended to- is ironically the most comfortable way to sit on it. The seat does not get too hot which is also nice. If the chair had actual reclining, this chair would be perfect. Also, the chair has some decent height adjustability aswell. The building process was easy and didn’t take that long to do. Overall, if you needed something that was comfortable enough, cheap, and reclining is not a need, I would recommend this chair.

headline: 45 minutes assembly -- piece of cake. Nice chair.
review_text_raw: Before I finally landed on this chair I read about a million articles with buying advice for ergonomic desk chairs, looked for second hand expensive chairs, read so many Amazon reviews. Obviously you can spend a whole lot of money on an ergonomic desk chair (even used ones), but I really didn't want to. I just bought this today, so the jury is out on long term wear, ,but I can say that the components feel solid, assembly was easy, it is *very* comfortable so far, and -- even more to the point -- VERY adjustable in so many different ways that physical therapists etc recommended in the articles I read. I am 5 foot 5; in order to put the chair at the right ergonomic height for my particular desk and keyboard, I need a footrest so my feet aren't dangling. But that would be the case with any chair in my setup. The headrest is great, the arms are soft and comfortable, the back support piece is perfect, and everything can be adjusted as you sit in it. Rollers are quiet and stable on laminate floor. The box was a good size and heavy enough (~32 lbs) to be awkward for an unfit middle aged lady to wrangle down apartment steps; however, the Amazon driver brought it straight to my door. The chair was carefully packed. Whoever wrote the assembly instructions (which are in English and Spanish) for this chair is some kind of technical writing genius -- I have never seen clearer or more easy-to-follow instructions. From slicing open the tape on the box to finished chair was 45 minutes for me. All you need for assembly is included -- also fabric gloves (for protecting your manicure? I guess?) and extra bolts and washers. Super buy. If I'd known I could get such an affordable and massive upgrade from my previous garbage chair I would have done it long ago. Great value for the money. I rarely write reviews but all the reviews I read helped me make a great decision, so here ya go.
