headline: Received a returned item
review_text_raw: I was so excited to finally get a new chair for my desk at home. When it arrived, the delivery driver even walked it down the hall to my apartment for me. Once I brought it inside, I saw that the box was kind of badly taped up, but I didn't think much of it at first. Once I opened it, the items inside were haphazardly wrapped in plastic and bubble wrap, but again, it's a cheap chair from Amazon, so not too worried yet. Then I pulled out the little plastic envelope with the toolkit and gloves and that's when I realized that this was not a new chair. The gloves were dirty and had clearly been used before and the toolkit was open in several places. Ugh! All of the pieces were included and I didn't see any obvious damage on any of the parts. Plus, the thought of trying to send it back was too much, so I decided to move forward. The first step was attaching the legs which went fine. Then I needed to insert the wheels. Four of the wheels snapped in very easily. The 5th wheel, however, would not budge. I tried it several times and on different legs and it wouldn't move. I noticed the other wheels have a little groove on them and the stubborn one does not. It looks like someone might have tried to create a groove, but gave up. Needless to say, I was disappointed and frustrated. I reached out to Amazon through their chat feature. (I should note hear that the person I dealt with was extremely kind and efficient). After explaining the issue (and pointing out that the chair was an obvious prior return), I was offered the chance to return the item. I didn't really want to do that; I just wanted the wheel I needed. I was then offered a refund of $19.45 and provided a link to purchase new wheels which would cost $11.99 (before taxes and shipping). I explained that wasn't sufficient since after repurchasing the wheels, my actual refund would be about $7.00! I was then sent a new link for wheels that cost $7.99; offered a refund of $25.94; and told I could come back to request a refund for the wheels I after they were delivered. I decided to go with that option instead. I won't get the new wheels until tomorrow, but I went ahead and assembled the rest of the chair. There were no other problems with the assembly. I did it solo, so it took me about 45 minutes and it was pretty easy. I really like the chair itself. It looks nice and works well. I like the ability to recline a little and to flip the armrests up. The seat is nice and wide and I appreciate having a headrest. I'm still annoyed that I was sent a repackaged returned item, but I appreciate the customer service i received from Amazon to resolve the issue.

headline: Bad, bad, and also not good.
review_text_raw: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable. Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

headline: Do you like living on the edge? Buying a chair online is risky!
review_text_raw: Paid ~$200. Price is rising. Knowing what I know now I would buy another at ~$250. There's only so much can be said for a seat you can not test for literally hours at a time. I grabbed this on a gamble. It has mostly paid off. It is not the most comfortable chair I've used. It DOES vaguely pinch on the sides of my thighs - but it is comfortable enough _FOR ME_ to sit in for hours at at a time. At 5'11", 220lbs I would NOT recommend this for ANYONE heavier. And likely not for anyone taller. For me? It has been OK. If you're smaller, and lighter, but sport a waist line wider than ~38" I would NOT recommend this chair. Hard to gauge any individual's proportions, but suffice to say, I am at the comfortable width, weight, and perhaps height capacity for this chair. South of my measurements? It's probably 'OK'. Be honest with yourself. Be really honest with your measurements. I'm laying it all out here on account of how risky it can be to buy a chair you never sat upon. Women especially gonna be a bit wider set in the hips than me. So don't be surprised if the 5 foot waif weighing less than half of me finds more than a mere slight pinch on her beautiful saddle bags. See: there IS pressure at the sides of my hips, but it has genuinely been fine. My immediate impression after first sitting on this thing was "oh no" But after hours of work in front of the computer I am still pleased enough to continue sitting. I figure you could do better, but these mesh chairs are always kinda lame, even the top end Herman Millers are notorious for odd ribs or struts pinching people the wrong way, and the mesh itself has a tendency to roll hip joint in themselves in an unnatural way that foam or even hard wood seats will not. The only thing these mesh chairs have going for them is a breathable butt, and even that is somewhat dubious. But I'm a male, and we run hot, so the luxury of a box fan directed beneath the family jewels commands something of a premium. Against my better judgement I rolled the die on this one and came out on top. Points of note Recline It's fine - has three stages to the tilt on a ratchet, so whereever you posture it remains at that incline until hitting those paddle things again. Pretty great, actually. First - neutral stage - it's comfortable enough. I don't like it, but have sat on it for hours with that posture. Second stage - slightly reclined - is where I usually adjust. Bad posture. I slouch and lounge. It worked perfect for me. If you're prim or proper posture type you may have a better/worse experience. Third stage is near full recline. I love it. I don't get any work done that way, but get yourself a monitor arm and direct a display at a high angle and it's a nice alternative for watching media or even reading. Peak degenerate incline. Use with caution. But bring your own foot rest. I put my feet on the desk! Full chair relines. This is not one of those arrangements where the back rest leans, causing occupants to slowly melt out. No, the seat tilts accordingly also, securing our lazy butts in a bucket of sorts, guaranteeing you will remain in your seat no matter how long you fall asleep while on the clock. Head rest It mostly works. One requirement I had was a head rest. Last thing I want to do when reclining is have to support my head. Madness. It's not bad. Again, I can reline like that for hours. Arm rests are something of a mixed bag. On the one hand, they fold away completely, a feature absent from dozens of competing products - including numerous premiums brands - that immediately ruled them out from my consideration. On the other hand they're somewhat dubious, having three axis for adjustment. You can rotate the pads. Extend the arms... and extend the arms further. Three axis! I don't really have any complaints. I just don't get any use out of the adjustments. Better they're there than not. But I'm not sure anyone shorter would benefit given the options, and I wouldn't recommend anyone taller, so.... Take this whole rating and review with a grain of salt. For what it is worth, I spent days scouring reviews for every mesh chair I could find. This one SEEMED to have fewer complaints of odd geometry that poked or jabbed people in sensitive areas, or and nothing consistent. So I felt confident that if anything DID arise as uncomfortable, it was unique to me, much as the few complaints I did find here. I absolutely can't speak for any of you personally but as of now with a few hundreds hours on this contraption, I can affirm my prediction that there is nothing objectively WRONG about this chair's design. Nothing is uncomfortable making me want to get up after 15 minutes... or 5 hours. Boredom will probably get to you before the deep vein thrombosis. That's pretty much the most I can ask for out of an office chair. Will it work for you? How much do you like gambling? Between price, comfort, and integrity, this one has all around been a winner for me. One star nicked for QA. You're gonna note all sorts of little burrs or rough edges, hinges left and right that behave different. Keep those provided Allen wrenches handy. It is likely something will need tightening. In my case, the left arm wrest hinge unwinds itself. For all that COULD go wrong, and what we would expect out of customer support, I consider myself extremely fortunate and above all, blessed. For anyone else that won't be so fortunate: You are seen. Probably not seen by CAPOT. But I see you. I see you, and thank God I am not you. You have my prayers. In all seriousness, I hope CAPOT support is great and they succeed. This chair is really as much as I could ask for. I would buy another if I had another office space, even granting the inflating price for all the reasons everyone would expect from early 2025. Paid ~$200. Looking at $230 at time of this review. I would still buy at that price.

review_text_raw: To be honest. I had high hopes for this chair. Now. I hate it, I don’t know who is sitting on this for extended time. I can’t. Its supposed to be for bigger people. Im not huge. Its not wide enough with the arms down. I changed the wheels because it didn’t roll correctly. I added a pad because its too firm. The mesh is supposed to be more comfortable. The support is more stiff than relaxed. The design of the head rest is awkward. You’re supposed to be able to adjust it. It got locked into place. Now the height of it is too low. I misplaced the directions. I know there is a way to re-adjust it. Its just not clearly noticeable; such as a knob or button. As far as quality, its well made, as far as sturdiness goes. The thing is that when i go to sit down, there is that lip in front. I have to have an arm down on the chair, hold onto it, then sit down, otherwise the chair rolls away and I would fall on my butt. So, in that way- its not really safe. Even though I have this cushion on it, its still hard and my back hurts all the time Im sitting there. Not immediately, but soon afterwards. If I could return it, I would. That’s the thing about furniture, tho, isn’t it? Once its together, you can’t really take it apart and rebox it and send it back. It takes a week or so to figure it. Then the box is gone. Maybe if it were a little higher. I don’t know. Im fairly sure its all the way up. So yeah. Make sure your surface is really flat. Even changing the wheels doesn’t help. It moves well enough when you’re not in it. But trying to get in it and moving around in it is a different story. Also. I always feel like I’m leaning forward unless I intentionally sit back against against the back of the chair. Then it feels awkward where the headrest is and the back support. I don’t know. Im not a happy camper. Its the second mesh chair. Neither are actually comfortable. There really isn’t enough padding if you’re a bigger guy. This is supposed to support up to 400lb. Well its not breaking, but it’s also not comfortable.

headline: Replacement Chair Base Recommended
review_text_raw: I would love to give this product 5 stars, as the chair itself is WONDERFUL. Very comfortable, great for back support, and the ability to make micro-adjustments for lumbar support are game changing. After just over 1 year of daily usage for work, the material is still in great shape, very breathable, and comfortable. Unfortunately, the portion of the chair legs where the wheels attach have broken twice within the past 5 months. I reached out to the seller initially, and they graciously provided a replacement leg the first time free of charge, but now the leg has broken a second time in the 2 months since the initial replacement (I did not reach out for a second leg replacement). For context, the chair is rated up to 400 lbs and I am ~250 lbs, so my weight being that far below the limit could be a contributing factor? Either way, I do not think that metal chair legs should not be breaking at the welding point when the user is well under the max weight limit. I have opted to purchase a replacement chair base from another seller as well as a floor mat in hopes that this will remedy the issue. The chair itself is 11/10. The base is 3/10 with regular usage, at least in my experience.

headline: Great Instructions, Straightforward Assembly
review_text_raw: I just received this chair today, so my product review is mostly on the packaging, instructions, and assembly. The product was well-packaged, and it was obvious when I unboxed it that a lot of care and thought went into packing it in the most efficient way that would also protect the parts. I was positively impressed with the packaging. I was also incredibly impressed with the instructions and assembly process. I am used to cheaper products where the parts only half fit or important components are missing, or where the instructions were confusing and unclear. This chair's instruction manual was very clear and concise. The diagrams were easy to understand and neat. The screws came labeled and separated and also included the scew types and sizes/lengths, which is handy in case you need to pick up extras at a store somewhere. But they also included one extra of each type of screw, washer, and cover, which I appreciated during assembly. (I didn't find myself worrying what would happen if I dropped a screw, which is something I would normally be distsracted by while working.) The only things I would take points off for were these: 1. The instructions said the chair came with gloves for assembly, but no gloves were included. That was fine with me, but why mention them if you won't include them? The instructions even later say not to use the chair if not all components were present...but all the important ones were, so I assembled it without gloves (as I probably would have done anyway, since it was for me and not another person). 2. It matters which side of the seat is the front, but the sticker was confusing. The instructions show a sticker placed on the side that is the front, and that is where my sticker was placed. However, the sticker says "FRONT" and has an arrow pointing somewhere. In the instructions this arrow pointed to the front. On my seat, however, the arrow pointed to the back. So am I supposed to believe the sticker placement (it was diagonal, so it looked haphazardly slapped on) or the arrow? On that particular step the piece you are screwing into the seat can fit both ways, but thankfully there is a later step where it becomes obvious which side is the front vs. the back. (The arm rests can only be attached to the back.) So I wish that had been clearer up front, but otherwise it was okay. Recommendations for assembly: - To attach the wheels, apply firm, direct, straight-down pressure. I tried screwing them on at first but you just push. Make sure they go in the whole way like the picture shows. - When they say to tighten the screws to only 60%, it's a helpful tip, because you can't fit the armrests on both the seat and chairback at the same time with the screws completely tightened. Just tighten them enough to fit the pieces on, then later you can tighten up the screws. So far I find the chair to be very comfortable and I'm exceedingly happy with it. The lumbar support seems like it could potentially be a little chafy or scratchy, but I'll give the chair a chance before deciding if it's problematic or not. Like I said, I only got the chair today, so I can't speak much to its long-term comfort, durability, or longevity. But I was so impressed with how easy and straightforward they made the assembly that I had to write a review to show my appreciation.

headline: Comfy with Lots of Room
review_text_raw: My wife has a lot of back problems, and her old office chair seemed to be exacerbating this condition. She works from home, so any chair she got would have to not just be comfortable when she first sits down, it has to remain comfortable throughout the day. We went on a quest looking for just the right replacement, and for a while it was a Goldie Locks experience: this chair's too hard, this chair's too soft... this chair's arms are too narrow... this chair's... you get the drift. Long story short, reviews led me to blindly order the same chair you're looking at now. I didn't know what to expect other than most reviewers raved about how comfortable it is and how much lumbar support it offers. Those were the main objectives, so I figured it was worth a shot--especially since it looks like we'll soon be paying more once tariffs hit, and this was on sale NOW. Within days of placing my order, I received a big, heavy box. I bring this up in case you're like me and you live in an apartment complex. Depending on your setup, you may have to lug this thing from the office to your unit. The box weighs roughly 40lbs, which isn't too bad, but it's big enough to be an awkward carry. Especially if you'll have stairs to fight, so please plan accordingly. But there's a reason for all that weight, as you'll soon find out when you open the box. The included instructions are easy to follow, and you'll have all the materials you need. Once done turning screws, you'll have a sturdy and well-padded place to rest. The seat has plenty of cushion--but the real star of the show is that lumbar pad. It's fixed in place, meaning you can't remove it, and at first you might find it a bit intrusive. Stick with it for a minute or two: most chairs have lousy back support, so having a chair with GOOD back support might feel strange to you at first. Very soon, though, I think you'll agree that pad's one of the best things to happen to office chairs since the invention of the home office. My own office chair is a Herman Miller which cost quite a bit more than this chair, and I'm jealous of this thing. The upholstery is pleather, so indeed you can expect it to start flaking off after a few years. That's just the nature of the beast here. That said, the stitching is good, and the padding is plentiful. The cost for what you're getting is far beyond reasonable. The overall build quality is what you would expect from a mid-tier chair; nothing about it feels "cheap." The arms fold up when you're done working for the day, so you can push it under your desk with ease. You have two adjustments: height, and whether or not you'd like to lock the chair into a rigid upright position or allow some tilt (there's also a tension knob underneath so you can adjust how much resistance the chair gives while leaning back). It's too soon to tell if this chair makes a difference to my wife's back, but I will say that out of everything we tried, she took to this one instantly. By all appearances, we're at the part where Goldie Locks finds a chair that's "just right." That's good enough for me! Highly recommended!

headline: Mostly comfortable but seems well made
review_text_raw: Having had to sit in a chair (from a major manufacturer) that had its flaws but lasted about 6 years, this chair was a change for me. The biggest change was the lumbar support as I never had one before and I'm still getting used to it. As a reference, I am 6' tall and weigh about 200 pounds, so chair size was a concern for me when I did my shopping for a replacement. This chair seems a little small for a larger person BUT I sat in only one other chair for years so this may be an issue I just need to get used to. New shoes can feel odd at first too. I do agree the lumbar support seems to push a person forward and does somewhat restrict the length of the chair seat - about 3 inches of my legs, at my knees, do hang over without support but so far I have not experienced any discomfort. I have learned to sit flush against the seat back (VS slouching) which also maximizes use of the lumbar support which feels good but also odd as I never had the support before. Assembly was pretty easy - always a challenge to add the arms when doing it alone, but I managed. Everything else was VERY easy, and the instructions were helpful and provided enough information. The leather also seems of good quality but only time will tell. I do use the chair every day but never for more than about an hour at a time, but several times a day. The color is also nice - pleasant and nicer than bright white. I would suggest to Amazon however, that they increase the height of the seat back for us taller folk - right now it only comes to about my shoulders because I do not slouch, so resting my head against the back is impossible unless I slide my butt forward, which then offsets the use of the lumbar support. Overall, I am satisfied with my purchase and have no regrets.

headline: UPDATE: DEFECTIVE... it was a Great chair... a bit short for tall people!
review_text_raw: I purchased this chair four years ago and really liked it. However, when it was damaged during a move, I attempted to replace it. Unfortunately, the replacement chair had a construction issue that had been repeatedly mentioned in numerous comments spanning over a year at least. This defect prevents the chair from being completely assembled, rendering it unusable (screw holes don’t line up). Amazon has failed to address this issue by removing these defective chairs from its inventory. You won’t be aware of this problem until you’ve almost completed assembling the chair. At that point, you’ll have to disassemble it, rebox it, and return the box to UPS. This is an incredibly inconvenient process, and Amazon must take immediate action to rectify this issue before anyone considers purchasing this chair again. Old review from 2023: Based on someone else's review, it would seem that this chair is perfect for average-height people but less great for those of us who are a bit tall or (according to her) a bit short. I'm 5'9 with most of my height in my legs. I like a chair to be tall enough that my legs can be straight to the floor from my knees to my feet and still have support under my knees. This chair is too short for that, even at it's highest setting, but it can be fixed with a simple replacement of the gas lift cylinder for a mere $20 (search for gas lift cylinder on Amazon). And the extra $20 is worth it because other than that one issue, this chair is great. My first experience with this chair was at work when the firm replaced all of our desk chairs. I loved it so much that I bought it for myself when I went into private practice. The lumbar support hits in just the right spot and moves with your body as you lean in and out. I love the cream color, and the seat is padded nicely. I especially love the liftable arms. I sit at my desk for 8+ hours straight 5-6 days a week, and I never have body pain-- Granted, I am only 36, but I have definitely experienced this with other office chairs that claimed to be "ergonomic". With a simple lift cylinder replacement and a movable standing desk (which I never actually stand at), I can finally sit at my desk without my knees hitting the underside of the desk or my legs having to be extended out to have support under my knees. These two things mean that I don't slump at my desk anymore, and my neck and back thank me! :)

headline: Comfort Meets Functionality in One Great Office Chair
review_text_raw: I am very happy with this chair and would absolutely give it 5 stars. It is incredibly comfortable, and one of my favorite features is the wider seat. I'm 5'8 and 126lbs, so I don't necessarily NEED a wide chair, but I LOVE not feeling cramped while sitting. I tend to tuck one leg up in a sort of half-crossed position, and this chair is perfect for that siting style. The flip-up armrests are another huge plus! They lift completely out of the way, allowing me to slide the entire chair neatly under my desk when I'm not using it, which helps save space. The lumbar support is adjustable and provides great support. Because I tend to sit closer to the edge of the seat, I still prefer using an additional lumbar cushion. However, for anyone who naturally sits further back in the chair, the adjustable lumbar support would be ideal. The headrest is also adjustable up and down, making it easy to find a comfortable position. The mesh material feels high-quality, supportive and breathable which I really appreciate considering I work from home and am in this chair for long periods of time. Assembly was straightforward as well. I put it together by myself in about 30 minutes to an hour and I wasn't rushing. The instructions were easy to follow, and all of the pieces were clearly labeled. The only small issue I encountered was that one black washer was missing from the hardware pack. Fortunately, I had a spare from another piece of furniture, so it wasn't a problem for me. Overall, this chair exceeded my expectations. It's comfortable, adjustable, well-designed, and versatile enough to accommodate different sitting styles. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a supportive office desk chair.

headline: Decent chair but not for us taller people
review_text_raw: I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with. For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive. After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected. The good: 1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal. 2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems. 3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me. 4. Appearance. Very nice. 5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy. The not so good. 1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

product_title: TRALT Office Chair Ergonomic Desk Chair - Gaming Chair with Lumbar Support
headline: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
review_text_raw: I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended. Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame). The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for). While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down. Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes. Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

headline: Quality and comfort
review_text_raw: This office chair looked nice in the listing photos, but it’s even better in person. I ordered this for my home office space which previously had an armchair that my kids broke by tipping in it. I love the light gray color of this one, since my desk is gray wood, and I love that it is a leather-type material that can be wiped down, since I have messy kids. It has a nice, stylish sleek look to it that elevates my office space. The chair was easy to assemble, but it does come with some assembly needed. It took about a half hour to get it assembled. For reference, I am 5’6”, and at max height my heels are about 3” off the ground. In the middle setting, my heels just touch the ground, with a couple more inches to drop. As far as width, I would say it’s standard for a full-sized office chair. I am about average in size, but I do think it’s more accommodating for larger adults than many others, due to the fact that the sides are mostly open, and the arms easily lift up. It’s also a pretty deep seat bottom and tall seat back. The build is also very sturdy. I couldn’t ask for a better office chair. I’m super happy with the overall quality, features, and design of this chair. I can’t imagine that it would disappoint anyone who bought it.

product_title: ALLGOD Office Desk Chair, Big and Tall Computer Gaming Chair with footrest
headline: Comfortable adjustable-lumbar chair, kind of annoying to assemble
review_text_raw: I don't have much experience putting furniture together. This was probably the most challenging piece I've assembled so far. The two armrests were by far the hardest part. Start to finish, it took me about an hour to put the thing together. First, the instruction manual also has a typo worth knowing about. One step lists screw (11) as M6 x 25 mm, while the parts legend and the screw bag both show M6 x 30 mm. This happened right in the middle of the hardest part. I spent a while convinced I had the wrong screws before realizing it was just an error in the booklet. At least the parts are labeled, with FRONT printed on the seat plate, so orientation wasn't a guess. Still, the typo cost me a lot of wasted time. Not worth deducting a star in the review, but a real annoyance. Once it's together, though, the chair is really comfortable. I like office chairs with soft arm support. These armrests stay comfortable through long stretches of sitting. The headrest pillow is a nice touch and gives good support when I lean back. My favorite feature is the inflatable lumbar support. With a pronounced lower back curve, I find pumping up the lumbar makes a real difference. A separate back cushion isn't something I've needed. The faux leather feels pleasant to the touch. There wasn't any chemical smell when I started using it. Because it's a leather-style surface, it breathes less than a mesh chair. Where I live it gets hot and humid, so that's definitely a tradeoff. Anyone who sweats a lot might want a different material. The wheels roll smoothly across wood floors without sticking or catching. Moving it around my workspace is pretty easy. Overall, the assembly could be smoother or better documented, but the comfort, the adjustable lumbar, and how easily it rolls make this a solid office chair... once it's put together.

headline: Mr. Picky loves the chair
review_text_raw: The Mr. Picky I live with is loving this chair after rejecting many others. It is super comfortable and looks and feels like quality furniture. It is high enough to support his frame of six feet and support his neck which was a problem with other chairs we tried. It was very easy to put together and only took me 40 minutes. I just have a few notes to make it easier for you. There is a QR code to scan for a video or the chair comes with an instruction booklet in the bag with the seat of the chair. I showed in a picture that you may have to move the arm piece a little to see all four holes that will attach the arm to the back and seat cushions. The instructions talk about 25 and 30 mm screws in the instructions book where you attach the arm but there are only 30 mm screws included and only these are needed. One tip not mentioned is you need to lean the back piece on something like the box to make it easy to attach the arm and then the seat cushion also to the arm. These are all minor and I hope will save you time when you put together this chair. I think it is well worth the cost (and even more) and it is so comfortable to sit on. The wheels were able to easily glide on my low pile carpet. It is an added bonus that the arms lift up to push the chair closer to your desk if needed. It looks good in any office or even a living room.

The new VIOLET mesh computer chair is extremely comfortable even after spending most of my days and nights sitting in it since i spend many, many hours daily working, communicating and gaming on my desktop computer. the chair may appear to be lightweight; however, it's got a decent amount of weight to it because of the high quality materials used to make it, especially the solid metal parts that make up the strong and stable base. The lumbar support is especially helpful to maintain proper posture and spinal alignment, yet again there was a small issue in that i generally sit with a slight forward lean or, as stated earlier, with my shoulders directly over my hips. in order to have full back support, you must lean back slightly, and that's an awkward position for me in any chair. the arm rests can be moved down at your sides or in an upright position as if there were no arm rests at all. and i have found myself switching back and forth between the two depending on what i am doing and how much movement i require in the chair. they can also be moved forward and backward a short distance, which i did find a little bothersome when the arm rests were down and i bumped them when i happened to move my arm(s) a little. they do not lock in place, but i'm positive that this is just another little concern that i can easily get used to since the old chair's arm rests were not adjustable at all. did i mention that it's PURPLE!?! review_text_raw: I'll start off by addressing the title. It's not the most comfortable chair. If you sit and play games for 10 hours a day, you might as well go a little higher and get something with a bit more cushion. I personally loved the style of this chair, and it was quite a bit off the standard price. So for me, I think it was worth a shot. I really like it. As a larger person 6'5" 240lbs it holds my frame and weight well. The footrest however, feels a little flimsy, and is also fairly small. I probably won't be using it. It DOES tuck completely away under the seat when not in use. The chair is SILENT so far, and rolls well. All the parts work, reclining is easy and smooth. I love the mesh back, as it has some softness, give, and breathability. The head and back support are a little hard, but they probably need a bit of wear to break in well. The chair was easy to put together. With an allen ratchet it took me about 25 minutes. This is not my first chair to assemble, so a first timer with the tools provided might take an hour or so. If you want a little style, and need that gaming look, this is a solid chair. Maybe a BIT higher than some other chairs, but I think the quality is worth it. My chair DID say GTRacing not Player but it is not a knockoff. Other than that stitching, it is exactly like the description and image. They make chairs that say both. Not an issue for me, but that is a possibility I guess. Recommended if you want the gaming chair look and can spend a bit more than a budget chair.

There's also a locking mechanism to keep the chair fixed upright or allow it to tilt. The force needed to tilt can be adjusted via a large tension handle underneath, but I found it just right out of the box. As far as comfort - the material is made of a mesh like fabric, which breaths really well, but it that material on the armrests does feel a little rough on the forearms near my elbows, but only just barely. The seat cushion is very comfortable, and overall, I think the chair is really very comfortable to sit in for long periods of time.

headline: Great Lumbar Support, Simple Design — but the Seat Cushion Misses the Mark
review_text_raw: I really wanted to love this office chair because it has a few standout features, especially the removable lumbar support, which honestly feels fantastic. It hits the lower back in just the right spot and makes long work sessions a lot more comfortable. The adjustable headrest is another nice touch — easy to position and supportive when you lean back. Where this chair fell short for me is the seat cushion. Even though it’s advertised as a high‐resilience memory foam cushion, it just didn’t feel plush or supportive enough during longer use. I found myself shifting around more than I expected. This is definitely a simple office chair in terms of adjustments. You get height adjustment and the ability to move the lumbar support up or down, but there’s no way to tweak the seat angle or depth. If you prefer a chair with lots of fine‐tuning options, this one might feel limited. On the positive side, the mesh back is breathable and keeps things cool, and the wheels glide smoothly across basic office carpet and hard floors. Assembly was straightforward, and the chair feels sturdy once put together. The base of the chair is solid, but the chair itself is pretty lightweight. It has a great size and weight balance, looking clean and professional for any office desk! Overall, I’d say this is a good everyday office chair if lumbar support is your top priority. The back and head support are genuinely great — I just wish the seat cushion lived up to the rest of the design.

review_text_raw: Honestly I hate to write this review, one because I hate complaining and two I was super excited for a new gaming chair...... The back support is leaning to the side even after trying to adjust the T-bar support bracket, it’s the tilt mechanism that is causing it to lean, even after trying to reposition and tighten everything possible and the knob that the backrest T-bar slides into the tilt mechanism, it has too much play due to parts not fitting properly causing it to much free play to move around....... Also wouldn’t call this a massage chair with this super cheap non adjustable vibrating block (which you barely feel) that someone clearly ripped the backrest foam out with their fingers and it’s super uneven and crooked.(see attached images) Lastly, chair is on the smaller side! I’m 5’ 7” about 185lbs and the cushions are not too comfortable. I can feel the hard support under the seat cushion luckily the backrest and neck support pillows allow some sort of comfort for the backrest. I’ve sat in cheap $70-80 chairs that were 10x more comfortable and better quality, wish I knew the names and would have definitely purchased one of those instead, I figured spending double I would get a decent chair that I would enjoy ....... headline: Easy recline, difficult foot rest
review_text_raw: The main frame of this chair feels sturdy. The cushioning on the chair itself is thin but supportive. The lumbar and neck cushions are separate and allow many placement positions. The lumbar pillow has a solid gel like cushion (see photos), the neck pillow has a kind of fibrous filling. They are both zippered. The zippers slide easily. The chair easily reclines, and the levers for adjusting are easy to access and work well.

headline: Its much better than nothing and much cheaper than higher quality chairs
review_text_raw: I'm a big believer in "you get what you pay for" and I usually advise to save up, make one purchase, make one investment and don't worry about it for a few years. But something about this chair's value really scales, especially if you can grab it on sale. I got mine in white for $75 including tax and shipping. Many quality gaming chairs cost hundreds of dollars. There a handful of cheap office chairs you can snag for $60. This chair compared to one of those generic office chair is worth the extra $15. If you're looking at this chair for $90 or higher, then the former statement is true (save up). Anyway. I've had this chair for a day now and it isn't perfect. I'll go over what I like and what I don't like. Appearance: It looks nice. Doesn't look or feel too cheap. The base is metal with plastic feet. Many chairs have plastic base with plastic feet.+1pt Functionality: This chair has a handful of features-- You can adjust the height. +1pt But it only has about a 3in range -1pt It has a lock to let you remain upright and can be unlocked so you can recline back. +1pt It does NOT have a way to lock in the reclined position. -1pt Comfort: This chair is pretty comfy. It has a removable/adjustable head pillow and a removable/adjustable lumbar pillow as well. +1pt It is a little stiff. Some people may like that. It also may break it after a while. I've only had it one day so I will update if something new develops. The chair has a *mostly* comfortable width to me. It measures 19" for arm to arm. But it has this little "cushion" that tries to contour your legs that makes it a little uncomfortable to sit with my legs spread even a little. I have to keep my knees closer together than I normally would to keep the "cushion" from digging into the side of my legs. Because of this, there is really only about 16" of room for your butt or the sides of your thighs. I'm about 5'10" Male 215lbs size 38 pants XL shirt. I think I am at the cusp of being able to comfortably sit in this. It was not made with larger people in mind. It does state a 250lb weight limit while we're on the topic. -1pt Assembly: I've assembled several office chairs before and this process was similar and just as easy. +1pt If you aren't experienced or if you struggle with Ikea stuff, you may find it difficult. The hardware that they include is kinda junk. If you have the luxury of using your own hardware (or hand tools at least), I would highly recommend it. I had one bolt that had really junky threads from the factory and I couldn't do much about it, just had to cross thread it and tighten it the best I could. I had another bolt that stripped and the thread never would grab. Luckily there was one extra included in the packaging and I ended up being able to tighten it without cross threading. I think I got lucky. 90% of the assembly was smooth sailing and the few snags that arose, I knew exactly what to do. Again, if you aren't experienced with this, it could easily turn into a headache and a return to amazon over poor quality hardware

review_text_raw: What I have learned from many years of purchasing and putting together chairs like this is it's always best to buy a chair upon which the arms are separate from the body of the chair. There are many chairs on the market that are put together such that the entire support of the chair rests on the arms connecting the bottom of the chair to the body of the chair. headline: Doesn't Have Advertised Features (ex. Rocking) & Support Doesn't Honor Free Replacements Advertised
review_text_raw: UPDATE 5: The seller responded and AGAIN refused to honor their advertised free gas cylinder replacement, even though the original they provided failed within 3 months. Their excuse was that we were past the return window. The problem with that excuse is that we contacted them well within that window with a replacement request, and they repeatedly pretended not to understand the request, then to reject it. So they're stalling customers until they can say you aren't eligible for anything anymore. Also, if you read reviews, you'll notice a "warranty department" is mentioned, and that's who supposedly sends out the replacement parts they advertised. This apparently doesn't exist. Strongly suspect there might be some fake reviews in here given the way the company uses false advertisements and a complete lack of support. Will be reporting them to Amazon today. You should note, they seem to have removed the image that offered the free wheel replacements (though I believe I still have a screenshot for that report I'll file). But they do still mention free gas cylinder replacements in the original is too high (which is what I originally requested). I've now had to spend more money on replacement wheels because the seller lied about offering free replacements (the rubber ones safe for hardwood floors). And now I'll have to buy another cylinder for it. 100% not letting this go. I'm so tired of companies selling furniture items here with false advertising, knowing it's too difficult for most customers to return those items. UPDATE 4: Exactly 3 months from the day we ordered this chair, and after refusing to honor their advertised offer for a lower replacement cylinder, the original gas cylinder for this chair failed. No one using it uses it roughly. No one using it even comes close to the advertised weight limit. It was just being used in a stable position and suddenly failed. We reset it, and it failed again within minutes, making the chair unusable for us. I'm going to contact the seller one more time and insist on a replacement cylinder given they outright advertise they provide one, but if they refuse again, I'll be taking it up with Amazon, because this combination of quality issues and poor support is not acceptable. UPDATE 3: I definitely cannot recommend this chair. After weeks of use (with the wrong wheels and gas cylinder size because the company refused to honor their offer to send replacements), this chair causes a lot of pain. Lower back pain in particular is really bad. I suspect it's due to the combination of the very hard seat (disappointing given I looked for a spring-based seat intentionally -- if they're there, they're too small to be of any use as you still feel like you're sitting on a hard board) and the lack of lumbar support. Despite their description, there is basically NO lumbar support with this chair. It's incredibly painful even after minor use. I may even have to go back to the old chair this was replacing as the entire point was to reduce pain and increase comfort, of which this chair does neither. It's poorly made. It feels very unbalanced if you lean at all (especially with the lack of proper tension to prevent you falling backwards all the way). Way too many cracking and creaking sounds for a chair this new being used well below its advertised weight limit. Not supported at all by the seller (other than offering minor refunds to keep the junk and figure out how to dispose of it yourself at a loss). Just overall feels unsafe, uncomfortable, and I can't trust either the chair or the seller. UPDATE 2: After several back-and-forth messages with the seller here on Amazon, they've repeatedly ignored requests for the free replacement wheels (needed if you use it on hardwood floors) and the free replacement gas cylinder (if the original is too high) that are advertised on this page in the product images. After ignoring the request repeatedly, along with any tips on getting the tension to actually provide... tension... they flat out refused to honor their advertised offer for those replacement parts. All they did was offer a very small refund if we're willing to keep the chair... without the wheels needed for our floors... without the appropriately-sized canister... and without any reasonable tension function to lean back safely (forget "rocking" as noted in the description because this chair can't do that). It would cost us more to buy our own wheels and canister than what they offered, and that still doesn't address the false advertising of this being a rocking office chair or the unsafe lack of tension for the recline function. I would absolutely never do business with this company again, and we'll be contacting Amazon to see what can be done about them refusing to honor what they advertised. Extremely disappointed after a very long search for a replacement chair. UPDATE: This page, in the images, says the company will provide free replacement rubber casters / wheels if needed (which you need for hard floors), and a free lower replacement gas cylinder if the chair is too high (which it is for my wife). After asking them to send these multiple times via Amazon's messaging system, they've so far refused to do so (will update if they sort this out soon). They've also responded to questions about fixing the lack of tension and the misrepresentation about this being a "rocking" chair (it's definitely not; just reclining), and all we ever seem to get is a copy/paste response offering a small partial refund if we agree to keep the chair. We keep trying to tell them we're hoping to keep the chair, but we needed info on getting the tension to increase and we need the replacement parts they offered to make it work. But they've mostly ignored specific questions and just keep saying the same things. Until the last message where they said they couldn't send replacements for the "missing parts," even though we never said anything was missing. We're just requesting the parts they offer to send right in their Amazon description. Not happy with support at all so far. -- ORIGINAL REVIEW I have mixed feelings on this chair. First, it feels like a sturdy build. And if you're on the larger side, the cushion offers plenty of support -- firm, but mostly comfortable. The exception to the seat's comfort is that the front edge is very firm, and it can cut into the back of your thighs, negatively impacting circulation. This was the problem with my old chair and why I was replacing it. Normally I prefer a higher chair, but this is causing issues even at its lowest setting. The seller does mention in the images they'll send a lower cylinder if necessary, so if I keep the chair and receive that, I'll update on how that affects the pain at the front of the seat. The seller also offers to send replacement wheels if you need the rollerblade-style kind for hard floors. The plastic ones are extremely loud and totally inappropriate for hard floors and their protective mats, so it's nice they provide this option. But if you know you'll need them, I'd request them early. Otherwise you won't be able to fully assemble things until they arrive, or you'll have to risk damage to your floors using the defaults until the replacements can be swapped in. While I like the sturdy sense I get from the chair, there are two big problems for me. I've contacted the seller hoping I'm just not figuring out the settings properly, but I'll update if appropriate later. 1. The description advertises this as a "rocking" office chair. With office chairs, that means something very specific -- the back and seat move in unison in a true rocking action. This looks like the seat can angle back a bit based on the video, but it doesn't seem to do that when "rocking." All it does is lean the top back. That's not a rocking office chair, which was an absolute requirement in me choosing this as a replacement for my old chair. Again, I'm hoping I just missed a control or something and that this will work as-advertised. Oddly though, when the foot rest is out, the seat itself does seem to recline back, so it clearly *can.* It just won't rock otherwise? And if you have heavier legs, or longer ones like I do, the leg rest isn't really usable because your center of gravity will get thrown off (and that's the one thing that doesn't seem sturdy in general). So, for a chair advertised for bigger users, are we simply not "allowed" to use the rocking function because it's tied to the leg rest?? 2. I'm also having issues with the tension knob. All the way in one direction and the back of the chair practically falls backwards the moment you touch it. All the way in the other direction and there's barely any more tension that that. It leads to a very insecure feeling unless you lock the "rocking" function, which again was a major deciding factor in choosing this chair. I'm hoping I'm missing something here too because I've never seen an office chair with this lack of tension. Other than that, the back is comfortable, and I like that the arms are adjustable (width during installation, and height while in-use). Aside from the rocking and tension, two things would make this chair near-perfect though: 1. Adjustable lumbar support. Fixed lumbar support is all but useless in an executive chair because if you're sitting properly you're not going to be leaning back all the time. Proper lumbar support doesn't require you to recline back. It should help you stay upright and maintain your posture. 2. I agree with another reviewer who was disappointed in the lack of head rest. For all the padding on the back of this chair (which is soft, yet dense enough it feels like it will hold up for quite a while), there's no real head rest. The head area is relatively flat and sits too far back, so your head won't even touch it unless you're lying back in more of a reclined position. The only other comment I'll make for now is that any reclining is pretty loud. There's a surprising amount of squeaking and creaking for a new chair. If I keep it, I might see if something needs to be greased. But if not, just know that could be an issue if that sort of noise bothers you. Oh, and like another reviewer, my box also arrived quite damaged. The entire bottom was split open. At first we were afraid we received a used chair after ordering a new one, but the internal pieces seemed OK and everything was there. But if multiple people are receiving damaged, open boxes, I'd make sure you have somewhere sheltered for this to be delivered. Had this been left by our garage in the rain (as many larger packages are here), the chair would have been ruined before we even opened it.

All the way in one direction and the back of the chair practically falls backwards the moment you touch it. All the way in the other direction and there's barely any more tension that that. Fixed lumbar support is all but useless in an executive chair because if you're sitting properly you're not going to be leaning back all the time. Proper lumbar support doesn't require you to recline back. It should help you stay upright and maintain your posture. 2. I agree with another reviewer who was disappointed in the lack of head rest. For all the padding on the back of this chair (which is soft, yet dense enough it feels like it will hold up for quite a while), there's no real head rest. The head area is relatively flat and sits too far back, so your head won't even touch it unless you're lying back in more of a reclined position. The only other comment I'll make for now is that any reclining is pretty loud. There's a surprising amount of squeaking and creaking for a new chair. If I keep it, I might see if something needs to be greased. But if not, just know that could be an issue if that sort of noise bothers you. Oh, and like another reviewer, my box also arrived quite damaged. The entire bottom was split open. At first we were afraid we received a used chair after ordering a new one, but the internal pieces seemed OK and everything was there. But if multiple people are receiving damaged, open boxes, I'd make sure you have somewhere sheltered for this to be delivered. Had this been left by our garage in the rain (as many larger packages are here), the chair would have been ruined before we even opened it.

product_title: EXCEBET Big and Tall Office Chair with Footrest, PU Leather High Back Executive Office Chair 400lbs, Ergonomic Computer Chairs Lumbar Support for Heavy People (All Black)
headline: Great Chair...bit of a read, but good info maybe...
review_text_raw: This is a bit long, but maybe will help someone. The chair is great. I have been looking for a chair for several months, and finally settled on this one. My only hang-up was that I really wanted genuine leather, which this chair is not. The chairs with genuine leather are either (a) priced well over $1k, or (b) are cheap junk. This chair replaces my old, genuine leather chair, that was less than 3 years old. Unfortunately, it fell into the "cheap junk" category, as I came to find out. I had ordered that chair, just based on the leather...and in fact that is the ONLY part of the chair that held up. I replaced the base when it broke, replaced the hydraulic lift when it broke, and had to re-work the arm rests so they would stop falling off. The sides and back were also deteriorating...so quite literally, the ONLY "good" part of that chair was the actual leather itself. So, apologies for the back story, but that leads me into the review of this chair. In putting it together, I could easily see that this chair is hands down much more well-made than my old one. The base of the old one appeared to be a cast metal or some kind. Problem with cast metals are that they tend to be brittle...which is exactly what happened to me...one of the legs broke off with no warning. This chair's base is welded steel...I'm pretty confident it's not going anywhere. Second is the comfort. Lesson learned from the old chair is that if it appears to be thin padding, it definitely is. After a year or so, I had to add more fill to the old chair to keep it from being so "flat.” It was filled with some sort of cubed foam. This chair has the spring-cushion seat, and bolstered back with lumbar support. It is very comfortable, and the padding is 2, maybe 3 times thicker than the old chair. While the covering of this chair is not genuine leather, it does have a very good feel, looks to be of high quality, and is breathable - which would have been my biggest complaint had it not been. The arm rests are generous in size, and fit comfortably under the desk without hitting. I probably could have done without the footrest, but suppose it may be nice to have at some point. The tilt features work very well...plenty of firm resistance, but not so much to force you up straight, or be horizontal with a simple lean back...the tension is just right. Putting the chair together was easy...took me maybe 30 minutes, and half of that was easily spent just unpacking all the parts, as they were well protected in the box. I would agree with what some others have said about needing a second set of hands with getting the back on. I managed okay, just me, but probably should have had my wife come help...but you know, men can do it all on their own... So, all in all, I'm very happy with this chair, thus far. Hopefully it will withstand the test of time...if I can even get three years out of it, that's okay...I feel a lot better about getting a $2-300 chair every 3 years, than I do about spending $700+ each time. Some photos for reference...you can see how thick the padding is, compared to the other chair.

product_title: EXCEBET Big and Tall Office Chair with Footrest, PU Leather High Back Executive Office Chair 400lbs, Ergonomic Computer Chairs Lumbar Support for Heavy People (All Black)
headline: Good Price Good Comfort
review_text_raw: For reference I'm 6'2 and 275lbs (~125kg). I work in an office 5 days a week, 9am to 5pm so I needed something that would at least let me be comfortable while I type my life away. Assembly was fairly easy, just make sure that when you get to the part where you have to put the back rest and the seat together that you actually keep the 4 screws that attach to the back rest loose so that it will fit into the slot of the seat. In terms of cushion I'd give it a solid 7.5 maybe 8 out of ten. It's not a recliner couch you have at home, but for an office chair at this price it's pretty dang close. It's definitely enough to make you start dozing off if you're not too careful. The main reason why I went for this one though was for the leg rest. Kinda have to get used to it to find the sweet spot because if you're fully upright and you try to use the leg rest the chair will lean forward a lot due to how it's built, it's not the most sturdy thing in the world so you gotta balance it out by reclining a bit. For a big and tall chair the leg rest isn't as big or wide as I would hope for it to be, I find myself really squeezing myself to try and fit both of them on and end up just crossing my legs most of the time, but it's still comfortable. I'd give it a 7/10. In terms of back support and the firmness of it, I haven't had issues with it or my posture, but for those that slouch, do be careful as it's not built fix or support poor posture. I'd give it a 6/10, but in my opinion this shouldn't take away from the overall score since that's not really what these are for, if you want ergonomics and good lumbar support you go for chairs designed for that. If you want casual comfort at the workplace and you're able to get up and walk around a lot then this is fine as it's not killing your spine as long as you're not fully set into it all day without breaks. Overall for the price I would highly recommend it. There are a few other chairs I'm looking at that's more expensive than this that'll surely beat it, but for fast delivery and pretty dang good comfort for a big fella, would definitely recommend.

product_title: EXCEBET Big and Tall Office Chair with Footrest, PU Leather High Back Executive Office Chair 400lbs, Ergonomic Computer Chairs Lumbar Support for Heavy People (All Black)
headline: My Goldilocks Chair
review_text_raw: I wish I could fully express how long and hard I was searching for what I'd begun to call my "Goldilocks chair." I had incredibly specific things I was looking for: - a padded seat (I work and game at the same desk, so I spend the majority of my day in my chair) that was wide enough for me (a 5'7", plus-sized woman) to sit cross-legged - padded armrests (surprisingly difficult to find) that wouldn't get in the way - or could be moved out of the way - if I did sit cross-legged - a back that would recline (not rock, which was sometimes hard to differentiate in product descriptions) - my white whale: a footrest to prop my legs up on for crochet and reading I ordered a possibly insane number of chairs only to return them (and for some of them, eat the cost in my depseration); I tried finding search points I could compromise on (especially that footrest - I'd all but resigned to get a tiny ottomon for my itty-bitty space under the desk); I took to Reddit forums and talked to friends, family, coworkers, family's coworkers; I gave up and continued on sitting in my old gaming chair that was quite literally falling apart several times, only to resume the search when I had the emotional fortitude to do so. This chair was like a God-send. It fulfills *every* *single* *one* of my criteria. The back, seat, and arms are plush, but supportive and (after wearing it in a little) incredibly soft and comfortable without feeling like it's going to go flat on you. After lifting the armrests high enough I'm able to cross my legs without pressing against them at all. The reclining feature is exactly what I needed (though for my purposes, I mostly just need the recliner to lock at a preferred angle for day-to-day use; the seat does tilt back some when you recline, which can be annoying, but *how* annoying depends primarily on *why* you're reclining, and whether or not you have room under your desk for your footrest to be a little higher than usual.) The back is tall enough for me to rest my head against with no issues. The footrest can be fully extended or pressed against the seat as an extra cushion for when my legs don't want to cross quite as tightly as usual (or it can be used as a tiny platform for my yarn ball!) And the pale purple and design on the cushion are pretty! At the time it felt like a gamble; I'd been burned so many times. But when this came in and my husband put it together it fit me like a glove. Everyone has different needs, so I don't know if this will meet yours or not, but I couldn't be happier.

product_title: Corsair TC500 Luxe Gaming Chair – Premium Breathable Fabric – Wide Seat – Five-Way Adjustable Armrests – Adjustable Built-in Lumbar Support – 90-135 Degree Recline – Sherwood
headline: Great chair
review_text_raw: This is is such an upgrade from my last sub $100 chair. The adjustable back support is worth the cost alone. I was hunching over in my last chair and now my posture is correct. These chairs are made of soft fabric. I am 5’4 and it adjusts to my height. There is a qr code for build instructions on the top of box when you open it. The arm rests can be adjusted multiple ways. There is a tab on each arm that lets you move them up and down. I didn't notice this at first, so I couldn't reach the arm rests till I moved them up. The box is very heavy and very large. You will need 2 people to pick it up or you can turn it on its side and roll it like i did if you don't have help. Cons: The fabric has a break-in period and might feel stiff at first, but it will adjust the more you use it. I recommend getting a memory foam cushion if this bothers you. There is a primer-like new smell but will go away in a few days. You might want to open a window during this period if it bothers you. Since the arm rests move if you pull on them, I recommend grabbing the wings near the top of the chair to move it.

product_title: Corsair TC500 Luxe Gaming Chair – Premium Breathable Fabric – Wide Seat – Five-Way Adjustable Armrests – Adjustable Built-in Lumbar Support – 90-135 Degree Recline – Sherwood
headline: A Great Chair.... Almost
review_text_raw: First I want to start off by saying I really wanted to love this chair so badly! I was so excited to buy this and get it into my office setup, but it really fell short of expectations. The 3 star rating is for the $550 price point - I was able to get it on a considerable sale, so for the price of about $300 it’s more worth it and would give it 4 stars but I cannot recommend this chair at full price. Cons: - My office does get warm with my gaming computer and this chair absolutely gets hot after sitting for a couple hours compared to my old mesh one, not sweaty but uncomfortable. - The back has awful padding. The lower portion with the adjustable lumbar feels like a rock pushing into your back if you actually use it so I have to keep it almost all the way depressed. Then right where it transitions from the diamond stitching to the flat part where the wings are, it’s like there’s a metal rod going across (likely the top of the adjustable lumbar thing) but man it’s really not comfortable to lean back into or use that fully reclined position. So overall the lower back is really hard, then there’s this middle that’s extremely plush, and then at the top middle back below your shoulder blades it’s hard as a rock so it’s unfortunate. Not as comfy as most good reviews make it out to be but it’s also not unbearable just being picky due to price point. - It squeaks!!! I was hoping a few of these reviews were just a couple bad batches but nope. Same thing others have said, right where the metal hinge is on the left side, if your sitting and using the rocking feature it creaks and squeaks every time you rock. Thats something that was just fully unacceptable for a chair at this price. - The hip bolstering really digs into the sides of my legs if man spreading and hurts after a while. - Overall the chair just doesn’t seem too sturdy/stable on the base. It has a fair amount of play when moving around but again not the end of the world it’s still fairly solid. Pros: - The bottom cushion is actually really comfortable for me sitting in it all day long even though it’s more on the firm side. It’s also big so even at 6’2 with all height in my legs I can kick a leg up. - While the backing is annoyingly uneven, I think it promotes much better posture than my other chair. - It looks just so good!! and it is definitely made out of good premium materials, I do see this chair lasting a long time! - Building it took maybe 15 minutes and you really don’t need any instruction, it’s common sense for anyone who’s ever put something together. - The pillow is so comfy! - While the wheels are stiff, and the chair is heavy I was worried about how it rolled on carpet but man it’s a breeze! It rolls really well around the room on carpet. - For the most part it’s a chair that I can sit in all day and it’s comfortable. The backing is borderline making me want to return it, but I got a great discount so I’m sticking with it. - Oh and the arm rests! At 6’2 I have longer arms but what... they are perfect for me. They aren’t too far forward or too far back at all. That’s why they have the 180 design if you want to get closer to your desk just flip them around and scoot up! Overall, again don’t buy this chair at full price you’ll likely be disappointed as the creaking and the back padding are my biggest complaints. If you can get 40%+ off it’s more worth it but be warned if you’re looking into something that’s plushy. It’s very firm. But it’s really pretty to look at!

product_title: Corsair TC500 Luxe Gaming Chair – Premium Breathable Fabric – Wide Seat – Five-Way Adjustable Armrests – Adjustable Built-in Lumbar Support – 90-135 Degree Recline – Sherwood
headline: Great chair for a killer price.
review_text_raw: I have had a Secret Lab chair that I have been using for work for the past 6 years and have had my share of issues with it (their warranty is a joke). When I had to return to the office and took my Secret Lab back, I needed a chair for home. I refused to pay over $500 for a new chair. I looked into this one and got it around Christmas time for $250. At that price, this chair is a phenomenal value. It is a little smaller than my Titan XL but accommodates my 6-ft 280 Lb frame without complaining. It looks awesome. The green that I have really feels like a master chief OD green. (I'd love to embroider a Chief helmet on the back). The adjustment of the lumbar is great and I was able to make it more comfortable and supportive than my Secret Lab. My only gripe is the armrests don't lock into place. While they are great for their adjustability and range of motion, they can easily move when you are adjusting or really "in the zone." That's really the reason for 4 stars because the armrests are what you interact with the most after the seat itself.

headline: Comfortable and attractive desk chair
review_text_raw: My old desk chair broke last week after about 2 years of use. I ordered this one from Amazon and it arrived yesterday (delivery was delayed by 3 days without explanation) The chair was not super difficult to assemble but also not easy. Putting the last piece in required me having my son help as it definitely took more than 2 hands to get the 2 pieces to line up. I am tall (5'11") and I work very long hours at my desk for work and also sit at my desk for my hobby of writing fiction. This chair is good for me as it sits higher than my last chair did, I appreciate this as I am taller than many people. It is wide set, meaning the arms are further apart than my old chair which might bother some people but I like that it means I do not always have to sit in one position when I'm sitting here for a long time. I also appreciate the ability to rotate the arms up and out of the way as this means I can push the chair more fully under the desk when I'm not using it. The back is not as high as my old chair was which is a bit of a negative for me, I specifically ordered a high back chair and this is several inches shorter than my old chair. The back comes just above my shoulders by an inch or two, but I cannot lean my head back comfortably. Also, it is not a "leather chair" as the description says. It's bonded leather which means it is possible for the leather to wear off of the chair as others have stated. I had wanted to order the cream but I'm glad I ordered dark brown instead now that i know it's not a fully leather chair. The base is heavy, the wheels roll nicely and it's a very nice and solid chair. The box weighed about 50 lbs which shows how heavy duty the chair is. I'm hopeful this will help the chair last a long time.

headline: Big chair, good quality, with a trick to assembling it
review_text_raw: When I assembled this chair, I ran into a problem that I was eventually able to solve, but I couldn’t find any instructions that would have shown me how. So to save yourself some time and stress: when you attach the back of the chair to the seat, you will need to connect a metal tongue protruding from the back piece to a similar part protruding from the seat. But it may seem like the piece from the back isn’t long enough for the two parts to connect properly. What I didn’t realize at first is that you might have to pull the part sticking out from the back with some force in order to get it into position. The reason is that the part on the back is meant to move in and out: it actually operates the mechanism that makes the lumbar support protrude when you sit up straight but retract when you lean back. So if it’s not sticking out far enough, just pull it smoothly but firmly until it comes out all the way, and you should be able to connect the parts as per the instructions without difficulty. This is a big, strong, sturdy, comfortable desk chair. It’s a good choice for a biggish person who wants a lot of support while sitting. The price is quite reasonable. But it takes up a fair amount of floor space, it’s heavy, and the arms are wide set, so if you’re not a tall person, you might not be able to rest both your elbows at the same time. I suspect that a medium-to-small person might be happier with a more modestly sized alternative.

headline: Hurts my back
review_text_raw: I bought two of these chairs when the pandemic started - one for me and one for my kid. I had brown furniture in the family room, so I decided to add two desks and turn it into a make-shift office. It's been almost a year now, and I feel that I can write a review. I am not a fan of people who review 5 minutes after they bought a product. So here it goes. I liked the chair for the first month or two. Then the seat started sinking in, and the back was too far (I'm 5 ft tall), so I had to buy a back cushion. My hips started hurting, so I bought a seat cushion. The chair is no ergonomic, nor is it a long term solution. It looks comfortably overstuffed, but it's really not. I often feel like I'm sliding to the right, as if the seat is slightly tilted. My son is 10 and he is like any other bouncy boy - in and out of the chair during the school day. Unlike me he doesn't spend a solid 8 hours sitting down. He likes the chair, but he also doesn't weigh as much as me. I recently swapped our chairs and noticed that his seat was still hard (and not sunken in). The best features of this chair are the arm rests that can be raised so the chair can fit under the desk. Overall, I think it's a decent chair for short term use in wait rooms. But if you plan on sitting for 8 hours per day, you will regret this purchase within a month. The lumbar support deflates after a while and you will need a pillow or a cushion. My daughter has a simple black office chair and I find hers a lot more comfortable.
