headline: Hiding that lipstick in style!
review_text_raw: I freaking love this thing. I'm not a trend person, I go for function. And when my STB SIL got my fiancé a shiney new Stanley I decided it was time to replace my beat up Rtic with the mismatch lid and straw. I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame! First off, can we all agree that the marshmallow is gorgeous? THIS cup is spectacular. Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what! The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine. The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.) The "handle", which is generally the locking feature unless you're using it as a handle, is well placed and comfortable for my sized hands. Not to small and not clunky and large. STB SIL likes to talk about how great the Stanley handle is, which I don't really get. I like that this doesn't have a handle. I have one to carry it if I need it, and not if I don't. The seal is completely water tight. I occasionally put a drink mix in it and shake vigorously. No leaks whatsoever. In fact... It fits in a car cup holder upside down. That's how I transport it in the car. It doesn't fit butt down, so I put it top down. I've been known to do this with various bottles, so I tried it with this one and it fits ok. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing. Try it in yours! Since it's completely leak proof there's are no worries about spilling. (Just be careful when you remove it that it doesn't unlatch.) Another bonus of the covered straw is that germs don't get in the straw. Perfect because people in public often don't cover their sneezes. Ugh. And the coolest part? Lipstick messes are concealed with a flip of the lid! Easy peasy! I have noticed that the inside of the straw stains a little, which was disappointing. I don't like that I look at it and it looks dirty when it isn't. But I guess I shouldn't have used drink enhancers then. Also, my top color is very light. Other colors might not show that. Another thing that want fun was that when it fell, it dented! Oh no! So beware of that. It keeps my water super cold and I don't go anywhere without it. I love it so much that I'm thinking of getting another so I don't have to limit myself by style! Definitely worth the price since I use it constantly, every day. This one is so chill and Zen... The next one shall be colorful and crazy! One for every mood! I simply can't say enough about this darn water bottle... Does that mean I'm on trend now? Who knows! I just love my Owalla! I'm definitely a fan!

Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what! The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine. The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.) The "handle", which is generally the locking feature unless you're using it as a handle, is well placed and comfortable for my sized hands. Not to small and not clunky and large. STB SIL likes to talk about how great the Stanley handle is, which I don't really get. I like that this doesn't have a handle. I have one to carry it if I need it, and not if I don't. The seal is completely water tight. I occasionally put a drink mix in it and shake vigorously. No leaks whatsoever. In fact... It fits in a car cup holder upside down. That's how I transport it in the car. It doesn't fit butt down, so I put it top down. I've been known to do this with various bottles, so I tried it with this one and it fits ok. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing. Try it in yours! Since it's completely leak proof there's are no worries about spilling. (Just be careful when you remove it that it doesn't unlatch.) Another bonus of the covered straw is that germs don't get in the straw. Perfect because people in public often don't cover their sneezes. Ugh. And the coolest part? Lipstick messes are concealed with a flip of the lid! Easy peasy! I have noticed that the inside of the straw stains a little, which was disappointing. I don't like that I look at it and it looks dirty when it isn't. But I guess I shouldn't have used drink enhancers then. Also, my top color is very light. Other colors might not show that. Another thing that want fun was that when it fell, it dented! Oh no! So beware of that. It keeps my water super cold and I don't go anywhere without it. I love it so much that I'm thinking of getting another so I don't have to limit myself by style! Definitely worth the price since I use it constantly, every day. This one is so chill and Zen... The next one shall be colorful and crazy! One for every mood! I simply can't say enough about this darn water bottle... Does that mean I'm on trend now? Who knows! I just love my Owalla! I'm definitely a fan!

I love that it's easy to clean-there are no nook & crannies that can't be cleaned or reached! I just love it. Period.

headline: Holds water, somewhat logical design
review_text_raw: I needed a practical birthday gift for my mother and purchased this 32oz water bottle for her. She is probably the most hydrated she's ever been, which is a big improvement for her health as a senior. The transparency and tick marks make it easy for her to monitor her water intake and it has become a companion bottle for her whenever she's hanging out at home or practicing at the ballroom dance studio we are both members of. The plastic vessel is fairly durable, having been dropped a handful of times. However, the transparent top that covers the mouth piece seems more liable to break/snap if the bottle is dropped while the cover is open. The bottle uses a straw design for intake, which I think offers some comfort and reinforces hydration habits. It would have been nice if there was a hybrid mouthpiece instead, offering options to either drink by tilting the bottle or through the straw. Mouthpieces give me the ick. The straw can be difficult to clean and I've had to help her remove and affix the rubber-plastic straw to the lid whenever she wants to wash it. I recommend washing your bottle often to remain hygienic. The lid locking feature is nice, but wholly unnecessary since all water passing out of the bottle comes from sucking on the straw. If anything, the button release does a decent at securing itself and prevents any accidental opening of the top. It is also likely more durable than if it were a simple snap-into-place design instead. The 32-ounce capacity is the right size, making it easy for my mom to monitor her daily hydration goals. However, we both wish that the bottle was a bit wider to offset how tall the entire thing is (about one foot). It's a bit conspicuous but at least she can sit it in the cupholder of her car and it's difficult for her to misplace since it's a tall, pink vessel. Overall, it's a 4/5 for us. I think the pricing is fair ($10.99 at the time of my purchase) and it holds water well. Really, that's all anyone could really ask of a water bottle.

headline: Nalgene, hard to beat!
review_text_raw: Nalgene bottles just work. The Nalgene bottle is perfect for those who enjoy outdoors activities. As funny as it is to say it "just works" when it's as simple as a bottle, it absolutely does. For starters the material. Not only is it BPA-free, the Tritan material is perfect for a drinking bottle. It's extremely rugged, in fact Nalgene has gained a reputation for how long their bottles last. It also doesn't leave much of a taste! A lot of my experience with plastic bottles is that you can taste the plastic, the problem persists with metal as well. Nalgene bottles have a fairly neutral taste. It's also very resistant to trapping odors and tastes. My problem with alternatives is that if you hold coffee in them for a long time, then your water tastes like coffee even after a clean. 1L is a perfect amount of water to hold in my opinion. It's enough to be usable, but not overkill to where it's not a functional bottle. It's great for day to day use as well, I find myself finishing a Nalgene just fine. The size is great in this aspect, it doesn't waste space with insulation. I find a lot of metal bottles and other plastic bottles can only ever hold 500ml and some change because of their shape. The leak proof seal just works. A lot of bottles are finicky, if you screw the cap from an angle it still leaks. I've tried to do it from an angle but it always screws on properly, I've never had a problem with it spilling. Overall the Nalgene is the perfect bottle. It's a good middle ground of everything while having its strengths in durability, build quality, and price.

Whether I’m out hiking, hitting the gym, or just working at my desk, this bottle ensures that my drink remains icy cold throughout the day. Pros: Durable Finish: One of my primary concerns with water bottles is how well they hold up to daily wear and tear. So, for the clumsy folks out there (like me), this bottle might be your new best friend. Efficient Insulation: The insulation game on this bottle is top-notch. Even in the blazing summer heat, after leaving this bottle in my car for hours, I return to find my water as cold as when I first poured it in. That's a game-changer, especially for those of us living in warmer climates or who simply love their beverages ice-cold. Rugged Straw: For those who prefer sipping through a straw, this feature is a standout. The straw is durable, ensuring that it doesn't get squashed or dented easily. Plus, it allows for easy drinking, especially during activities where you don't want to pause or tilt your head back. Versatile Top Design: Flexibility in design is always a win in my book. The interchangeable top, allowing for either open drinking or through a straw, gives users the option to switch according to their preference or activity. A casual day at the beach? Given the durable finish, it's a bit ironic that it can become a challenge to grip if there’s condensation or if you spill a bit while refilling. It’s not a deal-breaker, but something to be wary of, especially if you’re out and about and your hands are sweaty or it’s raining. Just be cautious when handling it with wet hands!

It met my expectation very well. -- The slick finish takes a larger, full, strong hand to grasp & pour with one hand. Something to consider if buying for a youth (recommend 24oz size thermos instead) or hand size/dexterity concerns. -- The unit is spill proof, but ONLY when the simply designed lid AND cap are fully screwed on (lid screws onto bottle, and attached-cap screws onto lid). -- This is NOT a one handed flip-top, rather a screw top that flips back (yes, rachets into open position so does not flip back closed when in use); so, either two hands will be required to unscew lid, or one if user has the dexterity and surface to set thermos on. -- The spout is easy to drink from. The liquid flows uninhibited. A straw can easily be inserted, but not spill proof at that point. -- 3" diameter bottom feels stable enough, but no rubber to quiet setting in down or grip better to surface set on. headline: My Favorite Water Bottle
review_text_raw: I had been hearing positive things about Owala water bottles for years, so when I needed a new water bottle for an upcoming work trip, I figured it was time. The fact that Beauty and the Beast is my favorite movie made this particular model a no brainer. I absolutely understand the hype, your water stays cold all day, the lid is secure, I love the option to sip from a stray or chug. This particular size was perfect for me, easily fits in my diaper bag and my car cup holder, and is large enough to hold a decent percentage of my daily water needs. After one hand wash all the colors faded, so the slight up charge between a regular Owala and the Disney Princess version was kind of a waste, but I did add my own stickers and they’ve been just fine. That’s the only reason why I docked a star.

headline: Worth every penny
review_text_raw: I didn't get into the Stanley craze-I've had too many accidental spills with the whole cup & straw set up. So when my kids started insisting I get an Owala, I was skeptical. But then I saw the TikTok of that one guy using his Owala as a weapon to fight off the men who attempted to break into his house, and not only did he stop them, his Owala survived with just a dent (and a broken handle, if memory serves me right)! Then Owala does the of the best PR stunt/customer appreciation ever, and not only sends that man a safe, but filled that safe with several Owala bottles! I admire a company that can back their products up; but I will support a business who listens and recognizes their customers too! So I started looking for one; I got to thinking as a woman who often does her errands alone, "you know, I can always use it for defense and I can't be accused of carrying a weapon, because technically it's a water bottle." When Owala came out with this Amazon exclusive color, I knew it was kismet! I put it on my cart, but before I checked out, my kid saw what I was doing and she stopped me. She said, "lady, I already bought that for you. It's coming next week." LOL I guess she got tired of telling me to get one, and just grabbed it for me, knowing that burgundy is one of my favorite colors! I've had it for 5 months now. It's a little dinged up on the bottom-nothing too bad. I just dropped it one or two times (maybe more). I love that the mouthpiece is covered up and can be locked so 1)it will always be clean; and 2)it won't accidentally spill if it tips over, or you know, you accidentally drop it. It keeps me accountable-I fill that 40 oz 2-3 times a day to make sure I stay hydrated. I love that it's insulated so I can keep my drink cold or hot-depending on what I fill it with. I love that it's easy to clean-there are no nook & crannies that can't be cleaned or reached! I just love it. Period.

headline: Love it!
review_text_raw: I was influenced by a TikToker when I really didn't need another water bottle. I am out in the community a lot for work and carrying a water bottle in Arizona is essential but hard to do when carrying all of my other supplies. product_title: RAYMYLO Insulated Water Bottle 64 oz, Triple Wall Vacuum Stainless Steel
headline: Good product for $19 price
review_text_raw: This is the 2nd thermos-type "water bottle" I've bought in a month. -- The first, more expensive, actual Thermos brand 24oz ended up being the right size to replace the daily-use, plastic water bottle I was carrying in my tote-purse. But, a tad too small when trying to put two cans of bubble water in plus fresh squeezed citrus/pulp/peel AND ice. -- This 30 oz., generic Amazon brand bottle was the max size I was willing to go to fit in those 2 cans/citrus without moving to one with a formal handle; as, I became concerned of being able to grip with one hand while full of liquid. It met my expectation very well. -- The slick finish takes a larger, full, strong hand to grasp & pour with one hand. Something to consider if buying for a youth (recommend 24oz size thermos instead) or hand size/dexterity concerns. -- The unit is spill proof, but ONLY when the simply designed lid AND cap are fully screwed on (lid screws onto bottle, and attached-cap screws onto lid). -- This is NOT a one handed flip-top, rather a screw top that flips back (yes, rachets into open position so does not flip back closed when in use); so, either two hands will be required to unscew lid, or one if user has the dexterity and surface to set thermos on. -- The spout is easy to drink from. The liquid flows uninhibited. A straw can easily be inserted, but not spill proof at that point. -- 3" diameter bottom feels stable enough, but no rubber to quiet setting in down or grip better to surface set on. Also, it does NOT taper, so it does not fit in my van's dashboard or console cup holders. -- It comes with a built in carrying handle that lies flat when not in use; but, the plastic looks like it will be the first thing to break off after a few drops...and, the screw on attached-cap a close second (which would then negate the spill-proof function--time will tell, as this is 1st day own this new product type). -- Good, wide mouth (2.25") cup opening with a small, curved inside edge. Wide enough to fit a standard kitchen sink scrub brush (unlike smaller 24oz other brand I purchased that requires an actual bottle brush). -- See pix for grip size, surface, lid, inside curve, and outer metal ring a carbiner-corded handle (not included) fastens over well (but takes some effort).

product_title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 32 oz Summer Sweetness
headline: Best water bottle ever
review_text_raw: I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it: LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry. THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes. STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours. THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful. DISHWASHER SAFE! This one is self explanatory. It’s amazing and I love it. There are a few cons though. The first one is that the 32 ounce doesn’t fit in my cup holder. Not a huge deal since it’s leakproof—I just keep it on the passenger seat. But Owala does have cup holder friendly options now if that’s something you want. The bottle also does dent and scratch fairly easily. I dropped it getting out my car one day and it’s a little beat up now. Kind ugly, but it’s still my fave. It’s kinda disappointing because I have Yetis and Stanleys that have been through far worse and still look new. Just be mindful of that and baby it a little. Still 100% worth it though. Long story short, it’s a great bottle that will keep your water cold and everything else dry. As someone who has used this bottle regularly for years, I highly recommend!

product_title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 32 oz Summer Sweetness
headline: Hiding that lipstick in style!
review_text_raw: I freaking love this thing. I'm not a trend person, I go for function. And when my STB SIL got my fiancé a shiney new Stanley I decided it was time to replace my beat up Rtic with the mismatch lid and straw. I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame! First off, can we all agree that the marshmallow is gorgeous? THIS cup is spectacular. Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what! The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine. The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.) The "handle", which is generally the locking feature unless you're using it as a handle, is well placed and comfortable for my sized hands. Not to small and not clunky and large. STB SIL likes to talk about how great the Stanley handle is, which I don't really get. I like that this doesn't have a handle. I have one to carry it if I need it, and not if I don't. The seal is completely water tight. I occasionally put a drink mix in it and shake vigorously. No leaks whatsoever. In fact... It fits in a car cup holder upside down. That's how I transport it in the car. It doesn't fit butt down, so I put it top down. I've been known to do this with various bottles, so I tried it with this one and it fits ok. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing. Try it in yours! Since it's completely leak proof there's are no worries about spilling. (Just be careful when you remove it that it doesn't unlatch.) Another bonus of the covered straw is that germs don't get in the straw. Perfect because people in public often don't cover their sneezes. Ugh. And the coolest part? Lipstick messes are concealed with a flip of the lid! Easy peasy! I have noticed that the inside of the straw stains a little, which was disappointing. I don't like that I look at it and it looks dirty when it isn't. But I guess I shouldn't have used drink enhancers then. Also, my top color is very light. Other colors might not show that. Another thing that want fun was that when it fell, it dented! Oh no! So beware of that. It keeps my water super cold and I don't go anywhere without it. I love it so much that I'm thinking of getting another so I don't have to limit myself by style! Definitely worth the price since I use it constantly, every day. This one is so chill and Zen... The next one shall be colorful and crazy! One for every mood! I simply can't say enough about this darn water bottle... Does that mean I'm on trend now? Who knows! I just love my Owalla! I'm definitely a fan!

headline: Exactly What I Was Looking For
review_text_raw: This Iron Flask 40oz insulated water bottle was exactly what I was looking for. I work in public safety and am not always near the station to refill my water bottle and wanted something that would allow me a couple refills but keep the water cold until I needed it. This does exactly that. I used a 20oz shaker bottle as a water bottle, so this gives Iron Flask bottle gives me two refills until I need to fill it up again. It is the perfect size to keep on my passenger seat without taking up much room at all. I have not had any issues with the bottle leaking and it is very good quality. the bottle came with three different lids. One is just a standard lid that stays attached to the bottle when unscrewed and is stainless steel. There is a straw lid, with a silicone straw that goes into the bottle and a plastic straw on the plastic lid for drinking. The third is a plastic lid like a standard coffee thermal drinking lid. I have only used the stainless steel lid as I only use this to hold extra water to refill my other water bottle since I add a water flavor to it. All three lids have a handle source for easy carrying of the water bottle. I drop this thing all the time and it still holds up really well. Of course it is going to scratch or dent when you drop it, it isn't a magic water bottle. But it has not affected the lids or seals in any way. I like to put stickers on my metal water bottles anyways, so nothing a fun sticker cant cover up! I do not put hot liquids in this water bottle, so I cannot speak to how well it keeps liquids hot, but it keeps my water nice and cold so I wouldn't have any doubt in its ability to keep liquids warm for as long as it says. I would purchase more of this product in the future if I needed.

headline: Good product for $19 price
review_text_raw: This is the 2nd thermos-type "water bottle" I've bought in a month. -- The first, more expensive, actual Thermos brand 24oz ended up being the right size to replace the daily-use, plastic water bottle I was carrying in my tote-purse. But, a tad too small when trying to put two cans of bubble water in plus fresh squeezed citrus/pulp/peel AND ice. -- This 30 oz., generic Amazon brand bottle was the max size I was willing to go to fit in those 2 cans/citrus without moving to one with a formal handle; as, I became concerned of being able to grip with one hand while full of liquid. It met my expectation very well. -- The slick finish takes a larger, full, strong hand to grasp & pour with one hand. Something to consider if buying for a youth (recommend 24oz size thermos instead) or hand size/dexterity concerns. -- The unit is spill proof, but ONLY when the simply designed lid AND cap are fully screwed on (lid screws onto bottle, and attached-cap screws onto lid). -- This is NOT a one handed flip-top, rather a screw top that flips back (yes, rachets into open position so does not flip back closed when in use); so, either two hands will be required to unscew lid, or one if user has the dexterity and surface to set thermos on. -- The spout is easy to drink from. The liquid flows uninhibited. A straw can easily be inserted, but not spill proof at that point. -- 3" diameter bottom feels stable enough, but no rubber to quiet setting in down or grip better to surface set on. Also, it does NOT taper, so it does not fit in my van's dashboard or console cup holders. -- It comes with a built in carrying handle that lies flat when not in use; but, the plastic looks like it will be the first thing to break off after a few drops...and, the screw on attached-cap a close second (which would then negate the spill-proof function--time will tell, as this is 1st day own this new product type). -- Good, wide mouth (2.25") cup opening with a small, curved inside edge. Wide enough to fit a standard kitchen sink scrub brush (unlike smaller 24oz other brand I purchased that requires an actual bottle brush). -- See pix for grip size, surface, lid, inside curve, and outer metal ring a carbiner-corded handle (not included) fastens over well (but takes some effort).

headline: Not super cold, but decent.
review_text_raw: I purchased two for my kiddos (6 & 8) to use for sports. Right out of the box, first time using, one of them leaked a good bit. I’m not sure what changed but the next day we had a full day out in the sun and they didn’t leak anymore. I’m hoping it was a fluke and we’re in the clear moving forward. They definitely didn’t hold ice for very long. Maybe two hours? Probably shorter because it was fully melted when I took a drink about two hours after filling them. Water was still cold though, and after spending 8 hours in 100 degree weather, the water was still on the cooler side. When full, they are a bit heavy, but they hold quite a bit of water so some weight is expected. They aren’t very heavy at all otherwise. My kids were able to lug them around all day without any issues. We also used the fence-hanging feature. It was pretty cool. I do wish the handle would move though. So it’s a little awkward with the fence hooks just sticking out. Ultimately they worked for what we needed. They kept my kids hydrated all day without needing to refill a hundred times and they kept the water decently cool. We had no issues with taste or odor, as mentioned in other reviews. If you’re looking for something that’s going to maintain ice for long periods of time, this is not the bottle.

headline: Exceeds all expectations. You can pay more & get less.
review_text_raw: I waited a full week before writing this review, to test this and live with it a bit. I'd read so many reviews of different products of this Type- Including YETI, HydroFlask, etc. About 20 months ago, I'd bought a few Zojirushi water bottles as stocking stuffers for my wife and I- having already been-through a few other brands and types that ultimately didn't gain favor or last. And sadly, the Zojirushi though well-rated was similarly destined to replacement for various reasons I won't list here, but it was loud in its operation (think you want a quiet drink at 3am without waking your significant other, nope) and didn't "drink from" well, if that makes sense. Yeti- I was set to spring for them....but meh. More "Brand/Status identity" than actual performance & substance IMO...and overpriced because of that. And so forth. I am truly a buy-once, cry-once person; but I also understand VALUE. It's not always 'the most expensive' that is the best...and this Water Tumbler is a prime example of that. Ladies and Gentlemen, I introduce the Stanley IceFlow 2.0 Flip straw number. I've finally found the right water tumbler. Made by STANLEY- industry standard for years and I know it's more a utilitarian "brand" and not fashionable, but IT DELIVERS... and I could not be more exuberant over such a simple item. It handles well, travels well, & for me, the 30oz is just the sight size for overall day to day travel and errands, it hasn't leaked, temperature retention is EXCELLENT and it's well-made. I like the carry handle which tilts out of the way, but is robust enough for daily use without the concern over it breaking due to cheap manufacturing. And in its function- it's QUIET!!!! Flip the flip-straw spigot up and it quietly does so and just a quietly flips back into its sealed position. No waking the spouse at 3am with a click-click or other obnoxious noises that seemingly are amplified in the wee quiet hours of sleep time. This is important for me/us. lol I wasn't sure I'd like the straw-oriented setup, and I absolutely LOVE IT. Simple to manipulate the spigot, even when driving, if need be. The straw removes easy for easy cleaning, the entire tumbles is easily cleaned ( I hand-wash mine only) but it's dishwasher safe, BPA-Free (!!), and the size of the straw allows you to draw a good volume of water. And quietly. Now the finish- first, I chose the ASH color so as to not draw heat like darker colors will, and shows less handling smudges or gunk. BUT THE TEXTURE IS DA-BOMB!!! It's perfect for traction/grip, but not too coarse to draw unwanted oils and dirt AND it seems to be resistant to mars & scratches. I had an armful of shopping bags a few days ago and my car keys and gripping the side of the tumbler (not the handle in this instance) in the other hand, as my wife and I came home from the grocery store- and I'm thinking "okay those car-key edges are chafing the side of the mug and I'll probably have scratches on it"....not a single one. Nothing. So robust. Now I'm sure if I were to kick it down a gravel driveway that might be a different story, but you get the idea. The finish & material overall, is QUALITY. I'm seriously thinking of getting one or two more of these in different colors just for the "mood" that I may be in at the moment...lol, but honestly, this simple water tumbler has been the most surprising Amazon purchase I've made in a long time...maybe THE most. UPDATE 8/16/26: I put a handful of ice cubes into this tumbler last night before bed and filled it with water. As of right at at 6pm the following evening, the water in the tumbler is still cold enough to give you a brain freeze. Seriously. If that's not well-insulated, I don't know what is. (end of update) THIS IS AN EPIC WIN, and a must-have.

headline: Lives up to the hype — with one real caveat about the straw
review_text_raw: I'll be honest: I was skeptical about paying this much for a water bottle. A few months in, it's earned it. Insulation is genuinely impressive. I fill it with ice water in the morning and there's still ice in there at the end of a full workday. No other tumbler I've owned has done that consistently. The outside stays completely dry too — no condensation rings on your desk or car seat. The Flowstate lid is the feature I didn't know I needed. Three positions (straw, sip, closed) and it rotates smoothly. I use the straw position all day and the closed setting when I toss it in my bag. Cup holder fit: yes, it actually fits. The H2.0 redesigned the base specifically for this and it works — fits my car's cup holder without forcing it. The one real issue: if the tumbler tips over with the straw in, liquid leaks out through the straw opening. It's not fully spill-proof. I've had it knock over on my desk and it made a mess. Worth knowing before you put it near a laptop or in a bag without the straw removed. It's a lid designed for drinking, not for carrying around at an angle. The Rose Quartz color is accurate to photos — a soft, muted dusty pink. Not hot pink, not beige. Genuinely pretty. Worth the money if you actually use a tumbler daily. If you're on the fence about the price, you'll stop questioning it within a week.

headline: No Plastic Taste, Clean Fresh Water All Day
review_text_raw: I love this thing! After falling victim to 3 or 4 plastic water jugs that falsely claimed they wouldn't give water that weird plastic taste, this glass jug is the one that finally delivers. headline: Great Bottle with Minor Design Flaws - 4/5 Stars
review_text_raw: I've been using the WATERSY 1 gallon insulated bottle for about six months, and it's held up remarkably well. Build Quality & Durability: This bottle is built like a tank. I've dropped it multiple times, including on the cap, and nothing has broken or cracked. The handle is solid and shows no signs of wear even with daily use. The insulation works excellently - it keeps water cold for the advertised 48 hours, which is perfect for long hikes or all-day events. Ease of Use: The wide mouth opening makes filling, emptying, and cleaning incredibly easy. You can fit your entire hand inside for thorough cleaning, and ice cubes go in without any hassle. No concerns about mold or buildup in hard-to-reach areas. The Drinking Challenge: Here's where it gets tricky - tilting a full gallon of liquid to drink from the mouth can feel heavy and awkward. The air displacement while drinking creates a loud gurgling sound that can be disruptive in quiet settings like offices or meetings. A metal straw option would solve both issues and make this bottle perfect. The Bottom Plate Problem: The rubber on the bottom sits slightly higher than the metal rim, which creates two annoying issues. When you set it down on hard surfaces, it makes a bell-like ringing sound. Worse, the exposed metal rim will scratch tables, desks, and countertops because the bottle is so heavy. I've had to start using a placemat to protect my furniture. Bottom Line: Despite the drinking awkwardness and bottom plate design flaw, this is still an excellent water bottle for anyone who needs serious hydration capacity and temperature retention. Just be prepared to use a coaster and maybe invest in a separate metal straw. The durability and insulation quality make it worth the minor inconveniences.

headline: Sturdy, durable, holds temperature well, and easy to drink from
review_text_raw: I have a larger Camelbak insulated stainless steel water bottle, but wanted a smaller one for my daily walks. It's perfect. The handle on the lid makes it easy to carry when I'm out walking, and the smaller size means I'm carrying less weight. I chose the stainless steel bottle over plastic to cut down on consumption of microplastics and PFAs. (The lid is still plastic, but overall, there's less plastic.) The stainless steel has the added benefit of not picking up odors or emitting that plastic-y smell that some water bottles have. And the double-wall construction keeps my drink cool for a surprisingly long time, even in a hot car. The lid design is great for drinking on the go; the spout is wide enough to get a good gulp of water without spilling the whole thing when you're on the move. The magnet holds the spout's lid in place when you want to leave it open -- while you're driving, for instance. And I have never had any problem with leakage when the lid and the spout cover are both screwed on properly. Judging by my larger bottle, which I have had for a year, the stainless Camelbaks are quite durable. Even the enamel(?) finish is pretty durable. I have dropped my bigger one several times, and it still shows only minor scratches and a barely-visible, tiny dent. Cleaning is easy -- much easier than the Camelbaks with a straw. The bottle has a wide mouth, so it's easy to get a bottle brush inside. The lid requires a smaller brush to get into the crevices, but it's not difficult. (Not like cleaning the straw and bite spout on the straw models!) I've had Camelbaks for years, beginning with the straw-and-bite-spout, plastic bottle models. These stainless ones are my favorites. I rarely go out without it.

headline: Very small, keeps things cold/hot for a long time, not the best lid/cap.
review_text_raw: This is a nice bottle. I bought it to see if it would work as a replacement for my much bigger 64 Oz water bottle. It did not. I drink way too much water for this size to do anything for me, so I stopped using it 90% of the time. That said, it does function rather well and did keep my water ice cold longer than needed, so it is a good water bottle with a good seal and I didn't notice any metallic taste, but as I said I am used to my 64 Oz insulated bottle so I never minded any taste if there were one. The lid for this is not the best. If you're just doing water then it's not a huge deal, but if you're doing anything else, like coffee or hot chocolate, then you're going to need to scrub the whole thing out thoroughly after use which is mildly annoying. Cleaning aside I just don't like the cap for this bottle. It feels cheap and like it could break any any time. The odd hinge design is not satisfying to use because you can't absentmindedly flip it open. You have to consciously pull it up and out at the right angle in line with the strange sideways angled accordion mechanism. Overall, not terrible and it works well as a liquid storage device. But once you're used to a 64 Oz bottle these tiny bottles get emptied after one and a half sips. Also, I would definitely change the lid/cap for anything else because the stock one is bad.

headline: Simple, clean-tasting, and an easy stock-up win
review_text_raw: If you want no-drama drinking water for the house, car, gym bag, or emergencies, Amazon’s purified water bottles do exactly what they should: taste clean, stay sealed, and not cost a fortune. It’s the kind of neutral, crisp water you don’t think about—which is the whole point. What I notice (and why I keep rebuying) Clean, neutral taste: Chilled, it’s refreshing with no plasticky aftertaste. Because it’s purified (typically reverse osmosis) with a touch of minerals added for taste, it doesn’t have the “salty” edge some spring waters do. Grab-and-go size: The 16.9-oz (500 mL) bottles fit cup holders, treadmill holders, and backpack side pockets perfectly. Consistent seals: Caps twist off with a clean pop; I haven’t hit leakers or half-sealed bottles. Value: Case price per bottle is hard to beat, especially for keeping a few packs on hand for guests or a go-bag. Where it shines Daily hydration: Easy way to track intake—four bottles gets most adults near their daily goal. Workouts & errands: Neutral flavor is ideal when you’re sweaty; it doesn’t fight with electrolytes or mixes. Coffee machine/steamer safe: Purified water reduces mineral build-up vs. hard tap (still descale on schedule). Emergency stash: Two cases on a shelf = peace of mind for outages/boil advisories. The honest nits (no sugar-coating) Bottle thinness: They’re lightweight by design. Great for portability, not meant for multiple refills. If you squeeze hard, they’ll crinkle. Shrink-wrap case: The plastic wrap can tear if you grab from the side—lift from the bottom to avoid the cascade-of-bottles moment. Taste preference: If you love the mineral “snap” of spring water, purified can feel a bit “flat.” That’s normal—this aims for neutral, not terroir. Tips to get the best out of them Chill them. Purified water tastes best cold; keep a rotation in the fridge. Store smart. Keep sealed cases in a cool, odor-free spot—water can absorb nearby smells. Freeze hack: Half-drain a bottle, freeze it upright, then top with fresh water before heading out for a long day—instant ice pack + cold water for hours. Recycle everything your local program accepts (bottle + cap + label where allowed). Day-to-day, use a reusable bottle and lean on these for travel/emergencies. Bottom line If you’re after clean taste, reliable packaging, and real value, Amazon’s purified water bottles deliver. They’re an easy “set it and forget it” staple—perfect for stocking the pantry without overthinking it.

headline: Starts off excellent, then deteriorates, loses insulation, and NO support from MEOKY company
review_text_raw: I really like this! I pored over so many listings to find a product that had everything I wanted: steel construction, a top handle, a pair of folding side grip handles, a combination stray and spout opening, no-drip, and insulated. This has it all. It's honestly a beast of a jug, which is perfect for the gym. My only critique would be the insulation: it's adequate but not spectacular. If I fill the jug with cold water and a handful of ice today, then by tomorrow when I wake up the ice will be melted and the water more tepid than cold. But for same-day use, it'll keep your drinks cold without problem! Edit: All of the above is accurate...UNTIL you wash it. I ran it through a dishwasher on low heat with no heat dry, but even that seems to have destroyed its internal insulation. Less than a year old, and not only does it fail to keep anything cold anymore, it seems to actually accelerate warming! If I fill this with one-third ice before adding water, it now remains cold until early afternoon, by which time the ice has melted and the water is tepid, if not room temperature. That's when you discover that the company, MEOKY, offers no support whatsoever. Their website claims 24/7 support, but they do not respond to repeated emails. They promote a Facebook support page, which has many customer inquiries for years, with not one single response from the company to ANY of them. They have an Instagram, where they did reply to me to reaffirm that they have product support, and then not one single response since then, contradicting that pledge. This is exactly the design I want in a water bottle, but I won't buy from this company again because they haven't earned my loyalty. There are identical clones of this bottle, and I'll buy those instead as a replacement.

product_title: Simple Modern 40 oz Trek Tumbler with Handle and Straw Lid | Cup Holder Friendly Insulated Stainless Steel Travel Mug | Almond Birch
headline: This is *IT*
review_text_raw: Let me start off by saying that I'm not an influencer, nor have I received anything in return for this honest review. I also gave this tumbler a solid month of daily use before I put in my 2 cents. Also, the pictures were taken in broad daylight. The picture of me holding it upside down is the only time it leaked, but, ya know, I'm holding it full of water, upside down, and even then, only a tiny bit escaped. Through the straw, not the lid, mind you. When the straw was removed and I held it upside down, droplets escaped, one by one. I didn't purchase this for any other reason than to reduce my beverage goblin tendencies, and to support my laziness in regards to washing excess dishes. I bought this because I was tired of having a car cup and a house cup. My house cup is my favorite, it also holds 40 oz, but doesn't fit any cup holder because it's essentially a tank (I copped it on clearance at Walmart 2 years ago for like, $6, and it's the tits). HOWEVER, it really sucks to not be able to take it everywhere, and it's definitely not spill proof. So I had that tank for the house, and my 8 year old 30 oz Yeti for the vehicle, since it fits. I've never used a Stanley so I cannot compare, though I do own the Simple Modern 64oz summit, had it for years, and it's stood the test of time and regular use, both outdoor and indoor. But it's not practical because, although it's very well made, it's massive, heavy, handle-less, and rolls out of the passenger seat onto the floor and out of reach, leaving me parched and annoyed. This tumbler is well-made, from the unit itself to the lid and straw, and the price point is beyond reasonable. I'd have paid $40 for it because of how well it's preformed. The handle is sturdy and comfortable, and it supports the full weight of 40 oz of ice water easily. I've dropped it several times and the powder coating hasn't chipped, nor has the metal dinged. Although most wouldn't think if it, it is SO nice to decide where I want the straw to be in regards to where and how I'm sitting and what hand I'm reaching for it with. It washes up easily. It's not obnoxiously large and it's overall appearance is low-key. It keeps my tea cold and fresh for 2 days indoors. I've left it filled with ice water in my vehicle for 2 days (in early June in the south, mind you). I got super thirsty after a grocery run and took a sip. It was room temperature, if not a skosh cool, but in no way was it warm, even though the cup itself was. It's fallen out of a backseat cup holder and laid on the floor for well over an hour without my knowledge, and although a few drops escaped from the straw, the carpet of my vehicle was dry, and the tumbler was still full of ice water. And, ya know, it keeps you hydrated because you can always keep that thang on you. I ordered the almond color. It's really more of a very light beige. Or coffee that's mostly creamer. A lot lighter than you'd think. It's definitely that boring popular aesthetic hue that everyone's so into, so if that's what you're going for, it's spot on. All in all, I really really REALLY like this tumbler and I'd definitely recommend it. Then again, Simple Modern products haven't ever really let me down, so it's not a huge shocker.

It was room temperature, if not a skosh cool, but in no way was it warm, even though the cup itself was. review_text_raw: This bottle is perfect for what I use it for! I work for the Railroad so I am very hard on my things and they need to last. This is extremely sturdy and made with high-quality durable parts. I have only used it for cold drinks because I don’t need any type of hot drink for 12 hours, but it does keep very cold and keeps ice floating around up to 48 hours without sweating or building condensation. Despite how heavy and awkward it can get when you are putting 128 ounces of fluid into it on top of its already solid construction, I find it very easy to carry, move, and drink from. The included flip top handle is great and can be adjusted up or down. The handles on the side are also great for carrying it and if you are not wanting to use them, they fold into the bottle itself. I think having both options for a straw and for a chug cap is an awesome feature that I didn’t realize the handiness of before I bought it. It has been perfect for filling up at home and especially at the gas station or wherever you get your drinks from. I believe out of every bottle I researched to buy, which was quite a few, the opening on this one was the widest allowing you to add many different types of ice or fill it using different types of spouts and machines at the gas station. Adding to that, so far the height has been just right. You can slide it under spouts or ice machines without having to tip it at an awkward angle. If you make sure you are properly tightening the top, the cap, and pushing the straw all the way down then you will have zero leakage at all. You can flip it around, roll it around in the car, or simply hold it upside down and it does not leak a drop. I searched for quite a while for a water bottle that met all of my needs and had all the features I wanted. I liked quite a few, but they all had something that I would’ve had to settle for or didn’t like. This one includes everything that I was wanting plus it is extremely affordable for all that it does. It is 1/2 up to even 1/4 the price of other insulated gallon jugs that do not have the same features. Finally, their customer service is responsive and cares about the customer. I left an email with pictures and videos on a Friday because I thought my jug was leaking. They responded within a day or two, which was still over the weekend, and made a detailed markup of my pictures respectfully showing me that I was more than likely using it incorrectly and causing the leaks. However, they told me I didn’t even need to try the solutions they recommended if I didn’t want to and if I wanted a replacement, refund, or anything else they would be more than happy to oblige. 100% recommend to buy

headline: Very Aesthetically Pleasing, Doesn't Leak, Easy to Carry Around
review_text_raw: I love this water bottle. I had been lugging around a 64oz bottle that could barely fit in the side pockets of my backpack, and while it was nice to have during 12 hour shifts, I got sick of it. I got the purple bottle with the chug lid. The color is beautiful, the design of the bottle is very cute and elegant, and the actual hole you drink from is much more desireable to me than the straws/nips a lot of bottles use nowadays. Even though it is only 32oz, I find that I don't mind refilling it once a day to get in my 64oz. I actually prefer it to a 64oz bottle, since I know I'll be getting fresh, cool water after the first fill runs out. I've seen some comment that you can't actually "chug" with this bottle...well, of course you can't! The bottle isn't the thin, bendable plastic that you get with the water bottles from the store...it's sturdy!! And while you can't "chug," you can most certainly get some big gulps in! I'm not a slow water drinker. I don't want tiny sips, I want to get that +64oz in! This bottle is definitely good for that. You can easily get 4oz, and even more, in a single gulp. Haha, I even did it now, just to be sure... I really love this thing. It is exactly what I was looking for, and the price is great. The lid is also very easy to open and close, but still very sturdy and secure. It also seems quite easy to clean, though I haven't had to do so just yet. For those who have seen mold growth on their water bottles...you must wash these things at LEAST once a week, if not more often, especially if you wear anything on your lips like chapstick, lipstick, etc. Even the slight bit of backwash from out filthy human mouths is enough to contaminate the insides of the bottle. If you live in a warmer climate, this is especially true and will result in the bacteria from your backwash contaminating the bottle resulting in the growth of things like mold. It has happened to me before and I was absolutely mortified. Another reason I prefer chug lids as opposed to straws...the things are a hell of a lot easier to clean. No hidden crevices harboring disgusting human bacteria...lol. I definitely recommend this water bottle for those of you looking to increase your intake. Very pretty, convenient, and simple to clean with the chug lid.

headline: Durable and easy to clean
review_text_raw: My second grader has been using these for a year and a half now. She takes it everywhere; school, classes, traveling, and even on her bike when playing with her neighborhood gang. This review is specifically geared to this use case. Pros and cons below. Pros: 1. The 18oz size is perfect to last through the school day and extended care, without being too big/bulky. 2. The bottle is very light. After trying other kid's bottles with silicone sleeves, double walls, sophisticated lids, etc. that add weight, this was a relief. 3. The bottle and lid are very easy to clean. There aren't any nooks and crannies that you would find with the auto seal bottles. There's no straw (we use the chug version). There's no abundance of those rubber/silicone parts that seem commonplace on children's bottles, but are also mold-magnets. The only soft part of the bottle that needs extra attention to prevent mold is where the flip lid seals against the chug opening. This area is very small so I don't mind the extra scrubbing. It also washes well in the dishwasher, but it's quick enough to wash by hand that I usually end up doing that. 4. The bottle is very durable. Kids drop things. A lot. My daughter's dropped it countless times but you'd be none the wiser. We've used Nalgene bottles made of Tritan for a few years now so we're aware of how tough the material is, but it's still impressive. I expected the finger loop to rip off within a few months given how much it's used, but it seems to be holding up just fine. 5. It has never leaked. I see reviews complaining of leaking with sparkling water, but I think that's to be expected with carbonated beverages and flip-style lids. We only use it with water and we've never had a leak. 6. The flip cover protects the entire area where one's mouth can come in contact with the bottle. While there are other bottles that do this too, this is the simplest, lightest and easiest-to-clean flip-cover bottle I've seen. Cons: 1. The bottle has an Achilles heel; the flip cover hinge. When the flip cover is fully closed, the bottle is ultra durable. But when it's open, you have all that leverage from the flip cover holding on by a thin strip of plastic. The hinge is certainly durable enough when the flip cover is used as intended, i.e. only open it to drink water and close it when you're done. But what invariably happens? You've just washed the bottle and set it out to dry, with the lid off and flip cover open. Your daughter later comes to get her bottle in a hurry to catch the bus, and she fills the bottle, and then starts screwing the lid on with the flip cover still open. product_title: Pogo BPA-Free Plastic Water Bottle with Chug Lid, 32 Oz, Quetzal Teal
headline: This water bottle REFUSES to break OR spill!
review_text_raw: I have been through TOO MANY water bottles in my life. The plastic ones shatter when dropped, the metal ones dent when dropped, and they're all just so easy TO DROP. And the LEAKS! I can't even tell you how many puddles I've caused from toting my water bottles around with me on the daily. I bought this water bottle for one reason: the PRICE. I was not looking for a good water bottle at the time, I guess because I stopped believing they were out there in the world, so I bought a cheap one assuming that it would have some kind of design flaw or break when I dropped it in a couple of weeks. I was WRONG! This is, hands down, THE BEST WATER BOTTLE I HAVE EVER OWNED. I have had it for over a year now, and I tote it with me on the daily, always on the move walking from class to class on a large outdoor college campus. There are THREE things that make this the best water bottle in the world: 1. It is HARD TO DROP, even for me! I just hook my finger through that little bendy hooky thing up top, close my fist, and that sucker stays on me! I walk everywhere with this thing, and when I'm holding it through the loop, it is basically UNDROPPABLE! When I'm drinking from it, the little hand indentation up at the top of the water bottle is a very comfortable fit, and even when the bottle is full and heavy, it feels very balanced. 2. WHEN I drop it, it DOESN'T BREAK! Let's face it: I am forgetful and clumsy. There are times when I don't hold the bottle the undroppable way. There are times when the bottle is sitting on my desk and I accidentally swipe it off. There was even this one time when I threw it into the air and then failed to catch it. But through all these drops, this bottle has not cracked yet. And a couple of my drops have been when the bottle was fullish. That being said, I haven't had TOO many major drops (thanks to the bottles undroppableness) so I wouldn't try pushing your luck with this one. But alot can be said just from the fact that this bottle has survived a year of daily use with ME, a certified water bottle destroyer. 3. IT DOESN'T LEAK! This bottle has something that's hard to find these days: A TOP THAT ACTUALLY WORKS! I have NEVER experienced a single leak with this bottle - NOT EVEN ONE! I throw my bottle into my bookbag all the time, with precious lecture notes and expensive textbooks, some of which are rented and must be returned, and I can do so with FULL CONFIDENCE that my water bottle will not leak on them! I'm not talking the side pocket of my bookbag, I am talking in the main zipper with all of my other stuff. I make ZERO EFFORT to be careful when the bottle is in my bookbag. All day long that bookbag bumps into desks, walls, people, gets turned upside down, gets thrown on the floor, sat on, turned upside down, etc. This sucker doesn't leak. And that's it. THREE things that go into making the PERFECT WATER BOTTLE. This water bottle also has the added benefit of having a killer price (I was happy to pay the price I paid for it even when I was still assuming it was nothing special). It also holds 40 ounces of water, which is kind of a large amount of water compared to most water bottles. I bought this bottle with ZERO EXPECTATIONS, and it has turned out to be one of my favorite buys from Amazon to date. It definitely sparks joy in my life! Thank you, Pogo water bottles. You have created something of VALUE.

headline: Top needs to go back more!
review_text_raw: My friends were trying to convince we to buy an owala, but the color I wanted wasn’t available in the 20 oz, so I decided to give this a try. I am so glad I did, because I actually like this one better! Looking at them both, they are very similar in design, but one main difference is that to drink from the o straw, you sip from the same opening where you free sip. This one has a straw piece that flips up behind the free sip area, which I like better. The cap seems sturdier, and the when the handle is down you can still press the button to open the cap to free sip. On the o, the handle prevents you from pressing the button, so you need to lift the handle to open the top to drink from it—I guess whether this is a pro or con depends on whether you want the button to be blocked or not. The button on this one is also easier to press to pop the top up. It does not leak at all, it fits in my car cup holder, and it kept my water cold for the 6 hours it took me to drink it. Even though I balked at spending $20 on a water bottle, it’s still cheaper than the other one by a fair amount, and I love the color—I will definitely be buying more in the other sizes! Edit: There are a few things I’ve noticed since I bought and have been using both the Encool and my Owala of the same size (35oz). The carrying handle is wider on the Encool, which I like better, and the bottom is rubberized, which is not the case on my o bottle. BUT one thing that this company needs to fix is that the top does not flip back far enough, so you are forced to tilt the bottle pretty far up when free sipping because it sticks into your forehead. I’m changing my review to 4 stars because this is pretty annoying, especially when I use the bottle to drink water, which I prefer to free sip. Dear Encool: Fix this problem and offer replacement tops to people who have already bought your bottles. They are perfect in every way EXCEPT for this incredibly annoying feature!

headline: Love this Bottle; Wish it didn't Leak on its Side
review_text_raw: I bought this bottle because I wanted a larger bottle that I would only need to fill up twice a day to get as many ounces of water as was my goal. I definitely got it in this bottle. I love this thing, and got a parachord handle to go with it, so when I go for walks or go to outdoor events it's perfect to take with me. I've dropped it more than a few times and while the paint will chip, it still holds up. What's a stainless steel water bottle without a few dings, anyway? It gives it character. However, I've learned that 32 oz is a little too beefy for me. First, it's a metal water bottle that holds water. It's going to be heavy, and heavy when you bring it up to your mouth to drink. But BE WARNED: don't drop this on your feet. It's going to hurt and you're liable to break something. Second, with how big it is, it doesn't fit in my cup holder in my car, and struggles to fit in any backpack bottle holder. Third, it will leak. Even before I dropped it it leaked if it was laying sideways, so when I use it and take it in my car, I'm careful to never let it lay sideways. All that being said, it's sturdy and keeps my water cold. I'd never heard of Iron Flask as a brand before this bottle but it's made me a loyal customer. And with it being easy to clean, it's fantastic. The bottle itself feels smooth but is easy to grip (I have small hands, but it's not slipping around in my hand). I have a Camelback bottle that has a similar paint, but it's more coarse and with my touch-sensitivity issues, I've had to get used to that. It made me appreciate my Iron Flask all the more because there was never that issue. I'm going to purchase a 24 oz Iron Flask so I can carry it in my cupholders in my car. I'm not one to follow brands, and the "hype" Hydroflask puts me off simply because it's so "everywhere". I'll stick to my Iron Flasks, thank you very much. Thank you for making a reliable product! Just please fix the leak issue.

headline: Good product for $19 price
review_text_raw: This is the 2nd thermos-type "water bottle" I've bought in a month. -- The first, more expensive, actual Thermos brand 24oz ended up being the right size to replace the daily-use, plastic water bottle I was carrying in my tote-purse. But, a tad too small when trying to put two cans of bubble water in plus fresh squeezed citrus/pulp/peel AND ice. -- This 30 oz., generic Amazon brand bottle was the max size I was willing to go to fit in those 2 cans/citrus without moving to one with a formal handle; as, I became concerned of being able to grip with one hand while full of liquid. It met my expectation very well. -- The slick finish takes a larger, full, strong hand to grasp & pour with one hand. Something to consider if buying for a youth (recommend 24oz size thermos instead) or hand size/dexterity concerns. -- The unit is spill proof, but ONLY when the simply designed lid AND cap are fully screwed on (lid screws onto bottle, and attached-cap screws onto lid). -- This is NOT a one handed flip-top, rather a screw top that flips back (yes, rachets into open position so does not flip back closed when in use); so, either two hands will be required to unscew lid, or one if user has the dexterity and surface to set thermos on. -- The spout is easy to drink from. The liquid flows uninhibited. A straw can easily be inserted, but not spill proof at that point. -- 3" diameter bottom feels stable enough, but no rubber to quiet setting in down or grip better to surface set on. Also, it does NOT taper, so it does not fit in my van's dashboard or console cup holders. -- It comes with a built in carrying handle that lies flat when not in use; but, the plastic looks like it will be the first thing to break off after a few drops...and, the screw on attached-cap a close second (which would then negate the spill-proof function--time will tell, as this is 1st day own this new product type). -- Good, wide mouth (2.25") cup opening with a small, curved inside edge. Wide enough to fit a standard kitchen sink scrub brush (unlike smaller 24oz other brand I purchased that requires an actual bottle brush). -- See pix for grip size, surface, lid, inside curve, and outer metal ring a carbiner-corded handle (not included) fastens over well (but takes some effort).

review_text_raw: This is the 2nd thermos-type "water bottle" I've bought in a month. -- The first, more expensive, actual Thermos brand 24oz ended up being the right size to replace the daily-use, plastic water bottle I was carrying in my tote-purse. But, a tad too small when trying to put two cans of bubble water in plus fresh squeezed citrus/pulp/peel AND ice. -- This 30 oz., generic Amazon brand bottle was the max size I was willing to go to fit in those 2 cans/citrus without moving to one with a formal handle; as, I became concerned of being able to grip with one hand while full of liquid. It met my expectation very well. -- The slick finish takes a larger, full, strong hand to grasp & pour with one hand. Something to consider if buying for a youth (recommend 24oz size thermos instead) or hand size/dexterity concerns. -- The unit is spill proof, but ONLY when the simply designed lid AND cap are fully screwed on (lid screws onto bottle, and attached-cap screws onto lid). -- This is NOT a one handed flip-top, rather a screw top that flips back (yes, rachets into open position so does not flip back closed when in use); so, either two hands will be required to unscew lid, or one if user has the dexterity and surface to set thermos on. -- The spout is easy to drink from. The liquid flows uninhibited. A straw can easily be inserted, but not spill proof at that point. -- 3" diameter bottom feels stable enough, but no rubber to quiet setting in down or grip better to surface set on. Also, it does NOT taper, so it does not fit in my van's dashboard or console cup holders. -- It comes with a built in carrying handle that lies flat when not in use; but, the plastic looks like it will be the first thing to break off after a few drops...and, the screw on attached-cap a close second (which would then negate the spill-proof function--time will tell, as this is 1st day own this new product type). -- Good, wide mouth (2.25") cup opening with a small, curved inside edge. Wide enough to fit a standard kitchen sink scrub brush (unlike smaller 24oz other brand I purchased that requires an actual bottle brush). -- See pix for grip size, surface, lid, inside curve, and outer metal ring a carbiner-corded handle (not included) fastens over well (but takes some effort).

headline: Stainless steel water bottle
review_text_raw: I bought this water bottle for a Cruise. I figured if I had to go and walk halfway across the ship for water, I wanted to fill up once and take it back to the room. I was very surprised when the water was still ice cold when I woke up in the middle of the night even more surprised when it was still cold the next morning when I woke up. I was absolutely floored when the water was still cold and holding ice at lunchtime. I thought I would never use this bottle after the trip I use it frequently. I just took it on another trip. I like that you just have to unscrew the cap and drink. I hate the straws because they take much more to clean, the cap comes off easy to fill and the handle has been great to use with the carabiner to clip to my bag or it fits in the Pouch on the side of my backpack backpacks I use this thing all the time. It’s one of the better things I bought and I am very pleased with it. If you’re on the fence, get it it does a great job.

headline: The Essential Facts
review_text_raw: All I wear is tee shirts. Okay, to be clear, I usually wear pants - shorts to be precise. I’m not a button down kind of guy. I wear tees from morning to night and sometimes all night, so I wear them out pretty fast. So I’m always here buying more, usually six at a time. I can’t see spending fifty bucks for one brand name shirt when I can get Amazon Essentials that are made in the same factories for a fraction of the price. But the pre-selected sixpacks almost always end up with one or even two colors I don’t want. THE ESSENTIAL SECRET Did you know that there are more than just one selection of their store brand shirts? They don’t make the subtle differences exactly clear so I had to filter by several factors to get a side by side comparison and even then sometimes a shirt of a different color or size can be made in an entirely different factory or even country for that matter. I narrowed it down to three listings, all called Essentials and all so similar it takes some effort to see how they are different. Pocket or no pocket? Moisture wicking or not? Slim fit or regular? Things like that. Most selections came in packs of two. And for a reason I will never understand, if I picked one color they were unbelievably inexpensive but another shade could be as much as double the price. THE REALITY So they all fit me about the same, yes the slim fit was slightly snugger than the regular but not by much. But here’s the thing that they don’t mention anywhere yet it is extremely important- some of the shirts were as much as three inches shorter than some others, or was it the other way around? This can spell the difference between a display of crack or not with some of my jeans. YES NO MAYBE Of the 3 sets of tees I chose, all from different listings of the same brand these were the longest, meaning they look the best on me and show less of the lower regions when I bend or sit.

review_text_raw: These shirts. Wow. If you're a bigger guy, you know how much of a pain it can be to find a shirt that fits fine. product_title: Gildan Men's Crew T-Shirts, Multipack, Style G1100
headline: Great value and quality
review_text_raw: I'll start out by saying I rarely give five stars, t-shirts that fit well are difficult for me to find. I usually go through several Brands before I find one I like and then I have to try several sizes to settle on one. With all of that being said, the shirts are a great quality for the price especially, and they are true to size. The fabric, stitching, and packaging are great for the price you're paying. I would consider these right in between a muscle fit and a slim fit, flattering in the arms and chest but not too tight in the waist, and the length seems to be just right. I wasn't really sold by the pictures of people trying them on but when I got the shirts in hand they seem to fit way better and look much nicer. If I have one thing that I could point out that isn't a complete positive it would be that the neck could be just slightly tighter and a bit more sturdy but that's really nitpicking because the neck does not sag at all, after a wash this might tighten up slightly and all the shirts seem to be identical and well made whereas usually when I order there might be one or two shirts that just aren't up to par. I got a 12 pack of the black and I will be ordering more for my day-to-day t-shirts, including a 12 pack of the whites. For a little perspective in rating these shirts, I used to buy the Haynes that were on Amazon and (I've noticed that the quality had gone down a bit) but those shirts usually run anywhere from 8 to $12 a piece and these are right up there with them if not better. Uptdate- i would settle at 4 stars, after a wash on cold and a no heat air dryin the dryer, the neck did firm up. The shirts definitely retain a thinner cotton feel and appearance. Great for every day or gym but youll want a nicer T for other occasions. Still great value but i would definitely see a xxl shrinking to a xl on heat in the dryer. Fantastic right out of the package, good after a wash.

review_text_raw: Update 7/5/22: Upon further washing and wearing, softness has improved considerably. Very comfortable and entirely satisfactory! --------------------------------------------------- I have these T shirts in both large and extra large---dark green. I am female, 5'2", and like to wear men's T shirts around the house. These Amazon Essentials Men's Regular Fit T shirts are adequate and acceptable, but not all I was hoping for. I like a bit closer--but not tight--fit, so maybe I should have tried the slim fit version. The medium size in regular fit would be too small for me, but the large size, and even more the extra large, bags under my arms and sides, with a bit too much fabric for my taste. They are nice and long on me, which I like. I also really like that they have printing on the inside back neck, instead of an annoying, scratchy label. I wanted a very soft T shirt, like most of my others. After one machine wash and dry, these were still what I would describe as more crisp than soft--although not too uncomfortably so. This might improve upon repeated wear and launderings. The fabric is medium weight, neither very heavy nor very thin. The shirts shrank just a little bit after washing, not too much. I would also prefer an army or olive green color. The dark green, which is a kind of forest or pine green, was the closest thing to that, but not my favorite. It did not fade in the wash--so far. The construction seems good and not flimsy, as I have come to expect of Amazon Essentials. I have many items of the Amazon brand and will almost always choose it if I can. They generally are of decent quality at a fair price. I kept these T shirts and they are perfectly fine, if not completely fitting my particular criteria. I expect they will hold up for a long time and give excellent value for the money.

Needless to say, we've used many brands over the years. I decided to try these this time I purchased his white tees based on the reviews and the price. I did go one size up from his usual size (Large) to an XLarge based on a few reviews regarding sizing. They fit perfectly. Not too big anywhere. They're not super tight around the neck like some under shirts can be, which drives my husband nuts. They are very soft right out of the packaging and haven't lost that softness with multiple times through the washer and dryer. I don't use fabric softener. I use wool balls as a natural fabric softener. So no chemical is being used to keep them soft. That's a plus for me because it means it's quality fabric. I actually purchased 3 white tshirts by Jockey at the same time I purchased these. I washed them all. Dried them all. Folded them all mixed together and placed them in a stack. I could see the difference. These are a bit thinner than the Jockeys. They aren't quite as white as Jockey. The sizing was nearly exactly the same as a Jockey Large. I wanted to see if my husband noticed a difference. He didn't! I've had these a few weeks now. They launder just fine. If there has been shrinkage it's been minimal and not noticeable. They still look brand new. Of course, in time I know they will wear out. All under shirts do when they are used as frequently as my husband must wear them. However, I'm pleased with them. My husband hasn't complained about them and trust me he WOULD complain if the shirts didn't feel right or fit correctly. I do think Jockey is a better quality overall, but I would buy these again. I do think they will break down sooner than the Jockey tees due to the thin material they're made of and the fact that these tshirts are worn, waged and dried A LOT. However, I would still recommend them. They are good quality and will last someone else a long time if they aren't been worn almost daily. This is a great deal for two quality white tshirts. **I would consider sizing up one size.**

product_title: Gildan Men's Crew T-Shirts, Multipack, Style G1100
headline: Good quality and value, comfortable
review_text_raw: Update 7/5/22: Upon further washing and wearing, softness has improved considerably. Very comfortable and entirely satisfactory! --------------------------------------------------- I have these T shirts in both large and extra large---dark green. I am female, 5'2", and like to wear men's T shirts around the house. These Amazon Essentials Men's Regular Fit T shirts are adequate and acceptable, but not all I was hoping for. I like a bit closer--but not tight--fit, so maybe I should have tried the slim fit version. The medium size in regular fit would be too small for me, but the large size, and even more the extra large, bags under my arms and sides, with a bit too much fabric for my taste. They are nice and long on me, which I like. I also really like that they have printing on the inside back neck, instead of an annoying, scratchy label. I wanted a very soft T shirt, like most of my others. After one machine wash and dry, these were still what I would describe as more crisp than soft--although not too uncomfortably so. This might improve upon repeated wear and launderings. The fabric is medium weight, neither very heavy nor very thin. The shirts shrank just a little bit after washing, not too much. I would also prefer an army or olive green color. The dark green, which is a kind of forest or pine green, was the closest thing to that, but not my favorite. It did not fade in the wash--so far. The construction seems good and not flimsy, as I have come to expect of Amazon Essentials. I have many items of the Amazon brand and will almost always choose it if I can. They generally are of decent quality at a fair price. I kept these T shirts and they are perfectly fine, if not completely fitting my particular criteria. I expect they will hold up for a long time and give excellent value for the money.
