headline: Good Quality Undershirts
review_text_raw: I usually buy white tshirts by Jockey for my husband as undershirts for his dress clothing, which he wears 5 days a week to work. Needless to say, we've used many brands over the years. I decided to try these this time I purchased his white tees based on the reviews and the price. I did go one size up from his usual size (Large) to an XLarge based on a few reviews regarding sizing. They fit perfectly. Not too big anywhere. They're not super tight around the neck like some under shirts can be, which drives my husband nuts. They are very soft right out of the packaging and haven't lost that softness with multiple times through the washer and dryer. I don't use fabric softener. I use wool balls as a natural fabric softener. So no chemical is being used to keep them soft. That's a plus for me because it means it's quality fabric. I actually purchased 3 white tshirts by Jockey at the same time I purchased these. I washed them all. Dried them all. Folded them all mixed together and placed them in a stack. I could see the difference. These are a bit thinner than the Jockeys. They aren't quite as white as Jockey. The sizing was nearly exactly the same as a Jockey Large. I wanted to see if my husband noticed a difference. He didn't! I've had these a few weeks now. They launder just fine. If there has been shrinkage it's been minimal and not noticeable. They still look brand new. Of course, in time I know they will wear out. All under shirts do when they are used as frequently as my husband must wear them. However, I'm pleased with them. My husband hasn't complained about them and trust me he WOULD complain if the shirts didn't feel right or fit correctly. I do think Jockey is a better quality overall, but I would buy these again. I do think they will break down sooner than the Jockey tees due to the thin material they're made of and the fact that these tshirts are worn, waged and dried A LOT. However, I would still recommend them. They are good quality and will last someone else a long time if they aren't been worn almost daily. This is a great deal for two quality white tshirts. **I would consider sizing up one size.**

headline: Great value and quality
review_text_raw: I'll start out by saying I rarely give five stars, t-shirts that fit well are difficult for me to find. I usually go through several Brands before I find one I like and then I have to try several sizes to settle on one. With all of that being said, the shirts are a great quality for the price especially, and they are true to size. The fabric, stitching, and packaging are great for the price you're paying. I would consider these right in between a muscle fit and a slim fit, flattering in the arms and chest but not too tight in the waist, and the length seems to be just right. I wasn't really sold by the pictures of people trying them on but when I got the shirts in hand they seem to fit way better and look much nicer. If I have one thing that I could point out that isn't a complete positive it would be that the neck could be just slightly tighter and a bit more sturdy but that's really nitpicking because the neck does not sag at all, after a wash this might tighten up slightly and all the shirts seem to be identical and well made whereas usually when I order there might be one or two shirts that just aren't up to par. I got a 12 pack of the black and I will be ordering more for my day-to-day t-shirts, including a 12 pack of the whites. For a little perspective in rating these shirts, I used to buy the Haynes that were on Amazon and (I've noticed that the quality had gone down a bit) but those shirts usually run anywhere from 8 to $12 a piece and these are right up there with them if not better. Uptdate- i would settle at 4 stars, after a wash on cold and a no heat air dryin the dryer, the neck did firm up. The shirts definitely retain a thinner cotton feel and appearance. Great for every day or gym but youll want a nicer T for other occasions. Still great value but i would definitely see a xxl shrinking to a xl on heat in the dryer. Fantastic right out of the package, good after a wash.

product_title: Men's Cotton T-Shirts Oversized Unisex Short Sleeves Casual Loose Wash Solid Basic Tee Tops
headline: Casual Comfort with Everyday Versatility
review_text_raw: Oversized cotton T-shirts have become a staple in modern casual wear, and this Men’s Cotton Oversized Unisex Short-Sleeve Basic Tee captures the appeal of that trend surprisingly well. It’s a simple piece, but when designed correctly, simplicity becomes its biggest strength. Comfort comes first The most noticeable feature is the relaxed oversized fit, which gives the shirt a loose, breathable feel that works well for daily wear. Unlike slim-cut tees that can feel restrictive, the dropped shoulders and roomy silhouette allow for easy movement and airflow. Oversized tees are intentionally designed to create a laid-back, boxy shape rather than a fitted look, making them popular for casual and streetwear styles. The cotton fabric also plays a major role in comfort. Cotton is naturally breathable and soft against the skin, which makes it ideal for warm weather or long days when you want something lightweight but comfortable. Minimal design that works with almost anything This shirt follows a solid-color, minimal design, which is exactly what many people want from a basic tee. Without graphics or heavy branding, it becomes extremely versatile. It pairs easily with jeans, joggers, cargo pants, or shorts, and it also works well layered under flannels, jackets, or hoodies. Because the style is unisex, it tends to suit a wide range of body types and fashion preferences. Some people wear it purely for comfort, while others incorporate it into streetwear outfits with oversized silhouettes. Good everyday durability A quality cotton tee should hold its shape after repeated washes, and many oversized cotton shirts are designed specifically to resist shrinking and fading with normal care. While lighter-weight cotton tees can sometimes wrinkle easily, most hold up well as everyday basics when washed in cold water and air-dried. A few small trade-offs Oversized shirts aren’t for everyone. If you prefer a tailored look, the extra room and longer sleeves may feel too baggy. Also, because the style is intentionally loose, choosing the right size can be tricky—some people prefer their normal size for a relaxed fit, while others size down for a slightly cleaner silhouette. Another consideration is fabric weight. Some basic tees use thinner cotton, which feels comfortable but may lack the heavier structure of premium heavyweight shirts. Final verdict The Men’s Cotton Oversized Unisex Short-Sleeve Basic Tee succeeds by focusing on what a good everyday shirt should be: comfortable, simple, and easy to style. It’s not designed to be flashy, but that’s exactly why it works so well. For anyone looking for a relaxed, versatile T-shirt that fits into almost any casual outfit, this oversized cotton tee is a dependable wardrobe essential that you’ll likely reach for again and again.

product_title: Men's Cotton T-Shirts Oversized Unisex Short Sleeves Casual Loose Wash Solid Basic Tee Tops
headline: Casual Comfort with Everyday Versatility
review_text_raw: Oversized cotton T-shirts have become a staple in modern casual wear, and this Men’s Cotton Oversized Unisex Short-Sleeve Basic Tee captures the appeal of that trend surprisingly well. It’s a simple piece, but when designed correctly, simplicity becomes its biggest strength. Comfort comes first The most noticeable feature is the relaxed oversized fit, which gives the shirt a loose, breathable feel that works well for daily wear. Unlike slim-cut tees that can feel restrictive, the dropped shoulders and roomy silhouette allow for easy movement and airflow. Oversized tees are intentionally designed to create a laid-back, boxy shape rather than a fitted look, making them popular for casual and streetwear styles. The cotton fabric also plays a major role in comfort. Cotton is naturally breathable and soft against the skin, which makes it ideal for warm weather or long days when you want something lightweight but comfortable. Minimal design that works with almost anything This shirt follows a solid-color, minimal design, which is exactly what many people want from a basic tee. Without graphics or heavy branding, it becomes extremely versatile. It pairs easily with jeans, joggers, cargo pants, or shorts, and it also works well layered under flannels, jackets, or hoodies. Because the style is unisex, it tends to suit a wide range of body types and fashion preferences. Some people wear it purely for comfort, while others incorporate it into streetwear outfits with oversized silhouettes. Good everyday durability A quality cotton tee should hold its shape after repeated washes, and many oversized cotton shirts are designed specifically to resist shrinking and fading with normal care. While lighter-weight cotton tees can sometimes wrinkle easily, most hold up well as everyday basics when washed in cold water and air-dried. A few small trade-offs Oversized shirts aren’t for everyone. If you prefer a tailored look, the extra room and longer sleeves may feel too baggy. Also, because the style is intentionally loose, choosing the right size can be tricky—some people prefer their normal size for a relaxed fit, while others size down for a slightly cleaner silhouette. Another consideration is fabric weight. Some basic tees use thinner cotton, which feels comfortable but may lack the heavier structure of premium heavyweight shirts. Final verdict The Men’s Cotton Oversized Unisex Short-Sleeve Basic Tee succeeds by focusing on what a good everyday shirt should be: comfortable, simple, and easy to style. It’s not designed to be flashy, but that’s exactly why it works so well. For anyone looking for a relaxed, versatile T-shirt that fits into almost any casual outfit, this oversized cotton tee is a dependable wardrobe essential that you’ll likely reach for again and again.

The black color is a true rich black, and after washing it twice, I haven’t noticed any fading or shrinking. Overall, this top is a great value. It’s comfortable enough for lounging or workouts, but also easy to style with high-waisted pants for a cleaner, more put-together look. I’m already planning to buy the light brown and army green colors next time they go on sale. If you’re looking for a soft, well-made, loose-fitting T-shirt that isn’t see-through and still has a flattering shape, this one is definitely worth buying.

headline: Comfort Colors T-shirt sizing is inconsistent from shirt to shirt
review_text_raw: Do a search in the reviews of these T-shirts using the word “inconsistent” and you’ll see others have similar comments to mine. With almost 27,000 reviews on these shirts, not sure if anyone will even see this review, but here we go. I have about 5 Comfort Colors T-shirts that I got in the past year; all are size Large, and they fit great in the body and neck with nice soft cotton, and they are fantastic T-shirts. I recently ruined a denim-colored Comfort Colors T-shirt using Spray-n-Wash on a couple food stains on the chest; the Spray-n-Wash faded the blue color in the treated areas. No worries, I’ll just order a replacement shirt.... I decided to order two replacement Comfort Colors T-shirts with one being blue jean-colored and the second being a denim-colored T-shirt. Both are blue with blue jean being slightly lighter blue than the denim, but I decided to order two since I like these T-shirts so much. The blue jean shirt arrived and fit great and is just like all my other large Comfort Colors shirts, and it’s a keeper. However, the denim shirt I received was too small: it was tight in the chest, the body was shorter, and the sleeves were shorter. I have attached two photos with one showing this new denim shirt on top of the shirt I ruined with Spray-n-Wash and another showing this new denim shirt on top of an orange Custom Colors shirt to show the smaller size of the new shirt. The neck-size in the new denim shirt I received was fine, but the shirt was noticeably too small in all other dimensions. I immediately ordered another denim-colored shirt hoping to get a “correct size” shirt, and the second denim shirt arrived the next day, and it was also smaller in all the dimensions exactly like the first denim shirt I had just ordered. All three of these new Comfort Colors shirts (one blue jean and two denim) and the denim shirt I ruined with Spray-n-Wash were sold and delivered by Amazon (i.e. none were third party vendors). I’m returning both of the too-small denim-colored shirts, and I’ll live without that color and enjoy my new blue jean shirt. As another point of reference, I purchased a pepper-colored Comfort Colors T-shirt from a third-party vendor on Amazon about 11-months ago in November 2024, and the neck on the pepper shirt was too large and gave the shirt a stretched-out and worn-out look even though the shirt was new. A third attached photo of the pepper shirt next to an orange Custom Colors shirt and shows the neck size difference. I messed up and didn’t return the pepper shirt within 30-days last year, but since I never wear it due to the way-too-large neck opening, it’s going to Goodwill. Ordering these shirts from Amazon as the seller has been hit or miss and doesn’t guarantee a consistent fit, and ordering shirts from a third-party seller on Amazon didn’t work out well when I did it in November 2024. So, I’m not sure what the lesson is here other than the sizing of these shirts is inconsistent; when the sizing is correct they're great, but ordering them online and getting correct sizing can be a PITA. It’s a bit of a hassle to have to take them to a UPS Store or other location to return the shirts if they don’t fit well, but at least if you order through Amazon Prime, the returns are free.

Always the same sizes and colors for the basic items. a. I buy Champion long boxer briefs, preferably made in Vietnam. b. I buy sock from Johnston and Murphy. c. I buy t-Shirts (and most other items) from Brooks Brothers Outlet. Unfortunately, Johnston and Murphy's over the calf blue merino wool socks change over the year. Double pipes at first, then single pipes close together, then triple pipes. All I want is the same exact blue sock and same exact grey sock year after year so that I can avoid matching socks out of the clean clothes basket. No, what should be the same exact sock is a big mix and match event every morning. Same thing with Champion. Why do I have to check to see what country they are made in before buying them. Why can't I just trust that Champion underwear are the same the world over. 3. I like high quality. Here is how I define quality: a. Don't skimp on material. b. Long staple threads. c. Ergonomically cut. Every single sock manufacturer out there is skimping on material on socks. Johnston and Murphy, Brooks Brothers, all shorter as the years go by. They make them a quarter of an inch shorter. It doesn't sound like a lot. But I have to keep pulling up my new socks. I never have to pull up my old socks. How much money is being saved by cutting the socks a quarter inch shorter? Brooks Brothers t-shirts are still pretty good. I have stuck with Brooks Brothers because every other t-shirt manufacturer that I've tried makes them an inch shorter, which means they come untucked. Brooks Brothers t-shirts always stay tucked in. And they don't pill after 10 washes. I hate pilled t-shirts. I hate them! Ergonomically cut: my mother bought me some gold toe socks. I have big calves. The elastic cut into my calves by the end of the day. Five year old Johnston and Murphy socks are butter smooth. The new ones are starting to cut with a sharp rigid thread around the top. Brooks Brothers has a nice soft elastic at the top--if you buy the non-outlet variety--which go for $25 - $50 per pair. That's a lot of money for socks when I like to keep 15 pair of blue and 15 pair of grey in the drawer after a full wash. That would be like $750 - $1,500 for socks. But the ergonomics on a sock make the difference between a beautiful day and a day that makes you feel like you've been sweating out in the sun. So, here is the scoop on the Amazon Essentials t-Shirts: 1. Value: They are $16 for 6 shirt. So, that's about $32 per year that I would spend on t-shirts. That's Awesome! 2. I'm sure they will find a better way to make something and that a change will occur every now and then. That's fine if they make an improvement. But I'm betting it will not be changing the number of pipes running down my socks. I'm sure other brands change the number of pipes because they found a factory in one country that makes they cheaper than in another country. And they are not made to Johnston and Murphy's specs. They are just socks already being produced by another manufacturer at a lower cost than the last factory. 3. Ergonomics: The t-shirts fit well. From what I can tell so far, Amazon Essentials t-shirts use long staple cotton that will not pill. But all of this is really to communicate to Amazon. Nice job with Amazon Essentials! Would you *please* make some over-the-calf dress socks. I will love you even more than I already do. Please consider making long inseam boxer briefs that somehow keep the legs from riding up or don't start slipping down. Also, I wear a lot of all cotton, non-iron dress shirts. I hate every reasonable priced sock, that I've tried, that is made today.

headline: Underwhelming, yet Affordable & Comfortable
review_text_raw: After being called out and having been offered to have new shirts purchased, I definitely had a reason to review this purchase. Please read on... I have been wearing T-shirts from another brand for over 6 years, but decided to go with Amazon since the price per shirt was more affordable. For reference, those other shirts have been worn once a week ever since they've been purchased and have been washed at the end of each week as well (at the very least: 52 weeks (once per week) x 6 years = 312 times). The older shirts were perfect, minus the stains that were accrued over the years. I only had 2 shirts left from the original 6 that were presentable, only due to the stains that wouldn't come off (not due to sizing or fit). I was still wearing all 6 of them, with the stains and all. I was overdue for new shirts as it was becoming apparent that the stains were no longer cutting it. Here comes my savior, Amazon! Right? Well, rightish... I received the packages (I purchased 2 bags of 6 shirts in each, thinking I'm getting a good deal) and replaced the 4 stained shirts. I wore the Amazon shirts for the week (once per day for the work week) and at the end of the week, I washed the shirts in the same washer with ALL of the same settings as the other branded shirts. After only 1 wash, the Amazon shirts shrank a couple sizes and went from an X-large to a medium... Not cool. Once again, I thought I was getting a good deal, hence why I purchased 2 bags. Obviously the return window has gone and now I'm stuck with 4 medium shirts and 8 X-large shirts that will become medium once they get washed one time! Now mind you, the shirt is very comfortable and since they are white, don't have any fading. Even after all of this, I have still given them 3 stars: affordability, comfortability/functionality (soft and lightweight), and fit. However, 2 star loss for losing size after only a single wash and false advertising (that X-large is a medium, sir!). Just to save a measly $5.09 (the other company was $22.99 for 6 shirts while Amazon was $17.90), I purchased the poorer quality shirt. I literally was called out today by my mother asking if she could purchase a new shirt for me since the one I was wearing was too short... In conclusion, do yourself a favor, if you wear a large, buy an XX-L, a medium = XL, a small = L, an X-S = medium, and an XX-S = small. I'm not saying don't buy it, all I'm saying is, be aware of the shrinkage.

headline: A nice basic tee that fits well.
review_text_raw: I’ve been wearing these exact shirts for several years for work as a home health nurse. They hold up for a really long time, don’t shrink and the color doesn’t fade. Eventually, after over a year of weekly wear, they kind of start to develop pills in certain areas so I just retire them then. They are super comfy. I can move easily in them and they don’t make me too hot. The fabric is thinish in a good way. It drapes nicely over the chest and feels comfortable in the shoulders and underarm area. The length is also perfect for me. I am 5’ 6 1/2” for reference and weigh 175 lbs with a bit of a tummy. I don’t like a short shirt or one that’s too long. I can easily reach, squat or bend all the way down to touch my toes without the shirt riding up too high in the front or back. I wear a size large. I am big busted and these fit fine for the girlies. I do wear a smooth bra underneath and it doesn’t show. Certain bras will show if they bulge out at all. It is, however, not see through at all. I just mean you can see little bumps with certain bras. I would say it’s a looser fitting, lightweight, casual tee shirt and the pics shown are accurate. As long as they keep making them I will continue to buy them. Be aware that they do go on sale. I wait for sales and stock up because their sale prices are unbelievable. I just got a bunch of them for $8.99 each. Different colors are different prices though so you may have to pay more for a specific color if you want it. Sorry but these work selfies are the only pics I have while wearing them but still thought they might be helpful to someone to see the fit.

review_text_raw: Update 7/5/22: Upon further washing and wearing, softness has improved considerably. Very comfortable and entirely satisfactory! --------------------------------------------------- I have these T shirts in both large and extra large---dark green. I am female, 5'2", and like to wear men's T shirts around the house. These Amazon Essentials Men's Regular Fit T shirts are adequate and acceptable, but not all I was hoping for. I like a bit closer--but not tight--fit, so maybe I should have tried the slim fit version. The medium size in regular fit would be too small for me, but the large size, and even more the extra large, bags under my arms and sides, with a bit too much fabric for my taste. They are nice and long on me, which I like. I also really like that they have printing on the inside back neck, instead of an annoying, scratchy label. I wanted a very soft T shirt, like most of my others. After one machine wash and dry, these were still what I would describe as more crisp than soft--although not too uncomfortably so. This might improve upon repeated wear and launderings. The fabric is medium weight, neither very heavy nor very thin. The shirts shrank just a little bit after washing, not too much. I would also prefer an army or olive green color. The dark green, which is a kind of forest or pine green, was the closest thing to that, but not my favorite. It did not fade in the wash--so far. The construction seems good and not flimsy, as I have come to expect of Amazon Essentials. I have many items of the Amazon brand and will almost always choose it if I can. They generally are of decent quality at a fair price. I kept these T shirts and they are perfectly fine, if not completely fitting my particular criteria. I expect they will hold up for a long time and give excellent value for the money.

review_text_raw: I usually buy white tshirts by Jockey for my husband as undershirts for his dress clothing, which he wears 5 days a week to work. Needless to say, we've used many brands over the years. I decided to try these this time I purchased his white tees based on the reviews and the price. I did go one size up from his usual size (Large) to an XLarge based on a few reviews regarding sizing. They fit perfectly. Not too big anywhere. They're not super tight around the neck like some under shirts can be, which drives my husband nuts. They are very soft right out of the packaging and haven't lost that softness with multiple times through the washer and dryer. I don't use fabric softener. I use wool balls as a natural fabric softener. So no chemical is being used to keep them soft. That's a plus for me because it means it's quality fabric. I actually purchased 3 white tshirts by Jockey at the same time I purchased these. I washed them all. Dried them all. Folded them all mixed together and placed them in a stack. I could see the difference. These are a bit thinner than the Jockeys. They aren't quite as white as Jockey. The sizing was nearly exactly the same as a Jockey Large. I wanted to see if my husband noticed a difference. He didn't! I've had these a few weeks now. They launder just fine. If there has been shrinkage it's been minimal and not noticeable. They still look brand new. Of course, in time I know they will wear out. All under shirts do when they are used as frequently as my husband must wear them. However, I'm pleased with them. My husband hasn't complained about them and trust me he WOULD complain if the shirts didn't feel right or fit correctly. I do think Jockey is a better quality overall, but I would buy these again. I do think they will break down sooner than the Jockey tees due to the thin material they're made of and the fact that these tshirts are worn, waged and dried A LOT. However, I would still recommend them. They are good quality and will last someone else a long time if they aren't been worn almost daily. This is a great deal for two quality white tshirts. **I would consider sizing up one size.**

headline: Comfort Colors T-shirt sizing is inconsistent from shirt to shirt
review_text_raw: Do a search in the reviews of these T-shirts using the word “inconsistent” and you’ll see others have similar comments to mine. With almost 27,000 reviews on these shirts, not sure if anyone will even see this review, but here we go. I have about 5 Comfort Colors T-shirts that I got in the past year; all are size Large, and they fit great in the body and neck with nice soft cotton, and they are fantastic T-shirts. I recently ruined a denim-colored Comfort Colors T-shirt using Spray-n-Wash on a couple food stains on the chest; the Spray-n-Wash faded the blue color in the treated areas. No worries, I’ll just order a replacement shirt.... I decided to order two replacement Comfort Colors T-shirts with one being blue jean-colored and the second being a denim-colored T-shirt. Both are blue with blue jean being slightly lighter blue than the denim, but I decided to order two since I like these T-shirts so much. The blue jean shirt arrived and fit great and is just like all my other large Comfort Colors shirts, and it’s a keeper. However, the denim shirt I received was too small: it was tight in the chest, the body was shorter, and the sleeves were shorter. I have attached two photos with one showing this new denim shirt on top of the shirt I ruined with Spray-n-Wash and another showing this new denim shirt on top of an orange Custom Colors shirt to show the smaller size of the new shirt. The neck-size in the new denim shirt I received was fine, but the shirt was noticeably too small in all other dimensions. I immediately ordered another denim-colored shirt hoping to get a “correct size” shirt, and the second denim shirt arrived the next day, and it was also smaller in all the dimensions exactly like the first denim shirt I had just ordered. All three of these new Comfort Colors shirts (one blue jean and two denim) and the denim shirt I ruined with Spray-n-Wash were sold and delivered by Amazon (i.e. none were third party vendors). I’m returning both of the too-small denim-colored shirts, and I’ll live without that color and enjoy my new blue jean shirt. As another point of reference, I purchased a pepper-colored Comfort Colors T-shirt from a third-party vendor on Amazon about 11-months ago in November 2024, and the neck on the pepper shirt was too large and gave the shirt a stretched-out and worn-out look even though the shirt was new. A third attached photo of the pepper shirt next to an orange Custom Colors shirt and shows the neck size difference. I messed up and didn’t return the pepper shirt within 30-days last year, but since I never wear it due to the way-too-large neck opening, it’s going to Goodwill. Ordering these shirts from Amazon as the seller has been hit or miss and doesn’t guarantee a consistent fit, and ordering shirts from a third-party seller on Amazon didn’t work out well when I did it in November 2024. So, I’m not sure what the lesson is here other than the sizing of these shirts is inconsistent; when the sizing is correct they're great, but ordering them online and getting correct sizing can be a PITA. It’s a bit of a hassle to have to take them to a UPS Store or other location to return the shirts if they don’t fit well, but at least if you order through Amazon Prime, the returns are free.

headline: Usual GAP comfort, but pricey
review_text_raw: Since I was in high school (which was decades ago), I've always liked Gap clothes. They're usually a good traditional fit, and try to be fashion-neutral instead of fashion-forward. For example: I typically don't go for shirts with pockets (like polos or tees), but don't find them too annoying especially if they're being worn as a base layer. This tee shirt is pretty much par for the course. It's 100% cotton, which makes it very soft and comfortable. I'm about a 37" chest, and the small size fit me well. It's just the right thickness to work as a base layer under most circumstances, and the pocket isn't that obtrusive. However, the price of this shirt does not justify the brand name. If all you need is a base layer, then this wouldn't be the best choice - there are more affordable options out there. But, if you want a t-shirt you can wear that has a bit of style, then this may be good for you.

review_text_raw: Finding a basic t shirt sounds easy until you actually start shopping for one. So many either shrink after one wash, lose their shape, feel rough against the skin, or fit strangely. I ordered this for my husband and this one ended up being exactly what he was hoping for in an everyday shirt. The first thing he noticed was how soft the fabric feels. It’s comfortable right out of the package and doesn’t have that stiff feeling that some new shirts have before they’ve been washed a few times. It feels lightweight enough to wear comfortably throughout the day but still substantial enough that it doesn’t feel thin or flimsy. The fit is another big win. It has a relaxed, easygoing look without being overly baggy. It sits nicely through the shoulders and chest and drapes naturally without looking oversized. The pocket adds a little extra style while keeping the overall look simple and classic. It’s the kind of shirt that works whether you’re running errands, traveling, relaxing at home, or meeting friends for a casual lunch. After several washes, I’ve been happy to see that it has maintained both its shape and softness. The stitching appears well done, and I haven’t noticed loose threads or signs of wear. That’s something I pay attention to because basic tees tend to get a lot of use in my husband's wardrobe. What I appreciate most is how versatile it is. It pairs easily with jeans, shorts, joggers, or even under a lightweight jacket. It’s one of those grab and go pieces that doesn’t require any thought because it always works. Those are usually the items that end up becoming favorites. GAP has always done a good job with wardrobe essentials, and this shirt is a great example of that. It’s comfortable, fits well, feels durable, and looks good without trying too hard. If you’re looking for a reliable everyday tee that you’ll actually want to wear regularly, this one definitely delivers.

headline: Great basic tees
review_text_raw: Listen, if you're buying this shirt, you probably already know what you're getting—it's the classic, reliable, do-anything, Gildan Heavy Cotton tee, just scaled down for kids! And honestly, it lives up to its reputation. I bought a stack of these for a youth group project (think messy paint, tie-dye, and a lot of running around), and they were absolutely perfect. The Good Stuff: • Durability is Top-Notch: It’s called "Heavy Cotton" for a reason. This shirt holds up to a ton of abuse. We've washed them multiple times now, and they aren't falling apart, the seams are holding, and the collar isn't getting all floppy. • Holds Color (and Vinyl) Great: The colors were bright and consistent right out of the package. For our tie-dye project, the white took the dye beautifully. If you're using heat transfer vinyl or screen printing, this fabric is thick enough that you don't have to worry about the design bleeding through or the shirt puckering. • The Fit is a Classic: It's a standard, roomy, boxy cut. It's not trendy and slim, but that's exactly what you want for a kid's uniform, camp shirt, or just a play tee. They have plenty of room to move around. • Good Value: You simply can't beat the price for the quality you get. It’s an easy, low-cost essential. A Note on Sizing & Feel: • Sizing is True-to-Size (BUT): I found the youth sizes generally accurate for the age range (e.g., a Youth Small is a true small). However, they are 100% cotton, so they WILL shrink a little in the wash, especially if you throw them in the dryer on high heat. If your kid is borderline between two sizes, or if you plan to dry on high heat, I would highly recommend sizing up one size just to be safe. • The Feel: It's "heavy cotton," not "buttery soft." It's not scratchy by any means, but it's not a premium, super-soft tee either. It's comfortable, but its main feature is being tough and thick, not super plush. Overall: If you need a great blank canvas for a team, camp, art project, or just a dependable, everyday play shirt for your kid, the Gildan G5 is the workhorse you need. Just be mindful of that initial wash.

product_title: MAGCOMSEN Men's Short Sleeve UPF 50+ T-Shirt Quick Dry Workout Athletic Running Swim Tops Tee Rash Guard Performance Shirts
headline: Quality and value
review_text_raw: I live in North Texas. Running for exercise during the heat and humidity of the summer is challenging. I am out the door between 0500 and 0530 because that's the only time during any 24 hour period the temperature is 80°F or lower. Even during the summer its still dark at that time, so along with reflective straps and a small clip-on flashing light, I need a really bright color to make it easier for me to be seen. For a long time, Russell DriPower shirts have been my go to. Unfortunately, they don't currently offer a neon or high visibility green shirt. It's either white or gray, but the gray tends to blend into the darkness too much. These MAGCOMSEN shirts are very similar to the Russell DriPower shirts in fit and in the weave of the fabric. They're just as heavy/thick enough not to feel flimsy while being thick enough to be durable and stand up to washing. I've purchased another brand, Liberty Pro, and while the shirts look good, the weave is too thick for this heat and humidity. The Liberty Pro shirts retain too much moisture and make you feel like you're wearing a wet sack. If you work out or work outside in a hot and humid environment, give these a try - I don't think you'll be disappointed. Hopefully they turn out to be as durable as the Russell DriPower shirts which I still have.

headline: Its perfect for what I need it for
review_text_raw: I had a little black book about 5x thicker than this and maybe another half larger than this one, which was hard back but had a nice soft leather like finish. Sadly it was 6 years old and my cat decided it no longer belonged on the table. I found the binding completely busted, separating at the seems and it was no longer of any use to me now. That also included pages that tore loose during the fall messing up information I had. Very very important information that I prefer to note down because I cant always remember everything all the time with a hectic and busy schedule. So i decided to search for a replacement and the Amazon Basics Classic Lined Notebook, 240 Pages, Hardcover was the one I finally decided on. It feels sturdy and the quality is nice but I didnt rate if it holds up or is super sturdy. Im not looking to test it out but my guess with it still being new, it can take quiet a few tumbles off of the table top by the cat for a few years without me worrying about it. --Update-- My cat and new puppy decided they would test out how durable this thing was. I know my cat likes to knock things off the table some times, and well our new 1yr mastiff puppy thought he would join in. I woke up to all fours ends of my notebook chewed on, but luckily none of my information in the book got ruined. The stretch band was still on it and not even damaged. Im still able to see all of whats in it, though the pages are damaged to the point I have to carefully pull them apart cause they sort of stick together. I bought two more of these cause im going to transfer the information from the damaged on to a new one and of course store it somewhere safe. I wanted a 3rd for backup or maybe for something else entirely. Maybe for recipes. I really love the quality of these books and even after the dog tried his best to shred through it, it held up enough to keep what was inside of it still legible

headline: Very nice...
review_text_raw: First, this is a very nice item for the price, you really can't beat it. The design is simple, yet still attractive. I got it for photography use, as a 'model', just stuff I'll use in still life photography. For my purposes, it's prefect, it's very inexpensive, it's very nice looking, and made well enough to last me a lifetime. I would think that the majority of people that buy this would love it, the outer cover is tough enough, although, it's a man-made material, plastic of some type. The reason I know this is, I bent it, crumpled it, hit it with blunt objects, rolled it up, and tried my best to make it appear older. It worked! The inside pages are printed well, the paper seems to be good enough, although, I honestly haven't written in it. For my needs, I halfway ripped out some pages and left them partially 'out' to give it a real, old world look. I used a green Scotch-brite pad to scuff it up some, making its appearance like it's been around the block a few times. I also used dirt to give it a 'dustier' look. To me, it looks like a bible, it's way too thin to be a bible, but when looking down on it, it looks just like one. So, in my photography world, it'll probably be used as a bible, along with other old looking things. I will probably upload a picture tomorrow, I'm sure that there aren't too many people that want to do this, but, there may be one that might. All in all, it's very much worth the little that you will pay to own this. Although the appearance has been changed slightly for my picture, it really works for my needs.

headline: Lovely, but not college rule
review_text_raw: Edit: I have only used this for a few days, but the corner on the top front of the journal has separated the cover from its backing. I'm gluing it down, but wonder if this is going to become a larger problem. Pros: This is a lovely journal. The cover feels good and is not too stiff or two soft. The brown is lovely and provides a feeling of leather. Pages lie flat. The paper is thicker than printer paper but not as heavy as some pages. I am using a fine point fountain pen and you can see that there is writing on the other side, but not to where it is heavy visibility. I like this larger size much better than the small ones. Cons: I don't like the notes at the top of the page. I think it ruins the free flow of the journal. And what is this page of personal information at the beginning? Why would you give that to just anyone who picks this up? Oh, I know -- if you leave it somewhere whoever finds it can get it back to you. No. Just no. This is not college ruled. It is normal rule in any notebook. I've attached a comparison of college vs. this page. I don't like that at all. I only ever use college rule, and I find it annoying using this and having all that space left because of the wide rule. If I ever used it again I would get it unlined (if available) and put a page of college ruled notebook paper behind it that had been darkened to show through the page. For that alone it has four stars instead of five. I'm aware that this one isn't described as college rule, but it is a huge annoyance to me in a journal. YMMV.

review_text_raw: I am a published author who writes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, and I have already filled a good portion of this notebook. I genuinely love it. review_text_raw: EDIT 3: Since I'm unable to do a separate review on the replacement the company sent, I changed this one to 5 stars and am leaving all the review text intact. Just know that the first remarks (marked with *) about a journal with wrinkles and weather/heat/water-like damage refer to the first journal I received and reviewed at1 star, and the second set of descriptions (marked **) belong to the replacement the company sent me, rated at 5 stars. *I was instantly in love with the cover, the silver wash on the page edges, and the bookmark. Beautiful and exactly as advertised, and the cover has a marbled sheen and texture that’s appealing as well. However, be aware that the pages are not at all like those in their bullet journals. They feel pretty low GSM. They are heavily rippled where they are fixed to the spine and my fountain pens are visible through, and make impressions on, the paper. It Is still functional (I don’t have to use fountain pens) and the visibility isn’t bad enough you can’t write on the other side of the pages, but the quality is enough of a step down and the page ripple is so irritating and unattractive that I wouldn’t give it as a gift. Hence 4 stars not 5. *EDIT: After using this journal for several days, I’ve found the pages are so thin and the ripple in them so stubborn that it’s like it was dropped in water. They are problematic to write on and difficult to keep open or turn. I’m reducing my review to 1 star so people read it and because had I not written on several pages, I would return it. EDIT 2: The seller reached out immediately after this review to offer a refund or replacement. I chose the replacement and am awaiting a journal I hope I’ll enjoy as much as I have others from the company. Thanks to them. I’m leaving the review as is for this product but hope to give a great review of the new one. **I'll just embellish my praise for the quality of the exterior: I loved the delicate, magical design on the deep blue cover, the silver wash on the page edges, and the high quality bookmark that went perfectly with the journal. Beautiful and exactly as advertised, and the cover has a marbled sheen and texture that’s appealing as well. Inside, the pages are lush and thick and lie flat when opened, no wrinkle or crease. They easly absorb any inks I've tried (other than alcohol markers of course, which are not meant for this type of paper). They are smooth but not too glossy for all my journaling supplies, washi tapes, and stickers; if it doesn't stick, it's the sticker maker at fault, because I've tried products from a *lot* of vendors on Tiefossi 160gsm paper and have not yet been disappointed. Just to wrap up, wonderful customer service experience! Thank you for being immediately so great. It's what I expected from a company whose products are so good that I've already placed an order for another journal since we made this arrangement and have others in my queue as gifts. I can't comment on whether the 100gsm paper journal experience was a fluke of poor construction on that one book, something to do with it shipping through areas of extreme heat last week, conditions in a specific warehouse or truck, or what. The company likely doesn't know either, since the journal itself has a 4.5+ rating. But they didn't care, they just made it good. For that I thank them both here and with future business. Best of luck, Precious Princess (I think that's the name of the Tiefossi vendor here). I'll keep my eye out for products you handle. You're a real one.

headline: Sturdy, beautiful, and perfect for heavy use.
review_text_raw: I use two of these journals at a time: one to plan my novel, and the other as a diary/braindump combo. I don't decorate the pages or do any impressive bujo designs, so I can't speak to how it would serve as a bullet journal. However, these babies see a lot of heavy writing use from me. I've purchased four of them so far and not a single one has disappointed. Page thickness is great. I accidentally spilled water on a couple pages and it didn't bleed through, which was shocking to me, given how affordable this journal is compared to most others listed. The pages are smooth and easy to write on, so be careful with any pens that might smudge or smear. The paper will certainly make it easier to pick up and spread wet ink on your hands. I'm a ballpoint user and I've noticed that finer tips work best, but even with the standard cheap-o pens, I just give them a minute or two to dry and then I'm highlighting all over them with no problem. It's solidly built. I've never had any issue with pages falling out, or the bookmark ribbons unfurling - and I'm writing in my journal at least 3 or 4 hours a day, constantly flipping back and forth through multiple brain dumps. (If you've got ADHD, you understand what I mean.) The color of the cover and ribbons are absolutely stunning, somehow prettier than the pictures show imo. I personalize the covers of my journals with stickers and writing, and whatever I put on has lasted. Overall, this journal has consistently impressed me by serving me well and I couldn't recommend a better one.

product_title: Project Cloud Womens Sneakers - Comfortable Fashion Sneakers for Women
headline: Very pleasantly surprised
review_text_raw: I wasn't sure how these would be for me, but I'm surprised and mostly very happy. Pros: I got the deep pink and it's as gorgeous as I hoped. Bonus: I normally wear an 8.5WW size, but saw the recs to size up so I tried a 9. These aren't shown as wide shoes, but they are only a smidge too narrow to fit perfectly properly, but I"m keeping them because they fit well enough. Cons: these are VERY slippery on my kitchen linoleum floor, so "no slip" is quite a stretch. These are fine on pavement, but I really wouldn't wear these if it was raining or if I was going somewhere with very smooth floors. But mine are also suede-ish, so I wouldn't wear those in the rain anyway. The insole padding is...adequate, but I am not 110lbs, and as they are these are a 3K step/day shoe, not a 10-20K step/day shoe. That is, I wouldn't take them on vacation when I average 15-20K steps per day. I already know that would be a painful world of hurt. Though the insoles do seem to be removable, so replacing them with something more formidable could help a lot. The bump/bone below my big toe, which is at about the second lace hole, that's a bit narrow for my feet and will be a hot spot until I stretch it out, but I also have rather wide feet, so someone with narrower feet shouldn't have that concern. The back of the heel seems soft enough that it won't cause blisters, but that's yet to be seen -- these arrived yesterday and I've been wearing them around the house today. Overall, I really do like these, though I'll probably get better insoles so I can wear them for more than an errand or two. These are a great deal for the $30 I paid for them, even if they just become low-step day shoes.

headline: For Weight Lifting
review_text_raw: I purchased the New Balance 608 V5 while it was on sale, mainly for weightlifting. These shoes aren't the cutest, but they perform well where it matters most for strength training. The sole is firm and very stable, keeping my feet flat and securely planted on the floor during barbell squats. Unlike cushioned walking or running shoes that compress under weight, these provide a solid, stable base that makes me feel more secure when lifting. Because of that firm construction, don't expect a soft or plush feel. The cushioning is noticeably less than what you'd find in walking or running shoes. The comfort is okay, but that's because the shoe prioritizes stability over softness. The arch support is also fairly minimal. I personally wouldn't recommend these for running since the shoes are quite rigid. If most of your workouts involve walking, jogging, or other cardio, there are more comfortable options available. However, if your main focus is weightlifting or strength training and you want a stable platform for exercises like squats, these work very well. The shoes fit true to size, and I had no issues with the fit. **Pros** * Good stability for barbell squats and strength training * Firm sole keeps your feet flat and securely planted * True to size * Great value when purchased on sale **Cons** * Design is fairly plain and not particularly stylish * Minimal cushioning compared to walking or running shoes * Fairly minimal arch support * Too rigid for running and may not be the best choice for cardio-focused workouts Overall, I think the New Balance 608 V5 is a good choice for anyone looking for a versatile gym shoe with a stable, supportive base for lifting. Just don't expect the soft cushioning or flexibility of a dedicated walking or running shoe.

headline: Surpassed expectations on vacation with zero break-in period
review_text_raw: Initially thought they might perform poorly. Was insanely impressed. These shoes came and I almost immediately thought of my 70 year old dad--they are bulky, blinding white, and very "utilitarian", thought grandpa shoes are having a moment and I was also sort of going for that look. I panic-bought these the night before a 10 day Ireland vacation because the options i owned for city and country walking shoes were primarily limited to chacos and some very thin mesh runners. I thought the plastic vinyl on these would perform better than my existing footwear and boy---did they.! They arrived 24 hours before departure so I had zero break in. I wore them to the airport to save space in my luggage and to test them out. Guys--I never took them off. These shoes kept my feet warm and dry in an absolute monsoon hike, handled city streets without causing me any back or leg fatigue, and looked equally stylish with my skirts and dresses as with pants. I had zero blisters or pain. They still look excellent despite being put through the ringer and logging over a hundred miles in 10 days. I cannot recommend these enough and am honestly not sure what I would have worn the entire trip had I not brought them along.

headline: Great for pregnancy related foot pain
review_text_raw: I've been wanting a pair of hokas for the last few years but couldn't justify the price. I'm currently 20 weeks pregnant and starting to experience a lot of foot pain at the end of active days and my other pair of tennis shoes are nearing their end of their life so I decided now is the time. They are definitely worth it. I took my dog for a long walk after work as I sometimes do and usually my feet would be hurting when I get home and need all night to recover, but with these, my feet felt pretty normal. Since I'm pregnant, I got the 8.5 and they fit well. I have just a little extra room in case of swelling or flattening. I hope they last all of my pregnancy and a few months after postpartum. Then I'll probably considering getting another pair.

headline: Good shoes that live up to expectations
review_text_raw: I've had these for about 6 weeks now and have worn them almost daily for varying lengths of time. I work from home, so for much of the day I am barefoot, but I wear shoes when going out in the yard, walking my dog, or going out places. Super easy to slip on, as the name implies, and they fit perfectly. I wear a women's size 11 and that's the size I bought. I like the color (I got the off white) and I think when my current pair of black tennis shoes bites the dust I'll probably replace them with these in black.

headline: Insole breaking down after 3 months
review_text_raw: I love these shoes! They have been comfortable from the first time I wore them. They slip on easily, stay on, and support my feet well for walking without becoming sore. I have washed them a couple of times (about once a month) as directed by manufacturer in cold water & let them air dry; haven't noticed any issues with washing. I've put a lot of miles on them, & the outer sole shows hardly any wear. My only issue is that after 3 months I noticed the interior where my toes rest is starting to break down. I really wanted to wear these without insoles because those interfere with the easy slip on feature, but I finally added insoles to prevent further breakdown. I still love the shoes, but can't give 5 stars because of that. I recommend if you get these shoes that you add insoles from the beginning to get the most life out of them.

headline: Great Shoes But Plan Accordingly (Toe Space)
review_text_raw: I don't usually write reviews, this is not a professional opinion. I bought these for work shoes to replace a different brand I'd worn out. I appreciate the appearance, material quality, they're nonslip, they're warm, I think the soles are decent, and I haven't had much problems, except for my toes. The inside of the tip of the shoes curves in a way where there's too much room for my big toes and the side presses into my pinky toes, causing my toes to get squished together. When I first bought them and was breaking them in, I ended up getting blisters on the insides of my small toes. Taking steps with these shoes on was incredibly painful. My ankles have started hurting aswell. I tried buying some toe dividers which didn't work out too well. The laces don't go down enough to adjust the toe space. I've considered stuffing something in there while I'm not wearing them to stretch the toe space out a little, or maybe even trying to operate on the shoes, but I think I'm just going to go ahead and buy a different pair. I'm not sure if this problem is because I bought a half size too small, this could be entirely my fault. Just a word of warning to anyone planning on buying these. They're great shoes, but planning ahead goes far with these. I've only had them for a month, and my possible lack of attention to detail might have just set me out $70.

headline: Comfortable give them a try.
review_text_raw: First off a little back story I work at a warehouse and Im on my feet all day for 10 hours. I average around 40k to 50k steps each day and thats about 18-22miles per day.(see pic) My feet are burning by the end of the day. I wore $200+ steel/composite toe boots with $100 in soles but feet still hurt at the end of the day and im limping when I get off work, I had to do something. I went on a search for new comfortable safety shoes a friend of mine recommended these. But I looked at the price and I thought to myself they cant be better than my $300 shoes with insoles. He said try them they only $40. Still very skeptical I bought them anyway. When they first came in I wasnt too impressed they didnt come in a shoe box but were shrinked wrapped and put in an Amazon shipping Plastic bag! However I put them on it was like putting on sneakers with memory foam. Shoes were light and didnt feel like safety shoes at all. The first daywith these I worked half a day and clocked in about 20k steps and my feet were feeling good no pain. The 2nd day with these shoes I put them to the test, I clocked in 50k steps, about 24miles.(see pic) Usually by hour 7-8 in my old shoes I would feel the pain. With these shoes I started to feel real pain around the 9hr mark but not as bad. I think no matter how comfortable your shoes are if you walk a marathon in one day your feet will be in pain no matter what. But by end of shift my feet were tired they were sore but didn't hurt as much. Usually I would take of my work shoes in the parking lot and slip on my sneakers for the drive home but these felt like sneakers and I drove home with them on. Next day I think I clocked in 36k steps/17 miles. The end of the day my feet were sore but didnt hurt as much as they usually do with my other boots. Since I've only had them for a week I cant speak on durability.

product_title: New Balance Men's 515
headline: Fashionable kicks for the girthy-est feets. Finally.
review_text_raw: Historically New Balance only makes certain shoe models with their extra wide sizing. The retro/fashionable models haven't usually been included in that bucket. So when I saw these new 515's on my BIL's also wide feet and saw them being offered with this many colorways, on Amazon, for less than $100, it seemed too good to be true. I know I'm writing this like I'm about to bring up a big "but" with these shoes... But I'm actually not. They're actually extremely well made, breathable in the summer heat and surprisingly comfortable, even with just an EVA midsole and thin hard rubber outsole. I'm also one of those weird goth kids from the 90's who proved it wasn't just a phase, so the minimalist blacked-out colorway also gave me a bit of the fizz. The wider 4E fit and footprint is also identical to what I'm used to with my other New Balance faves (the 410v5 dark Trail Runners) but the materials feel even more substantial and quality. Though I will admit that the sole response of the 515's is less springy and athletic-feeling than those kicks. That said, I've been wearing these shoes a LOT this summer and they haven't disappointed yet. The leather has held up and stayed clean with no fraying at the seams or obvious signs of wear inside or out. The midsole has well broken into the shape of my foot and toes, providing a decent amount of support and grip without looking agressively athletic. Which seems to leave the 515's striding a happy line between looks and functionality that have made them my go-to running around town shoes going forward. If you have wide feet, you could do a lot worse.

It was these thick rounded "protrusions" of material so that the laces could go through, and the way these "eyelets" are shaped (thicker and flat) you would need fewer of them to make the shoe lace stretch out over what would be two eyelets. This is good because on one hand it may be trouble to string a shoe lace over a lot of regular style eyelets (holes on the area which I think may be called an "eyestay") but then if you skip putting the lace into some eyelets then , in my opinion it gives the distribution of of the lace on the sneaker a very awkward look, if you can get what I mean. I really dislike lacing systems in which there are just thin strips of string (or sometimes short strips of "ribbon" ) sticking out of the sides on top of the sneaker where the tongue is. If the string or strip of ribbon breaks then it is not easy to repair or is even impossible to repair. It makes the entire sneaker useless. So the lacing system on the Under Armour Men's Charged Surge 4 Sneaker is overall my favorite kind . I also like that the area of the highest eyelet is not rigid and hard. It is important for the upper-eyelet area of a sneaker or shoe to be properly flexible and /or cushioned (though also not of flimsy material). The area of the upper-most eyelet is the area that will push right into your upper foot as you bend your foot in the process of walking or running. This can hurt or cause friction. However , as with other Under Armour sneakers I find that at least certain styles can have odd sizing. I normally use a Women's size 10 so that translates to Men's 8 to 8.5 (which can depend on the style) but I find that in Under Armour I have to use a complete size up. I ordered these UA's in size 9.5. I tried them on. They fit but I was not sure if they would start to hurt my toes should I start walking long distances in them. I could not risk it. I sent them back. I may re-order them in a larger size even though they would look a bit too big. Another thing I did not like about this sneaker is that the sole at the heel part is designed in a way that when you walk with the sneakers on they make a noise like a shoe with a very hard heel with sharp edges would make, not a softer light noise like a sneaker should make. I do wish that this sneaker came in slightly wider widths. It may feel more comfortable than having a rather pointed type of toe-box area. So there are pros and cons to this sneaker at least in my opinion. I would definitely recommend them though. It can depend on your needs.

product_title: New Balance Men's 608 V5
headline: Support properly, and perform their duty day after day
review_text_raw: I wear only New Balance Extra Wide shoes. The explanation is neither mysterious nor flattering: I carry more weight than I ought to, and my feet insist on reminding me. These provide the width I need along with an arch that actually supports rather than merely decorates the insole. In a marketplace increasingly devoted to fashion masquerading as function, that is no small achievement. I generally buy the 608 V5 cross trainers because they consistently have the best availability in Extra Wide. That alone earns them a place near the top of my shopping list. They also come in enough colors to satisfy whatever mood strikes you. I've accumulated black, white, brown, blue, and now gunmetal. Evidently, when I find something that works, I become a predictable voter. The shoes are comfortable from the first day, supportive during long walks, and forgiving during those moments when the bathroom scale reminds me that arithmetic is undefeated. They have become my everyday footwear, accompanying me through errands, appointments, and the ordinary business of retirement. No product is without its legislative amendments. Occasionally the shoelaces seem unnecessarily thick or comically long, as though drafted by a committee unable to agree when to stop. It's hardly a constitutional crisis, but every so often I find myself wondering whether someone at New Balance has a side business selling extra lace. Because these are my primary shoes—and because I place a bit more stress on them than their designers probably envisioned—they're generally ready for retirement after about six months. I don't regard that as a defect so much as the inevitable consequence of constant use and a user who could stand to lose a few pounds. Institutions endure because they reliably perform their intended function. The same may be said of these shoes. They are not flashy, they make no extravagant promises, and they will not transform your life. They simply fit well, support properly, and perform their duty day after day. In an era of exaggerated marketing claims, there is something refreshingly conservative about a product that succeeds by quietly doing exactly what it was designed to do. Five stars.

review_text_raw: This is a good shoe so it gets 4 stars. Minus a star because it lists upper as canvas, but it's really a mix of canvas and rubber. That combo makes them look sportier than I want, and also makes them stiffer and heavier than than I want. That said it's a well constructed shoe and as such, guessing it will hold up well. So, once they were discontinued, I was on the search for a replacement.... I didn't think of Skechers much as a "serious" brand, mostly because I didn't know much about them, but it turns out they do sell some wide fitment shoes, and these, for me, are an absolute great fit! I tried a pair, a few years back, and have faithfully replaced them every time, having once again found a pair of shoes I really love. They are very similar to the Air Walks, in comfort and durability, although, sadly, they don't last as long as the Nike's did. Then again, they are about half the price! So, I don't feel too bad having to replace these more often. I'd say a pair lasts six to eight months, where the Nike's used to last more than a year, but, as I say, these are a lot more affordable to replace, so I guess it kind of works out, cost wise. For me, the most important thing is having a pair of shoes that are comfortable, versatile and look good enough to wear to work with good Levi's and a sport shirt, yet can also be used for walks or even light hikes. Since they are all white I have the same problem I had with the white Air Walks, which is that they tend to get dirty kind of quickly, but, like the Air Walks, they also clean up beautifully with some shoe cleaner and a bit of Sneaker whitener, so they tend to look great until they simply wear out -- in my case it is usually the side that eventually blows out -- which was the same on the Air Walks, but just didn't happen as quickly. Even so, six to eight months of life is pretty good to get out of them, considering I wear these pretty often throughout the average week. So, I'm a fan now, and in fact will be getting a second pair of these to have around, since they also come in blue and white, and that way I don't have to clean these up as often, and that's actually an improvement over the Air Walks, since they only came in the white or solid black. With these, I can now have an all white pair, and now can also have a more "casual" sneaker for other looks or outfits or uses, and, since two pairs is not much more than one pair of what the Air Walks use to cost, I'm actually a bit ahead of the game. I'm very happy with these, and I'd certainly recommend them highly!

headline: Superb quality, but not for my feet
review_text_raw: I have been a huge fan of Sketchers for awhile now; their quality and craftsmanship are superb and their shoes are built to last! I am pretty tough on my shoes, and demand a lot from them. I need a shoe that offers sturdy support, as my back is pretty much a wuss, and will freak out about the littlest things, including lack of shoe support. Sketchers has always delivered everything I need in a shoe. I was excited to try this design, because I am on my feet a lot at work (I work 12-hour shifts on concrete floors at a manufacturing plant). From what I've read online, these shoes were ideal for my needs, because they offered the support I need for both my back and my feet. I also like the fact that these shoes have a very aggressive tread, as I do a lot of outdoor activities including hiking and camping, and I expect my everyday shoe to hold up for the task (even though I have dedicated hiking boots, sometimes you want a lighter-weight option, especially when you're carrying 60-80 pounds on your back). When these shoes arrived, I was impressed with the amount of tread and grip they provided. It wasn't like the dinky little tread you see on most shoes, it looked like they took a tire, cut it to shape, and put it on the bottom of the shoe - Sketchers meant business when they designed this shoe! The material is warm, but lets your feet breathe, so your feet stay nice and warm in the winter. I can't say how they are in the summer, as I didn't own them in the summer months. Inside, there is a lot of padding all around, especially in the tongue of the shoe, which is nice - it gives a real nice snug fit to keep the shoe in place without having to really strap down the lacing tight. There is a huge amount of padding in back on the bottom for your heels, which, for me, is where the problem comes in. For most people, this would be a very nice feature, but for some reason, it ended up hurting my heels pretty badly, almost to the point where I didn't want to walk from one end of the house to the other. After wearing them for just one 12-hour shift, my feet were screaming, and all I wanted to do was either sit back in a chair with my feet up or lay in bed, just so I wouldn't be on my feet. I understand that every pair of shoes needs to be broken in, and during that time the shoes can be a bit uncomfortable, but not this much. While I absolutely like these shoes and have absolutely nothing against them (other than the heel issue mentioned above), I am forced to return them to Amazon. Please remember that this is not the case for most people - my feet are extremely picky to begin with, and simply put, these shoes just aren't for me. I really like the quality and materials that Sketchers used to design this shoe, and I can honestly say that I believe they are a shoe that will hold up to use and abuse for quite a long time. Despite them not being the right shoe for my feet, I would still highly recommend them, but be aware that there is a large amount of padding in the heel area, and will lift the heel area of your foot upwards somewhat. I don't hold anything against Sketchers or these shoes. In fact, once my return is processed, I plan on buying a new pair of my go-to shoes, which are the Sketchers Men's Stamina Nuovo sneakers. All around, great shoe, just not for me (unfortunately).

review_text_raw: This is my first purchase of Puma shoes, and I love them. I am 5'6" tall, 135 lbs, and i exercise every day for about an hour doing a mix of aerobics and cross training. I wear an 8.5 women's size and while I am a medium width my feet are just short of a wide. These were true to size and roomy in the toe box which is important. If you haven't used cross trainers like these they might feel a bit odd at the beginning. The platform is very stable almost as if you can't roll your foot from side to side. But that is a huge benefit if like me your feet roll outward while walking. It's also a big benefit for cross training classes during which you make sudden side to side movements. These keep you firmly planted on the floor. They look like they would be very heavy, but they are the exact opposite. They are very light but well constructed. (avid 25+ year Converse All Star wearer here). they seem to have excellent traction, i've only worn them out once (after i received my exchanged pair) and it was a comfy walk on dry sidewalk. the shoe quality seems to be good, i have noticed a few frayed threads sticking out, but honestly, i do not care. i dislike wearing shoes inside my home, especially on a top floor apartment (noise to neighbors, yes im nice and do everything to prevent heavy walking), but recently have an issue with tendonitis in one foot. OBVIOUSLY from my chucks and getting older and how i walk around at home lol, but listen, I wore these inside for a hour and hardly any noise, i felt floaty... normally I just slide around in socks. OVERALL: the wearability seems on point, I don't have any complaints yet. they are for work where I will be on concrete all day. I already know these will help. I can't really say HOW to choose your size, just do the research and buy a pair with the idea- you may have to exchange for a different size, and with that said- DO NOT LOSE THE TAGS (i removed mine from shoes but kept in great condition inside box for the return), DO NOT WALK OUTSIDE, KEEP EVERYTHING IN GOOD CONDITION- IN CASE- you have to do an exchange. They're worth the money, I honestly believe so and I don't like any shoe but converse all-stars. oh, and they send you an extra set of longer laces which i prefer. hope this helps anyone :) **Update- I wore these to work in a bakery/coffee/cafe, where there is concrete flooring. And by the dish area and after mopping it is too wet for these. These have 0 protection on slip-resistant. They aren't stated to have it, but who knows, some say there is good traction on wet sidewalks, so thats a plus. I can no longer wear them at work, did it for 1 day and can't risk it. The other downside for me, they have memory foam which traps heat, living in Texas, this is a huge nono. I'm learning so much about shoes in the last week I could be a sales person. If you're looking for slip-resistant, breathable. No. I did size up to a Wide which I thought would help, but these shoes are too tight for my preference. That said- they form to your foot, if you like that. They ARE comfortable, but just not what I'm looking for. I'm bummed because cute and cozy, but my work demands a different type of shoe.

headline: Definitely size up!!
review_text_raw: Thank you to all the other reviews who already advised to size up! I am a us women’s 5.5 exactly and in brands that only have whole sizes I always go down to a 5. However, I listened to the reviews and purchased a women’s size 6 in this shoe and it was barely big enough! I could have probably fit a 6.5 in this shoe but the 6 WILL work. It is also true that this shoe is narrow and the toe box is especially small. I do not have wide feet for their length (very average), so it is working out, but if you do have wide feet this is not the shoe for you unfortunately. I imagine people with narrow feet would be even more comfortable in this shoe than I am. That being said, I am very pleased with this shoe especially for the price at purchase ($49.95). It looks very cute on and will pair with everything. The gold detail on the branding really sets them off and I feel the gum color sole gives them an excellent aesthetic dimension. They feel like they will become more comfortable after I have broken them in, after a week or two. Due to the narrowness, it did take some adjusting/work before they fit correctly over the bridge of my foot. They are a lightweight shoe, so I cannot be sure how long they will last with the materials used. Overall, size up and I do recommend this shoe!

headline: Good pair of athletic shoes for the price
review_text_raw: I will start off by saying that I'm not a runner. I do go to the gym a lot, and one of the things I do there is the step mill machine (stairclimber) and the treadmill. I also do a lot of walking (10k steps) in my neighborhood from time to time. I got these shoes for that purpose. While I don't mind paying good $$$ for a decent pair of shoes, the last pair of shoes I paid good $$$ didn't last all that long. In fact, its outer sole was equally as thin as those on the cheaper shoes. With that said, this time around I was a little more budget conscious, and wanted the best quality shoe for the price. I found these here, and after reading the product description and some online reviews, I decided to try them. The shoe fit is true to size. It wasn't too tight or too loose, even with thick socks on. The insole was comfortable and even after an hour of walking around doing everyday stuff, my feet felt pretty good. The insoles felt good and comfortable, although I have plantar fasciitis so I will wait and see how that goes after a longer period of wearing. The outer sole is rubber and felt firm and grippy. This shoe adds about an inch to inch and a quarter of height to my frame. My other shoes were somewhere in the order of half an inch to three quarters of an inch. The top part of the shoe is a mesh like fabric cloth, and allows for some breathability on a hot day. The overall quality of the shoe is pretty decent, and I detect no flaws in the craftsmanship. I am pleased with the shoe upon my initial experiences. Time will tell how the shoe holds up. But in the meantime, I am happy with it. For what I paid ($42), this is a pretty decent pair of athletic shoes. I can't speak to its performance for running, but for my intended use in the gym, this shoe fits the bill quite well without breaking the bank.

headline: Very pleasantly surprised
review_text_raw: I wasn't sure how these would be for me, but I'm surprised and mostly very happy. Pros: I got the deep pink and it's as gorgeous as I hoped. Bonus: I normally wear an 8.5WW size, but saw the recs to size up so I tried a 9. These aren't shown as wide shoes, but they are only a smidge too narrow to fit perfectly properly, but I"m keeping them because they fit well enough. Cons: these are VERY slippery on my kitchen linoleum floor, so "no slip" is quite a stretch. These are fine on pavement, but I really wouldn't wear these if it was raining or if I was going somewhere with very smooth floors. But mine are also suede-ish, so I wouldn't wear those in the rain anyway. The insole padding is...adequate, but I am not 110lbs, and as they are these are a 3K step/day shoe, not a 10-20K step/day shoe. That is, I wouldn't take them on vacation when I average 15-20K steps per day. I already know that would be a painful world of hurt. Though the insoles do seem to be removable, so replacing them with something more formidable could help a lot. The bump/bone below my big toe, which is at about the second lace hole, that's a bit narrow for my feet and will be a hot spot until I stretch it out, but I also have rather wide feet, so someone with narrower feet shouldn't have that concern. The back of the heel seems soft enough that it won't cause blisters, but that's yet to be seen -- these arrived yesterday and I've been wearing them around the house today. Overall, I really do like these, though I'll probably get better insoles so I can wear them for more than an errand or two. These are a great deal for the $30 I paid for them, even if they just become low-step day shoes.

There’s just no flexibility in the sole because of the platform. Tightening the laces helped but I’m sure you would have to constantly do that and that’s annoying. And they still slipped a little. I tried lower socks and thinner socks and basically if the sock is between your skin and the shoe it will slip around. If you’re just standing around, adorable. If you actually want to walk around with socks, there’s gonna be a problem. I tried them without socks and they’re much better. I personally just prefer socks with sneakers, so I’m still debating keeping them.

review_text_raw: This is the first time I’ve ever bought athletic shoes online and actually had them fit perfectly. Are they narrow? I’d say they are closer to normal and only slightly narrow. The fit is more fitted around the heel area which is perfect if you have issues with blistering from sliding. Your heel will not slide from side to side. The heel is nicely fitted with the right amount of support. I’ve got a heel spur and these have enabled me to get back into working out. Super light weight. One thing I like much more than I thought I would is the bottom of the shoe is flat under the heel. This is actually a great thing. I have a tendency to roll my right ankle. I’d really have to try hard to do that in these. The heel height isn’t high like many so called cross trainers with the sole that extends well beyond the shoe. It adds to their stability. Super quality materials. Plenty of toe room in the correct shape for my feet. The back of the shoe by the back of the heel is the right height to keep the shoe on without rubbing or coming off. Nice grippy shoe without being over done. Fantastic shoe over all. My average size is a 7.5 but can anywhere between a 7 to an 8 depending on the shoe. I normally wear mine way too snug and wanted a little more toe room so I bought a size 8.
