headline: Great Masculine Scent Variety, Clean Burn, Perfect Gift Set (Just a Bit Small)
review_text_raw: I picked up this men’s scented candle set not really knowing what to expect, but it turned out to be a solid buy — especially if you like deeper, more “masculine” scents. The variety is what stands out most. You get a mix like leather, smoke & vanilla, oak, and lavender, and each one has a distinct vibe. The leather and smoke scents are definitely the strongest and give off that warm, slightly cologne-like feel, while the lavender helps balance things out when you want something more relaxing. The candles burn pretty evenly and last a decent amount of time for their size. I also like that they’re soy-based, so they don’t produce that heavy, overpowering smoke some cheaper candles do. Scent strength is moderate — not weak, but not overwhelming either. It’s enough to fill a room without being too intense, which I prefer. Only downside is the tins are a bit small, so if you’re expecting large candles, these are more on the compact side. Still, they’re great for trying different scents or spreading them around the house. Overall, this is a great set if you want clean-burning candles with more rugged, unique scents instead of the typical sweet/fruity ones. Also makes a really solid gift.

headline: Level of fragrance really depends on the type of candle you choose!
review_text_raw: Have ordered 2 of these candles - the Peace + Tranquility (white) and the Reflection + Clarity (light blue). Both were excellent, but the Peace + Tranquility definitely had a lighter aroma / more subtle than the Reflection + Clarity. Saw several reviews stating they couldn't smell the candle. There are 2 likely reasons - 1: if you have a large room/house that you want to smell the candle in, I highly recommend the coffee table jar, which has 3 wicks and smells much stronger than the single wick candles. However, since it has three wicks, it does burn through faster. I light mine every night for a couple of hours after dinner while I clean the kitchen and they each lasted about 2-3 weeks with nightly use. Secondly, it definitely seems to vary with the the fragrance type you use. The Peace + Tranquility is very light and fresh smelling, but not at all strong. The Reflection + Clarity is very strong and pleasant, it kind of smells like laundry detergent though (this can be a good or bad thing depending on how you feel about your laundry detergent!). I have a large house with high ceilings and you can smell the Reflection + Clarity everywhere after being lit 30 minutes or so. I like to use the R+C type of I make a very strong-smelling dinner (with lots of garlic or onions) where I want to refresh the house. I use the P+T when I just want a nice calm scent. I will definitely order again, but will probably try another couple of types since they seem to vary quite a bit...

At this price for 12 unique scents, it’s an incredible value. The set comes together so well that it would make a thoughtful, versatile gift for housewarmings, birthdays, or just treating yourself. Having 12 options means there’s truly something for every season, activity, or guest. If you’re looking for a high-quality, multi-scent candle set that delivers on fragrance, burn time, and presentation, this is a fantastic buy. I’ll absolutely be ordering another set when these run out!

product_title: Yankee Candle Mid Summer's Night, Scented Candle, 22oz Large Jar with up to 150 Hour Burn, Giftable
headline: The Iconic, Bold Cologne Scent That Fills a Room
review_text_raw: If you’ve ever walked into a Yankee Candle store and smelled that specific, intoxicating scent wafting through the air, it was almost certainly Midsummer's Night. It is arguably one of their most recognizable and polarizing fragrances, but for those who love it, it's an absolute classic that's hard to beat. Scent Profile: This candle is unapologetically bold. Yankee Candle describes it as "a intoxicating and masculine blend of musk, patchouli, sage and mahogany cologne." That description is spot-on. It strongly evokes the feeling of a high-end men’s cologne—cool, fresh, and slightly woodsy, but with a deep, sensual warmth from the patchouli and musk. It is not fruity, floral, or traditionally sweet. If you prefer clean linen or vanilla cupcake scents, this will likely be too strong for you. But if you love deep, "dark" scents that feel sophisticated, this delivers. Throw and Performance: I tested this in the classic 22 oz large jar. The scent throw is phenomenal—a solid 10/10. Midsummer's Night is known for being a powerhouse. Within 30 to 60 minutes of lighting it, the fragrance easily fills my entire downstairs living area and kitchen. It lingers in the air long after the candle has been extinguished. Quality and Burn: The burn quality is consistent with the standard Yankee Candle reputation. The wax pool melts evenly across the surface, preventing tunneling, provided you let it burn long enough on the first few uses. The two wicks burn cleanly (remember to trim them before each light to minimize soot). The longevity is excellent; the large jar provides many hours of strong fragrance, justifying the price point. The Vibe: This is a fantastic year-round scent, though it particularly shines in the autumn and winter evenings due to its warm, musky notes. It creates a cozy, confident, and slightly mysterious atmosphere. It’s perfect for movie nights, dinner parties, or simply relaxing after work. Because it is so cologne-forward, some describe it as a "boyfriend's sweater" scent. Verdict: Midsummer's Night is a classic for a reason. It is a bold, long-lasting, and powerfully scented candle that delivers exactly what it promises. If you are a fan of deep, musky, or cologne-style fragrances and want a candle that will unmistakably scent your entire home, this is a must-buy. Highly recommended. Pros: Iconic, sophisticated, "cologne" scent Phenomenal scent throw (fills large spaces easily) Long-lasting burn time (Large Jar) Creates a distinct, cozy atmosphere Cons: The scent is very strong and may be overpowering for those sensitive to heavy fragrances Polarizing profile; definitely not for lovers of light, floral, or sweet scents

review_text_raw: Hello everyone, my name is John and this is my honest opinion on this product. You can buy candles almost anywhere. Now I have to say this was a gift for a friend but I have owned many different Virginia Candle Company Candles in the past and I have loved them all. They are a conversation piece around the holidays and whenever family is over I always hear, "What is that smell? It smells great!" or "What is that crackling sound, is that the candle?" Now, for someone who has never bought one of these candles before, you may not know that these candles actually do make a nice crackling noise as they burn. Nothing dramatic enough to make the in-laws think there is a raging, crackling fire in the other room at thanksgiving, but not quiet enough that you have to tell everyone to quite down so you can admire that satisfying crackling and popping coming from the candle. It is honestly probably my favorite attribute to these candles. Each of these candles smell just perfect. Now the reason I choose to review this specific scent of candle is because it is my favorite. It truly smells like vanilla bean, one of my favorite smells. Another notable attribute to these candles is the duration of burn time you have. Unlike your traditional wick, these candles burn longer and better. Plus they give a pretty little flame which looks a bit different from your generic candle. Anyway, thats all I really have to say. In conclusion, I would highly recommend this candle or any other candle by Virginia Candle Company. If you ask me how high these candles raise the bar, I would tell you that they are the bar. Nothing can beat them. But in all seriousness, I really do enjoy these candles and have given quite a few of them to my friends and family as gifts after they had asked me about them. These candles really are unique from any other because of the wick they use. If you are considering these candles, I really would encourage you to purchase one because you will not be disappointed with it. I will admit they are a bit pricey compared to your generic candle, (I mean seriously, 18 dollars for a candle) but these truly are a higher quality of candle compared to other brands. headline: I really loved, most the features of this candle.
review_text_raw: So let's start with the smell, it was beautiful and filled a rather large room. I love the woodwick candles! This was the first time I've purchased, a larger wicked candle if that makes sense? The candle is oblong so the wicked is close to 2" wide. I love the sound and light ambience the woodwicks put off, they are one of a kind and I think they are the most amazing candles all around. The reason I'm not giving 5 ☆'s is due to 2 reasons. 1st the candles do not last long at all, unfortunately they burn in less then 1/2 the time a candle 1/2 is size does. 2nd it is a huge, HUGE fire hazard! These larger wicks burn like you've lit a stick on fire in your living room! I burn my new candles on top of my wood stove to see how they burn before placing them out of direct eye site. There is nothing else on, near or above my wood stove and thank God for that because it blew my mind how this candle burned! The flame is gigantic in comparison to any other candle, it almost seems like a candle you would light for the fire not the smell? I highly recommend WOODWICK candles, but if you go with a larger wick one keep in mind it burns like a fire not a candle and keep it in sight at all times while it's burning! Other then these reasons its a wonderful product and the sound! I have to mention the sound of these candles, it sounds like a camp fire on low volume 😃 I HIGHLY RECOMMEND WOODWICK CANDLES!!

review_text_raw: Okay, listen. This isn’t just a candle—it’s basically a personality. The scent situation? Wild. This candle has three layers, three different colors, and three totally different vibes. It’s like aromatherapy speed-dating: one minute I’m sniffing warm vanilla woods, then boom—suddenly I’m transported to a citrus grove, and before I can process that, I’m chilling in a pine forest wondering if I should be chopping firewood. My nose has never been so entertained. The wide wick is basically the MVP—no tunneling, no sad little wax puddles. Just big, bold, “I’m a candle and I know it” energy. Honestly, if this candle had legs, it would probably roast marshmallows for me. 10/10 would buy again. In fact, I’m low-key worried this thing is going to give me main-character energy every time I light it.

Very pleased with this line of candles and highly recommend them if you're looking for a more earthy and not fruity/strawberry smelling candle.

headline: Nice 3-Pack for Variety, But Not Premium Quality
review_text_raw: I got these for my wife and the biggest positive right away is that you get three different pairs in one set. It is nice having options depending on what she is wearing or just being able to keep a pair in different places like the car, bag, or around the house. Style-wise, they actually look really good. The smaller rectangular shape has that retro 90s/Y2K look, and all three color options are easy to match with different outfits. They definitely look better on than you might expect, especially for a multi-pack like this. That said, these are not what I would consider premium sunglasses. You can tell pretty quickly by the feel and weight that they are more on the budget side. The frames are very lightweight and while they are not flimsy, they do not have that solid, higher-end feel either. They are fine for casual use, just not something I would expect to last forever with heavy use. They do a decent job in the sun and are comfortable enough to wear for longer periods. The product page states they offer UV400 protection and lightweight comfort, which seems to line up with how they perform in normal day-to-day use. One thing to note is that while this is a 3-pack, it only comes with a single cloth storage bag, which feels a little odd. It would have made more sense to include one for each pair. Overall, this is a good set if you want multiple stylish pairs without spending a lot. Just go into it knowing the quality is more average than premium, and you will likely be satisfied.

headline: Not Dark Enough
review_text_raw: I’m a nocturnal creature, always have been. Naturally I am up until dawn, and only rouse at dusk. Being that I do 12 hour night shifts, I really don’t have a need “flip” my schedule, and can exclusively live the vampire life. I don’t know if it is cause or effect, but I’ve always been photosensitive as well. As a child, I didn’t realize that it wasn’t normal to squint constantly on a sunny day. I ruin every photo from the flash. I even get light-triggered debilitating migraines. I NEED my sunglasses. So after losing my second pair of Ray-Bans, I couldn’t stomach the cost knowing that I have a tendency to set things down and walk away absent mindedly. Most likely I had dropped them in a parking lot from my purse or hoodie pocket, as I had done in numerous occasions, documented by the scrapes and scuffs on the lenses. It’s just not practical for me to splurge on the item I never prioritized when juggling keys, phone, and bag. My first lost ones were black and silver Clubmasters which I’ve had a hell of a time replacing in those classic colors, much less the polarized ones. I really missed how stylish they were. Then my classic Wayfarers disappeared. In scoping out to actually buy new Clubmasters, did I come across this package deal with both styles and super affordable. I wouldn’t feel shame about my treatment of sunglasses at this price point. When I received them I was super impressed. They were a little lighter weight, but overall seemingly sturdy and nice quality. Superb style, I wouldn’t be ashamed of not wearing designer. So I threw them in my bag to leave for work in the evening, to keep one in the car and save one for my purse. The next morning leaving work, it was nice and bright outside, and after a long shift, it is just the worst to be tired and blinded on a congested commute home. As soon as I hit the exit, I whip out my new glasses, and noticed I still had some eye strain, chalking it up to physical fatigue. Drive home, same thing. The next day I used the other glasses, and it again felt too bright. It only then occurred to me that these are not as dark as I was used to with my Ray Bans. I gave it a few more days, and realized these just don’t seem to make a difference for me. Feels like I’m wearing nothing at all. (Nothing at all, nothing at all...) Taking them on and off, I feel as if there is barely a difference, like they’re a placebo. I had focused so much on getting polarized, I forgot how the most crucial part of sunglasses is the darkening effect. They appear to be dark when you look at them, so it’s kind of an odd thing, and why it took me a day or so for it even to click with me with what was wrong. These are so weak, I feel like the polarized effect didn’t even do much for glare. I can even see clearly LCD displays that I couldn’t see previously even with other discount brands, so I’d say even this feature isn’t as good as it could be. Perhaps these may be useful in other sporting uses that people wear these glasses for, or could even be tinted enough for some, but absolutely not for me. If you’re truly dependent on eye protection and can’t leave the house without them like me, just keep looking.

product_title: Ray-Ban RB3025 Classic Aviator Sunglasses for Men for Women
headline: The Real Deal
review_text_raw: My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens. So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed. Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses: - they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing. - For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available: --- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized' --- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others --- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available --- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT: ----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm ----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length ----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length --- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass: ----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140 ----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135 ----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145 ----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140 ----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160 ----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135 ----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135 ----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135 - once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs: - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get. I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly. Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

(I'm not saying sunglasses will have a perfect seal, but the gap is bigger than other sport glasses I've tried) Besides that, you really can't beat the price. product_title: Ray-Ban RB3025 Classic Polarized Aviator Sunglasses
headline: The Real Deal
review_text_raw: My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens. So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed. Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses: - they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing. - For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available: --- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized' --- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others --- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available --- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT: ----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm ----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length ----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length --- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass: ----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140 ----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135 ----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145 ----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140 ----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160 ----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135 ----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135 ----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135 - once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs: - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple - Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get. I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly. Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

review_text_raw: Let's be honest. At a certain point in life, a man has to make a decision. Do you embrace the full "I buy my sneakers based on orthopedic recommendations" lifestyle, or do you make one last respectable effort to suggest that you may have been cool at some point? These sunglasses are that effort. They're comfortable, fit well, and look good without screaming, "Hey everyone, look how hard I'm trying to look young!" Which is important, because nothing ages a dad faster than trying too hard. I've always admired aviators on other people. Unfortunately, every time I've tried a pair on, I look less like a fighter pilot and more like a guy being questioned by airport security. These, meanwhile, strike the perfect balance. Modern enough to look good, practical enough for everyday wear, and subtle enough that nobody immediately assumes I'm having a midlife crisis. I've worn them driving, coaching kids' sports, running errands, and standing in the driveway pretending to understand whatever home improvement project I'm currently avoiding. Bottom line: Comfortable, stylish, and ideal for dads looking to project the image of a man who still has things under control. Whether that image is accurate is a separate discussion.

headline: 6 month update
review_text_raw: I purchased these in July of 2014. I paid $189 for the black frame/netural gray Glass lenses. They have held up very well. No scratches, and the temple springs are as good as they were when new. I take good care of them, keeping them in their case when not in use, and clean them regularly using a bit of dish soap. I love the clarity and weight of the glass lenses, as they are superior to any of the composite lenses I've had a chance to compare them to, including their own brand's plastic lenses. (I spent some time in a Bass Pro Shop comparing these to Costas, Smiths, and Oakleys) These are my everyday casual and business wear glasses. These are great for driving; the polarization on these lenses is superior to Oakley in my opinion, and I love how well the polarizing lenses cut glare. These also work fantastic for cutting glare on watery surfaces like lakes and rivers, but honestly I am too fearful of losing these in the water to wear them near it! I would not wear these for any activity requiring a lot of movement, such as playing sports, since they are heavy, and because most of the weight is in the lenses, they are likely to fall off. During every day use though, these are secure enough that them falling off your head is a non-issue (unless you try to "store" them on the top of your head when not in use - DON'T do that!). My only grip with these is that after wearing them continuously for more than an hour, they do become a bit uncomfortable on the bridge of my nose.. taking them off for a brief period helps with any discomfort, but this is the sacrifice I'm willing to make to wear glass lenses. I will admit I keep a pair of Oakley flak jackets around for outdoor activities, and for times when I worry about scratching the lens (such as bumming on the beach). However, the quality of these are fantastic and I am glad I purchased them... I will buy another when the time comes. Couple of tips: - In my opinion, I would NOT suggest purchasing these glasses in a composite lens... the glass lenses are so much clearer. In my opinion, these frames are designed to hold a heavy glass lens in place. I would prefer to purchase a composite lens in a "frameless" or "semi-frameless" option to take advantage of the lighter weight of the composite lenses, and the ability to swap lenses on some brands of frames. - The shiny black frame, on the inside of the frame actually reflects light at some angles, and can be distracting. Wearing a hat eliminates this completely, but if you're looking for a frame that completely blocks the sun due to the way it wraps and fits your face, this probably isn't going to be sufficient.

review_text_raw: After a visit to the eye doc it was presumed that my "fave" sunglasses may not be up to the protection job they might have had when new. I was told that many brands of glasses only lightly "coat" the lenses for UV protection especially the "plastic" lenses. Cheap glasses may not have any UV protection at all despite the claims...who tests them?? Nobody?? What apparently isn't told is that these coatings may/do deteriorate over time AND using alcohol lens cleaners and dish soaps may also remove coatings. My research indicated that the more expensive brands have higher quality and more durable UV coatings (impregnated or baked into the glass) that are important to protect your eyes from sun damage -- not just shading. Although my "Faves" were not inexpensive, they were 4 or 5 years old and apparently had inferior to perhaps zero UV blocking abilities today! Long story short, I researched the MJs and found that these glass lenses have superior harmful UV blocking. my Polycarbonate "faves" lenses...less so and were (only effective when new) likely "coated". I did a side by side comparison between these and my old "faves" and I was blowen away by the superior clarity and color crispness of these Maui Jim glasses. You only have one set of eyes...treat them with respect and invest in quality eye ware...not for fashion but, so you don't lose you vision acuity in later years when it's too late to undo damage. Suffice it to say....these are GREAT sunglasses and even look good...a bonus!!! My eyes deserve the investment. Yours do too!!

review_text_raw: I recently purchased my 3rd pair of Maui Jim’s. Love how they fit and the clarity of the lens, especially when driving. Very disappointed in Maui Jim’s decision to downgrade from the quality protective case to the cheap cardboard “sunglass case” that was sent. The previous pairs I have purchased both came with very solid cases. The first pair came with a hard case that had strong hinges that snapped closed and kept my sunglasses safe and I never worried about it coming open on its on and my sunglasses being damaged. My second pair came with a case that had zipper closure with a latching hook at one end. I was able to attach the case for easy access. Great case that made it easy to grab my sunglasses from my bag or off a belt loop always providing a safe place to keep my sunglasses whenever I took them off. That sunglass case was even shown in a photo on the Maui Jim website when I was scrolling through the photos and specifications for the Stingrays I purchased from their website. I thought my sunglasses would be shipped inside that case as the previous pair. I was happy when my sunglasses arrived but very disappointed in the folded cardboard “case” that came with them. I don’t feel confident at all tossing it into my bag as I was accustomed to doing with the two previous cases that my Maui Jim’s arrived in. Cutting corners over there?? Why not just tack on an extra $10 to the purchase price and keep your customers happy and our purchases better protected?

product_title: Lamicall Aluminum Cell Phone Stand, Adjustable Desk Phone Holder for iPhone
headline: Good quality and value, smaller than I would like for my iPhone 6+
review_text_raw: Pro’s; - Economical, nice fit, finish and packaging especially for the price. - Protective adhesive pads on the contact points for the phone as well as on the stand base. - Sturdy construction. It appears as if it will stand up to frequent use without scratching or scuffing and should not easily bend or dent if dropped etc. - The large hole in the stand to easily run your charging cable through was well thought out. Not unique to this brand but much appreciated. Con’s; - It seems a little small for my iPhone 6+. When I opened the package and saw the stand I thought perhaps I had not ordered the right model for a 6+ but the description clearly listed the 6+ as compatible. It certainly does fit the 6+ plus but with the low weight of the stand combined with it’s relative size (and weight) compared to my iPhone 6+ I have some concerns about stability or resistance to tipping over if lightly bumped or if the lightening cable it plugged in and gets snagged on something. - A wider base footprint with a little more weight would relieve some of my concerns as the elevated phone makes these two combined very top heavy especially in portrait mode. Although they have diminished significantly in the last few years we had a spat of mild earthquakes in central Oklahoma a few year back could easily topple this with a phone in portrait mode. I would have more faith in the phone and stand not toppling over under normal conditions if; - The base foot print was wider and perhaps a little heavier (if you have a semi permanent location in mind double sided tape might be an option). - the back support reached at least 2/3 of the way up the back of my 6+ but with my case installed it reaches less than 1/2 the way up (2/5 the way up to be exact) See included pic from the back with my phone in stand. *Back support is 66mm tall. - the phone support arms were a little wider apart. *The product description does clearly show that the outer edges of the phone support arms are 54mm/2.14” apart so you can compare with your phone before ordering. With my relatively small protective case my 6+ is 82mm/3.125” wide in portrait mode which leaves just over an inch difference or 1/2” on either side if perfectly centered. This may be partially more of an aesthetic preference but considering how top heavy the phone is on the stand I would definitely prefer less than 2-3 mm overlap on either side of the support arms. I set my old iPhone 4S with it’s case in the stand for comparison which is much lighter and quite a bit smaller. This seemed a near perfect fit with the back of the phone support reaching at least 1/2 way up and virtually no phone overlap on the support arms. Although not stated anywhere in the description the picture with the exploded diagram of internal “hinge” led me to believe the amount of tension required to change the angle was adjustable so you could lock down a preferred angle which you cannot. That was my misunderstanding however and so far the tension seems adequate to prevent accidental movement while also allowing easy adjustment. This is not really a con and possibly actually a pro that they achieved a perfect balance on the tension assuming you don’t want the option to lock the angle down to prevent accidental manipulation. Overall a good product especially at the price but I would gladly pay more for a similar design that covered my stability concerns.

product_title: Phone Stand for Desk, Foldable Cell Phone Stand Holder, Black
headline: Simple phone stand that just works perfectly
review_text_raw: I was getting neck strain from constantly looking down at my phone during video calls and needed something to prop it up at eye level. This little stand has been such a simple fix for a problem I didn't realize was bothering me so much. The adjustable height thing is clutch - I can set it up for video calls, watching videos in bed, or even following recipes while cooking. Takes like two seconds to adjust and it stays put once you get it where you want it. Way more stable than I expected for something this lightweight. My phone doesn't wobble or tip over even when I'm tapping the screen aggressively. Works great with my case on too which was a concern. The angle adjustment is smooth and holds position really well. I can get it perfectly positioned for whatever I'm doing instead of trying to prop my phone against random objects and having it fall over constantly. Folds up super compact which is great for travel or just tucking it away when I don't need it. Takes up basically no space in my bag or on my desk. Build quality seems solid - no cheap plastic feel or wobbly joints. The hinges feel sturdy and it doesn't seem like it's going to break anytime soon. Works with different phone sizes too. I've used it with my phone and my tablet and both fit fine. Only minor thing is that the base could be slightly heavier for extra stability, but honestly it works fine as is. And the rubber pads keep it from sliding around on smooth surfaces. For the price this thing is a no-brainer. Such a simple solution that makes using your phone way more comfortable. One of those purchases that makes you wonder why you waited so long to get one.

headline: iPad with rear cover in place will fit the slot
review_text_raw: tl;dr One of the rare brands in this style of tablet stand that has a wide enough slot to hold an iPad with a rear case on it. Holds 11” basic iPad (aka iPad 10, iPad A16) WITH Moko flexible plastic rear cover on the back of the tablet, which of course adds to the thickness of the iPad. This is a rear cover only case, and no such luck with a combo case with a front flap screen cover tied to the rear case. The plastic insert provides edge scratch protection for an un-cased iPad (or other metal cased tablet - plastic body tablets are less prone to marring, or at least hide it better). However, the plastic insert reduces the overall thickness of the slot, and on top of that is tapered like a V. My iPad is held securely with or without the insert in place, with or without the rear cover on, but sits much deeper with the insert removed if the case is on. ThereforeI travel with the insert in place, but remove it for the iPad in its rear only case. I prefer the plastic insert in place with uncased tablets like my Fire HD 10. Note that this tablet stand is aluminum except for the piece that rotates to the rear. The stand relies solely on the front leading edge to provide surface grip - it has dual rubber pads to prevent slippage. The rear plastic “prop” has no rubber pads, and is fine on kitchen counters but keep an eye on wood tables for potential scratching or marring over time. There are only two negatives. The first is the “locking button” on the edge of the top. Some knuckleheads have been known to assume it’s a simple “push to rotate” design with detents, and break the lock by trying to muscle it open or closed. This is user misunderstanding, but so common that a warning label should be on the front left arm. The second negative is that the plastic cushion insert isn’t wedged in the slot very well, and easily falls out; right now it is under my typing desk. Yes, I recommend this. User tip: use the box your iPad came in to elevate the height of this tablet stand.

headline: It'll HOLD an APPLE!!
review_text_raw: Okay, the fact that it holds an apple may only be helpful for still-life painters looking for a compact, mini travel easel but it's just good to know. Right? This little stand is AWESOME. It's much stronger than you may think it is. It holds my Galaxy Tab S4 tablet with supreme confidence. The stand doesn't wobble AT ALL. As soon as you feel the weight of it you know it's gonna be super solid. You can quickly and easily set it to a multitude of angles by pushing the big button on the hinge. Once you push the button in you can hold it in and move it to any angle you want or SLIGHTLY move the leg back you can then release the button and it will stay depressed until it hits the next preset angle. There are MANY angles. I counted. 23 total angles it can be set to. Because the stand rotates 270 degrees around, I find only 9 of those 23 settings usable if you want to incorporate the lip in front to hold a table, phone, etc. Out of those 9 angles, I found that I only really used 2 or 3 or em' so don't worry at all about the other 14 angles. Just know that if you want to get creative with this thing, it'll GIVE you angles. For a goof, You could use it as an easy access pen holder if you wanted to (see photo). I love the fact that there is a removable insert to fit phones or tablets with cases, even thick ones (see photo). I DO think it would've been really cool if there were a neat little storage area for the insert on the stand itself cuz you could lose the insert if you're not keeping track of it. The insert doesn't "snap" into the lip but it kinda wedges in tightly. It's well engineered. I tried to shake out the insert and it wasn't budging. Oh, also, you CAN open this with just one hand (see photo) but you may need to prop it up against your leg or a table or something like that. I bought 2 of these cuz I liked it so much and you just never know when you need it. Currently, we are using this when we go out to a restaurant with our 3-year-old so he can watch Peppa Pig on Mommy's phone and we can savor a brief moment of peace over a meal. LOVE it. Recommend it to anyone looking for a tablet/phone stand...or a mini, travel easel. Hope this was helpful.

I recommend putting your devices on the stand before bed and letting them charge overnight rather than expecting extremely fast charging during the day. Being able to charge three Apple devices in one compact location helps keep everything organized and makes it a great addition to a nightstand, desk, or office. product_title: SENSYNE 62" Phone Tripod, Extendable Selfie Stick with Wireless Remote
headline: Im kicking myself right now
review_text_raw: Why did I wait so long to get this? So Ive been thinking about getting a phone compatible tripod for a while but didnt want to end up with another piece of junk equipment that just sat unused in the corner. After seeing this on sale I decided to go for it. First off it's sturdy, when I pulled this out I was actually surprised how hefty it was. Not necessarily heavy but the majority of it is a lightweight metal when I was expecting it to be mostly plastic. Even then its less than 2lbs with my phone on it so those who need portability, youre good. It comes fully assembled other than choosing which adapter you want to use (phone or go pro) so no annoying instructions and zillion little pieces to deal with before you can use it. The feet are adjustable to fit the footprint of whatever area you have from quite small to fit on a small tabletop to spread out for more stability on the floor, and you can lock them at whatever place you need them. The phone adapter easily fit my iPhone 14ProMax. Height is easily and infinitely adjustable from about 16" tall to 62" tall and feels very stable even at full height (although at full extension I definitely recommend spreading the feet out as far as you have room for) Initially I wasn't even going to use the remote but its as easy to connect as a pair of ear buds, through bluetooth settings, and worked perfectly even with my 3rd party camera app. If youre even considering one of these just get it now while it's on sale. Like I said in the title, Im kicking myself that I didnt do it much earlier. Its a great item at a great price.

The selfie stick feature is another thing he’s mentioned he really likes. Portability is another reason he’s happy with it. He says it fits easily into his bag and doesn’t add too much bulk, which is great for someone who’s always on the go. As for the build quality, he mentioned that it’s solid but not too heavy-duty. It’s more than sturdy enough for regular use, though. The phone mount is adjustable and keeps his phone secure, even when he’s recording for extended periods. All in all, my friend’s been super happy with the SENSYNE 62" Phone Tripod & Selfie Stick. He told me it’s made a big difference in the quality of his recordings, and he finds it super easy to use. Based on his experience, I’d definitely recommend this to anyone who’s looking for an affordable and versatile tripod or selfie stick for social media content creation!

product_title: Yamaha JR1 FG Junior 3/4 Size Acoustic Guitar, Natural
headline: Very Good, But Small 3/4 Accoustic Guitar
review_text_raw: I am basically an advanced beginner, having started out about a year and a half ago on the Yamaha 3/4 Size Classcal Guitar (with nylon strings.) Also taking lessons. I recently purchased this Yamaha FG 3/4 Size Accoustic Guitar. In my opinion, it has good intonation, has a more than decent rich sound to it. It is definitely not a "toy" guitar. After about five tunings at the beginning, it has held its tune well--only very few tweaks. The action is low without buzzing, which is good for tender finger tips, and just plain, overall fretting. I have to agree with some of the reviewers who believe this to be smaller than a 3/4 size guitar. This one is pretty small. I don't think it's 3/4 size--more of a half-size. I am only 5 feet tall, female, with small frame and fingers, and I find the distance between the strings to be a bit of a tight squeeze. Distance in frets is okay for my stature. I was worried that going to a steel string accoustic guitar would be painful on the tips of my fretting fingers since I have nerve damage in my fingers--one of the reasons I started off on the Yamaha 3/4 size classical with nylon strings (which is a great nylon string guitar for beginners), but I don't realize any difficulty or pain with this steel string guitar. I have calluses by now, but even so, for one just starting out on a steel string, I don't think it's any more painful than starting out on nylon strings. A setup by a luthier, I don't think it is at all necessary unless you are at least an intermediate, at which point you probably own a $500+ guitar that has a louder sound (I think this one has more than average projection, and aginn, intonation). Besides a bit of a problem with the string-to-string closeness, the only other thing I can think of is the fretboard, compared to the overall size of the guitar, and the body, is more than average heavy--not a real biggie, but I thought I'd mention it. Because of its small size, if you are taller than five feet, or have average or large hands, I can't give it five stars. If you know enough about guitars and think you can handle a guitar this size, I would give it five stars, especially for a small child. All in all, if you are looking for a beginner steel string accoustic guitar, especially for a child just starting out, I don't think you could go wrong with this guitar. You get a real guitar at a very good price, that's pretty vibrant, while keeping in mind that it is on a small scale. Here, I would give it five stars. If I had a child who wanted to start playing a steel string accoustic guitar, I would not hesitate to purchase this guitar. If you are taller than five feet, or have large fingers, I do feel this good guitar would be a bit of a tight squeeze, and also possibly not as comfortable to hold. If, on the other hand, you want to purchase a very nice quality guitar without shelling out big bucks, especially for a beginner, I would highly recommend this guitar.

I did finally cut that material off and no longer have an issue.

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!
review_text_raw: I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings. The finish is very satin and may not be pleasing for those that enjoy glossy guitars though i think it's OK and seems tough enough. My GL1 came with a small blemish in the wood on the back which is an imperfection in the wood itself and not the finish. I would take 1/2 a star for the blemish but quality control is overall pretty good and the fret ends aren't noticeably sharp. I would not recommend this instrument for beginners due to the short fret spacing and slightly more difficult fingering for some chords. A 1/2 or 3/4 scale classical or steel string guitar will be a better choice for learning the fundamentals and will have more volume for performances later on when the player gains confidence. Who is this instrument for? number one, it's for me. I have been playing guitar for decades and have a soft spot for small bodied instruments and recently started playing my wife's ukulele due to my guitar being down for the count. Ukulele players might enjoy this instrument as a way to cross over to six string though the string spacing will take some getting used to. Guitar players who want a sturdy travel guitar will be well served by this instrument but will have to make peace with transposing everything up a fourth. Some players have used high tension strings to allow for standard guitar tuning. I'm not sure I will do so as I like the sound as it is and also play ukulele music. Overall I think the Yamaha GL-1 is a reasonable value for the money and I'm very happy with it so far.

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: A quality instrument from Yamaha
review_text_raw: 69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes. This thing came quicky to me in Hawaii, and it is in perfect condition! Since it had nylon/classical type strings, it is going to take much longer for the strings to settle down and stop sretching. Way longer than my steel stringers. So, don't write a review after a few days complaining about this. All classical style nylon string guitars do this! Pick it up,tune it, play it, and keep tuning it. The tuners on mine seem just fine. It is a total blast for me to play. It sounds great, especially for the small body size. It has very good volume and sustain too. A bit stingy on the fret markers, both on the fingerboard and side of the neck. If you have big fingers, some chording might be a bit crowded. It doesn't have a truss rod. But, many classical guitars and many other guitaleles don't have them either. I have yet to read a review, or watch a video review, where the owner had a neck warp. In short, I should have bought one of these long ago. Update after more than a year now. I still love this little 6 stringer! I have been selling some of my amps and ukes etc. I had considered selling my Yamaha, but cannot do it! It is just such a great insrument. Mine is still perfect. Drawbacks? Few. The 17" scale is a bit tight for me. One string started unravelling after not too much playing. I was able to buy the one string and replaced it. I read a review somewhere where the writer returned his due to various flaws. Looking at mine it's hard to believe. I think Yamaha should make an option of the GL-1 that would come with an under saddle pickup with tuner and volume/tone controls. Great price, great instrument, great FUN!! 2/28/2025 update: Just wanted to say my estimation of this instrument has gone up if anything. I am taking super good care of it. It us holding up great. I had one of the wound strings start to unravel early and replaced it. Zero problems. After break in it holds tune as good or better than my other string instruments. That alone is saying a lot. The climate here in the Puna District on the big island plays he'll with stringed instruments. Most go sharp sitting overnight, and flat sitting during the day. This little guy is built very well. I wish it had come with an active pickup with tuned and equalizer, but it's still a keeper!

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: Perfect little guitar for fun and travel
review_text_raw: This little thing is one of my dearest possessions!! I've played guitar as a hobby off and on for about 18 years and have a couple of full-sized acoustics. About a year ago I started researching smaller instruments because I wanted something easy to travel with. I looked into 1/4 size student guitars and I looked into the Little Martin and its Taylor equivalent. While the Little Martin has great reviews and a great sound, it costs 3-4 times more than this little guy does. It's definitely worth that price, but I didn't have that kind of money to spend. For about $100, the Yamaha Guitalele is excellent. It has a beautiful sound and it's very easy to pick up and take it with you on trips! (To keep it safer for long trips I bought a hard shell tenor uke case which works really well for it. I also bought one of those little Snark clip-on tuners and have been very satisfied with that as well.) Two things which take some adjusting to if you are used to playing a full-size guitar: 1) The strings are a lot closer together and your fingers may feel fat and clumsy at first. I got used to this pretty fast though. 2) The guitalele is tuned to A instead of the standard E tuning of a full-sized guitar. Basically this means anything you play on the guitalele is like playing your reg. guitar with a capo on the 5th fret. So when you play a C-shape chord on this guy, you are actually playing a G chord. I was used to playing a lot of songs on my regular guitar and had to figure out how to translate them to continue playing them in the same key. (It's possible to lower the tuning to E if you want, but the strings have a slack, kind of rubbery sound and they don't stay in tune as long.) I'd recommend checking out the YouTube video reviews for this instrument before you buy it if you have any more questions. You can hear what it sounds like and get some expert input! It really is great. I love mine to the moon and back and have had a blast playing it!

review_text_raw: This guitalele has opened up a bit since I got it. I started playing ukulele 2 years ago, and started learning guitar almost a year ago. After having Amazon cancel an order I placed on an acoustic guitar from the Amazon Warehouse. (Grr! Btw on that! I feel really cheated considering the same guitar turned up with a seller who refabs and resells damaged instruments, and I was extremely excited about it, until I got the message "they couldn't find it," last minute on delivery day!!! 😠 That's so wrong imo.) I chose this guitalele in it's stead however. It has issues with frets not being cut long enough in spots but nothing that makes it unplayable. It's cosmetic for the most part. There's a few other purely cosmetic issues. Mine has a couple spots the factory missed applying the wood filler to, on the body to make it smooth. Theres a small spot on the bottom of the neck where the wood chipped before assembly and it wasn't filled with filler or even glue to fill the gap. It's a mass produced instrument at an affordable price. I was expecting small imperfections. The sloppy fret cutting job is the only kind-of annoying one to me. The one I have is actually a replacement for one I exchanged which had a mfg. defect which made it unplayable. The first one wasn't inspected properly and shouldn't have left the factory in the dangerous condition it was in. Amazon took care of me immediately and the exchange was smooth and painless. Hopefully yamaha corrects the quality control issues in their factory. For my own play style I had the nut filed down so my hand could glide over the nut. The stock nut height stopped my hand down there like a brick wall, and having the nut done cost as much as the guitalele. This probably won't bother most people. I'm just throwing it out there, that the nut sticks up above the string height, and if you like to slide in or out by the nut, it might be something to consider for someone. The piece of wood that was used on the back of the one I received is unexpectedly pretty. I got lucky. The top has nice strait grain. The neck is ugly. It's constructed in a few pieces and mine doesn't remotely match. One side appears to have had a patch of tear out or something, and Yamaha filled it really nicely with filler, but the filler is darker than the neck wood and adds to the kind of sloppy franken-neck look. Again, not a deal breaker. I can't feel a difference, and they have to keep costs down. When I got it, it sounded a little "stuffy." After playing it daily since I got it, the wood seems to have opened up a bit on all tones except the low A, which still sounds the same. If it does open up, this instrument is pretty impressive sounding for the money in my opinion. Someone said in another review the thing is built like a tank. I agree. It's not a delicate feeling instrument. It seems pretty well constructed until the fret wire though. Overall it's been fun to play. It's the perfect size. I left sheerness blank in the star rating. Not sure how that applies to a guitalele or any stringed instrument? Thickness doesn't really apply either, but I rated it 4 because the wood is thick. I might update this review in the future if anything changes, but I'd probably get another one if something happens to mine.

Hopefully yamaha corrects the quality control issues in their factory. For my own play style I had the nut filed down so my hand could glide over the nut. I'm just throwing it out there, that the nut sticks up above the string height, and if you like to slide in or out by the nut, it might be something to consider for someone. Not sure how that applies to a guitalele or any stringed instrument? Thickness doesn't really apply either, but I rated it 4 because the wood is thick. product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: decent, doesn't need to be tuned up a full 4th to sound OK
review_text_raw: Mahalo used to make a similar product for less than half the price, so this guy seems a little overpriced to me – but since the Mahalo seems to be discontinued, there's no real competitor, and this hardly breaks the bank. It has entirely acceptable playability, sound, intontation, etc. I especially like to play it like a mandolin, flat-picking single lines, but of course it can play full-chord accompaniments, sounding just like a ukulele but lower. Travels fine, though one thing to note about the classic camp-singalong use is that the nylon strings are suuuuuper sensitive to temperature changes, so it's a bit frustrating playing it outdoors in chilly air next to a hot campfire – you might need to invest in a steel-string alternative if you can't abide that. You *can* tune it to standard guitar tuning (E2, A2, D3, ...), which is useful if you want to use it for, say, composing on the go and not get confused about which key you're in – but down there the strings sound like garbage and don't stay in tune. The recommended tuning is up a 4th, which I find a bit high, since you can't even play G2 (de facto a lot of things you play on guitars tend to be in keys like G, D, C ...). One solution is to use the recommended tuning but with "drop G" (lowest string = G2), which sounds fine. But you also can just tune the whole thing a major 3rd higher than a guitar (major 2nd lower than the recommended tuning), rather than a 4th (so: G2, C3, F3 ....) which IMHO sounds just as good and stays in tune just as well. (I just personally keep getting confused by the mental arithmetic that requires – what you expect to be a G major chord is actually Bb major ... etc.)

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: I take mine everywhere
review_text_raw: I love this thing. I tied a strap to it with some shoe strings, I slap it on my back, get on my bike. I take it with me when I go hiking, to school, to the beach, or anywhere really. The tuning on it is ADGCEA which would be equal to as if you had a capo on a regular guitar's 5th fret, which means that you can play the same chord shapes as a regular guitar, the notes will just be higher. As far as quality goes, I'm pretty happy with it. Some people said the strings that they got were no good, but I've had mine for about 3 months now and I have no complaints. The strings are very sensitive though. They bend very easily, so sometimes the chords played sound good and other times they might sound a little off. I see as a very delicate instrument.. when I press down my fingers for chords I press them straight down and make sure I'm not bending them. A;so, because they bend easily, it can go out of tune pretty easily too. I tune mine often, to make sure they are good to go. I have always tuned my normal guitars by ear, however I find that it is harder to do with the guitarlele, so I use a tuner usually. Visually I have no complaints, the wood and finish are nice, the neck has good action and feel, although a small part of me wishes that they had some artwork around the soundhole. As for sound quality, I love it.. the higher strings/notes do stand out more in a way, and definitely have the ukulele sound, but if you play gently enough it creates a nice balance. The resonance is beautiful. It has a very warm, mellow sound. It's pretty loud for it's size too. And it is so versatile, you can play Spanish style chords like Em and Am which sounds awesome (Onda Vaga uses a uke, perfect example, youtube them), .. you can emulate a mandolin to an extent.. I'm not saying it sounds exactly like a mandolin since it obviously can't replicate the resonant-sound of the double layered strings, but it does have the high notes from the strings that at least sound somewhat similar to a mandolin, if you want to cover a song with one. Or you can just play regular songs, normal chord shapes, even powerchords sound good. It's just like guitar. Just tuned to much higher notes. If you know music theory, you can do a lot with this little guitar. I even have used a capo on mine and it sounds good, although when I put it too high up the fret spaces are so small it's hard to make the chord shapes ;-) Before I saw the guitarlele I was looking at rogue instruments because they sell cheap mandolins and ukuleles. I checked out reviews of their instruments on youtube and they had some mixed reviews.. they didn't seem like very good quality. I saw someone mention the guitarlele on the comments, and when I looked it up I knew it was the 'travel' instrument I wanted. 100 bucks, for a completely unique Yamaha brand instrument? You can't go wrong. Yamaha aren't the super-high end guitars, but my bigger acoustic is a yamaha and I don't have any complaints about that one either (a friend gave it to me to replace my epiphone acoustic which I need to get a new saddle for). I hope this review was helpful. If you get one, enjoy it. I know I enjoy mine. I've even started buying other travel instruments like a melodica and a Buffalo Drum.. so yeah. Enjoy!!

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: Here is the "real deal" review on this Guitalele
review_text_raw: I've been playing, and writing music since 1984. I play a myriad of instruments and currently, I write and record commercially licensed music under BMI, Inc. My Wife bought this instrument for me for a holiday gift, but I wanted to check it out before it gets wrapped.. just in case of damage. I am glad that I did. I also know how to setup and do maintenance on both electronic and acoustic instruments. The good things about this instrument: This instrument sounds really good, as it seems to be structurally sound. I do not see any cracks in the body or missing glue around the neck joint. The strings are nice wrapped around to tuning pags. The open faced tuners and gears seem to be of a higher quality than others that I have seen. The bad things about this instrument: The bridge saddle is WAY too high. I have no issues in regards to setting up a bridge saddle, but I expected Yamaha to be a "bit more" on the quality control side of things and at least have the saddle to a more "normal" height. The fretboard and body of this instrument was "very" dry. I used some Music Nomad f-one oil on the fretboard and some of the body as it needed it "badly". The thing that was VERY surprising to me, is there were run-offs / rough spots in the back and sides of the instrument. For a more inexpensive instrument from a no-name company.. I could see that. .but for the price and the Yamaha name.. again.. VERY SURPRISING. I'm also having some issues in regards to getting a partial from Amazon for some reason, but I have amplified that further up the chain on the Amazon side. Other things to think about: I was able to tune this to a standard guitar tuning, that is very possible. The neck is "wide" just like a classical guitar. A lot of people think this is a hybrid instrument of an acoustic guitar and a baritone ukulele. It's really a cross between an Classical Guitar and a baritone ukulele. Conclusion: I am sure that I will have a really awesome time opening this on Christmas day and setting up the saddle on the bridge. And I can probably buff out the rough spots in the finish.. but buying this really changed my mind in regards to Yamaha quality control. UPDATE: I was able to take off a lot of material from the saddle, and lowered the strings, so the playability is better, but I still am a bit suprised in regards to the rough spots in the finish. The instrument should be priced in the $50.00 USD mark. Other than that, it does make a nice portable instrument in regards to classical guitar or baritone ukulele. - Tom

product_title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
headline: A Delightful Addition to the Collection!
review_text_raw: This little guy is so much fun! I love playing the ukulele, but sometimes it can be a little frustrating. With only four strings, uke chords often end up in awkward inversions, having a chord tone other than the tonic as the lowest note. By adding two strings to the bass side, you can always have the inversion you want. For uke players the chords will be a little more complex with two additional strings to deal with. Also, in strumming the "uke sound" you'll need to get the hang of not hitting the bottom two strings. But it's all worth the effort and makes for a more "musically complete" sound. For uke players aspiring to play guitar, this is a great bridge. I think guitarists will find it fun as well. The chords are all familiar but will sound a fourth up. Guitarists who are familiar with using a capo won't have any problem with this. Videos online show how to restring the instrument so it can play down in guitar range, but I think it's more fun as a "super uke!" I like the sunburst style and mahogany back and sides. It has a nice, warm uke-y tone. I'm glad I got it!

If you are seriously looking to learn how to play the guitar then I suggest paying a little more to get a good guitar. We paid almost 100 dollars for this, and more since to replace strings and fix the frets in an attempt to optimize it the best we could. Paying more upfront for a good working guitar with correct fret placement is the best thing to do. I guess we will know better next time. Don't waste your money unless you are looking for a decoration for your room.

headline: It’s not worth it
review_text_raw: Review – Fender FA-25N Nylon (3/4) This guitar is very disappointing unless you’re buying it strictly for a small child. If you have slightly wider fingers, chord shapes are uncomfortable right away. The neck feels narrow, and even basic chords like C major are awkward and frustrating to play. The biggest issue is the extremely high action. The strings sit very high off the fretboard, making the guitar hard to play and tiring on the fingers. It’s obvious this is done at the factory to avoid fret buzz, but it completely kills playability. The guitar does not feel inviting to play at all. The instrument is lightweight, and the body doesn’t look poorly assembled, but build quality alone doesn’t make a good musical experience. Comfort and playability matter — and this guitar fails there. Yes, it’s cheap, but the overall playing experience is bad. If you have any prior musical experience or basic expectations, this guitar is not worth it. Conclusion: Only suitable for a young beginner with small hands. Otherwise, I do not recommend it. I’m very disappointed and would not buy this model again.

review_text_raw: READ THIS IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS GUITAR!!! I bought this used - very good for 45 bucks about a year ago. I probably would not pay full price, as much as I love it. That being said, IT IS NOT JUNK GIVE IT TIME! I swear half the people leaving negative reviews have no idea how guitars work. I am a full grown adult guitar player, and I've been playing since high school. I'm in college now, and I needed something small and light to travel with. I DON'T USE THIS AS MY EVERYDAY GUITAR! I reach for this guy if I'm messing around with chords, my fingers hurt from my metal strings, or I'm just trying to relax. It's great to practice on, but not so much if you're trying to actually play in front of people. Nylons aren't meant to be used like metal stringed acoustics, they're a separate instrument! It still works for that purpose, though, you can play the same exact songs and chords. If you tune it properly it gets the job done. Great for my college dorm or throwing in the car for a camping trip cus it's super light. Great to practice on when I don't feel like lugging my full sized acoustic around. This is a decent product for the price I PAID. Being a nylon string guitar, you have to stretch the strings and tune it quite a bit (2-4 days is recommended for the strings to settle - watch a youtube tutorial on how to do it) Furthermore, the plastic strings that everyone complains about are standard on a nylon. Heck, the C40 from Yamaha, well established nylon, has the same type (but higher quality, I bet) if I recall. They do go out of tune pretty frequently, especially at the start, but it's not even that much - just retune them! The tuner works well for me, but if you don't like it, just get an app like GuitarTuna. Now, for the guitar itself, it's what I expected when I bought it for 45 bucks, barely even damaged since I got a higher quality used (or less damaged I guess) version, and I have to say, it has really grown on me. Guitars are instruments, not toys. You can't give it to a kid and expect them to learn the ins and outs. If you really want them to learn guitar, buy them a cheap acoustic like a rogue or Yamaha, a C40 is a great nylon but you could also get them a metal string, and get them lessons! Find a music store near you, it might be a bit pricey but it's the best way to learn. Originally I recommended swapping the strings, but it's not worth it to be honest. I got it back in 2021 for 45 USD used, and I love it for what I use it for. If you're dead-set on a cheap starter guitar, or you want an affordable spare, grab this but follow my advice. If you really want to learn, shell out the extra money and buy a tried and true brand. For the full price, 80 bucks is not worth it. Get a rogue for that money. Anyway, that's my rant, hope this helps! (I even bumped my review up from 4 to 5 stars - when I first wrote it, it was 1 star because I didn't understand stretching the nylon strings - IT TAKES TIME! but I genuinely love this thing!) Enjoy!

headline: 20+ years playing - this is a fine instrument
review_text_raw: First off - this does not come set up in any way shape or form. If you are not familiar with guitars and buy this for a child please know that it's not a horrible instrument just because the strings come loose. The first thing I did is replace the strings - I got the nylon version and nylon strings are notorious for taking forever to stretch out to their final length. Another thing to be aware of - the guitar going out of tune with brand new strings is not the guitar's fault - that's just the nature of classical guitars and since it wasn't setup or tuned from the factory it's going to take a while after you get it for it to stay in tune because the strings are stretching out slowly. I pick the guitar right up by the strings and bounce it a bit to help stretch things out when I change nylon strings. Second, this is a 70 dollar guitar, manage your expectations. I have about 10 different stringed instruments in my possession in varying qualities. I've bought cheaper instruments when I was planning on spending a chunk of money because the cheaper instruments can sometimes play and sound much better. You don't need to spend a massive amount of money for a solid instrument - and frankly the Pyle brand is pretty excellent for the cost. I own a bunch of their microphones and they are pretty epic honestly. I've had people listen to my podcast and tell me how impressed they are with my sound quality and think I'm using 100$+ microphones - and I'm finding the same with the guitar quality. Good tuners, decent bridge, it's really not bad. The finish is not great though - if you are purchasing an instrument for aesthetics this probably isn't for you. They put some weird coating on the fret board that was already flaking off when I got it - though I bought this as a beater guitar so I really don't care. There was also cracking in the finish at the bottom of the guitar. None of this affects playability or sound - so I don't care. I bought some fun fret marker stickers since this doesn't have any inlays, and the new strings I bought are funky colors. It looks pretty awesome for the 90$ I spent in total with the strings and inlay stickers. It sounds good. It feels great in my hands. I can toss this one in the car or put it on the floor and I couldn't care less if it gets scratched - money well spent.
